items.quote: In the recently concluded Board meeting, our Board of Directors have declared an interim dividend of INR2. Including this dividend, our payouts in the last 1 year, we would be returning in excess of $3 billion in terms of the cash back to shareholders.

items.statement: Mindsprint acquisition closed; integration moved to execution; seeing opportunities in food and agriculture sector
items.quote: During the quarter, we closed the acquisition of Mindsprint and quickly transitioned from integration planning to execution. While we continue to deepen our relationship with Olam Group, we have also started to see good opportunities in the food and agriculture sector.

items.statement: Headcount down 2,500 QoQ excluding Mindsprint acquisition; attrition well controlled
items.quote: Just to add, outside of Mindsprint, the head count has actually gone down by 2,500 people.

items.statement: AI deals vary: cost-optimization deals have forward productivity baked in; Reimagine AI and data/AI advisory services command premium pricing
items.quote: Wherever the intention is to use AI for you to be able to drive higher productivity and take costs out for a large operations for a client where the cost take-out is priority, you will see that, there will be a lot of productivity, forward productivity that gets baked into deals. The Reimagine AI that Srini spoke about, the parts which are newer, where you are going to be seeing newer spends on ac

items.statement: Competitive pressure in traditional IT/BPO as clients compress budgets and demand AI deployment; pricing varies by client AI readiness and token cost considerations
items.quote: From a broader industry perspective, Abhishek, if I look at it, AI is reshaping most of the spend allocations. So what that means is from a client perspective, the tradition al IT, the traditional BPO that we do and the support aspects of it, those budgets are getting compressed.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical under pressure from US structural/demographic forces, budget reallocation to compliance and AI; no specific recovery timeline given
items.quote: The impact that we had is because of the US Healthcare ecosystem, right, which is facing sustained pressure both from structural and demographic forces due to the situation which is very much within the -- in the US context, right?

items.statement: Investing in AI-native business unit: talent, infrastructure, platforms, Wipro Ventures ($500M targeting AI/data/security startups), 10 innovation networks, ecosystem partnerships
items.quote: We want to invest in our new AI-native business. We want to -- because when you're doing an AI-native business, you also need to have the right talent, you need to have the right infrastructure to build the new products, new platforms and solutions as well.

items.statement: Guided cost-to-income ratio around 45% and expect it to remain in that range
items.quote: We have guided for around 45% and we expect it to remain in that range.

items.statement: Guided credit cost to remain within 1% for remaining quarters
items.quote: for the remaining quarters, slippages and credit cost should remain within our guided range of 1%.

items.statement: Expect gross NPA to reach 1.50-1.60%
items.quote: We expect gross NPA to reach 1.50-1.60%, and I do not see any challenge in achieving that.

items.statement: Recovery guidance of Rs.4,500-5,500 crore for the year, achieved Rs.1,900 crore in Q1
items.quote: Against our rec overy guidance of Rs.4,500-5,500 crore, we have already achieved almost Rs.1,900 crore

items.statement: Expect advances growth of 13-14% with balanced growth approach
items.quote: Growth of 13-14% is also a good outcome.

items.statement: NIM guidance range 3.15-3.25%, upper end achievable
items.quote: Hopefully, yes. There is currently no major trigger for further margin expansion unless interest rates rise or further repricing occurs.

items.statement: ECL transition impact expected around Rs.3,000-3,500 crore, Rs.1,000 crore already provided
items.quote: We expect the ECL transition impact to be around Rs.3,000-3,500 crore. Earlier, I had indicated that we would try to provide Rs.1,500-2,000 crore during the year, of which Rs.1,000 crore has already been provided.

items.statement: Plan to raise USD1.5-2.0 billion through FCNR(B) and ECB
items.quote: Going forward, I expect to raise between USD1.5 billion and USD2 billion.

items.statement: Agriculture growth expected to return to 15-16% range
items.quote: Going forward, we expect agriculture growth to return to the 15-16% range.

items.statement: Treasury profit assumed around Rs.600-700 crore in annual plan
items.quote: In our annual plan, we have assumed treasury profit of only around Rs.600-700 crore.

items.statement: Expect performance towards upper end of guided ranges based on Q1 results
items.quote: Based on the Q1 results, we expect performance to be towards the upper end of the guided ranges.

items.statement: Domestic and global NIM expanded by 6 basis points sequentially
items.quote: Both domestic and global NIM expanded by 6 basis points.

items.statement: Cost of deposits declined despite tightening in first two months, bulk deposits unchanged at Rs.1.61 lakh crore
items.quote: Bulk deposits remained unchanged at around Rs.1.61 lakh crore between March and June.

items.statement: Prefer borrowings at 5.00-5.25% over bulk deposits costing 100-150 bps more
items.quote: Borrowings are available at around 5.00-5.25%, whereas even short-duration bulk deposits of 30 or 60 days can cost at least 100-150 basis points more.

items.statement: Shed Rs.6,000 crore of thinly priced loans, disciplined approach to continue
items.quote: On a sequential basis, we shed around Rs.6,000 crore of loans where pricing was highly competitive. We expect this disciplined approach to continue.

items.statement: Margins may expand marginally by 2-3 basis points, no major trigger for significant increase
items.quote: Margins may expand marginally by around 2-3 basis points.

items.statement: Total jewel loan book is Rs.1.32 lakh crore
items.quote: The total jewel-loan book is Rs.1.32 lakh crore.

items.statement: NBFC book declined Rs.6,000-7,000 crore between June and March, added Rs.3,000 crore in Q1
items.quote: The NBFC book had declined by around Rs.6,000-7,000 crore between June and March. During this quarter, we added around Rs.3,000 crore.

items.statement: Gross NPA declined 115 bps YoY and 12 bps QoQ to 1.86%, net NPA flat at 0.15%
items.quote: Gross NPA declined by 115 basis points year-on-year and 12 ba sis points sequentially to 1.86%. Net NPA remained flat at 0.15

items.statement: Slippage ratio declined to 0.77% from 0.96% in March 2026, recoveries Rs.1,885 crore vs slippages Rs.1,250 crore
items.quote: The slippage ratio declined to 0.77% from 0.96% in March’ 26. Recoveries were Rs.1,885 crore, compared with s lippages of Rs.1,250 crore

items.statement: SMA book broadly flat, SMA-2 above Rs.5 crore increased Rs.190 crore due to one DCCO-related account
items.quote: The overall SMA book remained broadly flat. SMA-2 accounts above Rs.5 crore increased by around Rs.190 crore, mainly because one account moved into SMA-2 following a DCCO-related issue.

items.statement: Made floating provision of Rs.1,000 crore for ECL during the quarter
items.quote: Yes. We made a floating provision of Rs.1,000 crore during the quarter.

items.statement: SMA-1 approximately Rs.7,000 crore, SMA-2 approximately Rs.7,700 crore
items.quote: SMA-1 is approximately Rs.7,000 crore and SMA-2 is approximately Rs.7,700 crore.

items.statement: Home loan rates around 7.15-7.20%, no bank taking lead in reducing rates further
items.quote: The bulk-deposit market has cooled suddenly, but home-loan rates remain around 7.15-7.20%. No bank is taking the lead in reducing rates further.

items.statement: FCNR(B) mobilisation USD150 million as of today, pipeline of USD1 billion, target USD1.5-2.0 billion including ECB
items.quote: On FCNR(B), we ha ve raised a round USD150 million as of today, until yesterday, the amount was USD135 million. Going forward, I expect to raise between USD1.5 billion and USD2 billion

items.statement: CASA ratio improved 6 bps sequentially and 76 bps YoY to 39.73%
items.quote: The domestic CASA ratio improved by 6 basis points sequentially and by around 76 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Return on equity stood at 19.48%
items.quote: Return on equity stood at 19.48%.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio 17.58%, CET1 16.51%
items.quote: The capital adequacy ratio is 17.58%, and CET1 is 16.51%.

items.statement: Made Rs.310 crore provision for West Asia crisis in previous quarter, added Rs.13 crore this quarter
items.quote: We remain watchful. That is why we made a provision of Rs.310 crore for the West Asia crisis in the previous quarter and have continued it. With the exposure increasing by around Rs.12-13 crore, we made a further provision of Rs.13 crore.

items.statement: No visible MSME stress yet, SMA book declined YoY from 7.99 to 4.69 and QoQ from 4.73 to 4.69
items.quote: We had also expected that there might be some MSME stress, but so far it is not visible. The SMA book declined year-on-year from 7.99 to 4.69 and sequentially from 4.73 to 4.69.

items.statement: IBPC transaction only around Rs.200 crore, not significant
items.quote: Only around Rs.200 crore. The amount was not significant.

items.statement: Insurance expense bracket one
items.quote: We are in bracket one.

items.statement: QAAUM was INR9.35 trillion, up 13% YoY, with 11.2% market share (12.4% excluding ETFs)
items.quote: Our QAAUM stood at INR9.35 trillion, up 13% Y-o-Y, with a market share of 11.2%. Excluding ETFs, our market share stood at 12.4%.

items.statement: Actively managed equity-oriented QAAUM grew 16% YoY to INR5.74 trillion, equity orientation at 65.7% vs industry 56.6%
items.quote: Our actively managed equity -oriented QAAUM grew 16% year -on- year to INR5.74 trillion. Our equity orientation continues to be meaningfully higher than the industry. Equity -oriented assets accounted for 65.7% of our QAAUM versus 56.6% for the industry.

items.statement: Debt QAAUM at INR1.66 trillion (12.9% share), liquid QAAUM at INR851 billion (10.7% share)
items.quote: On the fixed income side, debt QAAUM stood at INR1.66 trillion with a market share of 12.9% and liquid QAAUM at INR851 billion with a 10.7% market share

items.statement: Unique investors grew to 17.1 million, added 0.46 million in quarter; penetration at 28% vs 25% a year ago
items.quote: On unique investors, we added roughly 0.46 million during the quarter when the industry added 0.53 million, taking our base to 17.1 million. Our penetration in the mutual fund industry now stands at 28%, up from 25% a year ago.

items.statement: Systematic transactions (SIP+STP) at INR48.1 billion in June 2026, up 20% YoY
items.quote: Systematic transactions, which is SIP plus STP, stood at INR48.1 billion in June 2026 compared to INR40.1 billion in June 2025, a Y-o-Y growth of 20%.

items.statement: Alternatives AUM (AIF, PMS, advisory) at INR148 billion, up from INR60 billion a year ago; private credit fund closing this quarter, VC/PE fund approved with $50M seed commitment
items.quote: Total alternatives AUM, which includes AIF commitments, portfolio management services business and advisory mandates sto od at INR148 billion, up from INR60 billion a year ago.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to INR11 billion; operating profit grew 10% YoY with operating margin of 35 bps of AUM; PAT grew 12% YoY to INR8.4 billion
items.quote: Our revenue from operations grew by 14% year-on-year to INR11 billion. Other income at INR2.6 billion. Total cost for the quarter was INR2.7 billion as against INR2.1 billion in Q1 of last year. Operating profit for the quarter grew by 10% year -on-year with an operating margin of 35 basis points of AUM. Profit after tax stood at INR8.4 billion, a growth of 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Equity yields 58 bps (active equity 61 bps), debt 28 bps, liquid 13 bps monthly; TER-to-BER transition and 5 bps exit-load removal effective April 2026
items.quote: our e quity yields, total blended equity yields were 58 basis points. Debt was 28 basis points and liquid was 13 basis points monthly. Our CSR expenditure is actually a function of how our sort of CSR partners require the funding

items.statement: Commission structures optimized to offset TER-to-BER impact; margins maintained at 33-35 bps of AUM corridor
items.quote: Our approach has been to offset this through optimization of commission structures, along with prudent management of both direct and indirect costs. So, what I can say is we have been able to maintain our margins.

items.statement: No explicit capex guidance; investing in people (92 added YoY), digital, AI, marketing, international, PMS, alternatives platforms
items.quote: We won't shy away from investing in the business. And one of the biggest investment that we make is people, right? So , hiring the best possible talent and ensuring that we provide them the best possible environment to make the most of the opportunity, which is in front of us.

items.statement: Employee count up ~92 YoY for new platforms (international, PMS, alternatives, digital, AI, marketing, institutional sales); 37 MF investment professionals, 6 each on PE/VC and private credit, 8 on PMS
items.quote: A good part of that increase is I told you about building some of these new platforms, hired people and like on the international business, on PMS, alternatives, even on our domestic mutual fund side. Of course, on the institutional sales in our digital, AI, marketing, across functions.

items.statement: Industry QAAUM INR83.1 trillion (+15% YoY); equity-oriented AUM INR47 trillion (+16%); SIP contributions INR318 billion in June 2026 (+17% YoY); folios 279M (+15%), unique investors 61.9M (+12%)
items.quote: Quarterly average AUM stood at INR83.1 trillion for qua rter ended June 2026, up 15% Y -o-Y. Equity -oriented AUM crossed INR47 trillion, up 16%. And this 16% growth is during the year when there were bouts of challenges due to external factors and the impact of same on local economy and markets.

items.statement: SIP flows remain structural habit; industry SIP at INR318B in June 2026 (+17% YoY); fintechs registered 8.6M new SIPs in quarter; first-time investors growing but behavior in extended downturn untested
items.quote: If you look at the industry, June '26 number was INR318 billion, INR31,800 crores. If you compare with June '25, this was like INR27,300 crores. So that is a 17% Y -o-Y growth in a year which has been like quite volatile.

items.statement: Debt funds seeing outflows due to rate/currency/crude volatility; liquid funds gaining; industry needs to make debt funds more attractive for retail (retirees, regular income seekers); SEBI lifecycle fund circular provides opportunity
items.quote: On the debt side, the last two consecutive quarters, we have seen significant outflows. And I mentioned earlier, maybe it's the volatility in interest rates, I think what's been happening on the crude oil, geopolitics, currency and all of that.

items.statement: Equity most margin-accretive, then debt, then liquid; alternatives (PMS/AIF) slightly better than MF equity (80-90 bps fees); PMS discretionary in line with equity margins, non-discretionary tight economics
items.quote: So, equity business for us makes maximum money, second comes debt and then comes liquid funds. So that is the way our margins tend to be. So more in equity will actually enhance our overall margin.

items.statement: Launched SIF: H-SIF equity ex top 100 long-short fund approved by Board; building full SIF suite; expanded active, passive, sector/thematic, PMS, AIF (private credit, VC/PE fund of fund)
items.quote: In fact, today, only our Board has approved our first SIF offering, which will be H-SIF equity ex top 100 long -short fund, which will be launched in the near term. I mean this is just the start. Our aim is to build a full suite of SIF products over time.

items.statement: Fintech channel growing rapidly (8.6M SIP registrations in quarter vs ~400K in FY19-20); banks still high flow share but relative share declining; direct plan via fintech, app/portal, RIAs grouped together
items.quote: I was just seeing fintechs have registered 8.6 million SIPs in this quarter. And to put this number in context, if I remember correctly, in FY19, FY20, total number of SIPs they would have registered would be close to 400,000.

items.statement: Folio growth 28% YoY vs industry 15%; 3-year CAGR 37% vs industry 23%; unique investor growth 25% YoY vs industry 12%
items.quote: Last one year, industry folios have grown by 15% and our growth is 28%. Last 3 years, industry has grown by 23% CAGR. Our growth has been 37%.

items.statement: CSR expense timing uneven (partner-driven); Q1 CSR higher than Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY26; no one-off items; IT spend also contributed to opex increase
items.quote: If you see the increase in operating expenses quarter-on-quarter, that's from March quarter to the June quarter, this is largely driven by CSR expenditure. And to explain the year -on-year increase, it's a function of what we spent on CSR as well as certain IT-related spend.

items.statement: No debt discussed; balance sheet surplus ~INR8,000 crores invested cautiously mostly in debt instruments
items.quote: The INR8,000 crores that you are referring to is our treasury surplus, which is in our balance sheet. On that, we are very, very cautious investing that ca pital. And hence, large part of that money is invested in debt.

items.statement: Marquee global investor proposed $50M seed commitment for new VC/PE fund of fund; private credit fund closing this quarter
items.quote: A marquee global investor has proposed to seed this new fund with a commitment of $50 million.

items.statement: Buyback vs dividend decision rests with Board; Chairman addressed at AGM; Board heard investor requests
items.quote: I think this request was made by a few , the Board has heard the request of certain investors at the AGM as well. It's the prerogative of the Board to decide what it does on buyback and dividend.

items.statement: Investor behavior in extended market downturn untested for new SIP cohort; jury still out on sustainability if downturn persists several quarters/years
items.quote: Having said all of this, I think we remain watchful of how investor behavior evolves in a more extended market downturn. I mean, if the downturn persists for several quarters or years, that is one scenario this cohort of investor has not really been through yet. So, jury on that is still out.

items.statement: TER-to-BER transition effective April 2026; 5 bps exit-load TER removed; brokerage limits on cash market rationalized; SEBI lifecycle fund circular creates new opportunities
items.quote: The first was the removal of the 5 basis points of additional TER that AMCs were earlier permitted to charge in lieu of exit load. The second is the shift from TER, which included levies to BER plus statutory levies. And the third element is the rationalization of brokerage limits on the cash market transaction.

items.statement: Gold/silver ETF pricing competitive; industry highly competitive; benchmarking and margin optimization ongoing across products
items.quote: Our industry is highly competitive. I'm sure be it investors or be it distributors, I think they all compare each other. And of course, I mean, a lot of pricing is kept by the regulation. But within that, wherever there is competition in some of the fixed income funds or the ETFs, etceter a, I think we all do the right benchmarking and always try to optimize our margins everywhere.

items.statement: No AUM growth guidance; target operating margin corridor 33-35 bps of AUM; ESOP non-cash cost: FY27 INR79-80 cr, FY28 INR63 cr, FY29 INR41 cr, FY30 INR11 cr
items.quote: We've typically operated in the 33 to 35 basis points range. And that's the objective for us to stay within that corridor. That's the way we look at the business on an overall basis.

items.statement: Opex growth guidance (12-13% ex-ESOP) replaced by margin corridor focus; will not underinvest in growth opportunities
items.quote: We have been running a very, very tight ship and have always been, I think, very prudent when it comes to spending. Having said that, we will not shy away from investing in the future, and I must say this because in a growth business like ours and the opportunities that I outlined before, the real risk is underinvesting and we will not underinvest.

items.statement: Other income largely mark-to-market gains on balance sheet equity/debt investments; closing AUM INR9.32T, active equity AUM INR5.93T, alternatives INR148B, international business building steadily
items.quote: To sum up our closing AUM stood at INR9.32 trillion, actively managed equity-oriented AUM at INR5.93 trillion. We have 28% penetration in the industry in terms of unique investors. Beyond mutual fu nds, our alternatives platform has scaled to INR148 billion, and our international business out of GIFT City continues to build steadily.

items.statement: AUM projection for FY27 is INR4,000-4,200 crores; INR10,000 crores target for FY28-29 remains intact
items.quote: This year, the AUM projections that we had given was around INR4,000 crores to INR4,200 crores, and we will reach those numbers this year. That's the projection, yes.

items.statement: Pretax ROA target for FY27 is around 2.5%
items.quote: So as of now -- so in this year, as I said in the last call also, we have taken a pretax ROA of around 2.5% for this financial year.

items.statement: Retail GNPA expected to stay sub-4% and NNPA sub-2% for FY27
items.quote: We are expecting the GNPA to be sub-4% only throughout the financial year for the retail segment. And there is no change in the ECL policy of the company so as the PCR, so NNPA would be sub-2%.

items.statement: GNPA reduced to 3.94% in Q1 FY27, down 182 bps YoY; retail GNPA at 3.49%
items.quote: Our GNPA level reduced to 3.94%, representing a decline of about 182 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: ARC deal sold INR203 crores of stressed assets at 45.6% average valuation; write-off pool INR83 crores, GNPA pool INR120 crores
items.quote: So third ARC has 2 components wherein write-off pool of the company, which was there, wherein we are -- we have started getting recoveries as we have a specific focus now. So that pool was -- comes to INR83.18 crores. And then there is a normal GNPA pool of the company, which has a DPD of around more than 600 days. So that pool has also been sold to ARC. So in totality, INR203 crores have been sol

items.statement: 14-month MOB GNPA for 2-wheeler improved to 1% from 3-3.5% last year
items.quote: So on 14-month MOB, we are seeing a GNPA of 1 percentage, which used to 3% and 3.5% when we spoke in the last year Q1.

items.statement: Public deposits crossed INR100 crores at ~150 bps lower cost than borrowings
items.quote: we are also aggressively building our liability franchise, which is at almost 150 bps lower than our borrowing cost

items.statement: Retail AUM grew to INR2,851 crores YoY; co-lending book reduced to INR499 crores with zero incremental business; CV/used car grew 40% YoY, construction equipment 75% YoY
items.quote: The retail portfolio of the company, which was a year back close to INR2,300 crores, now we closed at INR2,851 crores. We have seen a significant growth in that retail portfolio. Co-lending portfolio, which was close to INR1,000 crores a year back, now it has been closed at INR499 crores. And safe to say that we are having a zero incremental business from the co-lending.

items.statement: Used car yield 18.6%, CV/CE blended yield 17.5%, 2-wheeler blended yield 22%, used 2-wheeler yield 26%
items.quote: We started used 2-wheeler, which has given a yield of 26%, while my 2-wheeler and the loyalty loan and others, the blended yield for the entire 2-wheeler has come to 22%, while my CV and CE having the blended yield of 17.5% and used car is operating at 18.6%.

items.statement: Target to reduce 2-wheeler share to ~30% of AUM over 3-4 years, grow car/CV/CE/tractors to 70%
items.quote: Over a next 3-, 4-year horizon, the objective is to bring down the 2-wheeler book to around 30% of the overall book and 70% being contributed by car, CV, CE and maybe we will get into tractors.

items.statement: 2-wheeler industry grew 14% YoY in Q1; MCSL disbursements grew 6% with credit acceptance at 35-40% vs industry 75-80%
items.quote: Q1 automobile industry saw good growth. The 2-wheeler industry recorded a 14% year-on-year growth. At Muthoot Capital, we delivered a 6% growth, which may be slightly moderate compared to the industry growth. But all our internal analysis indicates that the gap was not driven by market demand, but primarily due to the fact that our credit acceptance ratios were kept moderate. We were approving abo

items.statement: Plan to scale up disbursements from end of Q2 through Q3 (festival season) using new internal scorecard
items.quote: Now we've seen how the last 1.5 years portfolio has behaved. And now, therefore, we are bringing in a scorecard-based model, which is getting built internally. And we are going to scale up our disbursements from Q2 -- end of Q2 to the rest of the year. And of course, Q3 happens to be the biggest time of the year.

items.statement: Heavy investment in AI-driven technology: AI bots handle 55% of X-bucket collections; AI used in welcome calling, audit, compliance, ticket segregation
items.quote: We have brought in AI in multiple fields now. Our entire X bucket collection is being done by AI bots. So AI bots continue to collect about -- so this month, our resolution on with AI bots on the X bucket was as high as 55% and we'll continue to expand there. Other use cases of AI has been on our welcome calling, our audit and compliance, our automatic ticket segregation of customer complaints.

items.statement: 15-20% of incremental sourcing from group entities (Muthoot FinCorp, Microfin, MHFL, Chits); target 40%; acquisition cost lower than market
items.quote: So 15% to 20% of our incremental sourcing every month comes from group entities today. And the objective is to take it to 40% of the incremental sourcing.

items.statement: Muthoot FinCorp branch activation at 25-30% (contributing 1+ vehicle loan/month); target 50-60% by year-end (~2,000-2,500 branches)
items.quote: Muthoot FinCorp has 4,000-plus branches. We have a branch activation of about 25% to 30% right now, which means about 25% to 30% of Muthoot FinCorp branches contribute to at least 1 vehicle loan per month for capital services. And the objective is to, by the end of the year, take it to 50%, 60%, okay, which means around 2,000, 2,500 branches of Muthoot FinCorp will be doing at least 1 vehicle loan

items.statement: Liquidity maintained at 125-130% of LCR requirement; surplus invested in SLR, PTC, collateral deposits at 6.71% yield
items.quote: The liquidity position of the company remains stable, wherein the company is always having a balances over and above the LCR balance, which is required to be maintained from the RBI. So when RBI is 100%, the company is -- averagely company is having a fund balance of 125% to 130%.

items.statement: Equity raise in discussion with 2-3 investors; data sharing done; meetings expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We are speaking to investors. There are 2, 3 investors who are already sharing, data sharing ha s also been happened with them. So as and when the valuation will click, so wherein we are expecting some meetings to happen in Q2 only

items.statement: Additional INR2.5 crores impairment taken in Q1 for macroeconomic factors; ECL model revision due in 4 weeks; LGD for used car/CV may be revised from 50% to 40-42% but not taken yet
items.quote: Therefore, if you see the Note number 5, which we have placed, we have additionally taken INR2.5 crores on the impairment because we know that in Q2. When the ECL -- so ECL model is something which we are going to revise every year so that we should know that any macroeconomic factor, which as you have asked, is impacting the impairment, how it could be done. So we have done an analysis in the Q1

items.statement: CRISIL rating upgraded to AA- stable; enhances access to diversified capital at competitive pricing
items.quote: First and foremost, we receive d a CRISIL rating upgrade to AA minus stable. We believe that this is a very strong external validation of the transformation that the company has undergone over the past couple of years, and it reflects a sustained improvement in our asset quality, our governance standards, our funding profiles, among many other things

items.statement: Implementing internal risk-based pricing with weekly monitoring; will price higher-risk customers significantly higher to cover credit losses
items.quote: We are planning to rework on our risk-based pricing also where we will be -- you are pricing the higher-risk customers significantly higher so that it covers the possible credit loss that we will incur. So -- and this risk-based pricing will be a very dynamic one, which we will continue to monitor on a weekly basis.

items.statement: Operate in Tier 2/3 markets where competitors price in similar range; no significant NII pressure seen
items.quote: Our markets are largely the Tier 2, Tier 3 players. And we have a very nuanced approach of the competition whom we face. And the competitors that we face in these markets operate broadly in the same interest rate range as we do. So I don't see a significant pressure on the top line in terms of NII, et cetera, as of now.

items.statement: Long-term VAP revenue growth target of 25% and milk procurement growth of 7-8% annually
items.quote: The long-term trajectory, what one should expect is that -- and this is something that we have mentioned in the past as well, is that we are aiming to grow in the mid- to high teens, so 16 to 17 percentage kind of growth is what we are aiming to deliver, which requires milk to grow at about 7% to 8% and value-added products in the range of 25%.

items.statement: Target VAP contribution to reach ~50% of revenue by FY30 from ~39% in FY26
items.quote: So, we would like to end at around 50% by FY30. Now that's a goal that we have.

items.statement: Targeting high single-digit EBITDA margin (7%+) over time, not just 6%
items.quote: Our objective is not a 6% EBITDA. That's not what we are aiming for. We are looking at high single digits EBITDA.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at ~INR250 crore for paneer project, ghee project and procurement investments
items.quote: So, at this point in time, we have two projects that is being constructed, that's being executed. One is a paneer project and another one ghee. We have some other investments into raw milk procurement side, also minor cape x. All of it should add up to about INR250 crores for the

items.statement: New ice cream facility ramped to ~40% utilization in Q1 FY27, manufactures Alpenvie and Get-A-Way
items.quote: Supporting this momentum, our newly commissioned ice cream facility ramped up well during the quarter, reaching approximately 40% capacity utilization.

items.statement: VAP volumes grew 35% YoY in Q1 FY27 driven 80% by distribution expansion and 20% by market share gains
items.quote: Primarily, you can say that 90% or 80% of the growth is primarily due to distribution expansion, new distribution points opened in existing geographies. We have not opened any new geography whatsoever. 20 to 25 percentage of the growth is on account of consumer traction increasing, which is where we have gained market share.

items.statement: Liquid milk volumes stable YoY in Q1 FY27; month-on-month growth seen from March to July
items.quote: On the demand side, milk sales volume remained stable, while average milk sale prices improved 4% year-on-year to INR58.68 per liter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 4.6%; Milk EBITDA 3.03%, VAP EBITDA 8.06%
items.quote: Consolidated revenue increased 18% year-on-year to INR13,381 million, marking another important milestone for stood at INR619 million with an EBITDA margin of 4.6%

items.statement: Gross margin declined ~2.5% YoY due to cow milk price increase, higher SMP consumption/cost, and packing material cost
items.quote: So net , we have ha d about 2.5%. And the other third impact that we have had is packing material . On account of the war, the packing material also had a significant material impact, almost 30 basis points of bottom line impact

items.statement: Weighted average price hike of 5.12% in VAP and 4% in liquid milk in Q1 FY27; further hikes taken in July across markets
items.quote: Price hike, we have had price hike of about 5% in value-added products, weighted average. 5.12% weighted average price increase across value-added products and the balance 35% is all volume driven.

items.statement: Continuing calibrated price increases across markets to pass on raw milk cost inflation
items.quote: Even this week also, we have seen price increases across several of our markets.

items.statement: Milk procurement price rose 7% YoY to INR46.61/liter in Q1 FY27; cow milk up ~INR1, buffalo milk up ~INR4.6 YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, milk procurement prices increased 7% year-on-year to INR46.61 per liter, reflecting continued supply tightness across key milk producing regions.

items.statement: Cattle feed ingredient costs rising month-on-month since Q3 FY26; Q2 FY27 expected to be heavier on costs
items.quote: And they are increasing month-on-month. It started somewhere in quarter 3 of last year, and it's moving until today. Quarter 2 as well looks quite heavy on the cost part.

items.statement: VAP revenue grew 40% YoY to INR5,636M (44% of revenue); broader VAP including ghee/butter grew 39% to INR6,322M (49% of revenue)
items.quote: Consequently, value-added products contributed a record 44% of consolidated revenues compared to 36% in the corresponding quarter last year. Including our consumer pack ghee and butter portfolio, the broader VAP portfolio grew 39% year-on-year to INR6,322 million, contributing a record 49% of consolidated revenues versus 41% a year ago.

items.statement: Curd share of VAP declining (68.9% in Q1 FY27 vs ~75% earlier) as paneer, ice cream, drinkables grow faster
items.quote: Currently, it's at 68.9%. So it's about 69% of our value-added. So it used to be about 75% some time back.

items.statement: Gained market share in organized channel across curd, paneer, buttermilk in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We have gained market share in curd. We have gained market share in paneer. We have gained market share in butter milk. So this is something that we celebrate as well.

items.statement: All branded dairy growth comes from unorganized sector; Heritage gaining share from other organized players in measured channels
items.quote: No, of course, all dairy growth, not just for Heritage, for every single branded company in the country, all growth comes from unorganized sector, right? So that's a given. I was mentioning market share gain in the organized channel. In the organized channel, there is only organized brand. So when we are gaining share, we are gaining share from other branded players.

items.statement: Government may allow duty-free milk powder imports if scarcity worsens; may incentivize exports in glut scenarios
items.quote: Just to give you a history, if you see in the last 15 years, there were years where the scarcity of milk was very high in India. Milk prices went up, then government intervened and allowed duty-free import of milk powder from Australia, New Zealand, Europe and then control the consumer prices.

items.statement: Operating leverage improving: other expenses down to 9.01% of revenue from 9.64%; employee costs down to 6.74% from 7.21% YoY
items.quote: You can see the operating leverage kicking in already. Like if you see the operating cost, which is what is shown as the other expenses in the P&L as a percentage of revenue, Q1 of FY26, which is last year quarter 1, operating cost was 9.64% of revenue. Now it is 9.01% of revenue.

items.statement: Heritage Novandie Foods became wholly owned subsidiary; stake in Peanut Butter and Jelly Ltd increased to 71%
items.quote: Heritage Novandie Foods became a wholly owned subsidiary, reinforcing our presence in the fast-growing high-protein yogurt category through Livo brand. We also increased our shareholding in Peanut butter and Jelly Limited to 71%.

items.statement: Milk procurement volume 18.10 lakh liters/day (+2% YoY); VAP volume growth 35% YoY; ice cream revenue INR550M (+65% YoY)
items.quote: Despite these industry-wide challenges, Heritage increased milk procurement volumes by 2% year-on-year to 18.10 lakh liters per day through its sustained investments in farmer engagement, vet services, cattle nutrition programs and timely payments.

items.statement: Heritage Nutrivet revenue INR728M (+37% YoY) with PBT INR20M despite elevated input costs
items.quote: Heritage Nutrivet reported revenue of INR 728 million, represent a robust growth of 37% year-on-year despite elevated input costs across the animal nutrition industry, while delivering a PBT of INR20 million.

items.statement: Milk procurement outlook uncertain due to weak mini-flush, El Nino risk, regional weather divergence; prices stable but may rise in Q2
items.quote: This time actually, this season generally, we expect a mini flush in April, May, which -- because of this weather condition, climatic conditions that could not happen much. And however, we have procured about 18.1 lakh liters during Q1 and the prices have gone up actually.

items.statement: Buffalo milk volumes declined >20% YoY in Q1 FY27 due to availability constraints
items.quote: But we saw in this quarter a heavy decline in buffalo milk volumes. We actually had over 20 percentage of decline -- degrowth in buffalo milk. It was very difficult to get buffalo milk.

items.statement: Added ~5,000 farmers in Q1 FY27; targeting another 5,000 in Q2 FY27 to secure procurement
items.quote: We've added close to 5,000 farmers in Q1, and our intention is to add another 5,000 farmers in Q2 itself.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 expected around INR 150-160 crore, similar to FY26
items.quote: Yes, it's going to be around the same range also.

items.statement: Capex spent on acquiring property and building own offices to save rental expense, e.g., Bhopal
items.quote: Last year, sir, if you remember, we had taken a call 2 years back that wherever we are paying high rental, better to acquire the property and build it on our own.

items.statement: Print advertising grew ~10% YoY broad-based across sectors except education (flat) and auto (down)
items.quote: Our consolidated advertising revenue continued its strong trajectory, growing by around 10% year-on-year to INR 4,320 million compared with INR 3,933 million in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Radio advertising revenue grew ~12% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We had about this quarter about 8% increase in our revenue across our 37 stations.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps YoY to 26.1% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Consequently, our EBITDA margin expanded by 250 basis points to 26.1% compared to 23.6% in Q1 FY26, demonstrating the strength of our business model.

items.statement: Newsprint prices rose ~13% YoY and ~8% QoQ in Q1 FY27; expected to rise further in Q2 then decline from Q3/Q4
items.quote: Newsprint price, if you see in quarter 1, we have seen around 13% hike. Now quarter 2 also, we believe the price will continue to go up because in quarter 1, we had sudden stock lined up from the earlier quantities. But we clearly see an indication from Q3 and Q4, the prices will start coming down.

items.statement: Digital MAU ~19-20 million in Q1 FY27, flat vs Q4 FY26; digital revenue miniscule and growing but base too small
items.quote: In Q1, the number is around 19 million, 20 million. So the number has been hovering around the same 19 million, 20 million.

items.statement: Advertising growth broad-based: government ~14-15%, real estate ~11-12%, education ~20% (flat due to NEET shift), auto down to single digit
items.quote: Education, as you know, in the quarter 1 is the highest contributing sector, so in the range of around 20%. Government was around 14%, 15%. Real estate was around 11%, 12%. Automobile came down from double digit to a single-digit, jewellery around 5%.

items.statement: DAVP price hike of ~26% kicked in, contributing to double-digit government ad growth
items.quote: It has kicked in. That's the reason the government numbers are also growing in double-digit.

items.statement: Circulation copies ~38 lakh in Q1 FY27 vs 39 lakh in Q4 FY26; market share gained in Rajasthan and MP
items.quote: So the circulation number in Q1 this year is around 38 lakh copies. With all our efforts, I think some of the impact of the summer also is in this, but it would be in the range of 38 lakh, 39 lakh only.

items.statement: Average cover price flat at INR 4.93 in Q1 FY27 vs INR 4.90 in Q1 FY26; minor weekend price tweaks of 2-3 paise overall
items.quote: One second. INR 4.93 is the average cover price.

items.statement: Radio EBITDA grew ~29% YoY to INR 148 million in Q1 FY27; 37 stations operational, 7 more lined up
items.quote: EBITDA grew by around 29% year-on-year to INR 148 million compared with INR 115 million last year.

items.statement: Other operating income increased due to higher job work revenue and wastage revenue
items.quote: This is because of the increase in job work revenue and wastage revenue.

items.statement: Cost savings driven by company-wide effort across all team members, not just HO
items.quote: So rather than only limited people sitting in HO looking at the cost, we have now taken it to all the team members. Everybody is trying to save costs wherever they can.

items.statement: Circulation copies declining structurally (~43-44 lakh two years ago to ~38 lakh now); management expects industry decline of a couple of percent
items.quote: I think it's a mix on the ground because let's get it right, there is some impact of people -- some people, those who are not very serious readers moving on to digital, a little bit of them, a couple of 2%, 3%, 4% like that.

items.statement: Digital team size not disclosed for competitive reasons; 14,000 stories/day generated by combined print+digital reporters, 1,800 videos/day digital-exclusive
items.quote: Sir, for the big reason of the confidentiality to protect the competition to know much more detail, I can't diverge more. You will appreciate that.

items.statement: No revenue guidance given for FY27; management says all teams working hard
items.quote: I can't give any guidance, sir, but everybody is working hard. That much I can assure you.

items.statement: Annual circulation promotion spend ~INR 20-25 crore
items.quote: I think all the expenses of circulation, promotion and all would be in the range of around INR 20 crores, INR 25 crores annually.

items.statement: Micro-drama series using AI launched on Dainik Bhaskar app; content based on news, not fiction; promoted on YouTube
items.quote: So as you rightly noticed that we are doing a couple of micro dramas using the AI on our platform, and we've been getting good response from the readers.

items.statement: English app micro-dramas later; resources focused on Hindi and Gujarati
items.quote: Sir, English app slightly later because all the resources are in Hindi and Gujarati. So to be very honest, English, but later, not now.

items.statement: Print advertising strong vs broadcasters' soft Q1; management attributes to team efforts and advertiser confidence in print
items.quote: On a lighter note, I would say it's going well, so let it be. But on a serious note, good thing is that, that shows that the efforts made by the team and the confidence of the various categories on the print.

items.statement: Print and other EBITDA (print+digital) grew 18% YoY to INR 1,499 million in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Print and other business EBITDA grew by 18% year-on-year to INR 1,499 million as compared to INR 1,270 million in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Circulation revenue stable at INR 1,204 million in Q1 FY27
items.quote: At the same time, our circulation revenue remained stable at INR 1,204 million, reflecting the continued loyalty of our readers and the strength of our market-leading publication despite an evolving media landscape.

items.statement: Radio EBITDA margin improvement driven by revenue growth and cost control
items.quote: We have 7 more stations lined up. We are looking at a good growth this year on the bottom line because we have also put in a lot of cost control checks.

items.statement: Book growth CAGR target of 20%+ over Lakshya 2031 period
items.quote: We had set ourselves a Book growth CAGR of 20%+ over the Lakshya period. As explained above I am pleased to report that we are tracking well in line with this target, achieving a robust 27% growth in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Credit cost target of 2% or less by FY31
items.quote: Second, on the Credit Cost front, we will endeavour to drive Credit Costs down to a level of 2% or less over the Lakshya period.

items.statement: RoA target range of 3.0-3.2% for FY31 with 2.8% threshold in Q4FY27
items.quote: Our Return on Assets (RoA) target remains in the range of 3.0 –3.2% for FY31. Against that, we recorded an RoA of 2.48% in Q1FY27, vs. 2.37% in the corresponding quarter in FY26, up 11 bps YoY. We remain committed to work on achieving the 2.8% RoA threshold in Q4FY27 as communicated earlier.

items.statement: RoE target range of 16-18% by FY31
items.quote: Against a Lakshya 31 RoE target of delivering a Return on Equity (RoE) in the range of 16-18% by FY31, RoE increased to 12.71% in Q1FY27 from 10.86% (RoE after macro prudential provisions) in Q1FY26.

items.statement: WACB expected to rise 4-5 bps in FY27 to 7.35-7.40%
items.quote: But on an aggregate basis, FY27 I think may go up by about 4 to 5 basis points on an overall basis. So yearly WACB may actually go up from 7.35% for FY26 to maybe about anywhere between 7.35% and 7.40% that is what we are currently envisaging.

items.statement: Consolidated book reached ₹1,29,634 Cr, up 27% YoY
items.quote: Our consolidated book crossed another important milestone, reaching ₹1,29,634 Cr, reflecting a healthy YoY growth of 27% with an R oA of 2.48%, reflecting a growth of 11 basis points

items.statement: Retail disbursements of ₹23,852 Cr, up 36% YoY
items.quote: This has been achieved on the back of robust quarterly retail disbursements of ₹23,852 Cr, up 36% YoY, with contributions from all our lines of business, demonstrating the continued strength of our diversified retail franchise.

items.statement: Gold Finance book grew 182% YoY to ₹3,829 Cr with 343 branches
items.quote: The business has grown to a book size of ~₹3,800 Cr, registering a growth of over 180% YoY. On the footprint expansion front, our speed to market remains exceptional. Following the launch of 200 branches in FY26, we are now working on deploying ~500 new branches in FY27, accelerating our velocity to ~1.4 branches addition daily.

items.statement: NIMs+Fees stable at 10.47% despite NIM compression of 24 bps QoQ
items.quote: Consol NIMs + Fees for the quarter stood at 10.47% vs 10.22% for Q1FY26 and 10.47% for Q4FY26

items.statement: NIM fell 24 bps QoQ to 8.54% due to higher debt-equity and surplus liquidity
items.quote: we can see clearly that the NIMs have reduced by 24 basis points from 8.78% in Q4 to 8.54% in Q1FY27. The yields, if you look at, have actually gone up by one basis point, but our debt-equity has been rising, which is leading to interest costs going up by 25 basis points.

items.statement: Credit cost moderated to 2.54%, down 10 bps QoQ
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that consequently credit cost moderated to 2.54%, reflecting another quarter of sequential improvement of 10 basis points, supported by our continued focus on strengthening credit administration, collections excellence and AI-led portfolio management.

items.statement: Personal loans gross non-starters below 3%, net non-starters at lowest in recent quarters
items.quote: In fact, our gross non -starters in Personal loans business is lower than 3% right now. That means for the number of customers whom we lent to, 100 customers, only in the first couple of months only about 3% of customers bounce their first cheques and again net non-starters is much, much lower.

items.statement: Deliberately forgone ₹1,000-1,200 Cr disbursements to protect asset quality
items.quote: We proactively tightened our credit guardrails during the quarter, deliberately letting go of about ₹1,000 Cr to ₹1,200 Cr in potential disbursements, foregoing a few percentage points of additional growth to firmly protect our asset quality.

items.statement: Personal loans disbursements up 126% YoY to ₹4,380 Cr, book up 80% YoY to ₹16,917 Cr
items.quote: In the Personal Loans business, we achieved our highest ever quarterly disbursement of ₹4,380 Cr, translating into a stellar growth of 126% YoY, with the book size at ₹16,917 Cr, an increase of 80% YoY.

items.statement: Two-wheeler disbursements up 41% YoY, prime share at ~90%
items.quote: With 90% of June 2026 Two Wheeler disbursements in the Prime segment, we continue to prioritize high-quality growth and optimized risk-adjusted returns.

items.statement: SME disbursements up 23% YoY to ₹1,567 Cr, cautious on West Asia exposure
items.quote: In the SME business, quarterly disbursements stood at ₹1,567 Cr, up by 23% YoY. The book stood at ₹8,884 Cr , up 28% YoY . The growth in business volumes was aided through an increase in direct sourcing and an existing strong network of distribution channels.

items.statement: Gold loans disbursements impacted in April by new RBI tiered LTV guidelines, recovery in May-June
items.quote: Gold Finance again, you know, April was a month in which the new RBI guardrails came into effect where assessing customer basis a tiered loan demand became mandatory as per RBI guidelines and, you know, it is not only us, but the entire industry also saw an impact of adjustment to these new guidelines.

items.statement: Targeting Project Hercules rollout by Q3FY27 for cross-sell platform
items.quote: We are targeting rollout of this platform by Q3FY27.

items.statement: Private cloud build-out 70% cheaper than hyperscale over 5 years, GPU procurement initiated
items.quote: Crucially, this strategic transition to an open -source private cloud will be 70% cheaper than relying on hyperscale clouds over a 5-year total cost of operation. Concurrently, to support our intensive ML and AI workloads, specifically for running open-source LLM and SLM packages, we have initiated the design and procurement of high-performance GPU server augmentations.

items.statement: Project Cyclops rollout to Rural Business Finance and Mortgage businesses during FY27
items.quote: We intend to take Project Cyclops live in our Rural Business Finance and Mortgage businesses during FY27.

items.statement: Project Nostradamus implementation for RBF, SME and Farm businesses in FY27
items.quote: Project Nostradamus is currently live in Two-Wheeler and Personal loans in a beta-mode and we intend to implement this for our RBF, SME and Farm businesses in FY27.

items.statement: Gold Finance expanding ~500 new branches in FY27 at ~1.4 branches daily
items.quote: Following the launch of 200 branches in FY26, we are now working on deploying ~500 new branches in FY27, accelerating our velocity to ~1.4 branches addition daily.

items.statement: Surplus liquidity of ₹4,200 Cr maintained due to geopolitical situation, deployed earning fee income
items.quote: the other reason is also due to the geopolitical situation being a bit difficult on account of war in Iran , we had maintained slightly higher surplus liquidity of close to ₹4,200 Cr. The overall liquidity was ₹13,000 Cr +. So, the net result has been a reduction in NIM by 24 basis points. However, what is worth noting is that this surplus has been deployed in various instruments on which we have

items.statement: New RBI tiered LTV guidelines for Gold Loans effective April impacted industry origination
items.quote: April was a month in which the new RBI guardrails came into effect where assessing customer basis a tiered loan demand became mandatory as per RBI guidelines and, you know, it is not only us, but the entire industry also saw an impact of adjustment to these new guidelines.

items.statement: RoA at 2.48% up 11 bps YoY, RoE at 12.71% up 185 bps YoY
items.quote: Consol RoA stands at 2.48%, up 11 bps YoY Consol RoE at 12.71%, up by 185 bps YoY

items.statement: Cautious on SME disbursements due to West Asia war fallout on certain sectors
items.quote: SME we have been cautious during this quarter primarily because, you know, we were cautious about the fallout of the, you know, West Asia war on certain business lines as well as certain sectors, so we have been cautious and we sort of on our own cut disbursements in some of the SME sort of cohorts.

items.statement: Monsoon deficit 14% as of July 10, reservoir levels sufficient from prior good monsoons
items.quote: if I look at till 10th of July rainfall is only about 14% sort of deficient . Now the IMD projection is about 10% deficient and if I look at -- what we have done is that we are also very carefully projected the reservoir stocks all across the country and because of two back -to-back good monsoons before this year's monsoon, I think the reservoir levels are at an acceptab

items.statement: Targets 80 bps PBT RoA improvement to reach 3-3.2% Lakshya threshold; 20 bps from ARC drag disappearance over 2-3 years, 30-40 bps from credit cost and credit administration efficiency gains, remainder from business expansion
items.quote: On your question on R oA and R oE trajectory, yes, we need to improve about, you know, 80 basis points, from whatever point we are currently at to get into that Lakshya threshold of 3 % to 3.2%.

items.statement: Guides credit cost to 2-2.2% by Q4 FY27; FY28 modelling can assume same or lower trajectory
items.quote: For modelling exercise, yes, you can plug that in, because that is what we are committed to. If you have said that by Q4 we are between 2% to 2.2%, then obviously in FY28, if we have to maintain our good performance, we have to be in that trajectory or lower.

items.statement: Maintains NIM corridor guidance of 10-10.5% despite cost of funds volatility
items.quote: In terms of NIMs implications, you know, we stick to the corridor of 10% to 10.5%, which we have given.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds to increase 5-7 bps for full year FY27; budgeted range 7.35-7.4%
items.quote: So, the situation being very volatile, that's the reason I've said that it could be in the range of 7.35% or 7.4%.

items.statement: Weighted average yield on Personal Loans ~16%+; DSA channel 12-13%, digital channels ~19%
items.quote: Overall, our weighted average yield in the Personal loans business is about 16% odd, 16% plus is our weighted average yield in the Personal loans business.

items.statement: Cross-sell to existing customers has 1/4 to 1/5 acquisition cost of new customers and lower credit risk
items.quote: the acquisition costs of, you know, customers of selling products or deepening relationships with existing customers is probably one-fourth or one-fifth of acquiring a new customer.

items.statement: Gold loans, Micro-LAP, and Personal Loans are high-yield thrust areas; Microfinance share may decline in percentage terms but absolute growth continues
items.quote: the Gold loan book is going to be one of the thrust area, Micro-LAP will be another area, Personal loans will be a third area. And if you look at all these three are reasonably high yielding products

items.statement: Spent ~Rs 38 Cr on Cyclops, ~Rs 33 Cr on Nostradamus; total capitalized AI projects ~Rs 102 Cr with additional CWIP
items.quote: Overall, we have spent roughly about ₹38 Cr to build Cyclops and overall we have spent roughly about ₹33 Cr for Nostradamus and ₹37 Cr for Cyclops

items.statement: Building private cloud to reduce AI compute costs; will run tier-2 and tier-3 applications initially
items.quote: we are starting to move towards building o ur own private cloud. However, can we run tier - one applications on private cloud? Probably the answer is no. But can we run our tier-three and tier-two applications on our private cloud? Probably the answer is yes

items.statement: Cyclops implemented in Two Wheeler (18 months) and Tractor (18 months); Microfinance and Mortgage implementation this year; Nostradamus expanding beyond Personal Loans and Two Wheeler
items.quote: for Microfinance as well as Mortgage, Cyclops will be implemented this year and Nostradamus will be implemented for other lines of business apart from Personal loans and Two Wheeler

items.statement: Microfinance industry deleveraged from Rs 4.4L Cr to Rs 3.3L Cr; customers with >3 loans <5%; expects 18-24 month Goldilocks period post asset quality cycle
items.quote: The Microfinance industry has deleveraged from a peak book size of ₹4,40,000 Cr to about ₹3,30,000 Cr right now. So, the industry has deleveraged ₹1,10,000 Cr

items.statement: Wholesale book Rs 2,000 Cr all standard except Supertech (61% PCR); GS3 increase due to settlement transition, will reverse next quarter; ARC SR pool PCR improved from 58% to 68%
items.quote: The PCR on the SRs, the security receipts, when we started off on this resolution process was 58% and that has now actually gone and increased to 68%.

items.statement: Two Wheeler bot-driven self-cure rate improved from 10% to 40%; ShigraM legal co-pilot reduced title search from 4-8 hours to 30-60 minutes
items.quote: in the Two Wheeler business the self -cure rate has gone up from 10% to 40

items.statement: El Nino monsoon 14% deficient to July 10 vs IMD 10% projection; reservoir levels acceptable except South India; expects normal year for rural and tractor portfolios
items.quote: if I look at till 10th of July rainfall is only about 14% sort of deficient . Now the IMD projection is about 10% deficient

items.statement: Insurance commission regulatory changes industry-wide; building payments business as fee revenue diversification over 2-2.5 years
items.quote: it is not only for us, it is for the industry. And I do believe that the insurance industry along with the regulator and as along with the, you know, end consumers of the insuran ce products, which is the BFSI industry, will come to some acceptable solutions

items.statement: Taking CGFMU coverage on ~35-40% of current year Microfinance disbursements for new geographies and new-to-credit customers; CGTMSE on risky SME cohorts
items.quote: in this year itself, we will cover about 35% to 40% of the total disbursement that we make in the current year for Micro Finance.

items.statement: LCR declined 18 percentage points QoQ; management committee meets weekly to adjust liquidity proactively
items.quote: when I look at the LCR numbers between the two quarters, that shows a decline already of 18 percentage points.

items.statement: FCNR(B) scheme could benefit AAA NBFCs like L&T Finance if large funds mobilized
items.quote: Reserve Bank of India has come up with the FCNR (B) scheme. And if we are able to mobilize huge amount of funds through that mode, ultimately it will be 'AAA' NBFCs like us who will finally benefit

items.statement: Expects headcount normalization over FY29-FY30 from AI agentic frameworks; urban businesses to see efficiencies, rural high-touch remains
items.quote: as we move into, you know, FY29 and FY30, the impact of all these sorts of implementations will be visible in our head count attrition as well.

items.statement: Rural group loan villages activated monthly; 220,000 total villages, number reflects new activations plus reactivations of inactive villages
items.quote: we have 2,20,000 villages into which we go and distribute our microfinance products, right. Now some of those villages become inactive in a quarter, so the objective is to go and activate it once again.

items.statement: Payments business build-out: eliminate opex drag first, then agentic commerce model targeting prepaid fee revenue pools; calibrated 3-4 year build during Lakshya 31
items.quote: Our model is to independently go, first and foremost serve our own customers. And because we do not have a payments stack at this current point in time, there's a opex drag that we have been trying to facilitate payments for our customers.

items.statement: Confirmed sequential revenue and margin growth in coming quarters; 13-15% CAGR over next 5 years with EBIT margins of 16-17%
items.quote: Finally, looking ahead, we remain committed to our aspiration of delivering 13 -15% CAGR over the next 5 years while maintaining EBIT margins of 16-17%

items.statement: Expect mid-16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27
items.quote: With that, we remain on track towards our aspiration of achieving a mid -16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Expect effective tax rate to remain in 26.2% to 26.7% range
items.quote: We expect ETR to remain in the range of 26.2% to 26.7%.

items.statement: Expect combined DSO to remain in 80-85 days range going forward
items.quote: Going forward, we expect combined DSO to remain in the range of 80 to 85 days.

items.statement: Expect free cash flow to net income in 90-95% range for the year
items.quote: you try to keep it between 90% to 95%, that is for certain that we can deliver for the year

items.statement: Mobility segment showed 2.3% sequential growth, broad-based across Aerospace & Rail and Trucks & Off-Highway
items.quote: Mobility delivered 2.3% sequential growth. This was broad -based, led by Aerospace & Rail and Trucks and Off-Highway

items.statement: Sustainability segment grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY driven by strong execution of recently won programs
items.quote: Sustainability remains a strong growth driver, delivering 11.3% YoY and 4.3% sequential growth, driven by strong execution of recently won programs

items.statement: Tech segment operated in measured demand environment; expect headwinds to ease over next few quarters and return to growth from Q2
items.quote: The segment operated in a measured demand environment during the quarter. We expect these headwinds to ease over the next few quarters and a significant deal in Telecom to close in early Q2

items.statement: Confirmed double-digit growth for Sustainability for FY27
items.quote: I'm confirming double -digit growth for Sustainability for FY 27, right?
