items.quote: Broking continues to be a powerful gateway product with nearly 60% of our mutual fund clients engaging with us first through our broking services, while a meaningful proportion of mutual fund first customers subsequently participated in broking activities.

items.statement: Operate with security-by-design approach; ISO-certified systems, compliance with SEBI CSCRF framework, alignment with digital privacy standards
items.quote: We continue to operate with a security by design approach supported by ISO-certified systems, compliance and SEBI's CSCRF framework and alignment with evolving digital privacy standards.

items.statement: No liquidity issues from RBI circular; funding position normalizing; client funding risk limited due to exchange margins and strong risk management
items.quote: No. I mean, we are not seeing any kind of a liquidity issue as far as the funding position is concerned. So I mean, I think this is something which is transient and over a period of time will even out.

items.statement: Client funding book risk very limited due to exchange-prescribed margins and strong risk management framework; no issues during past market declines
items.quote: on the MTF, on the client funding book, th ere is actually very, very limited risk to us because we have exchange prescribed margins an d sometimes, we go over and above that as well. So we stay quite

items.statement: Employee cost flat YoY at ~₹11 billion; headcount stable despite increments; focus on efficient growth
items.quote: if you recall in the conversation that we were having in April, I had mentioned that we would be more or less flat as far as our employee cost is concerned vis-a-vis the last financial year.

items.statement: Credit disbursement moderated QoQ due to lender risk/pricing calibration and tech partner friction; long-term thesis unchanged, 130% YoY growth
items.quote: lenders keep calibrating their risk and their pricing on our base over time. So, quarter-over-quarter, some of these do impact our disbursals.

items.statement: Wealth management focused on ARR-led AUM growth; unit economics improving; 3-4 year breakeven visibility on track
items.quote: We've always maintained that we have a plan that we are working with, which gives us about 3 to 4 years in terms of having a more potential breakeven visibility. And at this point in time, all parameters are pointing towards that region.

items.statement: AMC business 15 months old, passive-only initially; product suite now complete; expanding beyond passive; greater strategy visibility in 3-4 quarters
items.quote: AMC all along has been a passive-only approach for us at the start. Passive businesses take a long time to mature. We started this about 15 months ago, not too long ago.

items.statement: AI embedded across user onboarding, face match, signature validation, grievance automation, content generation, software development, analytics, portfolio intelligence
items.quote: Beyond user-facing experiences, AI is embedded across user onboarding for face match, real-time signature validation, grievance and ticket automation, content generation, software development, analytics and portfolio intelligence.

items.statement: Active AP count is approximately 10,000 as of June 2026.
items.quote: Count of AP was the question, I guess. So it should be around 9,800 at this point, active APs.

items.statement: AP channel to expand into multiproduct distribution including mutual funds, loans, and insurance.
items.quote: So yes, that is a natural progression, which is making our APs more salient with regards to their capabilities and their ability to offer multiproducts.

items.statement: No plans to originate small DSAs for loan distribution via AP channel.
items.quote: No, not at this point.

items.statement: Wealth and AMC businesses together burned 400 basis points of operating margin this quarter.
items.quote: Overall, as far as the operating margin decrement is concerned, it's about 4% for both the AMC and the wealth businesses put together from the overall.

items.statement: Full-year burn for Wealth and AMC expected at 3-3.5% of operating margin.
items.quote: But overall, I think we will be in the range of about 3%, 3.5% as at the financial year.

items.statement: Wealth and AMC businesses target incremental breakeven in 3-4 years.
items.quote: As of today, as I said, in the past also we mentioned that from the beginning, we are contemplating in about 3 to 4 years this business should incrementally breakeven.

items.statement: Employee productivity expected to increase over next 2-3 years; no specific headcount guidance given.
items.quote: And overall, I don't want to give a guidance on employee count, but you will see employee productivity increase for sure as we have all this -- access to all of these things.

items.statement: Wealth AUM split: UHNI (₹50Cr+) dominant; ₹1-50Cr segment at ~₹3,400-3,500 Cr AUM.
items.quote: Now as far as the second business is concerned, where currently we are at close to about ₹ 3,400 crores, ₹ 3,500 crores of AUM.

items.statement: UHNI client acquisition driven by high-quality RMs bringing their own clients and strong referral flywheel.
items.quote: The UHNI business usually works with high-quality RMs bringing in their customers, and usually the reference flywheel in a UHNI business is extremely strong.

items.statement: Wealth product strategy includes exclusive, contextual products like international experiences, private/unlisted assets, with suitability guardrails.
items.quote: We look at products as exclusive, contextual to market, strong guardrails of having gone through suitability and product approval, committee approvals.

items.statement: Client acquisition moderation reflects softer industry trends (CDSL data); spend adjusted based on client LTV and segment quality.
items.quote: If you see what is sort of the CDSL number for client acquisition, that itself actually has been softer last few months.

items.statement: Cash realization increased due to November pricing change, higher ticket size mix (>₹20k), and new value-added assisted plan uptake.
items.quote: If you look at it over a period of time, there was -- in November, we had made a small pricing change. That definitely has an impact.

items.statement: No further cash realization increase baked in; mix-driven and can change quarter-to-quarter.
items.quote: Look, it's very hard to predict, especially on the mix side. So I wouldn't bake in any further increase from here.

items.statement: Loan Against Securities (LAS) in pilot (COG mode); full launch expected in 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: We are in COG mode right now. As and when we get more experience from the customers, we'll open up the entire base, and in next two or three quarters, you should see that business becoming big.

items.statement: Personal loan distribution active with 7 lenders (banks, large NBFCs, fintechs); non-scaling partners offloaded.
items.quote: On the PL side, we work with 7 lenders right now, and over time, some of the lenders come in and they scale with us and some of the lenders who don't scale with us, we sort of offload them.

items.statement: US equities offering upgrade planned; GIFT City license obtained; pricing not finalized.
items.quote: We got a GIFT City license also on that front, as you would have seen. We can't talk about any pricing at this time because we haven't launched the product.

items.statement: US equity investment limits governed by RBI LRS limit of $250,000 per year per customer.
items.quote: So it's really $250,000 is what the LRS limit is. But depending on like what you're doing, there are different limits may apply.

items.statement: Restricted basket (RSM) is internal risk policy beyond SEBI rules; CEO reviewing specific customer complaint.
items.quote: In terms of the risk, as you know, we have our own risk management on top of what SEBI would prescribe because brokers have their own requirement to do things.

items.statement: Mutual fund SIP momentum strong; AI-driven query resolution and UX/UI improvements rolling out to boost engagement.
items.quote: We are actually seeing momentum in mutual fund. It's an important business to create wealth for our investors. And so one of the metrics that we look internally at is just how many active SIPs and what is our share of that.

items.statement: No plans for stock advisory; Ionic wealth platform offers full solution set.
items.quote: Look, not at this time. We do -- of course, we have RAs and we provide calls, as you know, those are different. But no plans on the stock advisory front.

items.statement: Lending business at very small base; small fraction of customers have taken loans; long-term responsible growth focus.
items.quote: We are actually at a -- where we want to go compared to that, we are at a very small base. So you will see it rise from there. Also, a very small number of our customers have ever taken loans from us.

items.statement: IPL spend classified as long-term branding cost, not client acquisition cost; acquisition cost creeps up during IPL but normalizes after.
items.quote: Look, the IPL costs are really not a acquisition cost. It's a branding cost, very, very long-term cost. So that has to be kept very much out of it.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%
items.quote: We see, yes, so 25%, 30% growth is what we forecasted, and that's what we stick to. So yes, in pure mathematics terms, we are saying that, yes, we should maintain this run rate.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20-22%
items.quote: As I always say, so unfortunately, we have lost 1 quarter with a little lesser margin, but I would still stick to 20%, 22% margins in guidance.

items.statement: Electrolyte Salts FY27 revenue guidance INR40-60 crores
items.quote: It will not be up to -- so between INR40 crores to INR60 crores revenue is what we still hold the guidance.

items.statement: Board approved INR200 crore greenfield facility, groundbreaking 20 July 2026
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that our Board of Directors has today approved the establishment of a new greenfield manufacturing facility involving an investment of approximately INR200 crores. We have scheduled the groundbreaking ceremony for this on 20th July 2026.

items.statement: New greenfield facility targeting operations within 18-21 months
items.quote: Theoretically, we want to finish it. So theoretically, we say we want this site to be in place within -- into operations within 21 months. Internally, we are pushing to get it through within 18 months, if possible.

items.statement: Current capacity supports up to INR800-850 crore revenue, Dahej site saturated
items.quote: We are doing some debottlenecking stuff. We have one small block where we can do maybe 4, 5, 6 reactors or stuff like that, but not something which can really address the growth or the coming of demand. So, in reality, anything beyond this INR800 crores, INR850 crores will look -- we should have a place already, infrastructure in place to cater to this growth.

items.statement: SDA demand strengthening with Euro 7 implementation, global demand growing
items.quote: The implementation of Euro 7 standards has now begun translating into revenue and there is a very visible customer demand, validating the opportunity that we have been anticipating. We are witnessing encouraging momentum across our customer base and the overall business environment for this segment is very robust.

items.statement: Semiconductor chemical first commercial batch qualified by customer
items.quote: I'm extremely proud to share that our first batch produced on commercial plant scale was delivered to the customer during this quarter, and this batch has been successfully qualified by the customer.

items.statement: 5 semiconductor products in pipeline, 1 plant-scale qualified, 1 pilot-scale under evaluation, 3 in development
items.quote: Currently, we have 5 products on pipeline. So, one of this is now produced from the plant scale. We have another one produced from pilot scale, which is currently under evaluation from the customer side. We have 2 other products, 3 other products which are in the development phase. So totally, we are working on 5 different products in this space.

items.statement: Price pass-through started in last 40-50 days after raw material cost increases
items.quote: Now we are pushing for price increase. So now we are translating that we are -- so since last, I would say, since last 40, 50 days now that price pass-on has started, customers have started accepting the higher price because they know there is no other way to go.

items.statement: Electrolyte Salts production delayed by raw material shortage due to Middle East crisis, now streamlining
items.quote: Severe short supply of certain key raw materials due to Middle East crisis led to significant production delays, impacting the revenue recognition for the quarter and the situation is now gradually getting streamlined in terms of its availability.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% CAGR over next 3-4 years
items.quote: So over the next 3 to 4 years, if you let us pick because Jolva was getting commercialized. So let us say about coming 4 years from today, we should envisage at least 20% to 25% compounded growth year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Targeting post-tax ROIC of 20-22%
items.quote: But when we talk of ROIC, we look at about 20%, 22% should be a decent achievement, and that is what we are focusing to in that direction.

items.statement: New facility expected to generate INR300 crore revenue at peak with 1.2-1.5x asset turnover
items.quote: And as far as the revenue is concerned, we would be looking at somewhere around 1.2x to 1.5x asset turnover ratio, which means we would end up having around INR300 crores of revenue at peak utilization.

items.statement: 2 products currently on continuous flow chemistry, 7-8 more expected in near future
items.quote: Now majority of the development what we are doing. So it may not be in all stages of a product. But what I see is, let us say, about 7 or 8 products in near future getting into commercial phase or piloting phase. All of these products either have electrochemistry or continuous flow chemistry.

items.statement: No execution risks seen for FY27 guidance, all customer demand visible
items.quote: None of them. We don't foresee any obstacles to this year's guidance because all the demand from the customers and the segments are quite visible. And I don't think there should be any obstacle in achieving this target.

items.statement: Chinese subsidy removal may benefit Tatva Chintan but too early to predict
items.quote: Most of the subsidies in terms of specialty chemicals or agro intermediates or pharma intermediates is expected to go away. So that would, of course, push -- that would be in terms of Tatva Chintan per se within the chemical space. Companies like Tatva Chintan should see some benefit deriving out of this change. But it is too early to predict and you never know what China is going to do.

items.statement: Flame retardant products not commercializing soon due to unfavorable polymer industry economics
items.quote: No, it still continues to remain in such situation. Basically, it is directly connected to the polymer industry, and still the situation there is not much reversal in the situation. We are not getting into commercialization of those products in very near future for sure.

items.statement: Semiconductor customer is an MNC supplier, not direct fab manufacturer
items.quote: Someone else. So, semiconductor companies will never directly buy such thing. There are always MNC companies who would end up supplying this to the semiconductor or the fab manufacturers.

items.statement: Hybrid vehicle battery customer commercialization starting Oct-Nov 2026, full scale-up late 2027
items.quote: Hybrid vehicle batteries customer is into the process of commercialization. So it's now just beginning to get into commercialization phase. So this should happen from October or November of this year, calendar year '26, whereas the major part of the demand is coming from a couple of customers using these electrolytes into stationary energy storage systems.

items.statement: 8-9 mature pipeline products expected to commercialize before 2028 (excluding semiconductor)
items.quote: In mature pipeline, we have about 9 different products now. The semiconductor products I'm not including because these are long term. So, it's not going to happen before 2028. So, what will commercialize before 2028, we are looking into 8 or 9 different products which are now mature.

items.statement: Euro 7 implementation expanding geographical market access for SDA
items.quote: With Euro 6, we had certain geographical limitations in terms of sales, which goes away with Euro 7. So that will be an added benefit for us in terms of growing our market share.

items.statement: Company celebrating 30th anniversary, entering fourth decade with renewed confidence
items.quote: This year marks 30 years of Tatva Chintan, and this milestone belongs to every stakeholder who has been a part of our journey. As we enter our fourth decade, we do so with renewed confidence, stronger capabilities and an unwavering commitment to creating value through innovation, specialized chemistry and responsible growth.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth guidance of 25-30% for FY27 if gold prices remain flat
items.quote: if there is no price drop, and if the price remains flat also over the year, that means, let's say, let's look at March to next March, the price would have remained flat, even then we would have given a gold AUM growth of about 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Entity-level AUM growth guidance of 20-22% for FY27
items.quote: And at an entity level, we are expecting to grow about 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Mortgage AUM growth guidance of 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: And the mortgage AUM will grow between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at sub-1% for FY27
items.quote: At the start of the year itself, we said the credit cost guidance will be sub-1%.

items.statement: ROA expansion guidance of 20-30 bps over FY26 average ROA of 2.4%
items.quote: I had guided that we will expand the ROA by about 20 to 30 bps over the average ROA, that we had given last year. Last year, FY '26, we had given an average ROA of about 2.4%.

items.statement: Branch expansion guidance of 200 branches for FY27 maintained
items.quote: This year, we plan to add 200 branches. Our guidance remains, we have not changed our guidance.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 77% YoY to ₹11,191 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Gold Loan AUM increased to ₹11,191 Cr, up nearly 77% year-on-year.

items.statement: Mortgage AUM grew 15% YoY to ₹9,777 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Mortgage AUM also remained on a healthy trajectory and closed at ₹9,777 Cr, growing approximately 15% year-on-year.

items.statement: Total AUM crossed ₹21,000 Cr milestone at ₹21,136 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Consequently, total AUM crossed the ₹21,000 Cr milestone during the quarter coming in at ₹21,136 Cr

items.statement: Gold loan disbursements rose 15% YoY to ₹6,087 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Gold Loan business continued to lead this growth, with disbursements rising 15% YoY to ₹6,087 Cr

items.statement: Mortgage disbursements increased 4% YoY to ₹673 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Mortgage business continued to demonstrate steady growth, with disbursements increasing 4% YoY to ₹673 Cr

items.statement: Core NII grew 12.3% QoQ and 40.6% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Core Net Interest income grew 12.3% sequentially QOQ and 40.6% YOY.

items.statement: Yields (ex-DA) grew 10 bps QoQ to 15.7% on average loan book
items.quote: Yields (exc. DA) grew QOQ sequentially by 10 bps to 15.7% on Avg loan book

items.statement: Weighted average cost of borrowing reduced 3 bps QoQ despite incremental borrowing costs rising 20-30 bps
items.quote: we were able to bring in our Weighted average COB marginally lower QOQ by 3 bps.

items.statement: PPOP grew 50% YoY to ₹187.5 Cr in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Pre-provisioning Operating Profit at Rs 187.5 Cr growing 15.2% sequentially and 50% YOY.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 1.6% from 1.9% in Q4 FY26, net NPA below 1% at 1.0%
items.quote: On asset quality, our GNPAs reduced 30 bps to 1.6% in Q1 (from 1.9% in Q4 ) and net NPA also reduced 30 bps falling marginally below 1.0% for the first time.

items.statement: Stage 2 assets increased to 2.7% from 2.2% due to regulatory transition to periodic interest servicing
items.quote: Our increase in Stage II from 2.2 % to 2.7% is entirely due to this re-adjustment.

items.statement: Credit costs contained at 0.8% in Q1 FY27, up 6 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our Credit costs are marginally up 6 bps Q0Q due to the combined effect of the above, however we have been able to contain it at the 0.8% levels.

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio increased to 38.36% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our provision coverage increased to 38.36 % in Q1.

items.statement: RBI revised LTV framework effective April 1 requiring onboarding LTVs on bullet loans to be calculated on total amount due at maturity
items.quote: Effective April 1, the RBI revised the LTV framework, requiring onboarding LTVs on bullet loans to be ca lculated on the total amount due at maturity — that is, principal and interest together — rather than on principal alone

items.statement: Company adopted periodic interest-due structure and operates at LTVs below regulatory limits
items.quote: In response, and to support our customers while maintaining prudent risk standards, we have adopted a periodic interest-due structure, and we continue to operate at LTVs below the regulatory limits.

items.statement: Gold tonnage grew 1% QoQ in Q1 FY27 despite regulatory changes and gold price decline
items.quote: We have also been able to marginally grow gold tonnage by 1% sequentially QOQ in Q1.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 8.1% QoQ in Q1 FY27 despite 15% gold price decline and regulatory changes
items.quote: In spite of these two head-winds of adverse price movement and regulatory changes, we delivered a 8.1 % QOQ sequential growth in Gold loan AUM.

items.statement: Leverage increased from 4.6 to 4.89 due to co-lending transition issues moving CLM business to own balance sheet
items.quote: Due to transition-related issues with the new regulatory guidelines across our co-lending partners, a large part of what would otherwise have been CLM business was booked in our own balance sheet in Q1 resulting in leverage going up from 4.6 to 4.89.

items.statement: Expect co-lending business to normalize and de-leverage in next few quarters
items.quote: We hope that most of these issues will get streamlined over the next few months and our co-lending business will normalise, helping us de-leverage in the next few quarters

items.statement: George Oommen joined as Business Head – Gold Loans with 30+ years experience
items.quote: Mr. George Oommen has joined us as Business Head – Gold Loans, bringing over 30 years of experience across retail banking.

items.statement: Shardul Kadam moved to Chief Transformation Officer role
items.quote: Mr. Shardul Kadam has steered our Small Ticket LAP business through a challenging period and played a pivotal role in stabilizing it. He will move into a new role of Chief Transformation Officer.

items.statement: Jagadeesh Rao assumed additional responsibility as CBO – Small Ticket LAP and Home Loans
items.quote: Mr. Jagadeesh Rao, who serves as Chief Business Officer – Gold Loans and Chief Marketing Officer, will assume the additional responsibility of CBO – Small Ticket LAP and Home Loans.

items.statement: Gold loan LTV on AUM at 67.9%, up from 61% due to gold price decline
items.quote: The increase in gold loan LTVs by 7% - is attributable primarily to the decline in gold prices. Our on-boarding LTVs remain at levels similar to last quarter.

items.statement: Opex to average total assets improved 70 bps QoQ to 4.8% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: For Q1 – we came in with an Opex to Avg. total assets of 4.8% (an improvement of 70 bps) sequentially QoQ.

items.statement: Cost-to-income improved over 400 bps QoQ to 52.8% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our Cost-to-income also showed an improvement of over 400 bps sequentially Q0Q – coming in at 52.8% (from the annualised number of 57.2% in FY26).

items.statement: CRAR at 20.71% in Q1 FY27 vs 22.4% in Q4 FY26 due to CLM book moving on balance sheet
items.quote: Our CRAR came in at 20.71 % (compared to 22.4% in q4). Some part of this reduction was attributable to the shrinkage in the CLM book – which came on balance sheet.

items.statement: Reported overdue levels expected to remain elevated near-term due to customer behavior transition to new interest servicing structure
items.quote: As customer repayment behaviour is unlikely to change immediately, reported overdue levels are expected to remain elevated in the near term. We view it as customer behaviour in transition rather than an asset quality concern.

items.statement: No stress seen in mortgage portfolio from macroeconomic conditions as of Q1 FY27
items.quote: Mohit, right now we are not seeing anything. Maybe it will come in Q2 or Q3, maybe after the monsoon plays out. But as of now, we are not seeing anything and we have not declared any stress on, because of the macroeconomic environment.

items.statement: Expect strong double-digit organic revenue growth for FY27 with services as primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI-led efficiency and disciplined cost management
items.quote: Based on our current visibility, we continue to expect strong double -digit organic revenue growth for FY27 with services as the primary growth engine and margin expansion supported by scale, utilization, delivery productivity, AI -led efficiency and discipl ined cost management.

items.statement: Customers prioritizing programs that accelerate product launches, improve efficiency, reduce cost, strengthen software capability and support transition to intelligent, connected software-defined products
items.quote: Customers are prioritizing programs that accelerate product launches, improve efficiency, reduce cost, strengthen software capability and support the transition to intelligent, connected software-defined products.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 10 bps sequentially to 16.1% in Q1 FY27; services gross margin improved 120 bps partly offset by 250 bps decline in Technology Solutions margins and upfront investments in large deal mobilization
items.quote: We maintained strong operating discipline during the quarter with operating expenses increasing 5.8%, slightly below revenue growth of 5.9%. Resultantly, EBITDA grew 6.1% sequentially to INR267 crores, while EBITDA margin improved 10 basis points Q-o-Q to 16.1%.

items.statement: Won $100 million strategic engagement with Tenneco spanning engineering, digital technologies, AI-enabled processes and operational modernization; secured strategic engagement with North American industrial equipment manufacturer; deepened
items.quote: The most significant win was our $100 million strategic engagement with Tenneco , which expands our relationship beyond traditional engineering services into a multiyear transformation program spanning engineering, digital technologies, AI -enabled processes and operational modernization.

items.statement: Services revenue 78% of total; automotive non-anchor revenue $43.9M (6.7% QoQ, 56.3% YoY); Aerospace revenue ~$10.2M (6.4% QoQ, 38.1% YoY); IHM revenue ~$15M; embedded and software business grew 8.5% QoQ in dollar terms
items.quote: Automotive non -anchor revenue reached $43.9 million, growing 6.7% quarter-on-quarter and 56.3% year -on-year, reflecting continued progress in reducing customer concentration and expanding our presence across global OEM.

items.statement: Anchor account contribution to services revenue reduced to 48.9% in Q1, improvement of 150 bps sequentially; growth broad-based across anchor and non-anchor and geographies; Tenneco deal is US deal; uptick in Germany despite headwinds; mome
items.quote: Resultantly, the contribution from anchor accounts to our services revenue reduced to 48.9% in Q1, an improvement of 150 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Upfront investments in talent, ramp-up, capability development, transition activities and delivery readiness for large strategic engagements and full vehicle programs in mobilization phase
items.quote: In addition, several large strategic engagements and full vehicle programs entered the mobilization phase during Q1, requiring upfront investments in talent, ramp -up, capability development, transition activities and delivery readiness ahead of revenues re aching steady state levels.

items.statement: Total headcount 12,579 associates at end of Q1, net reduction of 67 employees (0.5%) sequentially; optimizing delivery capacity with balanced approach between full-time employees and outsourced resources; disciplined and selective hiring fo
items.quote: Our total headcount stood at 12,579 associates at the end of Q1, representing a net reduction of 67 employees or 0.5% sequentially. This primarily reflects a continued optimization of our delivery capacity with a balanced approach towards managing the mix between full -time employees and outsourced resources.

items.statement: Trailing 12 months voluntary attrition declined to 16%, improvement of 20 bps YoY; delivered over 9,000 learning hours across GenAI, software-defined vehicles and cybersecurity to over 2,000 employees; over 20,000 training hours delivered t
items.quote: Our talent metrics continue to remain healthy with trailing 12 months voluntary attrition declining to 16%, an improvement of 20 basis points year-over-year.

items.statement: Net cash position INR 880 crores at end of Q1; DSO stable at 97 days; billed DSO 65 days vs 59 days in Q4; unbilled DSO 32 days vs 36 days in Q4
items.quote: At the end of Q1, the net cash position stood at INR 880 crores, while the DSO remained stable at 97 days, reflecting healthy collection efficiency. Our billed DSO came in at 65 days compared with 59 days in Q4, while the unbilled DSO were at 32 days compared with 36 days in Q4.

items.statement: Europe revenue ~$67.9M (10.1% QoQ); Germany strengthening as key growth market; BMW TechWorks crossed 2,000 engineers milestone; JV share of profit increased 43.5% QoQ to INR 9.5 crores, total contribution INR 17.8 crores including deferred
items.quote: Q1 revenue from Europe reached approximately $67.9 million , representing growth of 10.1% quarter-on-quarter and reinforcing our belief that the region will remain a significant contributor to future expansion.

items.statement: AI acting as force multiplier for productivity and ability to deliver China speed and China cost at global quality standards; developing full vehicles in 18-24 months vs 36-48 months for Western OEMs; AI not deflationary but enables acceler
items.quote: We are routinely and have demonstrated this consistently able to develop full vehicles and top hats anywhere between 18 months and 24 months. And again, we've demonstrated that, and we've got vehicles on the road today that are, again, proof points against those claims.

items.statement: Temporary headwinds in parts of Germany business as certain customers work through restructuring and cost optimization; annual wage increase in Q2 to be absorbed while still delivering sequential margin improvement
items.quote: We are also navigating some temporary headwinds within parts of our Germany business as certain customers work through restructuring and cost optimization initiatives. As we implement annual wage increase in Q2, we expect to absorb the associated cost impa ct, while still delivering sequential margin improvement through operational discipline and execution.

items.statement: Growth expected to accelerate in second half of FY27 vs first half; quarter-over-quarter margin expansion to continue despite Q2 salary increases; not focusing on specific margin milestone but balancing growth acceleration with margin ambit
items.quote: I expect growth to be much greater in the second half of the year than in the first half of the year. Bu t how that spreads across the quarters will be predicated upon the factors that I just referred.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue grew to ~$10.2M (6.4% QoQ, 38.1% YoY); targeting $100M Aerospace revenue in next couple of 3 years with ~40% CAGR; growth broad-based beyond Airbus to propulsion players in North America
items.quote: I think that we've cemented not only the relationship with Airbus, but with key components of Airbus's supply chain. And we've also been able to build very strong relationship with some of the propulsion players in North America. So, the growth now is not just predicated upon a single customer. It's much more broad -based and by association, it's much healthier.

items.statement: Es-Tec acquisition completed November last year; cross-selling at BMW and VW progressing; BMW TechWorks JV providing access and influence; Es-Tec platform supporting VW strategy to balance R&D concentration across geographies

items.statement: Q1 FY27 total deal wins $1.078B, up 33.3% YoY; broad-based across verticals with largest from manufacturing and HLS

items.statement: Clients >$50M revenue increased by 7 YoY
items.quote: The number of clients generating more than US$50 million in revenue increased by seven year -on-year, reflecting the trust our clients place in us and our ability to expand strategically within our key accounts.

items.statement: Continued investment in AI capabilities, Makers Lab, domain-specific and sovereign AI, platform ecosystem, and talent for AI at scale
items.quote: We continue to invest in AI capabilities. Our Makers Lab, which remains the core of our innovation engine, helps us translate emerging technology into practical enterprise solutions. At the same time, we're building differentiated capabilities in domain -specific and sovereign AI, areas where we believe demand will continue to grow as enterprises seek greater control, governance, and contextual re

items.statement: IT services headcount down 7% YoY due to AI-driven productivity gains in fixed-price portfolio; hiring expected to resume in remainder of FY27
items.quote: IT services revenues has continued to go up year -on-year. As you know, as we have shared in the past as well, our productivity for our fixed price engagements was below our expectations, and so we've driven with the help of the new AI tooling a higher level of productivity, which has meant lower headcount.

items.statement: Wage increases to be announced effective Q2 FY27 in phased fashion
items.quote: As far as the wage piece is concerned, we expect to be able to announce it effective Q2, obviously in a phased fashion which we will be announcing, to our employees in the days to come, so that will be effective, it'll start becoming effective Q2 in a phased fashion.

items.statement: Competitor irrationality: 70-80% productivity baked into 5-7 year deals; guaranteeing infrastructure pricing despite 20% YoY chip/memory inflation
items.quote: I think one example is obviously the level of productivity baked into, 5 to 7 year deals. Now, obviously, we want to make sure that we are aggressive, but getting into a 70%, 80% productivity benefit over a 5-year deal, I feel is getting into productivity benefits that are not visible today without very significant process or system changes by the client, so that is where we would hold back.

items.statement: AI-led BPS deals contributed overwhelming majority of BPS TCV; largest quarter was marquee AI engagement with large high-tech player
items.quote: Across our wins this quarter, AI operations contributed an overwhelming majority of our total BPS deal TCV. On internal transformation, our focus is not simply deploying tools, but reimagining the way we work.

items.statement: Agentic AI platform Orion deployed as enterprise-grade; 20+ agents on Google Gemini marketplace, 100+ active users
items.quote: Orion is being deployed as an enterprise -grade agentic AI platform and is available through major hyperscaler marketplaces. More than 20 Orion agents are listed on the Google Gemini marketplace, with over 100 users actively using Orion to develop agentic AI solutions for clients.

items.statement: Healthcare: US regional health system selected for integrated applications and infra managed services; Life sciences: AI vector squad compressed upgrade timelines from months to weeks
items.quote: A leading regional healthcare system in the US selected Tech Mahindra as a strategic partner for an integrated applications and infra managed services engagement. Leveraging our experience supporting 200 pl us health systems and deep healthcare transformation expertise, we will help strengthen operational resilience, accelerate modernization, and enhance caregiver and patient experiences.

items.statement: Telecom: Telefonica Germany multi-year engagement for AI-first private cloud platform with compute, storage, backup, containers, GPUs, ransomware protection
items.quote: In Europe, we expanded our relationship with Telefonica Germany through a multi -year engagement to build an AI -first private cloud platform. The partnership combines Tech Mahindra's platform engineering and AI -led operations with Telefonica Germany's telec om infrastructure modernization objectives.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 free cash flow $167M, up 94% YoY; DSO improved to 84 days, down 5 days QoQ; partly driven by accelerated payments and FX benefit that will normalize
items.quote: We genera ted US$167 million of free cash flow during the quarter, up 94% on a Y-o-Y basis. Higher collection efficiency supported the DSO improvement to 84 days, a reduction of five days on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: DSO improvement partly from accelerated payments and FX benefit; will normalize next quarter but long-term working capital focus remains
items.quote: Operationally, we did do well, that contributed to the performance, but there were some accelerated payments also that came in which will normalize for the next quarter. And similarly, there was some FX benefit on the AR side that contributed, which was negative last time but positive this time.

items.statement: Revenue $1.66B, up 6.1% YoY reported, 6.6% constant currency; organic revenue up 6.2% YoY constant currency
items.quote: In Q1, we reported revenues at US D1,660 million, representing a 2.2% quarter -on-quarter growth and a 6.1% Y -o-Y growth on a reported basis. On a constant currency basis, revenue grew 2.6% quarter-on-quarter and 6.6% Y-o-Y. Organic revenue grew 2.5% quarter-on-quarter and 6.2% Y-o-Y in constant currency.

items.statement: ROCE 28.3% in Q1 FY27, up 210 bps QoQ and 450 bps YoY
items.quote: Our return on capital employed stood at 28.3% for the quarter, reflecting a sequential improvement of 210 basis points. On a Y-o-Y basis, ROCE improved by 450 basis points driven by enhanced profitability and disciplined capital allocation.

items.statement: Acquired Avant Techno Solutions (Canada-based payments modernization and wealth platforms) to deepen BFSI presence
items.quote: During the quarter, we also announced the acquisition of Avant Techno Solutions, a Canada -based firm specializing in payments modernization and wealth platforms. This acquisition is aligned with our stated strategy of deepening our presence in payments and the wealth segments.

items.statement: European auto program accelerated delivery in Q1 (~1-1.3% revenue impact) will not repeat in Q2, creating headwind
items.quote: I would say around a 1 % to 1.3% range would be the impact coming into the next quarter. And as we have the large deal ramp -up which we'd mentioned, Mohit mentioned has not started yet, that will offset that and above and over and above that, the rest of the business needs to continuou sly perform to offset that and grow further for us for the next quarter.

items.statement: Comms vertical headwinds: Comviva seasonality and cloud pass-through revenue insourced by client post-acquisition
items.quote: For Comms we had the Comviva seasonality as a negative impact, and the second impact, as Rohit pointed out in his notes, was the case of, you know, of a client where cloud consumption was being routed through us as part of a larger deal, and as part of their takeover by a larger tech company, that cloud consumption is now being sourced directly, right?

items.statement: AI belt certification: 65%+ associates certified (white/blue/brown belt); 70% eligible developers enabled with AI pair programmer; 100+ productivity benchmarks established
items.quote: Our AI belt certification program continues to help TechM associates become increasingly relevant to client AI needs, with over 65% of our associates certified as white, blue, or brown belt. Across our delivery and internal adoption initiatives, we are seeing measurable progress. 70% of eligible developers are now enabled to code alongside an AI pair programmer.

items.statement: Recognized as Time's world's most sustainable companies, ranked #1 among Indian corporates
items.quote: Tech Mahindra has once again been recognized as one of the world's most sustainable companies by Time and ranked number one among Indian corporates.

items.statement: Management does not provide VNB margin or VNB growth guidance; focus is on absolute VNB growth
items.quote: We don't have a margin fixation. We've gone over that before as well. Absolute VNB is what we look at growing.

items.statement: Strong structural fundamentals support resilient demand for insurance products despite macro volatility
items.quote: Despite these near-term uncertainties, strong structural fundamentals continued to support resilient demand for insurance products.

items.statement: VNB margin expanded 200 bps YoY to 26.7% in Q1 FY2027 driven by product mix and operational efficiencies
items.quote: The VNB margin stood at 26.7%, an expansion of 200 basis points from the full-year FY2026 margin of 24.7%.

items.statement: Savings cost-to-premium ratio reduced 50 bps YoY to 13.6% despite input tax credit unavailability
items.quote: Consequently, our savings Cost-to-Premium ratio reduced by 50 basis points year-on-year to 13.6% in Q1-FY2027, despite the increase in expenses resulting from the unavailability of input tax credit.

items.statement: Total cost-to-premium ratio increased to 21.8% from 21.2% YoY due to higher protection business share
items.quote: Total cost-to-premium ratio for the quarter stood at 21.8% as compared to 21.2% last year, same quarter, primarily due to increase in protection business.

items.statement: Input tax credit unavailability will impact margins for one more quarter until Q3 base effect normalizes
items.quote: That's right. Yes, Shreya. It will continue for another quarter. That also will then form part of the base as we get into Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Protection share of APE increased; savings mix moderated from 78.1% to 72.1% YoY in Q1 FY2027
items.quote: Consequently, the savings business mix moderated from 78.1% in Q1-FY2026 to 72.1% in Q1-FY2027, while the protection business gained share.

items.statement: Non-linked savings par to non-par ratio is approximately 2:1 in Q1 FY2027
items.quote: In terms of par, non-par, we are about 2:1 on the par to non-par ratio at this point.

items.statement: Annuity growth in Q1 FY2027 led by regular premium deferred annuity plan
items.quote: Annuity in this quarter is led by regular premium as compared to what you had seen in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Retail protection APE grew 60.4% YoY in Q1 FY2027, third consecutive quarter above 40% growth post GST reforms
items.quote: Our core focus area, retail protection, grew by 60.4% year-on-year in Q1-FY2027, driven by the GST exemption on protection products and various Company-led initiatives. This marks the third consecutive quarter of retail protection year-on-year growth exceeding 40%, following the GST reforms.

items.statement: Group protection grew 37.8% YoY with MFI segment recovery and non-MFI momentum
items.quote: Our Group protection business, comprising credit life and group term, delivered strong growth of 37.8% year-on-year in Q1-FY2027. The MFI segment witnessed recovery after an extended period of moderation, while the non-MFI segment continued to demonstrate 5 healthy momentum

items.statement: Non-par savings demand subdued due to high fixed deposit sticker prices attracting customers
items.quote: The environment is such that there are products on the fixed income side that at this point are little more lucrative for the customer when compared to some of our products, purely from a sticker price perspective.

items.statement: Retail protection median customer age is 35 years, typically covering 30-35 year tenure
items.quote: The target market for protection typically centers around the 35-year-old. And again, one can understand this because typically, this is the age from a median perspective where people tend to take on greater responsibility.

items.statement: Partnership distribution channel has 1,500+ partners with no single partner exceeding 5% of business
items.quote: We've got 1,000 plus partners, and we keep continuing and diversifying this channel to become as large as we can.

items.statement: Standard Chartered partnership deeply integrated over 10 years across technology, processes, customer service; both parties value the relationship
items.quote: Now Standard Chartered has been a partner with us for the last 10 years, right? And in this decade, we have built a deeply integrated relationship that spans not just products, spans technology, processes and customer service.

items.statement: Investing in AI/ML across customer journey for demand generation, underwriting, retention, service, claims investigation
items.quote: One of them being the use of AI/ML, which is being embedded across the entire customer journey and that is driving targeted demand generation, automated underwriting, improved renewal retention, enhanced customer service and effective claims investigation.

items.statement: Agency channel recalibration via micro-market branch strategy, technology and analytics to enhance productivity
items.quote: We continue to recalibrate the channel, with our roadmap centered on a micro-market-led branch strategy, complemented by the use of technology & analytics to enhance productivity.

items.statement: Added ~15,000 advisors in Q1 FY2027; full-year target similar to ~70,000 added in FY2026
items.quote: Last year, we added about 70,000 agents.

items.statement: VNB grew 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 billion in Q1 FY2027
items.quote: We held our 26th AGM via video conference on June 30, 2026, and all the items specified in the AGM notice were duly approved by the Shareholders.

items.statement: PAT increased 27.8% YoY to ₹3.86 billion in Q1 FY2027
items.quote: PAT also increased by 27.8% year-on-year to ₹ 3.86 billion.

items.statement: New Business Premium grew 21.3% YoY to ₹48.66 billion in Q1 FY2027
items.quote: In Q1-FY2027, New Business Premium grew by 21.3% year -on-year to ₹ 48.66 billion, driven by 13.2% growth in the number of policies, reflecting the continued expa nsion of our customer base

items.statement: APE grew 14.6% YoY to ₹21.36 billion; RWRP grew 13.4% YoY to ₹15.38 billion in Q1 FY2027
items.quote: During the quarter, APE grew by 14.6% year-on-year to ₹ 21.36 billion and RWRP grew by 13.4% year-on-year to ₹ 15.38 billion in Q1-FY2027.

items.statement: Sum assured grew 31.8% YoY to ₹4.90 trillion; retail sum assured up 45.9% to ₹1.13 trillion in Q1 FY2027
items.quote: In Q1-FY2027, our sum assured grew by 31.8% to ₹ 4.90 trillion, supported by a strong 45.7% year-on-year growth in protection APE. Our sum assured market share stood at 11.8%. Retail sum assured increased by 45.9% to ₹ 1.13 trillion, driven by robust year-on-year growth of 60.4% in retail protection during the quarter.

items.statement: 13th month persistency stable at 84.0% in Q1 FY2027 vs 84.5% in Q4 FY2026
items.quote: No, across the quarter, you've seen that stability. It was 84.5% as we left March and it's 84.0% at this point.

items.statement: Solvency ratio robust at 225.4% as of June 30, 2026, well above 150% regulatory requirement
items.quote: We maintained a robust solvency ratio of 225.4%, significantly above the regulatory requirement of 150%, positioning us well to sustain future growth while maintaining financial strength.

items.statement: Assets Under Management stood at ₹3.34 trillion as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Our Assets Under Management stood at ₹ 3.34 trillion as of June 30, 2026, reflecting the scale of our franchise and t he trust placed in us by our policyholders

items.statement: IRDAI introduced regulations linking key management compensation to customer-centric outcomes and issued exposure draft on intermediary disclosures
items.quote: On the regulatory front, IRDAI has introduced regulations linking key management compensation with customer-centric outcomes and has issued an exposure draft on intermediary disclosures.

items.statement: Board approved name change to 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited' pending regulatory approval; PCHL reclassified from Promoter to Investor
items.quote: The Board, at its meeting held on July 6, 2026, has approved the proposal to rename the Company as 'ICICI Life Insurance Limited', pending regulatory approval. The name change follows the Board's approval of PCHL's request to change its status from 'Promoter' to 'Investor'.

items.statement: No en-masse repricing of protection products despite input tax credit unavailability; selective segment repricing only
items.quote: If you were expecting en-masse price changes, that has not happened, and we don't expect that at all. There will be certain segments that we will do repricing at, and these will be specific segments where we think they're not getting enough value and there is sufficient cushion that's on the table that we could reprice our products at.

items.statement: FY27 aspiration: grow in line with or faster than industry; deliver VNB growth broadly in line with APE growth
items.quote: For FY27, our aspi ration remains unchanged, t o grow in line with or faster than the industry and to deliver VNB growth broadly in line with APE growth

items.statement: Industry growth base case 15-17%; need to grow ~1% above industry for full-year industry-level growth
items.quote: So based on where the industry is at this point in time, the 15-17% kind of a number. If we continue with that base case, the requirement for us for the remaining nine months is to grow maybe a percentage higher than the industry for the full year basis.

items.statement: New business margin 25% in Q1 FY27, up 100 bps sequentially; residual GST impact 60 bps, on track to neutralize over coming quarters
items.quote: New bus iness margins stood at 25%, aided by better product profile, which helped absorb scale -related pressure and a GST impact of approximately 60 basis points

items.statement: Expect new business margins to remain range-bound at current levels, prioritizing growth over margin expansion
items.quote: Going forward, while margins should improve with scale and product mix, as stated at the beginning of this year, we will continue to prioritize growth over margin expansion. And hence , we expect new business margins to rema in range bound at current

items.statement: Q1 FY27 individual APE grew 7%, WRP 8%, overall APE 9%; 2-year CAGR individual APE 10%; retail private market share 16.3%
items.quote: We commenced FY27 with Q1 individual APE and WRP growing by 7% and 8%, respectively, while overall APE growth was stronger at 9%, supported by rob ust growth in credit life and gr oup business

items.statement: Retail protection grew 42% YoY; credit protect grew 19% supported by MFI recovery
items.quote: Retail Protection continued to outperform the company average growing by 42% and retail sum assured should also continue to outpace the industry, which is a reflection of the quality of our business mix and ou r sustained focus on long-term protection outcomes

items.statement: Product mix: ULIP 44%, non-par savings 22% (run-rate mid-20s), par 15%, retail protection 8%, annuity 11%
items.quote: Unit-linked products contributed 44% of individual APE, non-par savings 22%; participating products 15%, retail protection 8% and annuities 11%.

items.statement: Expect product portfolio to remain balanced; ULIP mix not to increase meaningfully; non-par savings share to improve gradually; protection to remain key growth driver but may moderate in H2
items.quote: We do not anticipate ULIP mix increasing meaningfully from current levels and expect the share of non -par savings products to im prove gradually as customers rebalance their asset allocation towards long -term guaranteed solutions amidst evolving market conditions

items.statement: Non-HDFC Bank channels grew 17% YoY; agency channel grew 21%; non-bank alliances retail protection grew 60%
items.quote: Channels other than HDFC Bank collectively grew at 17% in Q1 FY27, led by a strong performance by our agency channel and healthy momentum across non-bank alliances.

items.statement: HDFC Bank channel subdued but accounted share improved through quarter, trending closer to year-ago levels on run-rate basis
items.quote: Business through the HDFC Bank channel remains subdued this quarter, reflecting softer volumes at the overall bank level. We have worked closely with the parent and encouragingly accounted shar e within the bank improved through the quarter and is now trending closer to where it stood at the same time last year

items.statement: HDFC Bank channel contribution 47% of retail APE in Q1 FY27; market share back to Q1 FY26 levels
items.quote: Just coming to the contribution of HDFC bank in the retail APE. In this quarter, it has been at 47%.

items.statement: Added 250+ agency branches in past 24 months, contributing 16% of agency APE; new branches in Tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: And happy to share the branches that we opened in our agency channel, in the past 24 months, it contributes almost 16% to our agency APE.

items.statement: Branch breakeven 12-18 months in larger markets, 18-30 months in smaller markets; portfolio average ~18 months
items.quote: One branch typically takes about 18 months to break-even and start delivering margins and positive profits. And in about 2.5 years, it becomes more mature, that's a typical cycle for a branch.

items.statement: Agency channel active agent count and productivity improving; 70-75% of new business policies from Tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: Happy to share that now close to 70% to 75% of our new business comes from Tier 2 and 3 when you look at number of policies.

items.statement: VNB grew 9% to INR 879 crores; 2-year CAGR 11%; EV INR 65,860 crores; 5-year absolute EV accretion CAGR 18%
items.quote: Our value of new business grew 9% to INR 879 crores during the quarter, aided by improvement in new business margins by 100 basis points sequentially versus Q4. On a 2-year CAGR basis, VNB growth was 11%.

items.statement: AUM exceeded INR 4 trillion; solvency ratio improved to 185% after HDFC Bank preferential issuance of INR 1,000 crores
items.quote: We also cro ssed an important milestone this quarter with our assets under management exceeding INR 4 trillion. Following the successful completion of the preferential capital issuance by HDFC Bank, our solvency ratio im proved to 185

items.statement: Expect 13-month persistency in 84-85% range; difficult to return to 87-88% due to ticket size moderation
items.quote: We expect it to be in 84%-85% range. It's difficult to say that it will go up to 87%, 88% as we have seen. With the ticket size, moderation has happened. But we expect it to get better from the current level.

items.statement: IFRS implementation on track; awaiting clarity on risk-based solvency framework timeline; RBI third-party distribution regulations effective Jan 1; await IRDAI discussion paper on distribution remuneration
items.quote: On the regulatory front, IFRS implementation remains on track, and we look forward to further clarity on the time line for implementation of the risk -based solvency framework. Separately, the RBI regulations on third -party product distribution finalized last month and effective January 1 st, provide a framework around best -selling practices for distributo rs and we are working closely with our

items.statement: Solvency 185% with INR 500 crores sub-debt capacity (4% solvency upside); 15-18 months capital runway at current protection run-rate
items.quote: On solvency, yes, so as of now at about 185%-odd after the preferential allotment of INR 1,000 crores, we have additional sub-debt capacity as well, amounting to INR 500 crores, giving us potential of additional 4% solvency upside. The run rate that we are at this point in time, we're comfortable with a 15-18-odd months runway with the current capital that we have along with the sub-debt capacity.

items.statement: Geopolitical escalations and El Nino tracked as watch points; could impact oil prices and market sentiment
items.quote: Geopolitical escalations and risks can resurface quickly and we are watching this closely, given bearing on oil prices and broader mark et sentiment. El Nino also remains a factor we are tracking, though we do not see this as a broad -based risk at this stage

items.statement: Competitive intensity in non-par savings and HDFC Bank channel has mellowed; market share returning in key segments
items.quote: In this quarter, a lot of that has evened out. Most of the competition is no w completely benign on those products, which were obviously not profitable for t hem as well. And hence, we have seen the market share coming back

items.statement: Non-par savings run-rate crossed mid-20s aided by calibrated rate actioning and favorable yield environment
items.quote: Non -par savings crossed mid -20s on a run rate ba sis by the end of the quarter, aided b y cal ibrated rate actioning across select cohorts supported by a favorable yield environment

items.statement: Variable annuity attracting younger customers with longer commitment periods and lower ticket sizes than single premium annuities
items.quote: They are typically slightly youn ger in age than folks taking a single premium product. So, there we are able to widen the customer segment and offer ticket sizes, which are slightly lower than what we would do for single premium products as well

items.statement: Variable annuity margins higher than company average, between traditional annuity and non-par depending on structure
items.quote: On your var iable annuity question, yes, the margins will be higher than company average. It basically depends on the kind of stru cture that the customer chooses in terms of how many premiums they decide to pay

items.statement: HDFC Pension Fund Management market share 43%, AUM ~INR 1.75 lakh crores, 33% YoY growth; HDFC International Re steady with GIFT City traction
items.quote: Our wholly owned subsidiary, HDFC Pension Fund Management continues to strengthen its leadership position with a market share of 43%, with assets under management of approximately INR 1.75 lakh crores, delivering 33% growth YoY.

items.statement: Expects FY27 revenue flat to FY26 with potential 4-5% YoY upside; targets 20%+ YoY growth and 30% margin from FY28
items.quote: For this year, we will maintain the same numbers that we delivered last year, and if things go well, we may increase revenue by 4% to 5% year on year, maximum. But after this year [FY26-27], we will recover everything, and we will go with the speed that we have shown in the past, by maintaining margins of 25% to 30% year on year and quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Clients tightening budgets, delaying decisions, and rethinking technology roadmaps; two large clients ramped down engagements
items.quote: We began FY27 with geopolitical tensions and macro uncertainty that have made clients more cautious with technology budgets globally, and that caution has been visible across the industry. Clients are tightening budgets, delaying decisions, and rethinking their technology roadmaps.

items.statement: Mixed signals with some previously cautious customers now awarding new AI initiatives; pipeline building intensified
items.quote: Also, we are seeing mixed signals in the market, with several customers who were previously cautious on AI adoption now moving forward with new initiatives and awarding new business.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 30.3%, up 389 bps YoY; sequential margin flat despite revenue decline due to cost optimisation and AI efficiency
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 30.3%, compared to 29.3% in the previous quarter and 26.4% in Q1FY26. On a year-on-year basis, EBITDA margin expanded by 389 basis points, supported by the revenue growth and focused cost optimisation initiatives.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin to move towards upper end of 25-30% range as revenue scales; AI-enabled delivery improving execution efficiency
items.quote: We expect EBITDA margin to move towards the upper end of our target range as revenue scales and demand improves, with further potential for improvement in EBITDA margin through better operating leverage.

items.statement: Revenue impact from two large client ramp-downs to reflect fully over next 2-3 quarters; near-term revenue softness expected
items.quote: Q1FY27 Earnings Call 15 th July , 202 6 engagement ramp-downs occurred towards the end of the quarter, we expect the full impact to be reflected over the next two to three quarters, resulting in some near-term revenue softness

items.statement: Pipeline includes deals of $300K and $250K; approximately $1M total pipeline; conversion takes at least two quarters
items.quote: I have one deal in the pipeline where the size is 300K, and another one in the pipeline where the size is 250K. So I have approximately 1 million US dollars of pipeline at this moment.

items.statement: Two of top 10 clients (3-year relationships) suddenly reduced business; one due to management change, other due to losses; both may ramp up next year if conditions improve
items.quote: out of the 10, two customers have suddenly reduced their bu siness, and they had been with us for the last three years. They had started with a very small amount of work, but by now, they were large. And suddenly, they said that they want to stop the work, next year they may think about it again if everything goes well

items.statement: More than 80% revenue from repeat customers including wallet share expansion; new large deal wins also converting to revenue
items.quote: So, almost, I would say, more than 80% of our revenue comes from repeat customers. And this includes new additional work that these customers are giving us.

items.statement: Developer efficiency up ~25% (4 people's work now done by 2); senior developers up to 3x efficiency using AI tools like Claude
items.quote: The developer efficiency, I would say, is almost 25%, so what four people were doing earlier is now being done by almost two people, at a very high level. For some senior developers, it is triple, so one person is able to do more than two people's work.

items.statement: Investing in AI capabilities and certifications; strategic initiatives partially offset margin expansion YoY
items.quote: This improvement was partially offset by compensation increments, investments in AI capabilities, and other strategic initiatives taken.

items.statement: Geographic revenue mix: North America 63%, India 18%, Europe 6%, Australia 3%, Rest of World 10%
items.quote: Our geographical diversification remains healthy, with 82% of our revenue coming from overseas markets: North America continues to remain our largest overseas market, contributing 63% of revenue. This is followed by India at 18%, Europe at 6%, Australia at 3%, and the rest of the world at 10%.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with cash and bank balance of Rs 17 crore as of 30 June 2026; strong cash conversion and working capital management
items.quote: From a balance sheet perspective, the company remains debt-free, with a cash and bank balance of Rs. 17 crore as on 30th june 2026. We maintain strong cash conversion and prudent working capital management.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of Rs 4 per share for FY27 reflecting confidence in cash generation
items.quote: During the quarter, the board declared an interim dividend of Rs. 4 per share for FY27, reflecting our confidence in the cash generation capability and long-term sustainability of the business model.

items.statement: Large players not a threat due to high inherent costs and minimum deal sizes; Ksolves competes on niche Big Data/AI/ML expertise and lower cost structure
items.quote: Larger companies will still not be able to deliver, because their inherent costs are still going to be very high, even if they use AI. So, I do not see a challenge per se from that perspective.

items.statement: AI-enabled delivery improving team productivity; scaling efficiently with disciplined hiring approach
items.quote: AI-enabled delivery continues to improve execution efficiency and enhance team productivity, enabling us to scale more efficiently while maintaining a disciplined approach to hiring.

items.statement: Planning new verticals in cybersecurity and SAP to target large enterprises; Odoo ERP expertise for SMBs being leveraged
items.quote: For example, cybersecurity, which we want to start as a new vertical. We also want to start SAP, because right now, we are a very well-known name in ERP in India for Odoo. But Odoo is for small businesses. We want to target large businesses also.

items.statement: Strengthened global sales leadership with Eric Paul as VP & Head of Global Sales and Najib Saiyed as Head of Sales, North America
items.quote: We have strengthened our global sales leadership by appointing Eric Paul as the VP and Head of Global Sales, and Najib Saiyed as the Head of Sales, North America.

items.statement: Middle East new business not confident for next few quarters; existing Middle East contracts renewing
items.quote: For the Middle East, I am not confident. In the last quarter, I have not seen any new business from the Middle East, and for the next few quarters, I can again say that I am not confident we will get new business from the Middle East.

items.statement: Jio Credit Gross AUM surged 2.6x YoY to ₹30,667 crore
items.quote: Our lending business, Jio Credit, saw its Gross AUM surge 2.6x year-on-year, standing at ₹ 30,667 crores.

items.statement: Jio Payments Bank deposits grew 1.7x YoY to ₹617 crore
items.quote: Jio Payments Bank deposits grew 1.7x to ₹ 617 crores

items.statement: Jio Payment Solutions TPV grew 2.5x YoY to ₹19,208 crore

items.statement: Service EBITDA margin currently 13-14%, targeting 24-25% in next few years; corporate overheads to stay sub 5-6% of revenue
items.quote: I think I'll give this in terms of service EBITDA. I can maybe , once at the right time, we can also engage more. But from a service EBITDA point of view, today, we would be at about 13-14%. The expansion from 13-14% will go to in the next few years to about 24 -25%.

items.statement: Renewal service EBITDA margin is 2.5-3 times higher than new business service EBITDA margin
items.quote: It's about 2.5-3 times higher than the new service EBITDA.

items.statement: Renewal book revenue reached INR 230 crores in FY26, representing 20% of total revenues
items.quote: Some of the points that I made earlier with respect to our renewal book being 20% of our revenues , going to about INR 230 odd crores for the financial year FY26.

items.statement: Enterprise business contributes roughly 20% of platform premiums; added new accounts that will go live in coming year driving faster growth
items.quote: The premium growth there , is driven by, of course, the growth of their own businesses as well as the amount of digitization that they're able to drive, the change management and so on that they're able to do.

items.statement: Health business within general insurance grew more than 60% in FY26
items.quote: Dhirendra highlighted that our health business within that has grown at more than 60% in the last year.

items.statement: PoSP-driven insurance broking premium grew over 40% in FY26
items.quote: That grew in FY26 at about more than 40% for the year.

items.statement: General insurance is over 90% of platform premium vs life insurance; health growing strongly within GI
items.quote: Sir, what we have highlighted in the past is that general insurance businesses are more than 90% in terms of platform premium for us as compared to life businesses.

items.statement: Non-insurance revenue is 3% of total revenue in FY26; mutual fund AUM ~INR 1,400 crores, loan disbursement run rate ~INR 300 crores annualized
items.quote: On an annual basis in FY26, 97% of our revenues are in the subsidiary, which is Turtlemint Insurance Broking, and our revenue is commission. The remaining 3% is non -insurance businesses for now.

items.statement: Top 3 insurer partners contribute ~22% of business; work with 45+ partners with low concentration
items.quote: Top 3 are about 22% of our business. The difference between one to five is not very high. So, depending on the supply and depending on their underwriting requirements, insurance companies get their share.

items.statement: Receivables at INR 150-160 crores, representing 40-50 days; maintain positive cash cycle by paying PoSP commissions after collecting from insurers; ~99% PAT to cash flow conversion
items.quote: So, sir, from the balance sheet, if you were to compare the closing receivables on a consolidated basis, which has been roughly about INR 150-160 crores, and compare it with, let us say, our quarterly revenues that we just spoke about, we'll realize that we don't have more than about 40-50 days of receivables there, which reflects a strong collection cycle.

items.statement: Attrition better than industry; compensation includes fixed, variable, 4-year guaranteed bonus, and ESOPs covering 500+ employees
items.quote: I think whether it is the frontline teams or the non-frontline teams, we actually enjoy a better attrition as compared to the industry. This, I will credit to the compensation structures that the board has enabled for us.

items.statement: No immediate buyback/dividend; will consider distribution policy after 1-2 years of sustained profitability
items.quote: As we demonstrate, maybe one or two years of sustained profitability and strengthening profitability, we do look forward to having the appropriate dividend distribution policies for all the shareholders.

items.statement: 76% of premium comes from beyond top 30 cities; 98-99% PIN code coverage via PoSP network
items.quote: I think one point I mentioned, Nischint, is that about 76% of our premium comes from beyond the top 30 cities.

items.statement: More than 60% of active PoSPs operate across multiple product categories
items.quote: I would say, more than one category, people are more than 60%. People operating across categories.

items.statement: Government mission 'Insurance for All by 2047' driving penetration in Tier 3/4 markets where Turtlemint operates
items.quote: There is a mission of the Government, which is called, "Insurance for All by 2047" , which means that by 2047, everybody in the country should have insured for one asset, one health, and one life insurance policy.

items.statement: Management targets ROA of 3-3.5% by June 2028 exit
items.quote: we've given an exit of June 2028 at a 3%, 3.5% ROA. That itself could give you a sense of where we are today of 1.98%.

items.quote: We plan to add similar number of approximately 400-odd branches during FY27, largely in Tier 2, Tier 3 locations.

items.statement: Prime personal loan digital processing increased to 38% in Q1 from 33% in Q4 and 28% earlier
items.quote: In Q1, there's a 38% of disbursements that are processed through a fully straight-through digital processing, that's on the rise, it's increased from 33% in Q4 previous quarter and before that, the same figure was approximately 28%.

items.statement: Education loan disbursements grew 55% quarter-on-quarter with average monthly disbursement of ₹144 crores
items.quote: Within 1 year of launch, we are excited that we've delivered 55% quarter-on-quarter disbursement in Q1 with average monthly disbursement reaching ₹144 crores.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle monthly disbursement at ₹104 crores with 1,100+ channel partners across 70+ locations in 30 states

items.statement: Consumer durable disbursements of ₹433 crores with 17,300+ retail outlets across 339 locations
items.quote: On Consumer Durable, we are scaling efficiently with Q1FY27 disbursements of ₹433 crores. We have onboarded over 17,300 retail outlets across 339 locations on June quarter end.

items.quote: AUM at the end of Q1FY27 stands at ₹67,054 crores. This reflects a quarter-on-quarter growth of 11%.

items.quote: the share of long-term borrowings has gone up by approximately 2%, from 86.5% to 88.5% quarter-on-quarter. This number was 75.2% in Q1 of FY26.

items.quote: we raised ₹2,500 crores in the 1st week of April or 2 nd week of April and we are pretty much comfortable for the next 4 to 5 quarters

items.quote: Our opex to AUM has already declined year-on-year from 4.76% in Q4FY25 to 4.13% at the end of Q4FY26. We have achieved a further reduction of 7 basis points to 4.06% in Q1FY27.

items.quote: Our ROA, which I believe is an important metric, for us internally has moved up to 1.98%, reflecting a 17 basis point improvement over the previous quarter and 130 basis point improvement over Q1FY26.

items.statement: Profit after tax of ₹308 crores, up 20.8% quarter-on-quarter and 391.5% year-on-year
items.quote: As a result, we have achieved ₹308 crores in profit after tax, recording a 20.8% growth quarter-on-quarter, and a 391.5% growth year-on-year.

items.quote: Total AI projects grew by over 30% to 101 projects spanning 21 departments, of which 50 are deployed and 51 are in pipeline. This ecosystem has reached significant scale, approximately 130 smart agents live in production

items.statement: Domestic capacity now 200.1 million tons, total 205.5 million tons

items.statement: India Cements green power to reach 86% of requirements by end FY28
items.quote: a step change in the green power trajectory from around 3% of their power requirements to about 86% of their power requirements by the end of fiscal '28.

items.statement: Domestic grey cement volumes grew 13.1% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our domestic grey cement volumes growth of 13.1%, I believe will be well ahead of industry's growth, translating directly into market share gains.

items.statement: East region demand upcycle expected over next 2-4 years

items.statement: Operating EBITDA per ton steady above INR1,200 in Q1 FY27

items.statement: India Cements brand migration 100% complete, volumes up 19% YoY on like-for-like basis

items.statement: Total fund based outstanding to standard borrowers under resolution declined to 13.63 billion rupees at June 30, 2026 from 14.96 billion at March 31, 2026 and 17.88 billion at June 30, 2025
