items.statement: Net interest income increased 12.7% year-on-year and 6.1% sequentially to 243.84 billion rupees in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Net interest income increased by 12.7% year-on-year and 6.1% sequentially to 243.84 billion Rupees in this quarter.

items.statement: Management sees positive momentum in loan growth across segments, participating in system-wide pickup driven by fiscal and monetary policy measures; incremental momentum continues to be strong
items.quote: We are sort of participating in that, and we will keep looking at opportunities as they come. And the momentum continues to be pretty good as far as we can see it.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth driven by shift from bond markets, working capital utilization, and corporates maintaining liquidity buffers; healthy pipeline at reasonable rates this quarter
items.quote: Part of it is a shift from bond markets, part of it is working capital utilization, part of it may be corporates taking on some borrowings and just maintaining some liquidity buffers as they also want to be sort of have greater resilience in this uncertain environment.

items.statement: Retail asset demand stable; savings inflows stable; retail portfolio performance improved with unsecured additions coming down year-on-year
items.quote: No, we have not seen any change actually. In terms of inflows into the savings, etc., they are quite stable. We've not seen any change. And as you can see, the performance of the retail portfolio has only improved.

items.statement: FCNR(B) all-in cost after hedging estimated at 6.30-6.40%, lower than wholesale rates and competitive; no specific mobilization target set; early days for the scheme
items.quote: From a cost effectiveness perspective, 6%. If you look at kind of the all-in cost after hedging the coupon, etc., it will be somewhere maybe 6.30-6.40%, which is, of course, lower than wholesale rates and it will be competitive compared to the wholesale rates.

items.statement: Branch count increased by 97 in Q1 FY27 to 7,608 branches as of June 30, 2026; technology expenses were 11.4% of operating expenses
items.quote: Our branch count has increased by 97 in the first quarter. We had 7,608 branches as of June 30, 2026. The technology expenses were about 11.4% of our operating expenses in this quarter.

items.statement: Average deposits grew 14.0% year-on-year and 6.1% sequentially; average CASA deposits grew 12.1% year-on-year and 4.7% sequentially; average LCR for quarter was about 124%
items.quote: Average deposits grew by 14.0% year-on-year and 6.1% sequentially and average current and savings account deposits grew by 12.1% year-on-year and 4.7% sequentially during this quarter. The Bank's average liquidity coverage ratio for the quarter was about 124%.

items.statement: CET-1 ratio of 16.19% and total capital adequacy ratio of 16.84% at June 30, 2026; capital position remains strong
items.quote: The capital position of the Bank continued to be strong with a CET-1 ratio of 16.19% and total capital adequacy ratio of 16.84% at June 30, 2026.

items.statement: FCNR(B) mobilization in early days, no target set; will play out over next 8-10 weeks; balance sheet of international branches may expand materially if significant amount mobilized
items.quote: On the second question on FCNR {B), we don't really have any target or so on that we put out. I think it's a good scheme, and we will look to mobilize as much as we can, but it is very early days yet. This is something that will really play out over the next maybe 8 -10 weeks or so.

items.statement: Fee income grew 23.5% year-on-year to 72.86 billion rupees in Q1 FY27 off a low base; fees from retail, rural and business banking constituted 72% of total fees
items.quote: Fee income increased by 23.5% year-on-year to 72.86 billion Rupees in this quarter off a low base of Ql of last year. Fees from retail, rural and business banking customers constituted about 72% of the total fees in this quarter.

items.statement: Operating expenses increased 10.4% year-on-year in Q1 FY27 vs 11.5% in FY26; employee expenses up 5.5% year-on-year; non-employee expenses up 13.8% year-on-year
items.quote: The Bank's operating expenses increased by 10.4% year-on-year in this quarter compared to 11.5% year-on-year in FY2026. Employee expenses increased by 5.5% year-on-year in this quarter, reflecting mainly the impact of annual increments and promotions that take place during the first quarter of every fiscal year. Non-employee expenses increased by 13.8% year-on-year in this quarter.

items.statement: Total provisions were 12.60 billion rupees or 6.2% of core operating profit and 0.32% of average advances in Q1 FY27 vs 18.15 billion in Q1 FY26; credit cost 32 bps reported, normalized around 50 bps adjusting for chunky recoveries
items.quote: The total provisions during the quarter were 12.60 billion Rupees or 6.2% of core operating profit and 0.32% of average advances compared to the provisions of 18.15 billion rupees in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: ECL transition impact on net worth expected to be absorbed by provisioning buffers; ongoing impact will result in higher Stage 2 provisions partly offset by lower Stage 3 provisions; difficult to quantify ongoing impact in basis points
items.quote: On the net worth, we will not really have any impact. Our assessment based on whatever proforma estimates we have done based on the existing position of the balance sheet or the portfolio is that whatever impact is there will be well absorbed by our provisioning buffers.

items.statement: Agri portfolio remediation and validation process ongoing; no timeline given for provision write-back; granular portfolio requiring careful sign-off
items.quote: I wouldn't really be able to comment on the timing. But yes, we have been working on the required remediation of the portfolio. We just want to make sure that whatever we have done is correct and signed off and validated before we discuss a write-back of the provision.

items.statement: Competition not holding back growth; franchise capable of delivering more market share; calibrating based on interest rate and competitive environment; not doing business at rates quoted by some competitors
items.quote: Our belief is that our franchise should deliver more. And there is always some set of competition that you have to deal with. But I think there is enough business for us to do within our frameworks, and we keep calibrating based on sort of the interest rate environment and the competitive environment.

items.statement: Targets double-digit volume growth for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year.

items.statement: Expects cost increase of INR130-140 per ton sequentially in Q2 FY27
items.quote: I would expect the cost to go up by INR130 to INR140 per ton, all put together.

items.statement: Targets net debt to EBITDA below 1x for FY27
items.quote: Our belief is, and we are confident that this year also, we'll end the net debt to EBITDA below 1x.

items.statement: India Cements EBITDA per ton target of INR1,000 remains in sight with full benefit from Q4 FY28
items.quote: EBITDA of INR1,000 per ton for India Cements remains very much in sight with the full benefit of the capex program flowing through the P&L from Q4 fiscal '28.

items.statement: Cables and wires launch reaffirmed for Q3 FY27
items.quote: We reaffirm commissioning and product launch in Q3 fiscal '27, October - December '26 quarter, precisely as committed to you when we announced this investment.

items.statement: Projects under execution backed by INR17,000 crores capex over next 2-2.5 years
items.quote: Projects under execution for capacity growth are backed by a capex of about INR17,000 crores in the next 2 to 2.5 years.

items.statement: Cables and wires investment program of INR1,800 crores, INR888 crores spent or committed till last quarter
items.quote: We had approved an investment program of INR1,800 crores. Till the last quarter, INR888 crores has been spent or committed.

items.statement: Domestic capacity reached 200.1 million tons, total 205.5 million tons after 8.7 million tons commissioned in Q1 FY27
items.quote: around 12 million tons of new capacity has got commissioned in the country, out of which 8.7 million tons is by UltraTech, Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam and Patratu, tweaking our domestic capacity to 200.1 million tons and total capacity to 205.5 million tons.

items.statement: Grey cement capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by end of FY27, consolidated beyond 242 million tons
items.quote: We'll take our consolidated capacity beyond 242 million tons with grey cement capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by the end of fiscal '27 and further balance to be completed in the next year.

items.statement: Expects to exit March 2028 with 235 million tons capacity in India
items.quote: March '28 we should exit with 235 million tons in India.

items.statement: Demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate is very rich
items.quote: a demand pipeline across infrastructure, housing and urban real estate is as rich as it can be.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA per ton steady above INR1,200 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Operating EBITDA per ton has been steady above INR1,200 this quarter as well.

items.statement: Absorbed sharp imported fuel cost shock while holding per ton earnings flat and growing absolute EBITDA 12%
items.quote: We have absorbed and are absorbing the sharpest imported fuel cost shock in recent memory, during the quarter, on a volume base enlarged by acquired assets that are still ramping up to system profitability, and we held per ton earnings essentially flat while growing absolute EBITDA 12%.

items.statement: All India exit prices improved through June, East and South led improvements, industry expects prices to hold steady through monsoon
items.quote: Cement prices have been constructive during the quarter in the report. Our all India exit prices improved through June even as the monsoon now sets in, East and South led price improvements, Central and West were steady and North was more or less a consistent performer.

items.statement: Premiumization engine and blended cement in trade mix compounding blended realizations
items.quote: Our premiumization engine and blended cement in the trade mix continues to do quite a compounding work on blended realizations regardless of headline price movements.

items.statement: Green power at 1,897 MW met 47% of total power requirements at quarter end
items.quote: our green power of about 1 ,897 megawatts met ab out 47% of our total power requirements at the end of this quarter

items.statement: Targets 2.5 to 3 GW renewable capacity shortly
items.quote: We believe we will reach anywhere between 2.5 to 3 gigawatts very shortly.

items.statement: Cement lead distance reduced to 360 km
items.quote: cement lead distance for this quarter has come down to 360 kilometres.

items.statement: Pet coke more expensive than coal in energy terms, domestic coal more attractive
items.quote: Pet coke has become more expensive in energy terms than coal. So yes, coal becomes more attractive to buy, domestic coal becomes more attractive to buy.

items.statement: Retail sales 65-66%, institutional 35%, RMC 3.5% of UltraTech sales
items.quote: RMC, for us, it's about 3.5%. 3.5% of our sale is RMC. Our institutional customers would be 35% or thereabouts, give or take. 65% to 66% would be retail.

items.statement: India Cements revenue grew 21% like-for-like, volumes up 19% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: the revenues were INR993 crores as compared to INR821 crores on a like-for-like basis, which is a 21% growth in revenues, backed by a 19% growth in their volumes.

items.statement: India Cements EBITDA per ton improved from INR386 in Q2 FY26 to INR603 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: India Cements' EBITDA per ton has climbed from roughly INR386 per ton in Q2FY26 to INR400 to INR509 and INR603 this quarter.

items.statement: Cables and wires working capital to stabilize at 30 days plus/minus after initial ramp-up
items.quote: going forward and structurally we are working on financing our suppliers on cables and wires which should release working capital. So, excuse me for havi ng a higher working capital for the next six months after which we start stabilizing and coming down to 30 days plus-minus of working capital

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA improved from 0.94x to 0.87x in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We had started the year with a net debt EBITDA of 0.94 and the quarter, we have ended with 0.87x net debt to EBITDA.

items.statement: All growth capex and cost improvement initiatives funded through internal accruals
items.quote: All these growth capexes, the cost improvement initiatives are all being funded with internal accruals.

items.statement: India Cements turnaround on track, capex of INR2,000 crores deployed, green power to reach 86% by FY28
items.quote: Cost improvement capex of about INR2,000 crores is being deployed into waste heat recovery, preheater upgr adation, cooler upgradation, et cetera, and a step change in the green power trajectory from around 3% of their power requirements to about 86% of their power requirements by the end of fiscal '28

items.statement: West Asia crisis and fuel cost volatility remain key near-term risks
items.quote: Fuel cost, storm is a yoyo, we have to keep an eye on and wait through it, the West Asia crisis, I don't know when it will end.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance 11-12% and advances growth 14-16% for FY27
items.quote: Bank had released guidance about composition of our advances, RAM and corporate , and our guidance to market towards the resources side, 11% to 12% in deposit growth and 14% to 16% in advances growth.

items.statement: NIM guidance 3% and above, ROA 1% and above maintained
items.quote: Now coming to ROA and NIM. I have given guidance, NIM will be 3% and above and still we are maintaining. ROA 1% and above, that also we have maintained and remain 1% and above.

items.statement: RAM to Corporate credit ratio guidance 65:35 plus-minus 5%
items.quote: RAM to Corporate Credit ratio stands at 68:32, aligning with our guidance ratio of 65:35 plus-minus 5%.

items.statement: Quarter-on-quarter loan growth expected at approximately 3%
items.quote: Bank be able to maintain this growth rate, quarter-on-quarter growth will be approximately 3%.

items.statement: Yield on advances expected to reach 8% by March 2027
items.quote: So there, we expect that our yield will improve from 7.89% to anywhere between 8%, we are thinking that as of March '27, we will reach up to 8%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio targeted to reduce by 1.5-1.6% in coming year
items.quote: We are sure that in coming year, Bank will reduce cost-to-income ratio by 1.5% to 1.6%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 NIM at 3.06%, above 3% guidance
items.quote: Net interest margin is above 3%, aligning with our guidance to the market. It is 3.06%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 ROA at 1%, ROE improved to 14.92%
items.quote: ROA is 1%, ROE improved to 14.92% from 14.17%.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 cost-to-income ratio at 55.40%
items.quote: Cost-to-income ratio is at 55.40% it was 55.30% for June '25 quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 slippage ratio at 0.29%, improved 6 bps YoY
items.quote: Slippage ratio stood at 0.29% for this quarter and where we can mark an improvement of 6 basis points.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 credit cost at 0.40%, improved from 0.68% previous quarter
items.quote: We have maintained credit cost at 0.40%, there is an improvement from 0.68% of previous quarter '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 CASA ratio maintained at 46.61% of total deposits
items.quote: CASA being remained our strong point, we maintained 46.61% of total deposits.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 CD ratio improved to 74.10% from 64%
items.quote: CD ratio improved to 74.10%.

items.statement: Gross NPA at 2.60%, improved 53 bps YoY; Net NPA at 0.49%, PCR 95.86%
items.quote: Towards asset quality also, gross NPA stood at 2.60% , there is an improvement of 53 basis points year on year basis. We have maintained net NPA at 0.49%, PCR approximately 95.86%.

items.statement: ECL provisions of Rs 1,525 cr made out of Rs 4,500-5,000 cr total requirement; 80 bps CRAR impact if fully provided
items.quote: Under ECL, we have already made provisions of Stage 1 and Stage 2 for ₹1,525 crores out of approximately total requirement of ₹4,500 crores to ₹5,000 crores. So, for that purpose, I understand our current profit numbers are enough. Bank's CRAR is at 18.28%. Even though there are provisions, we can stagger it to 5 years or we can account it at once also, then only 80 basis points only impact we are

items.statement: Target recovery of Rs 2,200-2,500 cr from technically written-off accounts in FY27
items.quote: This year also, I'm expecting recovery of ₹2,200 crores to ₹2,500 crores out of technically written-off account.

items.statement: Target to sell 600-700 properties in FY27 vs 460 last year
items.quote: In the current financial year, we are targeting to sell 600 to 700 properties against 460 properties in the last financial year.

items.statement: Undisbursed advances approximately Rs 5,000 cr
items.quote: Undisbursed advances is approximately ₹5,000 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan book at Rs 36,000 cr with growth potential in South India
items.quote: In Gold Loan segment, total book is ₹36,000 crores. So, growth is good as compared to previous year, but still a lot of scope is available in terms of our presence in South India, which has very good experience of gold loan.

items.statement: 1,000 credit officers joining first week of October 2026; planned corporate finance and mid-corporate branches
items.quote: In people side, our 1,000 credit officers who were undergoing specialized training for credit, they are going to join us in the first week of October' 2026. We are going to deploy them on our all potential , credit centres. We have planned to open more corporate finance branch and mid-corporate branch.

items.statement: GIFT City IFSC Banking Unit inaugurated June 29, 2026; targeting USD 200 mn deposits and USD 500 mn trade book over next few years
items.value: USD 200 mn deposits, USD 500 mn trade book
items.quote: Deposit of USD200 million and trade book of USD500 million over the next few years, we are planning. As on 29th June only, it was inaugurated.

items.statement: Cost of deposits improved to 4.60%, 33 bps improvement; term deposits mostly repriced
items.quote: Cost of deposit improved to 4.60 % that is 33 basis point improvement registered. So, cost of deposit has stabilized.

items.statement: Yield on advances at 7.89%, up from 7.78%
items.quote: Yield on advances is 7.89% , it has improved from 7.78%.

items.statement: FCNR(B) mobilized USD 8.4 mn so far, targeting USD 400 mn by September 2026
items.value: USD 8.4 mn of USD 400 mn target
items.quote: FCNR (B) till now, we have mobilized USD8.4 million and we are expecting to mobilize USD400 million by September'2026.

items.statement: CRAR at 18.28%, CET1 at 16.24%, Tier 1 at 16.54%; no capital raise needed for growth guidance
items.quote: We already have CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% In that way, we are having enough capital, and we don't need capital to support our growth guidance, which we have given to the market, we are having enough capital.

items.statement: Board approved up to Rs 7,000 cr equity/BASEL III raise but no current plan to execute
items.quote: We already have CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% In that way, we are having enough capital, and we don't need capital to support our growth guidance, which we have given to the market, we are having enough capital. So therefore, we don't have any plan for raising capital as of now.

items.statement: Corporate growth driven by renewable energy, data centres, HAM projects, CRE
items.quote: major areas on corporate side is renewable energy, data centres and some projects i n HAM, good opportunities we are observing. We are getting good proposals under CRE

items.statement: Board approved wealth management, credit card, NRI and marketing verticals; entering credit card segment
items.quote: Bank is having 8.33 crores customer base. So therefore, we have got approval from Board for establishment of wealth management vertical, credit card vertical, NRI and marketing vertical. So, we are entering into credit card segment also.

items.statement: 85% of deposits under Rs 3 cr segment (retail); Cent Queen mobilized Rs 1,457 cr, Salary Cent Prestige Rs 787 cr
items.quote: Term deposit almost is repriced now and 4.60% is the cost of deposit. But in growth side, if you want to know, term deposit has grown by 12% in our bank and majority are below ₹3 crores, means retail deposits. 85% of our deposits are under ₹3 crores segment.

items.statement: 159 NRI desks operational; centralized forex and BG cells opened
items.quote: We have 159 NRI desk in our different branches. We are going to market all these products which Central Bank of India is having through our -- all the strength, physical presence and marketing team.

items.statement: Dedicated gold loan and SHG divisions created with heads reporting to Executive Director
items.quote: Bank brought in some structural changes also. Dedicated gold loan division and also SHG division are being opened where head of these verticals will directly work under the guidance of Executive Director.

items.statement: Agriculture KCC slippages of Rs 200 cr contributed to slippage ratio; debt waiver scheme expected to liquidate these
items.quote: If we can reduce the agriculture KCC numbers, which got slipped i.e. ₹200 crores out of total ₹986 crores and ₹989 crore in previous year, June '25. So that agriculture side, ₹200 crores was the contributor. You know that debt waiver scheme is coming, and those things will get liquidated.

items.statement: 90-95% of AUM in quartile 1 and 2 performance
items.quote: I think Arash will give you the number, but 90% to 95% of the AUM is in quartile 1 and 2.

items.statement: Expects growth to accelerate from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: I do believe that from these quarters on, we can see an acceleration in growth.

items.statement: Q1 saw slight moderation due to market volatility rub-off effect
items.quote: So, there was a little bit of moderation in Q1. So, it is slightly one-off. I mean, overall revenue-wise, yes, we've grown. But given the volatility in the last quarter there is some, obviously, some rub-off effect on us as well.

items.statement: Average client funding book (MTF + T+5) at INR 422 crore, up 3% QoQ
items.quote: Our average client funding book, which includes both MTF and the T +5 offering, which is also a related offering, now stands at I mean, for the last quarter stands at now it's much higher, but it stands at INR 422 crore, which was an increase of 3% QoQ.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM reached INR 2,073 crore, up 18% QoQ
items.quote: Our mutual fund assets under management reached INR 2,073 crore, which was an 18% increase QoQ.

items.statement: Launched OI Profile on Charts, OneClick execution, and AlgoSpace algo trading platform
items.quote: Our recent launches, which was the OI profile on Charts, OneClick execution, and the launch of AlgoSpace, which is the name that we've given to our algo trading platform.

items.statement: Launched AI insights for portfolio and stock analysis; building simplified MCP integration with major LLM provider
items.quote: On the app, we've launched both portfolio and stock insights. So, if you have a portfolio or if you have a stock, you're able to use AI to uncover insights on that, and we've seen very encouraging response.

items.statement: Raised INR 468 crore via rights issue in April for product, tech talent, partnerships, and growth marketing
items.quote: We raised about INR 468 crores in the rights issue as capital in the month of April, which is strengthened the balance sheet and which we're going to use for obviously continued investment in the product and tech talent for improving and taking a product to the next level plus partnerships and plus growth marketing.

items.statement: Focused on improving unit economics and operating leverage via revamped platform
items.quote: We're looking to also make meaningful improvements in our unit economics to improve our margin and overall PAT. The idea is to get to a state very quickly where we have operating leverage from it.

items.statement: Channel mix will change; refining allocation quarterly based on CAC and RPC metrics
items.quote: Yes, the channel mix will change. Percentage-wise, we keep refining where to put money and how much to put money on a quarterly basis depending on what kind of CAC plus RPC metrics we are seeing in each of these channels.

items.statement: Post Oct 2024 F&O changes, market saw moderation; 5paisa strategy is quality acquisition and retention over quantity
items.quote: after the F&O changes came in the month of October ‘24, there was a moderation across the board. On players which were, you know, who are major source of revenue from F&O, and then a lot of them are diversified. So, that is their strategy. Our strategy is, again, quality customer acquisition, not quantity, and then retaining them for over a longer period of tim e to drive higher revenue share

items.statement: Actively evaluating inorganic opportunities to accelerate journey and add talent
items.quote: Third, of course, we continue to selectively evaluate inorganic opportunities as well in the market, which can accelerate our journey and give us additional speed and talent to move forward as an integrated platform.

items.statement: ADTO dipped slightly in F&O but grew in cash segment; long-term customers drive high ADTO
items.quote: So ADTO growth for overall exchange, ADTO was on, at least for Q1. So, it was a slight dip for us on F&O. And on the cash side, it grew.

items.statement: RBI mandated brokers arrange own intraday margin from 1st July; 5paisa deployed INR 227 crore for exchange margin
items.quote: With effect from the 1st July, RBI said that bank can't do give any intraday facility to the broker, and hence, every broker has to arrange the money. We were lucky that we got the money on the right time, and hence, ultimately, we increase our margin.

items.statement: Repaid INR 150 crore loans to banks and CPs from rights issue proceeds
items.quote: Second, we had repayment of loan about INR 150 crore to different banks and the CPs.

items.statement: Investing in product and tech talent using rights issue proceeds
items.quote: We raised about INR 468 crores in the rights issue as capital in the month of April, which is strengthened the balance sheet and which we're going to use for obviously continued investment in the product and tech talent.

items.statement: Near-term focus on core platform; third-party distribution only in medium term if synergies exist
items.quote: In the very near future, no, because I think just to be our hands are full with what we are doing. We want to do a very good job at it. This is our core platform. And once that is done, then we can look at some of the other third-party distribution.

items.statement: Long-term growth target of 18%-20% annually, no formal yearly guidance given
items.quote: We don't kind of give an yearly guidance, but what we always guide is that we have been growing at 18%-20% since last 10-15 years and we should be able to maintain our growth rates in long-term growth rates around this level in future also.

items.statement: New plant capex of INR45 crores, commissioning planned for September 2026
items.quote: So, we are doing a capex of around INR45 crores in the new plant and typically our asset turnover has been 6x to 7x.

items.statement: New plant commissioning in September 2026, meaningful revenue contribution from Q4 FY27, target 80%-85% utilization by end of FY28
items.quote: So, I mean September we are kind of planning to commission the plant. So, any revenue contribution or meaningful revenue contribution one should expect only from Q4.

items.statement: Existing facilities operating at around 85% capacity utilization
items.quote: And secondly, our existing capacity we are working on an 85% around capacity utilization levels. So, we are quite optimally utilizing our capacity as of today.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR811 crores as of June 30, 2026, up ~10% year-on-year
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, our order book stands at INR811 crores providing strong revenue visibility.

items.statement: Volume growth of 5%-6% in Q1 FY27, impacted by high base effect and raw material price spike causing order postponements
items.quote: So, if we break out that volume and value growth, 5% to 6% is our volume growth and balance is large part of it is kind of derived by the price growth of aluminium and largely aluminium.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.9% in Q1 FY27 from improved operating leverage, favourable product mix, and cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 10.9% reflecting enhanced operational efficiency, while profit after tax grew by 37% to INR25 crores.

items.statement: Variable price contracts pass through input cost changes; fixed price contracts hedge by booking raw material at order time; ~20% of orders are fixed price
items.quote: Around 20%, roughly I am giving, I don't have the exact number but around 20% would be fixed price.

items.statement: Entered US market in Q1 FY27; US contributed ~15% of exports; distribution-led model via local distributors
items.quote: Breakup, I think US contributed around 15% of the total exports round about and the balance came from our traditional markets of Asia and Southeast Asia and Africa.

items.statement: Solar cables ~20% of revenue in Q1 FY27, expected to grow 25%-30% annually for next 3-4 years
items.quote: Our solar cable revenue has been around 20% in Q1 and on the full year basis also I think it should remain in the similar range.

items.statement: HTLS conductor and data center cables are futuristic investments; capex largely fungible with existing machinery; focus on product development and customer engagement
items.quote: We have started our product development process and approval process because these are the two critical things. On the capex side, we believe that most of the capex in these two areas is going to be fungible.

items.statement: Working capital turnover >4x; manage receivable days by negotiating trade terms and selecting favourable business; improve credit ratings to lower borrowing costs
items.quote: If you look at our past track record, we try to do around 4x plus our turnover, working capital turnover ratio is more than 4x compared to us, in our past track record if you look at it.

items.statement: Debt increased due to 25%-30% higher inventory value from rising raw material prices; debtor days stable on trailing six-month sales basis
items.quote: So, debt has gone up as compared to March and the major contributor for the debt to grow up is the higher value of the inventory -- the inventory carrying value has gone up because of the increasing raw material prices.

items.statement: Customer mix in Q1 FY27: government 16%, private 71%, exports 13%; railway signalling segment temporarily held back due to margin pressure and competition
items.quote: Customer-wise contribution in Q1 FY27 was around government sales 16%, private sales 71%, export 13%.

items.statement: Healthy competition in HV/EHV cable space as demand growth matches capacity expansion; new entrants like Adani and Birla focused on house wires, not power cables
items.quote: But fortunately, the demand scenario has picked up pace and is picking up pace with the expansion -- with the on-going expansion. And that is why whatever competition we are seeing in the market it's a healthy competition up till now.

items.statement: US market entry delayed by tariff and policy uncertainty; now licensed for HV/LV/MV cables; approval process is a key barrier to entry
items.quote: So, this quarter we finally entered into the US market. We started our first supply to the US market and it's a large, large market.

items.statement: Order booking slowed in April-May 2026 due to customer reluctance at elevated aluminium prices; only near-term orders being placed
items.quote: Sir, price is king. So, I mean nobody is willing to book material at such high prices for project executions in Q3. Nobody wants to do it.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on product development and customer engagement for new segments
items.quote: The only thing is that because of this business environment, we have held back for a while in this particular segment.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consumption was weak due to Adhik Maas (May 17–June 15) and cautious discretionary spending, with demand expected to improve in H2
items.quote: Consumption during the quarter 1 FY26-'27 was shaped by Adhik Maas that fell from May 17 till June 15, almost 1 full month inside our quarter. Adhik Maas, as you all know, is traditionally treated as inauspicious for weddings, griha praveshams and other major purchases that contributed to w eak consumption trends across our markets

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 12–15%
items.quote: Ma'am, I think like we already discussed, broadly, the revenue guidance for the full year will remain between 12 and 15 percentage, like we've discussed in the last interactions as well.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be better than FY26
items.quote: But on the EBITDA margins, you should be able to expect better than what we closed last year. I'm talking about the full year in perspective.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 gross margin target maintained at current level (~42%)
items.quote: We aim to maintain the same gross margins till the end of the year.

items.statement: FY27 SSSG target of 2–3% positive growth implied by 15% revenue guidance
items.quote: This broadly will classify in at least 2% to 3% of SSSG positive plus whatever additional revenue that comes forward.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 same-store sales degrowth of 7.5–7.8% driven by KLM Fashion Mall weakness and high base
items.quote: So our SSSG broadly was around 7.5 to 7.8 percentage. This was heavily driven by KLM's degrowth.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin declined ~1% due to same-store sales degrowth on fixed cost base; gross margin held near 42%
items.quote: EBITDA margins declined by about 1%, largely on account of the same-store sales degrowth given that the fixed cost base spread over softer like-to-like volumes. That said, I'm happy to report that gross margins held up well, remaining close to 42% despite the challenging environment.

items.statement: Gross margin lost 10–15 bps due to supply chain cost pressures (dying cost, fuel prices) but target maintained for full year
items.quote: Gross margin, as you see, I think ideally, we were expecting the gross margins to be a little bit higher. But with all of these things playing out, the gross margin hardly sustained. I think we've lost close to 10 to 15 basis points and broadly the gross margins remain.

items.statement: FY27 net retail space addition target ~100,000 sq ft; visibility for Q2 is 26,000–30,000 sq ft, Q3–Q4 target 40,000 sq ft with possible extra 10,000–15,000 sq ft in Q4
items.quote: we might add a little bit more than the 1,00,000 square feet before the financial year ends. At this point of time, the visibility that we have in quarter 2 is close to 26,000 to 30,000 square feet. We've already added 30,000 and this 30,000 will broadly bring it out to 58,000 to 60,000 square feet. And ideally, the target for Q3, Q4 is 40,000, but there are possible chances wherein in quarter 4,

items.statement: New state entry (Maharashtra – Pune, and Kerala) expected in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28
items.quote: Additionally, in terms of locations, in quarter 4 or early quarter 1 of next financial year, in that time is where our entry to the new state will be. We are looking at closing down on final location of one in Pune in Maharashtra. And we are also actively exploring opportunities in Kerala.

items.statement: KLM Fashion Mall: innerwear showing ~20% YoY growth; fashion jewellery just launched in phases; men's and kids' wear under pressure
items.quote: So with respect to innerwear, I think month-on-month, Y-o-Y, it is showing growth. We are expecting a 20% growth compared to last year in the innerwear category. With respect to jewellery, I think the jewellery that has been added is fashion jewellery, and it just started.

items.statement: Inventory per sq ft consistently declining due to cluster-based expansion improving replenishment efficiency; absolute inventory higher due to added space
items.quote: With this additional retail space, our overall inventory levels are naturally expected to be higher in absolute terms. However, I'd like to highlight that we continue to see a consistent reduction in inventory per square foot, which reflects the growing ef ficiencies of our cluster -based expansion

items.statement: Company remains debt-free
items.quote: The company continues to be debt-free. This reflects our continued focus on financial discipline and prudent capital management even as we invest in continued expansion.

items.statement: IPO warehouse funds unutilized; due diligence ongoing for 1–2 locations; deal expected to close by end of September 2026; full utilization target September quarter (Q2 FY27)
items.quote: We are closing one particular area where we wanted to put up the warehouse and discussing with them. Hopefully, we should be able to complete the deal by the end of September. And then that particular part of the amount for warehouse will be spent at that point of time. B. Rachamadugu: Apart from that, I think the entire utilization will be completed, the target being September quarter 2 of 2026

items.statement: Supply chain cost pressures: dyeing cost increased substantially; fuel prices rising due to war; rainfall deficit in core agri-dependent markets (AP, Telangana, Karnataka) may impact Q2–Q3 demand
items.quote: One more thing that I'm not able to comment very surely, but has a broader level impact is because of the war, the fuel prices rising, even with respect to the product wise also, the dying cost has increased substantially. So, therefore, the entire supply chain also has been something that has been impacting.

items.statement: Poor rainfall in core states and geopolitical factors (war, El Nino) may weaken consumption in Q2–Q3; impact difficult to quantify
items.quote: I personally believe that there will be some impact, but it's tricky to quantify how much exactly it will.

items.statement: Wedding days in Q2–Q4 FY27 are 5–10% higher YoY (2–3 extra days); Dasara shifted from Q2 to Q3 this year
items.period: Q2 FY27 / Q3 FY27 / Q4 FY27
items.quote: So broadly, Q2, Q3, Q4, if you take all of that put together, Y-o-Y, there are like 2, 3 days extra. If I have to put you in a percentage perspective, like about 5 to 10 percentage of additional wedding dates is what is there in quarter 2, quarter 3 and quarter 4.

items.statement: Employee cost lower in Q1 vs Q4 due to seasonal bonuses and temporary staff in peak quarters (Q3–Q4); no store closures in Q1
items.quote: Last quarter 4, we issued bonuses. In quarter 3 and quarter 4, we issue bonuses, which will spike the employee cost during that period. And secondly, during the peak seasons, Q3 and Q4, we employ substantial temporary staff for assistance.

items.statement: No plans to sell on marketplaces (Amazon, Myntra) due to 20–45% commissions and high return rates; 95–96% of sales are full-price offline
items.quote: We fundamentally don't want to get into the marketplace channels. We are not manufacturers of products where we have high gross margins. Marketplaces, such as the names that you have mentioned, have marketplace commission or marketplace fee that ranges anywhere between 20% and 45%.

items.statement: Management emphasizes evaluating business on full-year basis due to seasonal wedding/festive calendar; quarterly shifts (Adhik Maas, Dasara timing) distort quarter-to-quarter comparisons
items.quote: Given the inherently seasonal nature of the ethnic wear retail industry, companies like ours are best assessed on a yearly basis rather than purely on a quarter-to-quarter basis. As seasonal shifts are imminent and structural to how this business performs, our revenue and profitability are closely tied majorly around the festive and wedding calendar.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 maintained at INR500-600 crores, may change if large managed office deals materialize
items.quote: we hol d good on the guidance of between INR500 crores to INR600 crores, and that is the visibility that we have today. There might be some change if large managed offices come through the year, and we have to deploy some large capex for delivering those, but that we will know pretty much by the next quarter if any of that's going to hit basically by the end of this year

items.statement: Expects 20%+ year-on-year EBITDA and revenue growth for FY27 despite heavy H1 expansion
items.quote: we will definitely meet the guidance of 20% plus EBITDA growth and sort of earnings sorry, revenue and EBITDA growth of, you know, over 20%.

items.statement: Customization revenue run-rate expected at INR10-15 crores per quarter after amortization change
items.quote: typically, in the range of betwee n INR10 crores to INR15 crores in a quarter is what we kind of expect will be run rate when you look at this customization kind of revenue

items.statement: VAS revenue expected at 11-12% of total revenue, digital at 3-4%, combined ~16%
items.quote: I think we've historically been at 13% to 15% VAS revenues. We think that we'll hold basically at those levels consistently. So, 11% to 12% on VAS plus about 3% to 4% on digital, which is what stacks up to that sort of 16%.

items.statement: Operating 9.1M sq ft across 79 centers, 133.6K desks; contracted capacity 12M sq ft (~179K desks) including signed leases and LOIs of 2.9M sq ft
items.value: 9.1M sq ft operational, 12M sq ft contracted
items.quote: We operate 9.1 million square foot today, add signed leases and LOIs of another 2.9 million, and total contracted capacity is about 12 million square foot, about 179,000 desks.

items.statement: Expects to operate ~10.3M sq ft and ~155K desks by March 2027; FY28-FY29 supply in negotiation
items.quote: By March of 2027, we expect to be operating about 10.3 million square foot and around 155,000 desks. Beyond that, FY28 and FY29 supply is already in negotiation.

items.statement: Sold 12,700 desks in Q1 FY27, up 28% YoY; April was biggest sales month at 7,500 desks; 52% of sales to existing members
items.quote: We sold about 12,700 desks this quarter, which is up 28% year-over-year. April was our single biggest sales month with about 7,500 desks, and we did this without discounting, pricing multiples held steadily through the year. Worth repeating, 52% of what we sold went to members that are already with us, and that's not a one-quarter trend, that's been the base compounding.

items.statement: Members grew 30% YoY to 113K, outpacing 17% capacity growth; portfolio occupancy rose to 84.9% from 76.5% YoY
items.quote: Capacity grew 17% year-over-year, members grew 30%. Member growth ran at 1.7x the pace of capacity addition. Portfolio occupancy moved from 76.5% a year ago to 84.9% today.

items.statement: Rent per sq ft flat YoY, opex per sq ft up 5.6% vs revenue up 28%; portfolio break-even occupancy 56.6%
items.quote: Rent per square foot was flat over the year. Opex per square foot only rose 5.6%, while revenue grew 28%. That gap is our operating leverage. Portfolio break-even occupancy is just 56.6%, and even our newest growth centers are comfortably above that.

items.statement: Locked-in future revenue INR3,363 crores, up 60% YoY; locked-in rent obligations up only 30%; each rupee of new rent adds ~INR4.7 contracted revenue
items.quote: The best place to start is what's already contracted, locked-in revenue, future revenue of our members that our members have already signed up for stands at about INR3, 363 crores, which is up 60% from INR2,105 crores last year. Locked-in rent obligations only grew 30% in the same period. So contracted revenue is growing twice as fast as contracted cost. For every rupee of new rent that we committ

items.statement: Core workspace revenue INR603 crores (+30% YoY), VAS INR9.5 crores customization (down from INR47 crores), digital INR26 crores (+27% YoY, ~80% EBITDA margin)
items.quote: Core workspace grew 30% to INR603 crores, value-added services grew 10%, and digital grew 27% to INR26 crores. Digital is still under 4% of revenue, but those four products monetize the same square foot more than once and run at close to an 80% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: 77% revenue from enterprise members, 65% from global companies, 46% from North America; tech 28%, BFSI 17%; top 10 members only 22% of revenue
items.quote: On who drives the revenue, 77% came from enterprise members, 65% from global companies, and North America riding the GCC wave is 46% of the revenue on its own. No single sector dominates, technology leads at 28%, BFSI at 17%, and the rest is well spread. O ur top 10 members are just 22% of revenue combined, and there's no concentration risk here

items.statement: Free cash from operations INR141.9 crores, up 176% YoY; capex INR188 crores; FCFF negative INR46.1 crores due to H1 growth intensity
items.quote: Free cash from operations was INR141.9 crores, up 176%. We've invested INR188 crores of capex this quarter, nearly double last year. And even so, FCFF was negative INR46 crore, essentially flat with a year ago.

items.statement: Net debt INR31.6 crores, down 89% YoY from INR297 crores; cash INR371 crores; net debt/EBITDA 0.06x; cost of borrowing down to 8.5% from 10.4%; rating upgraded to A+ from A-
items.quote: Net debt is INR31.6 crores, down 89% from INR297 crores a year ago, against INR371 crores of cash on hand. Net debt to EBITDA is 0.06x, cost of borrowing is down from 10.4% to 8.5%, and our rating moved from an A- to an A+ over the year.

items.statement: Customization revenue accounting changed: large managed office customization now amortized over contract term instead of recognized upfront to smooth lumpiness
items.quote: But these large customizations which actually are specifically to one customer in managed office, what we are going to start doing is basically amortizing it over the complete term of the member's commitment itself. So, this will now from this year onwards actually smoothen out any type of lumpiness that we basically saw last year, and you'll have a more recurring base of customization revenue as

items.statement: Capex INR188 crores in Q1 FY27, nearly double YoY; H1 FY27 heavy opening stretch with 22,000 desk additions; FCFF negative INR46 crores but flat YoY despite doubled investment
items.quote: We've invested INR188 crores of capex this quarter, nearly double last year. And even so, FCFF was negative INR46 crore, essentially flat with a year ago. We doubled our investment in growth, and our own operations absorbed all of it.

items.statement: Cost of funds benefit of 40-50 bps expected but will not change in a hurry; borrowing mix at 11% vs industry 5-6%
items.quote: the cost of funds is the biggest opportunity on the margin where compared to our historical norms as well as compared to what we have seen in the industry as such, there can be 40, 50 basis points change, but it is not going to change in a hurry.

items.statement: Retail asset mix target 60% from current 52% to mirror consumption GDP share
items.quote: Today we are at a 52% retail mix. At our kind of an experience that we have seen, we were at about 60% or so and we always have thought that India's consumption component of the GDP is at about 60% and that's where we want to be as far as the retail mix is concerned

items.statement: Borrowing maturity profile shows INR 40,000-50,000 crores over next couple of years; replacing with retail TD saves 100-125 bps
items.quote: You'll see that INR40,000 crores or INR50,000 crores over the next couple of years you'll see that. And it does have a differential in rate. It's a little more than 7%, if you get a retail, it could be 6%-odd. So you can pick up 100 basis points, 125 basis points depending on the source of the time deposit.

items.statement: ECLGS 5.0 disbursement of close to INR 14,000 crores as of June 30, among highest for participating banks
items.quote: we have already as of 30th of June had a disbursement in that scheme of close to INR14,000 crores under the ECLGS scheme. And I think and I believe that's amongst the highest in terms of the participating banks

items.statement: Healthy credit demand seen in system; FCNR policy window and ECLGS 5.0 are good opportunities
items.quote: There is a very healthy credit demand that we are seeing in the system as we speak. We believe that the FCNR policy window that has been offered to the banking system is a great opportunity and we are focusing on that.

items.statement: Corporate/wholesale advances grew ~18% YoY; MSME business banking grew 22.3% YoY; retail disbursements strong across wheels, unsecured, mortgages
items.quote: we have seen, very good growth happen in our corporate and wholesale segment. We've seen that grow at about 18% and this is continuing from the growth that we had seen in the previous quarter as well, which was around those levels. We've also continued to see very good growth come in our MSME segment and out over there, we have seen a business banking which is the largest component of our MSME seg

items.statement: Branch productivity increased from INR 266 cr/branch (FY23) to INR 330 cr/branch currently; 40% branches <5 years vintage
items.quote: If you look at the per branch metrics, we are about INR 330 crores per branch currently. And if you go back to the FY'23 time period, we were INR 266 crores per branch. And if you go back even further, right, it's less than INR200 crores.

items.statement: ECL transition on April 1, 2027 expected to have some impact but nothing material; current provisioning adequate with floors at 1% unsecured and 5% secured for Stage 2
items.quote: Considering where we are today and looking 12 months down the line, we do believe that our reserving process and the reserving methodology is quite adequate. And for us to think about the stage 3 assets which is equivalent to the NPA today that you have, that coverage is quite adequate there.

items.statement: PCR at 66% headline; excluding agriculture book it is 70% vs 71% pre-merger; unsecured coverage in mid-70s+
items.quote: See, the overall coverage that you see now is 66%, right? I would draw your attention to go back to 2019. And the reason for that is in between there could be COVID, somewhere up, somewhere down in terms of coverage and subsequently there was a merger, somewhere up and then subsequently down in terms of various coverage.

items.statement: FCNR (B) mobilization documentation completed in June; expect significant market share in July-September like 2014-15 period
items.quote: you will see in the month of July, August, September, we have certain milestones. I'm sorry I can't sort of put a number to that in the public domain, but you will see a very handsome, or that's the endeavor to ensure that we are reasonably strong and significant market share in the market.

items.statement: Board and GNRC seized of MD/CEO reappointment matter; work in progress with announcements to follow
items.quote: the GNRC and Board is fully seized of the matter and that is work in progress and as they arrive at a conclusion, we will certainly make the necessary announcements in that regard.

items.statement: GenAI lighthouse programs going into production during the year; AI also used for security defence mechanisms
items.quote: We are on the cusp of harnessing some of the GenAI technologies on our processes and we do have a fair amount of lighthouse programs that will go into production during the course of the year.

items.statement: Cost of funds flat QoQ (+/- couple bps); down ~40 bps YoY
items.quote: Sequential quarter I think it's almost there flat a couple of basis points plus-minus, it's within the range. And over a period of a year, I think it's about call it 40, 50 basis points, 40 basis points or so year-to-year, Yes.

items.statement: Weekend reporting chosen to minimize regulatory transgression risk from market-hour disclosures
items.quote: There is a reason why most of us are all doing on Saturdays. It's not that we have a joy in coming to work on a Saturday, I can assure you that, or to spoil your weekend. There is a reason why because since the markets are closed and a fair amount of people will get exposed to this kind of information through the day, we just want to minimize some of the regulatory transgressions that may happen,

items.statement: Risks include weather disruptions (El Nino) and West Asia geopolitics; bank prepared to weather challenges
items.quote: Of course, there are risks in the horizon in terms of the weather-related disruptions like El Nino and also the geopolitical situation in West Asia. But I think the country has weathered these reasonably well. I think we continue to remain very sanguine.

items.statement: Customer base >100 million; focus on unit economics and quality acquisitions after fraud/mule account crackdown in FY24-26
items.quote: we are today little more than 100 million customers, and as we drive the unit economics, keep the cost in check and under control on efficiency so that we scale this. That's what is happening, the scaling is happening with unit economics slightly moving.

items.statement: Time deposit penetration opportunity: only 14% of customers have TDs; pursuing both CASA and TD growth
items.quote: time deposit continues to be a very big opportunity because only 14% of our customers have time deposits with us. So there is an enormous opportunity for a deeper penetration on that. And so it's not this or that, it's both.

items.statement: Profit growth should be at or above balance sheet growth over longer term; adjusted profit growth 9.8% vs balance sheet growth 13-14% in Q1
items.quote: We do think that in the longer term that the profit growth should be at or above the balance sheet growth. Yes, that's still in our plans and that's how we approach.

items.statement: CASA ratio target near pre-merger ~38%; currently ~34% with wholesale deposits rising from 17% to 20%
items.quote: the endeavor and our vision is to reach to somewhere near the pre-merger levels or just around the time of the merger, which was around 38.

items.statement: Investment phase largely done; now harnessing branch distribution and tech investments for efficiencies over next 2-3 years

items.quote: Private label sales for Q1 FY27 constitutes 20%, pharma being 10.7% and the non-pharma being 9.3% of our total revenue.

items.quote: Diagnostics revenue for the current qu arter grew to INR370.8 million compared to INR302.9 million in quarter 1 FY26. Diagnostics segment recorded an operating EBITDA of INR65.9 million compared to INR41.3 million in quarter 1

items.statement: Non-pharma private label supply disruptions in diaper range in Q1; expected to normalize by end of Q2
items.quote: For certain categories of our non-pharma products, especially the diaper ra nge, there were disruptions in terms of supply. It's now coming back on track. By the end of this current quarter, we should see the full impact coming back

items.quote: So there are as a strategy, we have been opening some large store formats because as a strategy, we would like to even test out that, which means that it is as good as 3 stores coming up as 1 store.

items.quote: Predominantly, it is the offering to the senior staff members who have been with the company for 3 years plus. So that's a retention strategy. And so that they also b ecome individual entrepreneurs

items.statement: Expansion plan: grow contiguously in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, then northwards and westwards
items.quote: So the plan is to actually grow contiguously in contiguous states. So we are there in Maharashtra right now in a significant number. And we have extended into both Ch hattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh. And on the southern side, we have actually gone

items.statement: Record order book of INR2,598 crores with book-to-bill ratio of 1.5x
items.quote: We recorded our highest ever order book at INR2,598 crores. That is a strong signal of demand and of confidence from our customers. Order intake for the period stood at INR551.9 crores with a he althy book -to-bill ratio of 1.5

items.statement: Order backlog increased to INR25,989 million, up INR1,832 million quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Our order backlog also remains strong at INR25,989 million, increasing by INR1,832 million quarter-on-quarter. This represents the highest order book level achieved so far and provides a good visibility for revenue execution in coming quarters.

items.statement: Book-to-bill ratio expected to remain at 1.5x for the year
items.quote: So, book-to-bill ratio will be at the same thing where we are today at 1.5x. So, we will be at that number for the year too.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.5%, up 147 bps year-on-year; four consecutive quarters of double-digit EBITDA margins
items.quote: Importantly, our EBITDA margin improved to 10.5%, representing an expansion of 147 basis points year-on-year. This margin improvement reflects the benefits of operating leverage, better revenue mix and disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Expand phase (FY27-FY29) targets EBITDA margins of 11% to 13%
items.quote: Because we are leveraging the same core stack into higher value sectors, margins step up roughly to 11% to 13%.

items.statement: Transform phase (FY30+) targets EBITDA margins of 13% to 18%
items.quote: This is the shift from being a service provider to owning product and intellectual property and that's what lifts margins to roughly 13% to 18%.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing logistics delays and cost increases but mitigated by inventory planning; Israeli order momentum continues
items.quote: What we are seeing even now today is there is -- there are some delays in the logistics in terms of shipments and we are also seeing some of the costs going up due to these West Asia crisis at this point of time. But we are already well planned in terms of our execution, so we have not seen any of those challenges in Q1 and we also just put a plan together to ensure that those things won't impact

items.statement: PCBA 48% of revenue (21% YoY growth), box build 21% (85% YoY growth), mechanical 10%, cables 1%
items.quote: PCBA continued to remain the largest contributor, accounting for 48% of Q1 FY27 revenue. The PCBA business maintained a high share and delivered 21% year-on-year growth. Box build was the second largest product category, contributing 21% of revenue but delivered strong year-on-year growth of 85%.

items.statement: Added two new logos in industrial and automotive segments; 70% order intake from existing customers, 30% from new customers added in last 4-6 quarters
items.quote: On customer diversification, we added two new logos during the quarter across the industrial and automotive segments. That matters because it broadens our base and reduces concentration, which is exactly the direction our strategy calls for.

items.statement: Order intake split: ~70% from existing customers, ~30% from new customers added in last 4-6 quarters
items.quote: So, if you look at that one, probably close to around 70% of that is -- where it is from our existing customers and the balance 30% is from the new customers whom we added in the last 4 equipment, at least from the last four to six quarters.

items.statement: Build-to-specifications lab expanded from 6,000 to 15,000 sq ft, more than doubling footprint
items.quote: We completed the expansion of our build-to-specifications lab from 6,000 square feet to 15,000 square feet, more than doubling that footprint and giving us headroom for the product platform development that underpins the transform phase mentioned earlier as part of our strategy.

items.statement: No significant additional capex needed for expansion phase; capex at 1.75x-2x of revenue, only regular annual capex
items.quote: The capex, I think, as you said, whatever we have today, closely around 1.75 x to 2x of the revenue. So, we don't need any such additional capex apart from a regular annual capex, which we'll be working out for our running the business.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 161 days from 145 days QoQ due to inventory and customer advances; inventory days 162, payable days 63, receivable days 77
items.quote: As a result, net working capital days stood at 161 days in Q1 FY27 compared to 145 days in Q4 FY26. This increase was primarily driven by the movement in inventory and customer advances as we continue to support a growing order book and the future execution requirements.

items.statement: Finance costs reduced 29% YoY due to lower working capital borrowings
items.quote: Importantly, finance costs reduced by 29% year-on-year owing to lower working capital borrowings.

items.statement: Key leadership hiring mostly completed, including Rama Alapati as Chief Strategy and Growth Officer
items.quote: Key leadership hiring has now been mostly completed, including the addition of Rama Alapati as the Chief Strategy and Growth Officer. This enhances our go-to-market capabilities and positions us to deepen customer engagement, expand into new opportunities and accelerate on our ambitions for growth.

items.statement: Gross margins slightly lower sequentially due to organizational investments budgeted for growth
items.quote: And in terms of the gross margins, what you said, even though it is slightly higher and it is lower than the last quarter because of some of the investments what we have made into our organization. So, the investments are where we have already budgeted and we already kept it because that is the one thing probably which is just driving up our gross margins slightly lower.

items.statement: West Asia crisis ongoing with logistics delays and cost increases; mitigated by strategic inventory build-up and alternative sourcing
items.quote: The quarter was marked by continued geopolitical uncertainties, evolving demand patterns and disruptions across global supply chains, including the ongoing developments in the Middle East that added further complexity to the operating environment.

items.statement: Positioned in high-reliability, high-value segments; not chasing commodity high-volume low-margin work
items.quote: We are deliberately not chasing commodity high-volume, low-margin work. We are positioning where complexity, reliability and engineering content command a premium.

items.statement: Completed Nadcap audit for cable harness assembly for Mysore unit, reinforcing aerospace credibility
items.quote: On quality and certifications, we completed the Nadcap audit for cable harness assembly for our Mysore unit. Nadcap is a demanding aerospace grade certification and it reinforces our credibility in the high reliability work that sits at the heart of our positioning.

items.statement: No acquisitions mentioned; organic expansion into robotics and AI data centres using existing capabilities
items.quote: I think for all this, we can use our existing capabilities. And probably, we need to have some of the skill -- experienced people in some of the areas in terms of application engineering. So that's where, I think, we are working out.

items.statement: B2S product revenue expected to contribute substantially in next 12-18 months, adding 250-300 bps to consolidated EBITDA margin
items.quote: So, we will be seeing it substantially a good revenues from them in the next one year to 18 months. That is what we will be seeing the revenues. And in terms of margins, as you said, the overall when you just look at the combined one, you will be getting additional 250 bps to 300 bps additional margins when we have a consolidated EBITDA margin due to the B2S opportunities.

items.statement: Order book reached all-time high of INR 761 crores with 77% from private sector clients
items.quote: Our total order book has reached an all-time high of INR 761 crores, providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Commenced execution of largest ever order worth INR 307 crores from Hindustan Zinc in Rajasthan
items.quote: During the quarter, we commenced execution of our largest ever order, valued at 307 crores, received from Hindustan Zinc in the state of Rajasthan.

items.statement: Secured extension of coal bed methane contract from Reliance Industries valued at over INR 166 crores
items.quote: We also secured an extension of our coal-backed methane contract from Reliance Industries Ltd., valued at over INR 166 crores, further strengthening our long-term revenue visibility.

items.statement: Expect significant growth in FY27 with H2 stronger than H1 due to favorable weather and higher project activity
items.quote: Historically, the second half has been our strongest period owing to favorable weather conditions and higher project activity and we expect this trend to continue in future as well.

items.statement: Reliance contract expected to contribute 35-40% of FY27 revenue (+/-5%)
items.quote: Yes, it should be on the same line, (+/-5%).

items.statement: Placed orders for additional drilling rigs and equipment to strengthen execution capabilities
items.quote: To support our growing business requirements, we have placed orders for additional drilling rigs and other equipment, further strengthening our execution capabilities.

items.statement: Jharkhand coal block Phase-I requires approximately INR 200 crores funded through internal accruals, bank debt and off-take agreements
items.quote: As we have been saying that in the 1st Phase, we shall be requiring around approximately INR 200 crores to start the project.

items.statement: Resource utilization exceeded 100% in Q1 FY27 due to outsourcing and hired rigs
items.quote: More than 100%. The reason is that we have outsourced some of our work to other contractors as well. So, the resource utilization has been more than 100%.

items.statement: Operate fleet of 43 advanced drilling rigs with purchase orders placed for additional rigs
items.quote: We currently operate a fleet of 43 advanced drilling rigs, supported by a team of experienced geoscientists and specialized geophysical and logging equipment.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 24.15% with EBITDA of INR 15 crores up 157% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at INR 15 crores, an increase of 157% year-on-year, while the EBITDA margin was around 24.15%.

items.statement: Margins expected to be maintained due to high entry barriers and CAPEX costs in exploration business
items.quote: The margin should be maintained because the entry barriers are quite high in this kind of a business. The CAPEX cost is very high, and it is difficult for a new entrant to come and showcase their capability.

items.statement: Strong pipeline across all domains including CBM, seismic, coal drilling, mineral exploration, aquifer mapping with visibility for 3-5 years
items.quote: It is looking great. In fact, all the domains are firing well right now. You talk about CBM, you talk about seismic, you talk about coal drilling, mineral exploration, coal, non-coal, aquifer mapping from Central Ground Water Board. So, all the things are doing well.

items.statement: 77% of order book from private sector clients supporting better cash flow and working capital efficiency
items.quote: Approximately 77% of our order book comprises private sector clients, reflecting the continued improvement in the quality of our order mix and supporting better cash flow and working capital efficiently.

items.statement: Empaneled by Oil India Limited for 2D and 3D seismic data acquisition services across onshore blocks
items.quote: During the quarter, we were also empaneled by Oil India Limited for providing 2D and 3D seismic data acquisition services across Oil India Limited's onshore blocks, opening up new opportunities in the seismic exploration segment.

items.statement: Jharkhand coal block has revenue sharing agreement with government at 24.25% of revenue
items.quote: In this block, we have a revenue-sharing agreement with the government, whereby we need to share 24.25% of the revenue with the government.

items.statement: Government auctioned around 200 coal blocks with focus on 500 mining blocks including critical and base metals
items.quote: The government has auctioned around 200 coal blocks, as far as I know. There will be more tranches coal block allocation through auctions. Apart from that the government will be focusing on approximately 500 mining blocks, including critical metals and base metals in the coming times.

items.statement: Oman JV mining services contract USD 125 million over 10 years running well with INR 3.5-4 crores quarterly profit share
items.quote: But yes, as you said, it's a USD125 million 10-year contract. It is running well right now. And in the last quarter itself, the total profit from this joint venture was around INR 3.5 crores to INR 4 crores.

items.statement: Oman operations unaffected by Middle East tensions; drilling rigs booked for 2-3 years
items.quote: So, it has not affected Oman as far as the Middle East tensions are concerned. So, we are in a pretty safe zone right now. And as far as contribution to right issue of Alara resources is concerned, the decision is quite strategic in nature for South West Pinnacle.

items.statement: Invested INR 2.8 crores (500,000 AUD) in Alara Resources rights issue Phase 1; may invest up to 1 million AUD in Phase 2
items.quote: INR 2.8 crores. So, we can invest anywhere up to 1 million in the 2nd Phase in this right issue.

items.statement: Received balance 75% consideration against warrant issues on preferential basis converted to equity shares strengthening capital base
items.quote: During the quarter, the balanced 75% consideration against warrant issues on preferential basis was also received, resulting in their conversion into equity shares and further strengthening our capital base.

items.statement: Net debt around INR 15 crores with debt-equity ratio less than 0.39; CRISIL upgraded credit rating from BBB to BBB+
items.quote: Currently, as far as the debt is concerned, I think Mr. Dinesh Agarwal would be able to answer your question. Dinesh Agarwal: Yes, it is around INR 15 crores at the moment with a very good debt-equity of less than 0.39

items.statement: Aim to become debt-free if no additional equipment CAPEX incurred given expected profits over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Currently, our debt equity is quite low, It's 0.39. The kind of profit we are expecting over the next two, three years, we shall be. And if we don't buy additional equipments, we don't incur any CAPEX, we are getting towards being a debt-free company.

items.statement: Coal production crossed 1 billion tonnes; expected 30-40% growth by 2030 driving exploration demand
items.quote: By 2030, we are expecting a further growth of 30% to 40% coming from only coal. Plus other minerals can also contribute to the growing demand.

items.statement: Underground coal gasification blocks awarded to two companies; tenders being floated for exploration
items.quote: These blocks for underground coal gasification were recently allotted to two companies in India. That was also done under the Ministry of Coal. Four blocks were awarded. The tenders are being floated by potential clients.

items.statement: Oil and gas ~25% of order book; remaining verticals each 15-30% including CBM, seismic, aquifer mapping
items.quote: Oil and gas would be around 25% and the rest of it. Basically, all the verticals, I would say, they are ranging from 15% to 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Business cyclical with Q1 subdued due to monsoon; Q2 depends on geographic rainfall impact
items.quote: Generally, Q1 is subdued Saket Ji b ecause the monsoon onset continues. And most of the clients want to complete the work by the end of the financial year. So, with the balance work that is done on the side, the client wants us to complete it by 31st March

items.statement: Working with two MDOs for exploration activities; evaluated acquisition targets in coal drilling but no decision yet
items.quote: We have already been approached by two MDOs and we have already started exploration for them. So, these mines were allotted by the Ministry to the bigger players and then they appointed MDOs. And now we are working with those MDOs for exploration activities in their respective areas.

items.statement: Yield improvement and cost efficiencies drove 20% operating revenue growth despite 7% AUM growth

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio range allows room for investments in areas like AI

items.statement: Fintech is integral partnership, direct share in line with industry at 27-28%
