This was achieved despite an additional impact of approximately INR15 crores relating to the ramp -up of our new asset in Frankfurt, which obviously includes preopening c osts also and commissioning of the new TajSATS kitchen in Noida outside of Delhi or Delhi-NCR.

items.statement: Major upgrades completed across marquee hotels including Taj Palace New Delhi, The President Mumbai, Taj West End Bengaluru and Taj Fort Aguada Goa with over 300 rooms renovated
items.quote: During the last financial year, we completed major upgrades across several marquee hotels, including Taj Palace New Delhi, the President in Mumbai, the Taj West End in Bengaluru and Taj Fort Aguada in Goa with over 300 rooms renovated.

items.statement: 20 hotels signed and 11 opened in Q1 FY27; portfolio at 382 operational and 265 pipeline hotels approaching 650 milestone
items.quote: We continue to deliver industry-leading portfolio expansion with 20 hotels signed and 11 hotels opened in Q1 of this year. Notably, 17 of the 20 signings were under Gateway, Ginger and Tree of Life brands across new and emerging markets.

items.statement: Leisure destinations Rajasthan and Goa saw ARRs up double digits with occupancy-led growth; business cities grew at healthy low-to-mid teens
items.quote: If I look at the Goa numbers, ARRs are up double digit comfortably and also in some properties in Rajasthan as well. And this time, there's also been a lot of occupancy-led growth. If you see the overall occupancy, they are up 6% on the base, which you saw the stand-alone numbers, which is representative of the domestic market for us.

items.statement: Growth brands Ginger, Qmin, ama and Tree of Life delivering robust performance; Ginger revenue INR183 crore with 20% growth and 39% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Consolidated revenue of Ginger s tood at INR 183 crores, delivering 20% growth year-on-year with an EBITDA margin of 39%. Qmin has grown to 100-plus outlets across multiple formats. Ama Stays & Trails has reached a portfolio of 380 -plus bungalows with 196 in operation and Tree of Life is now at 40 -plus resorts portfolio with 23 in operation.

items.statement: Management fee income grew 26% to INR168 crore; confident of sustaining high teens CAGR supported by strong pipeline
items.quote: During the quarter, management fee income grew by 26% to INR 168 crores from INR 133 crores in the corresponding period last year. This performance despite temporary headwinds, reinforces the resilience of our asset -light business model.

items.statement: Gross cash reserves over INR4,400 crore providing flexibility for brand and revenue-enhancing investments
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to be healthy with gross cash reser ves of over INR4,400 crores. This provides us with the flexibility to continue investing in brand and revenue -enhancing initiatives.

items.statement: Taj Bandstand project excavations 95% complete; targeting 450 keys and INR1,000 crore revenue upon commissioning in 2030-31
items.quote: 2030, 2031, once commissioned, it should -- unless there is some war going on or something like this circumstances, which we cannot dream of, it should start immediately w ith INR1,000 crores in revenue, 450 keys is the right number to assume.

items.statement: Standalone occupancy up 6% to 82% in Q1 FY27; domestic RevPAR grew 14% YoY
items.quote: If I look at the city-wise data, Bombay is up 6% to 15% occupancies, Delhi is also up 2% to 12%. So it's not that only leisure destination occupancies are up. Across the board, we have seen a pickup

items.statement: Frankfurt asset pre-opening costs impacting current quarter; expected to swing from negative to positive contribution from September
items.quote: I think as we commented earlier, Shaleen, the Frankfurt will swing from negative to positive. And then obviously, that's a contribution to margin that will start happening. And right now, as you know, the numbers already reflect the costs, which we talked about.

items.statement: International segment impacted by West Asia crisis affecting Dubai, Maldives, Sri Lanka; London and New York had property-specific disruptions now resolved
items.quote: It also has an impact in our international business in Maldives because a lot of traffic in Maldives, Sri Lanka, including in London and Cape Town is routed throug h Emirates as an airline. And if people are psychologically afraid of going to that region, they will not connect from there.

items.statement: Employee cost increase only 0.6% YoY due to labor code benefit reversal; normal payroll increases typically 7-8%
items.quote: There was some reversal we got from labor code benefit, which is there in this quarter as a result of which we had a lower cost increase. Effectively, the normal payro ll increases are typically 7% to 8%, and that is what we have.

items.statement: International hotels in Dubai, Maldives, Sri Lanka impacted by West Asia crisis and routing through Emirates; foreign tourist arrivals down but domestic demand compensating
items.quote: The one which is still under a lot of pressure is the leisure part, which is on the Palm. The Taj Exotica on the Palm is not even at 50% of the revenue it used to have. And -- so hopefully, they w ill also recover, but there is a direct correlation between Dubai and the West Asia crisis.

items.statement: 83 skill centers across 20 states; trained over 55,000 youth since 2020; on track to skill 100,000+ by 2030
items.quote: IHCL currently partners in operating 83 skill centers across 20 states in India. Since 2020, we have trained over 55,000 youth and are well on track to reach our goal of skilling 100,000- plus youth by 2030.

items.statement: ESG targets on track: 41% energy from renewable sources, 350+ EV charging stations at 170 locations, 88 hotels with bottling plants, 54% water recycling in Q1
items.quote: IHCL now uses 41% energy from renewable sources and has installed over 350 EV charging stations across 170 locations in India. Continuing our journey of eliminating single-use plastic, IHCL has installed bottling plants at 88 hotels and achieved 54% recycling of water used in the first quarter of this year.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR5,270 crores end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: At the end of Q1, the total order book stood at INR5,270 crores, providing healthy revenue visibility across both our international and domestic business.

items.statement: International order book at INR2,891 crores
items.quote: While international EBITDA margins improved materially to 15%, the international order book stood at INR2,891 crores, providing strong revenue visibility over the medium term.

items.statement: Domestic product order book at INR459 crores
items.quote: Order intake remained healthy with the domestic product division order book at INR459 crores at the end of the quarter, providing healthy revenue visibility.

items.statement: Domestic project order book at INR1,921 crores including INR530 crores O&M
items.quote: The domestic project order book stood at INR1,921 crores with about INR530 crores of O&M business.

items.statement: Product division order book INR1,029 crores, project division INR4,241 crores
items.quote: I think we have given product order of -- the product business order is INR1,029 crores, and the project order is INR4,241 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue INR501 crores, up 32% YoY
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue from operations for the quarter under review stood at INR501 crores, a substantial increase of 32% year-on-year.

items.statement: International revenue INR386 crores vs INR197 crores YoY
items.quote: International revenues for the quarter increased substantially to INR386 crores compared to INR197 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Domestic product revenue INR72 crores vs INR65 crores YoY
items.quote: Domestic product division revenue stood at INR72 crores compared to INR65 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Domestic project revenue INR43 crores, remained subdued
items.quote: The domestic project division remained subdued during the quarter with revenues for the quarter at INR43 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 15.04%, PAT margin 11.79%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR75 crores, while EBITDA margins were at 15.04%. PAT stood at INR59 crores with PAT margins at 11.79%.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 12.21%, PAT margin 5.41%
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, revenue for the quarter stood at INR115 crores, down by 37% year-on-year, while EBITDA stood at INR14 crores, EBITDA margins were 12.21%.

items.statement: Consolidated margin target range 15-20%, expect improvement from current 15%
items.quote: Our consolidated margin has hit 15%, and our standard range is between 15% and 20%, so we should see it improving only further.

items.statement: All businesses aim to operate between 15-20% EBITDA margin, expect roughly 16-17% for the year
items.quote: All our businesses, our aim is to operate between 15% and 20%, and this is something which we have seen is consistent with the performance. And I think there is minor fluctuations from quarter-to-quarter, division to division. But overall, in the year, we find that it is in this range, roughly around 17%, I think we'll get 16%, 17%.

items.statement: Domestic water sector improvement expected in second half of FY27
items.quote: We expect an improvement in the domestic water sector during the second half of the year as the sector issues are resolved.

items.statement: MP government debarment resolution target within next 1 year
items.quote: Our target is within, say, the next 1 year.

items.statement: Substantial JJM receivables inflow expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Yes. We believe there will be a substantial inflow this quarter.

items.statement: South African business 3-4 year contracts, execution to pick up further
items.quote: The South African business, as we have earlier mentioned, is 3- to 4-year contracts. So they are supposed to pick up. This is -- the business has started contributing to our revenues, as you can see by the drastic increase in international business. And this will further increase during this period.

items.statement: JJM receivables roughly INR300-350 crores pending, majority expected in Q2
items.quote: Roughly, I think, INR300 crores to INR350 crores, and we should get a majority of that.

items.statement: No JJM receivables received in Q1, funds lying in treasury accounts
items.quote: No, it's all linked to -- there is no -- it's not a thing that there is -- they will disburse slowly, the funds. It's all procedural in nature. So, if it is disbursed, most of it will get disbursed. It's all lying as payable in the accounts of the treasury, treasury accounts.

items.statement: Intention to reduce minority shareholding in subsidiaries over 2-3 years, PCI Africa buyout in 3 years
items.quote: Our intention is to reduce the minority shareholding on all our subsidiaries over the, say, medium 2 to 3 years' time. Say, for example, in this new acquisition, PCI, we have an understanding that in 3 years, we will buy out the other shareholders.

items.statement: MP government issued debarment notice for slow project progress, cannot bid new projects until old ones finished
items.quote: They gave us a debarment basically saying that you cannot bid for new projects until you finish the old projects. And we are addressing those concerns, and hopefully, we can resolve the issue soon.

items.statement: JJM projects slow due to fund diversion, but sector remains priority and funds will be released
items.quote: Yes. This is a good question, and I completely believe that the sector remains a priority and the funds will be released and future, there will be good traction in opportunity.

items.statement: Raw material mainly steel, short spike due to Middle East export issues but balanced out in medium-long term contracts
items.quote: Most of our raw material is steel. So, we have metals and steel. There was a short spike when a lot of materials were not being exported from the Middle East. But I think it is balanced out in our contract, which are pretty medium term, long term in nature. So, it's not much of an impact.

items.statement: Project work has price variation contracts covering cost escalations
items.quote: Yes. Most of our project work has got price variation contracts, so therefore, that takes care of it, which are longer term. And otherwise, not much of a concern on margins.

items.statement: O&M margins higher than normal EPC contract margins
items.quote: It is higher than normal margins on EPC contract. And we'll be able to give you a better picture when most of the projects start O&M, which is next year.

items.statement: Domestic project revenues drastically fallen due to sector issues and fund release delays
items.quote: Only due to the project invoicing, which is very drastically lower because the sector is still facing problems, our funds are not yet released. So I think these are sector issues, and all people in this sector are facing it.

items.statement: Rutschi Switzerland tax litigation ongoing, France portion favorable
items.quote: In France, we got a favorable reply. So that is good for us, and we are claiming the money back. And in Switzerland, it has not reached the stage yet. It will take time.

items.statement: Full-year AUM growth guidance of 18% maintained unless revised after Q2
items.quote: Our earlier guidance of 18% will hold good unless after second quarter, we revise it.

items.statement: Q2 AUM growth expected above 15%
items.quote: But we are confident that we'll be able to grow more than 15% at least for next quarter.

items.statement: Medium-term NIM target around 8.5% as new vehicle mix increases
items.quote: I believe the -- as new vehicle portfolio keep increasing within the hours run, we will be able to manage the NIM at around 8.5% in the medium term.

items.statement: Near-term NIM expected to hold at current levels for next two quarters
items.quote: See, immediate 2 quarters, I think the current NIM will hold good because we are utilizing the capital.

items.statement: Operational NIM guided at 8.5% excluding surplus liquidity benefit
items.quote: The operational NIM will hold at around 8.5%, and we continue to guide that.

items.statement: CV sales grew ~20% YoY in Q1 FY27 supporting disbursement growth
items.quote: The CV sales have gone up by nearly 20%, both M&HCV and LCV put together.

items.statement: Construction equipment sales turned positive after four quarters of negative growth
items.quote: Construction equipment recorded a growth of 8.8% with 25,176 units being sold against 23.147 units and showing a growth after negative growth in the last financial year.

items.statement: New vehicle disbursement share at ~16% of total disbursements, targeting 20-25% in medium term
items.quote: Right now, on the disbursement basis, it is around 16% of the disbursement is new vehicle. And increasingly, it will go up next 2 to 3 years as we reach out to more number of our earlier customers.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio expected to double to ~5% of book in 3 years from 2.5% currently
items.quote: We expect the portfolio to grow double in the next 3 years from around 2.5% of the overall book to around 5% because we feel that there's a very big opportunity for us to grow in the gold.

items.statement: MSME book targeted to grow from ~15% to ~20% of portfolio
items.quote: So from around 15% of the portfolio, the MSME will become around 20% of the book.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 at 4.64%, Net Stage 3 at 2.33% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On asset quality, gross Stage 3 in Q1 FY '27 stood at 4.64% and net Stage 3 at 2.33% as against 4.53% gross and 2.57% net in Q1 FY '26 and was 4.58% gross and 2.33% net in Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Credit cost at 1.66% of total assets in Q1 FY27, guidance maintained around 2%
items.quote: Our credit cost to total asset for Q1 FY '27 stood at 1.66% as against 1.64% for Q1 FY '26 and 1.68% for Q4 F Y '26

items.statement: MSME asset quality now comfortable after cautious stance last year
items.quote: MSME, we have been cautious in the last 1 year. We are now pretty confident about the MSME quality -- asset quality.

items.statement: Plan to add ~150 branches in FY27
items.quote: Tentatively around 150 branches.

items.statement: Excess liquidity of ~INR17,000-18,000 crores to be deployed for growth over 1-1.5 months
items.quote: The balance, what we have surplus of that will definitely come down because of higher disbursement.

items.statement: Overall liabilities reduced from INR2,50,690 crores to INR2,32,639 crores due to capital infusion
items.quote: On the liability side, this quarter, we didn't borrow much and overall liabilities have come down from INR2,50,690 crores as of March to INR2,32,639 crores because of use of capital in the current quarter, which was infused in April 2026.

items.statement: Cost of liabilities reduced 3 bps to 8.56%, incremental borrowing cost at 7.77%
items.quote: The cost of liability has also come down from 8.59% to 8.56%, 3 basis point reduction. The incremental cost is at 7.77%.

items.statement: No further liability repayment planned; fresh borrowing to resume end of quarter
items.quote: We don't look at any utilization towards liability repayment. In fact, we'll be looking at mobilization towards the end of the quarter of fund mobilization also.

items.statement: Lower borrowing costs passed to new vehicle customers, protecting overall margins
items.quote: Profitability, since we are passing on the reduced cost of borrowing to the customer, overall margins will not come down.

items.statement: New vehicle disbursement share increased from 10% to ~16-17%, targeting 30%+ of book in medium term
items.quote: from 10% our ne w vehicle volume, we have increased to around 16%, 17% now. And it will keep increasing to around 20% to 25% over the period. So definitely, new vehicle book will be around 30% of our book, 30% plus in our book maybe in the medium term

items.statement: AUM grew 15.26% YoY and 3.81% QoQ to INR3,13,798.39 crores
items.quote: Our assets under management as on 30th June 2026 registered a growth of 15.26% over Q1 FY '26 and of 3.81% se quentially. Our assets under management stood at INR3,13,798.39 crores as against INR2,72,249.01 crores a year ago and INR3,02,273.75 crores in Q4 FY

items.statement: Disbursements grew 19.51% YoY to INR49,974.49 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We registered a disbursement growth of 19.51% Y-o-Y. Our disbursement in Q1 FY '27 this year aggregated to INR49,974.49 crores versus INR41,816.75 crores in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Net interest income grew 33.67% YoY to INR8,055.70 crores
items.quote: Our net interest income in Q1 FY '27 registered a growth of 33.67% Y-o-Y. We earned a net interest income of INR8,055.70 crores in Q1 FY '27 this year as compared to INR6,026.43 crores in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: PAT grew 59.79% YoY to INR3,444.56 crores
items.quote: Our profit after tax grew by 59.79% and stands at INR3,444.56 crores in '27 as against INR2,155.7 crores in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 25.48% from 29.29% YoY
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio was 25.48% in Q1 FY '27 as against 29.29% recorded in FY '26.

items.statement: Monsoon deficit and El Nino impact on rural income remain key uncertainty for H2
items.quote: We would like to wait for another quarter because the net impact of the deficit in monsoon is a little less known.

items.statement: Management expects to meet or beat FY26 revenue growth but declines to give specific percentage guidance due to global headwinds and delayed project starts
items.quote: we will be at par or better than what we did last year from the growth perspective

items.statement: Management refuses to provide multi-year guidance citing geopolitical uncertainty and AI disruption
items.quote: nobody can give that guidance at this point because of the changes that are happening around the world

items.statement: Company has order book visibility for nine months providing predictable revenue
items.quote: We have order books for nine months. So, there is a predictable revenue for the next nine months.

items.statement: Demand exists with strong pipeline but customers are delaying project starts and contract signings due to cash flow concerns
items.quote: people are signing contracts and are delaying the start because the companies themselves are worried about their cashflow

items.statement: AI-led inquiries increasing with AI component now in every project unlike before
items.quote: A lot of AI-led inquiries are coming in. Yes, some of them are smaller, AI-related projects, pure AI-related projects are small, but whatever we are doing from a translation perspective, yes, there is a component of AI in every project that we are doing now, unlike before.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 11.1% with absolute EBITDA of INR 35 crores
items.quote: We have achieved INR 316 crores, which is about close to 7% year-on-year growth with an EBITDA of 11.1%, the EBITDA absolute number being INR 35 crores

items.statement: Q1 FY27 PAT margin at 7.1% with absolute PAT of INR 22.3 crores
items.quote: and a PAT margin of 7.1% and the PAT absolute number being INR 22.3 crores.

items.statement: Launched Phoenix.ai accelerator for legacy modernization at 80% faster and half the cost, and Structi.ai platform for enterprise intelligence
items.quote: Phoenix.ai is a product or an accelerator that we have launched which helps modernize enterprise legacy systems at almost 80% faster at half the cost

items.statement: Internal KAI platform delivering 30% efficiency gains in testing, business development and business analysis
items.quote: we have seen 30%, you know, efficiencies coming in in certain areas. Not all of them, but, you know, certain examples are like, you know, testing-related ones, you know, the business development side, also the BA side of it, analysis side of it.

items.statement: Won 5 significant client deals including Fortune India 500 conglomerate, UAE enterprise group, Middle East energy infrastructure company, global industrial services enterprise, and global pest management leader
items.quote: So, we have had some significant wins. So, I will just go over them one by one. 1. So, the first one is a Fortune India 500 conglomerate.

items.statement: Completed Oil India Optima digital oilfields deployment across 46 sites and 80+ wells in under 6 months
items.quote: that project has been successfully completed in less than six months. This is done in the Northeast in very difficult terrain across 46 sites of claims as they call them, covering about 80-odd wells.

items.statement: Acquired Snowflake Select Tier partnership strengthening data and AI capabilities
items.quote: we have acquired the select tier partnership with Snowflake. So, this is our emphasis on the data side. So, we just strengthened our partnership and moved up to the select tier partner during this quarter.

items.statement: Kumori acquisition contributed ~INR 4 crores revenue this quarter; acquired primarily for ServiceNow capability and certifications not revenue
items.quote: Just to ask a question on the revenue for Kumori, the last quarter, this quarter's revenue or the last quarter's revenue was about 4 crores. It's not much. That's the reason why I said we acquired that company more for capability and not for revenue.

items.statement: Second FCCB round delayed due to global headwinds and poor IT sector sentiment; will happen eventually
items.quote: The second round is delayed because of the global headwinds that we are facing, you know, you understand all the global headwinds that are going on, and also today, you know, IT industry is not, or IT companies are not seeing a good limelight.

items.statement: DSO at 100+ days due to Fortune 100 clients with 90-day payment terms and government clients with long clearance cycles; receivables growing proportionally with revenue
items.quote: if you look at our DSO days, we are at 100 plus days where we are. In addition to that, we also have customers in India, that is the government customers, the LICs, the HRMs of the world, where the lead cycle of getting invoices cleared is long.

items.statement: Minimal write-offs of a few crores over a year; receivables are collectible but slow
items.quote: we have not written off too much. We have written off probably a few crores, but we are talking about a handful of crores over a period of one year or so.

items.statement: Revenue grew ~7% YoY to INR 316 crores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We have achieved INR 316 crores, which is about close to 7% year-on-year growth

items.statement: EPS for Q1 FY27 is 42 paise
items.quote: The EPS for this quarter is 42 paise up.

items.statement: Global headwinds including war restart causing customer cash flow concerns and delayed project starts
items.quote: Unfortunately, right now, we thought that the war is going to end and it has restarted. So, a lot of customers for us, we have what we call delayed starts.

items.statement: AI disruption and rapid technology changes pose challenges but also opportunities for cutting-edge positioning
items.quote: AI is changing how we do business. It is like every quarter, there is a change. We have to transform ourselves and be current.

items.statement: JV with Action Energy targets 5% of billion-dollar digital oilfield market in 3 years and expansion across GCC starting with Kuwait
items.quote: the CEO of Action Energy has already stated that our target is to achieve 5% of the billion market, right, that is out there in this space, especially that transformation of the oil field and the digital oil field platform.

items.statement: Focus on AI-led modernization, partnership-led growth (ServiceNow, Microsoft, Snowflake), and expanding existing customer relationships with new capabilities
items.quote: We are also looking at enterprise modernization that is happening. Earlier, it used to be a digital transformation of the enterprises. What we are seeing now is beyond that. Right now, we are seeing AI-led modernization happening.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth targets: 10% for plywood, 25-30% for MDF
items.quote: We are confident to achieve the target of 10% volume growth in plywood and 25% to 30% volume growth in MDF segment for the full year and remain committed to delivering consistent profitable growth while creating a long-term value for all stakeholders.

items.statement: Plywood EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 10%+
items.quote: I think we still are very confident on the 10% margin guidance that we've given.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin sustainable at 16-17%, may rise 1% after new line
items.quote: So see, as per the capacity right now we have, the EBITDA margin will be around the 16% to 17% on a sustainable basis. Once the other line will come up, where we are doing around 70% extra capacity we are adding, so there will get some operating leverage on that time, the EBITDA margin may increase by 1% further.

items.statement: Peak net debt FY27 end: INR 710-730 cr, debt-equity 0.75x; target below 0.7x in six months
items.quote: Yes, so debt I think we've given a very clear guidance that in spite of all the capex that we've taken, at the end of this fiscal year which is 31st March '27, we will hit peak debt around in absolute value anything between 710 to 725, 730 something like that. And if you talk about debt equity that day we'll be at 0.75x.

items.statement: Hardware JV losses to break even by mid next year
items.quote: I think hardware business I mentioned it earlier, I think somewhere around next year mid is when we'll, you know, the losses will become zero and going forward from there I think it'll be positive.

items.statement: Furniture JV revenue target FY27: INR 120-150 cr
items.quote: I think we'll share that with you. I think should be around 120 crores to 150 crores, that range.

items.statement: FY27 capex ~INR 500 cr: GIL INR 47 cr, GSPL INR 100 cr, GSPPL INR 300 cr
items.quote: So for the current financial year, I think in the parent standalone GIL we would have about 47 crores of total capex including loss funding for SAMET. In GSPL we would have at around 100 crores and in GSPPL we would have around 300 crores of capex. So approximately 500 crores of total capex for this financial year.

items.statement: MDF flooring line commercial production started 20 July 2026; peak revenue potential INR 75-80 cr
items.quote: The potential peak revenue from this would be at about 75 crores, 80 crores, I think. Somewhere between 75 crores and 80 crores is a potential peak revenue.

items.statement: Vadodara MDF and Odisha plywood projects on track for committed timelines
items.quote: Our expansion projects, including the new MDF facility at Vadodara and the new greenfield plywood manufacturing facility in Orissa are progressing as planned and remain on track for commissioning within the committed timelines.

items.statement: Plywood target utilization 98-100%; MDF target 80-82% for FY27
items.quote: I think in plywood honestly, we've even gone up to 98, 99, or 100. So obviously the target will be to, you know, max out our, you know, available capacity. And in MDF I don't think it's practical to go above 80 %, 82%.

items.statement: Double-digit volume growth in both segments in Q1 FY27; plywood +13.8% YoY, MDF +24.7% YoY
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, we delivered double -digit volume growth in both segments, in line with our guidance.

items.statement: Plywood demand strong; lost sales in Q1 due to election-related labour disruption and lower outsourcing
items.quote: So, you know, honestly these two things work, the number could have been even better. So to be very honest, I think we've lost sales in Q1.

items.statement: Consolidated core EBITDA INR 78.3 cr, margin 10.8% (+50 bps YoY)
items.quote: Our consolidated core EBITDA was INR78.3 crores, with a core EBITDA margin of 10.8%, representing an expansion of 50 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Effective price hikes: MDF 7-9%, Plywood 3-5% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Consequently, the effective price increase currently stands at approximately 7% to 9% in the MDF business and 3% to 5% in the Plywood business.

items.statement: Timber prices stable with seasonal monsoon uptick; chemical prices rising again after June stabilization
items.quote: I think it's going to be quite stable and, you know, currently also there's not a big change. I think whatever change has happened is because of the seasonality.

items.statement: Chemical prices seeing new highs daily due to crude rise; availability not a concern
items.quote: To be very honest, April, May, June we had kind of started stabilizing in June and again this month things are going crazy. So yes, you are absolutely right, crude's going up and chemicals also seeing a new high every day. But availability challenge is not there.

items.statement: ContiRoll Tech implementation in plywood: 2 of 4 factories done, rest in H1 FY27; P&L gains from Q4 FY27
items.quote: As of now four factories in India, two factories process fully implemented, two factories during H1 of this year the implementation will happen. Major implementation planned in this month and the next and the next. And quarter four onwards you should start seeing some gain on the P&L because of that as well.

items.statement: MDF volume growth seen pan-India across South, East, West, North
items.quote: I think we are trying to focus pretty much pan -India. So, we've seen this growth across India, whether it is South, East, West, North. I think almost every area we've done decently well and we've grown across.

items.statement: Plywood gaining share from unorganized players; lost 2 years of hyper-growth planning vs Century
items.quote: I think this is, you know, whatever green shoots we are seeing as a category post-COVID, I think definitely we are eating the share of the unorganized, that's why we are seeing these green shoots.

items.statement: Iron foundry export project for US customer ramping up, expected to add INR2,000 million per year revenue, revenue recognition from next quarter
items.quote: We are now ramping up one big program for our American customers. So this will give us around INR2,000 million per year of new turnover that will fulfill our capacities in the country.

items.statement: H1 CY26 capex INR2.1 billion vs INR3.8 billion full year CY25; H2 CY26 capex expected significantly higher, focused on India growth projects including machine casting, gears, composites, stampings, forgings
items.quote: The capex during H1 C26 was INR2.1 billion as compared to INR3.8 billion in full year CY25. The growth capex is mainly concentrated in India. The capex in H2 C26 is expected to be significantly higher than in the first half of the year.

items.statement: Expanding capacity across verticals: iron foundry new line, gears plants in Rajkot and Chakan, stamping robotic line in Kanhe by mid next year, forging presses in Chakan and Bengaluru, evaluating brownfield and greenfield projects
items.quote: We are expanding our iron foundry business where we have now with the new project that Vikas mentioned in the introduction, we are now ramping up one big program for our American customers. So this will give us around INR2,000 million per year of new turnover that will fulfill our capacities in the country. So we need to expand our foundry, and we will build a new line, and we are launching that n

items.statement: Greenfield expansions planned in two verticals driven by customer location requests, also prioritizing four-wheeler aluminum diversification (currently INR500-750 million), EV composites and gears, and iron casting exports
items.quote: We are prioritizing our diversification into the four -wheeler aluminum business. That is a very important aspect that we are looking at for rebalancing the aluminum portfolio. We had comments upon on the balancing of the aluminum portfolio from the earlier participants. But we are doing that rebalancing and trying to move into four-wheelers. We have a very small business in four -wheelers and alu

items.statement: Cost inflation from West Asia conflict impacting energy, consumables and raw materials; aluminum prices up significantly but recognition delayed to next quarter; steel prices stable; countervailing measures to show in next two quarters
items.quote: Margins in the quarter have been affected by price inflation generated by the conflict in West Asia affecting mainly energy, consumables and als o part of raw materials. We are taking countervailing measures against these increases, which will show up in the next two quarters

items.statement: Aluminum vertical restructuring: exited loss-making products, reducing two-wheeler exposure by ~23-25% of India portfolio; focusing on four-wheeler aluminum diversification
items.quote: One, the restructuring of our business portfolio at our aluminum vertical, wherein we have let go of some loss-making products. So that we are below market growth rate as far as two -wheelers is concerned. Exports ha s been a dampener for the second successive quarter

items.statement: Key OEM performance: Mahindra, Maruti, Bajaj doing well; Hyundai negative growth (5-6% of business); Mexico revenues down 20% due to GKN contract renegotiation and insourcing
items.quote: in Mexico, I think there has been a drop of about 20% i n revenues in this quarter. So if you add that on to the market impact in Europe is what you are seeing in this quarter in Europe in revenue terms

items.statement: Metalcastello performing well with ~EUR13 million quarterly turnover and ~20% EBITDA margin, double-digit growth YoY
items.quote: In Metalcastello, we did -- in the quarter, we did almost EUR13 million turnover. That's the size of Metalcastello in the quarter. And the EBITDA margin was around 20%.

items.statement: Chinese OEMs gaining 10-12% market share in Europe registrations, currently importing from China; CIE engaging with Chinese OEMs for future localized production supply
items.quote: And if I'm not wrong, the market share for Chinese OEMs in Europe on the registration side, and here, we are talking registration, not producti on is roughly in the range of 10% or perhaps even higher than 10%, but 10% to 12%, somewhere around that number

items.statement: Europe sales INR8.9 billion up 7% YoY but down 3.7% QoQ; euro terms -6% with +13% FX translation benefit; Mexico now part of Europe segment
items.quote: Sales of INR8.9 billion in in Q2 C26 were 7% higher year-on-year versus Q2 C25, but lower sequentially by 3.7% versus Q1 C26. The sales growth in euro terms was minus 6% as there was an exchange rate translation impact of plus 13%.

items.statement: Consolidated net financial debt negative INR14.2 billion (net cash) at end H1 CY26; healthy liquidity for organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: The consolidated net financial debt at the end of H1 C26 was negative INR14.2 billion, which means we have healthy liquid cash available, and we are actively evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities.

items.statement: No capex limitation due to net cash position; will invest in profitable projects; inorganic growth active but Indian valuations too high for positive business cases
items.quote: There is no capex limitation as far as the business is profitable, we will go for it and that's the only limitation that we have. I mean, because we are in a net cash position, I mean we are free of debt. So the situation for us is very good to continue growing.

items.statement: Inorganic growth active but not executing due to high Indian market valuations; will pursue if proper business case found
items.quote: We continue being active and if we find some company with the proper business case, we will go for it also. So that's what we can explain about our strategy.

items.statement: Europe market weak, expected -2-3% this year and similar next year; ICE supply chain wind-down over 5-10 years; Chinese OEM market share growth threatens European suppliers
items.quote: The forgings, the market in Europe is weak as we highlighted, I mean, in the next years, the market will continue this weak, let's say, evolution. There will be a drop of around 2%, 3% this year. Next year will be similar.

items.statement: India H1 CY26 sales grew 14% YoY to INR32.7 billion but below weighted average market growth of ~16.5-16.7% due to aluminum restructuring and export underperformance
items.quote: Sales increased by 14% versus H1 C25 to INR32.7 billion. The double-digit growth was supported by favorable market growth in the period, but it could have been higher. Two reasons need to be highlighted, the restructuring of our business portfolio at our aluminum vertical, wherein we have let go of some loss-making products.

items.statement: Europe H1 CY26 sales grew 12% YoY to INR18.1 billion but declined 3% in euro terms due to weak automotive market; EBITDA margin improved to 15.8% from 13.1%
items.quote: In euro terms, sales declined by 3% due to the weak European automotive market evolution that can be seen on the table to the right. There was a healthy increase in EBITDA margin to 15.8% in H1 C26 versus 13.1% in H1 C25, thanks to restructuring actions taken in the previous year.

items.statement: Return on net assets 19.4% at end H1 CY26 vs 18.4% end CY25; healthy balance sheet and cash flow
items.quote: Return on net assets at the end of H1 C26 was 19.4% versus 18.4% at the end of CY25.

items.statement: EU tariffs on Chinese EVs (not ICE) driving Chinese OEMs to sell plug-in hybrids and ICE cars in Europe; Chinese OEMs may localize production via plant acquisitions
items.quote: Just to correct you one thing, you said about the tariffs on ICE vehicles on the Chinese vehicles and it's not ICEs Europe put on Chinese cars in EVs. That's why they are now selling plug -in hybrids and ICE cars, okay?

items.statement: Management philosophy: equal priority to growth and margins, investment discipline with non-negotiable ROI, sustainable growth over speed, net cash position enables flexibility
items.quote: And that's the way -- that's CIE philosophy of running things, whether it is in Spain or in India or Mexico or Brazil or anywhere else. That's the way they run. And that is the -- Abhishek, just let me complete and I'll come back to you. And that's the reason why there is resilience in that business model.

items.statement: Guided for at least 30% presales growth in FY27, with potential to exceed if launches stay on schedule
items.quote: The last quarter, I mean, like end of the financial year, so we have guided for at least 30% growth in the presales. That I think we should be able to continue to achieve. And if all the launches happen within time, probably we can do slightly better than that.

items.statement: Targeting 6-6.5 million sq ft project completions in FY27, up ~20% from 5.4 million sq ft in FY26
items.quote: We plan to complete about 6 to 6.5 million square feet for FY '27 as against last year's completion of about 5.4 million square feet, which can be about 20% higher.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margin to improve sequentially in H2 FY27, reaching 17-20% by Q4 from current 9.7%
items.quote: So, our expectation is that by Q4, as we currently, we are at about 9.7% EBITDA. So, as we leave the end of Q4, maybe hopefully, we should be able to do closer towards 17% to 20%.

items.statement: Record quarterly sales of INR 3,656 crores in Q1 FY27, up 76% YoY, with 2.34 million sq ft sold across 1,432 homes at INR 15,655/sq ft average realization
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that Q1 FY '27 has been a landmark quarter for SOBHA in terms of sales. We achieved our highest ever quarterly real estate sales, recording sales value of INR3,656 crores, representing 76% increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Forthcoming launch pipeline of 20.77 million sq ft across 17 projects; confident of launching 9 projects (8.2 million sq ft) in remaining FY27
items.quote: We currently have a forthcoming launch pipeline of about 20.77 million square feet across 17 projects. Of this, we are confident of launching 9 projects, aggregating approximately 8.2 million square feet during the remaining period of FY '27.

items.statement: Unsold inventory of 14.94 million sq ft at end of Q1 FY27, providing strong visibility for future sales
items.quote: As end of Q1 FY '27, we also have 14.94 million square feet of unsold inventory. Both put together, the forthcoming launch pipeline and our current unsold inventory, we have a strong visibility of inventory to be sold in the coming quarters and the years.

items.statement: Revenue yet to be recognized from sold units stands at INR 20,553 crores as of Q1 FY27 end
items.quote: As end of this quarter, the company has INR20,553 crores of revenue yet to be recognized from the sales that have already been done.

items.statement: Invested INR 370 crores in land and INR 70 crores in capex in Q1 FY27; full-year land spend may reach INR 1,500-1,600 crores vs INR 1,160 crores last year
items.quote: last year, we did about INR1,160 crores. And this year, we already did about INR370 crores. And we have identified a couple of opportunities where I think we can invest in Bangalore and in NCR. So, if we are able to complete those transactions, then we might look at closer towards INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores this year.

items.statement: Acquired 1.3-acre land in Mumbai for INR 180 crores and invested in Greater Noida joint development; combined GDV of INR 2,700-3,000 crores
items.quote: The Mumbai project is about 1.3 acres and we bought the land for about INR180 crores. And the Greater Noida project is a joint development for which we have paid certain dues for the authority and for the landowners. So, both -- so each one -- both put together, the GDV for this would be about INR2,700 crores to INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR 659 crores at end of Q1 FY27; gross debt INR 1,110 crores vs cash INR 1,769 crores; net debt ratio -0.14; avg borrowing cost 7.62%
items.quote: We ended the quarter with a net cash position of about INR659 crores, while maintaining a low leverage, low borrowing cost of about 7.62%.

items.statement: Approved NCDs of INR 1,000 crores to be issued in tranches over next couple of quarters as acquisition opportunities firm up
items.quote: We envisage the usage coming in the next couple of quarters. So, we would do it in tranches as and when we identify the acquisition opportunity or, let's say, firm up the acquisition opportunity, we would go ahead with the funding of NCD.

items.statement: Operating cash inflow of INR 1,924 crores in Q1 FY27 (up 8.2% YoY); real estate collections INR 1,756 crores; net operating cash flow INR 312 crores
items.quote: Total operational cash inflow during the quarter increased by 8.2% year-on-year basis to INR1,924 crores. Real estate collections stood at INR1,756 crores compared with INR1,599 crores in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Collections impacted by end-of-quarter sales timing and lower milestone billing due to labor shortages in April-May; expect improvement from Q2
items.quote: One is the collections from new sales have come towards the end of the quarter. And hence, I mean, there is more collection that would be coming from these new sales, but part of the collections only have come in this Q1. Second is typically, our milestone billing collections this time were relatively lower because some of the milestones we could not achieve due to labor shortage in -- mainly in A

items.statement: Projected margin cash flow of INR 12,000 crores from completed and ongoing projects (receivables INR 31,000 crores vs remaining cost INR 19,000 crores)
items.quote: We have projected receivable from sale and unsold value approximately INR31,000 crores. Against this, the estimated remaining cost to be incurred is INR19,000 crores, resulting in projected margin cash flow of INR12,000 crores from completed and ongoing projects.

items.statement: Expect margin expansion as FY23-sold projects complete; other businesses revenue steady at ~INR 170 crores/quarter with commercial rental at INR 23 crores
items.quote: We would see margin expansion as we complete the projects that we have sold from FY '23. Our backward integrated operating model continues to differentiate SOBHA in the market. During the quarter, our other businesses generated revenue of about INR170 crores, and we have a good order book visibility for those businesses.

items.statement: Demand scenario stable and steady post-launches; strong Q1 performance attributed to better launch preparation rather than cyclical shift
items.quote: Otherwise, the overall demand scenario seems to be quite stable from what we have seen in terms of the launches and also what we are witnessing post the launches also. It's been quite steady. So, we believe that it is a reasonably good demand scenario.

items.statement: Bangalore contributed 57% of Q1 sales (INR 2,067 crores); NCR delivered highest-ever quarterly sales of INR 1,384 crores driven by SOBHA Crescent launch
items.quote: Bangalore once again emerged as our strongest market, contributing 57% of the quarterly sales of about INR2,067 crores, driven by good response to our launches of SOBHA One World and Sacred Grove, a plotted development. The NCR region also delivered its highest ever quarterly sales with a sale value of about INR1,384 crores, mainly driven by a successful launch of SOBHA Crescent in Gurgaon.

items.statement: Forthcoming pipeline has greater joint development mix, reducing marginal cash flow vs prior fully-owned land projects like Hoskote
items.quote: So, the main difference for the new forthcoming majority -- I mean, the mix of the projects, a greater mix is towards joint development. And hence, that's the marginal cash flow, you would have seen reduction.

items.statement: Launched 3 new projects in Q1 FY27 with 6.89 million sq ft saleable area and INR 10,000 crores potential sale value
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched 3 new projects across Bangalore and Gurgaon with a combined saleable area of 6.89 million square feet and a potential sale value of about INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: SOBHA One World: released 3.4 million sq ft, sold 40% at launch; SOBHA Crescent: sold 60% in Q1; Crescent Phase 2 planned for Q3/Q4 FY27
items.quote: In SOBHA One World, out of the overall 3,484 homes across 47.4 acres, we released 3.4 million square feet. And out of the released, we could sell about 40% at the launch. In SOBHA Crescent, we sold about 60% in Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Average realization of INR 15,655 per sq ft in Q1 FY27 across 2.34 million sq ft sold
items.quote: We sold 2.34 million square feet across 1,432 homes with an average realization of INR15,655 per square feet, reflecting the strength of our product portfolio and brand.

items.statement: Karnataka minimum wage hike of 60% in May under evaluation; technician workforce already above minimum wage; impact expected to be absorbable within project budgets
items.quote: Yes, there has been, and we are still under the evaluation phase. But largely, our technician force that we have, that is above the minimum wage. However, it would have a little bit of impact on our overall cost. That is yet to be assessed. But I think we are considering -- it should be -- we should be able to absorb it within the budget that we have allocated for the projects.

items.statement: Mumbai project launch timeline uncertain due to approvals; not included in 8.2 million sq ft FY27 launch guidance
items.quote: Mumbai one, we would endeavor to do it. But considering the approvals, uncertainty, a clear timeline from -- there is a lot of work to be done there. And hence, although our endeavor i s to launch it this financial year. So currently, I have not included that in the projection that I have given in terms of 8.2 million square feet for this remaining 9 months

items.statement: Commercial project in Gurgaon (6 lakh sq ft) under evaluation for rental retention model instead of sales; removed from launch pipeline for now
items.quote: That particular project, it's still the endeavor to launch and develop it. We have, in fact, the entire TDR for it, and we can develop the entire project. But currently, we are looking at an option -- evaluating an option of launching it, but not actually selling it, but retaining for our rental income.

items.statement: Exports target to exceed 250,000 units per month from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: we are looking at moving exports to beyond the 2,50,000 per month level this quarter and onwards

items.statement: Capacity expansion of ~25% from 7 million to 9 million units per annum underway
items.quote: we are undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum across different businesses to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum

items.statement: EV two-wheeler capacity to increase from 50,000 to 60,000 units immediately
items.quote: we are right now at 50,000 units. We are limited at that for EV two-wheelers. And immediately through some productivity measures, both at our end and with the vendors, we hope to unlock it at 60,000

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 20.9%, up 10 bps sequentially despite 4.5% commodity inflation
items.quote: EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially despite the hyperinflationary commodity environment that I'd spoken about

items.statement: EV portfolio (2W+3W) now 30% of domestic revenue with double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: Taken together, our electric two-wheeler and three-wheeler businesses delivered their largest ever quarter and are now at 30% of domestic revenues with double-digit EBITDA percentage

items.statement: Nigeria retail doubled YoY, achieving ~60% market share in retail terms
items.quote: Nigeria led the growth, being in a pre-election phase, which increases institutional sales. By our estimates, a disproportionate share of this expansion was captured by us, doubling retails year-on-year and delivering a market share of almost 60% in retail terms

items.statement: Realized USD-INR rate INR 94.4 in Q1 vs INR 90.6 in Q4 FY26 and INR 85.6 in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The rupee depreciated through Q1, with a realized USD-INR rate coming in at INR94.4 versus INR90.6 in the previous quarter and INR85.6 in the same quarter last year

items.statement: Free cash flow INR 2,300+ crores in Q1, ~80% cash conversion of PAT
items.quote: We generated over INR2,300 crores of free cash flow during this quarter, almost double that of the same period last year, translating into a cash conversion of almost 80% of profit after tax

items.statement: Broader cost inflation spreading to proprietary components, electronics, labour, logistics, energy; Q2 impact uncertain
items.quote: inflation is no longer confi ned to the base metals complex. The cost pressures have become more broader, with proprietary components, electronics, electrical parts, labour, logistics and energy and conversion now moving up simultaneously and meaningfully

items.statement: Outpacing industry growth by 2x in top 30 export markets (80% of industry)
items.quote: Of the top 30 markets, which account for almost 80% of the industry, we continue to significantly outpace the industry growth by over 2x, thereby increasing our market shares very strongly in these important markets

items.statement: Lead-acid e-rickshaw permits not being renewed; migration to lithium-ion expected
items.quote: lead acid is not looked on favourably by the regulators for obvious reasons. And there have been now increasing instances where permits are not renewed or not given for lead acid based e-ricks

items.statement: KTM AG manufacturing ramping up; inventory normalization largely completed
items.quote: Manufacturing has now progressively ramped up through the year and is approaching underlying retail demand. Billing performance has improved in line with this recovery. At the same time, the planned normalization of dealer and plant inventories has largely been completed, with inventory levels now stabilizing at the desired levels across

items.statement: Steel +10%, aluminum/platinum/rhodium +40%, ABS/copper/nickel/rubber up substantially in Q1
items.quote: Steel rose by upwards of 10%, aluminum and platinum by nearly 40%, rhodium as well by 40%, while ABS, copper, nickel and natural rubber also moved up quite substantially through the quarter

items.statement: FY27 target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex; 36% of capacity guidance achieved by Q1
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to deliver our FY27 annual target of 3 GW capacity addition and ₹20,000 crore capex — having already achieved close to 36% of the FY27 capacity guidance, and surpassed about 87% of the total capacity added in all of FY26.

items.statement: Added 873 MW in Q1 FY27, cumulative 1.1 GW since April 2026; 225 MW added in July so far
items.quote: Q1 FY27 has been a landmark quarter for JSW Energy. We delivered one of the largest single -quarter capacity additions in our history — and among the highest in the sector — adding 873 MW during the quarter, taking cumulative additions to about 1.1 GW - till date.

items.statement: Completed ₹10,150 crore capital raise via promoter allotment, JSW Steel stake sale, and QIP; cash balance ~₹12,880 crore
items.quote: Another significant milestone in our journey was the deleveraging achieved through the successful execution of a ₹10,150 crore capital raise in the recent past — the largest growth capital raise in the Indian power sector.

items.statement: Net debt to TTM EBITDA improved to 4.95x from 5.2x in FY26; gross debt ₹74,000 crore, cash ~₹12,900 crore, net debt ~₹55,000 crore
items.quote: Our balance sheet discipline continues to strengthen, with net operating leverage on a trailing -twelve-month basis improving to 4.95x, from approximately 5.2x in FY26, even as we scale up our growth investments.

items.statement: Signed definitive agreement to acquire Maruti Clean Coal & Power (300 MW thermal plant with 195 MW PPA, 14-year residual life)
items.quote: Accordingly, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire Maruti Clean Coal & Power Limited, which operates a 300 MW thermal plant in Chhattisgarh. The plant has a long-term PPA of 195 MW (net) with Rajasthan discoms, with a residual PPA life of 14 years.

items.statement: Pump storage projects (Bhavali 1,500 MW, Kandhaura 1,680 MW) expected at ~₹5 crore/MW with high-teen IRRs; Mahanadi Unit 4 capex 25-30% lower than greenfield
items.quote: Not very far from this number, you can say that. Not very far from this number.

items.statement: BESS assembly external order of ₹440 crore expected to yield ~₹150 crore EBITDA annually at $2.75-3/kWh margin
items.quote: So I think here, in terms of the margin in dollar terms, it's in the range of about $2.75 to $3. If you look at the overall capacity running, it will be about $15 million in a year. So that's how we are saying you can get about close to ₹ 150-odd crores of EBITDA from this project.

items.statement: India Q1 FY27 power demand grew 8.5% YoY; July demand growth ~12%; peak demand hit 271 GW in May, expected to reach 300 GW near term
items.quote: India's power sector delivered a strong start to FY27, with Q1 demand growing 8.5% year -on-year — a sharp turnaround from the muted 0.9% growth in FY26.

items.statement: DAM prices rose to ₹5.10/unit in Q1 FY27 from ₹4.40 in Q1 FY26 (~16% YoY); API4 coal index up 25% YoY to $113
items.quote: DAM prices, which averaged around ₹3.86 per unit through FY26 on muted demand, have firmed meaningfully in Q1 FY27 — rising to ₹5.10 per unit from about ₹4.40 in Q1 FY26, a near ly 16% YoY increase.

items.statement: Shift to domestic coal kept resilience against 25% YoY rise in API4 coal prices; open capacity reduced to under 4%
items.quote: Coal prices witnessed a year-on-year increase. Taking a specific index like API4 as a reference, it stood at $90 in Q1 FY26 compared to $113 in Q1 FY27 — an increase of about 25%. Our continued shift toward domestic coal has kept us resilient to this adver se fuel price movement.

items.statement: Total installed capacity ~14.6 GW with 61% renewables, 5.7 GW thermal; RE generation up 29% (solar) and 3% (wind) YoY
items.quote: With the sizeable capacity that we added, our total installed capacity now stands at about 14.6 GW, with renewables constituting around 61%, complemented by 5.7 G W of thermal capacity providing reliable, dispatchable

items.statement: Fixed charges recognized in current quarter but cash collection expected over next 2-3 quarters for thermal PPAs
items.quote: However, while the revenue is recognized in the current period, the actual cash collection is expected over the next two to three quarters

items.statement: TGNA curtailment of 69 MU in Q1 (₹15 crore revenue impact); 300 MW under TGNA expected to convert to GNA by Aug 31
items.quote: See, wind plus solar put together, we had a curtailment of 69 MU during the quarter. But as I told you, this has to be divided into 2. There were curtailments under the GNA projects also, for which the power was being supplied under the PPA.

items.statement: Thermal PLFs: Utkal >91% availability in July, Mahanadi minimal backdown due to merit order, Ratnagiri/Vijayanagar capable of <50% technical minimum
items.quote: And the minimum load that we have seen in the case of Utkal has not gone below 60%; this has been the case in most cases. But overall, on a round-the-clock basis, if you talk for the month of July when the power demand has grown almost 12% till date, we have been operating at almost more than 85% PLF and more than 90% availability.

items.statement: Hydro generation down 26% YoY due to weak hydrology (Sutlej basin -39%, Ravi -24%); expects catch-up to design energy with monsoon onset
items.quote: However, overall portfolio generation declined by almost 26% YoY, owing to weak hydrology across the entire basin — national hydro generation was down 7% YoY, Sutlej basin was down 39% YoY, and Ravi basin was down 24% YoY.

items.statement: Acquired Maruti Clean Coal & Power (300 MW thermal); increased stake in Toshiba JSW Power Systems JV to 10.7% from 2.4%; acquiring GE boiler business
items.quote: Accordingly, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire Maruti Clean Coal & Power Limited, which operates a 300 MW thermal plant in Chhattisgarh.

items.statement: Salboni Phase 1 (2x800 MW) TG order placed to TJPS, boiler from GE Durgapur acquisition (1.1 GW nameplate, scalable to 1.6 GW); Mahanadi Unit 4 on track for FY28 via Chinese suppliers
items.quote: Salboni, as we have announced earlier also, maybe 2 x 800 Phase 1, with the turbine generator order has already been placed to TJPS, Toshiba JSW Power Systems, and the work has already started, the suppliers deliveries and commissioning are in line with the PPA timelines

items.statement: Wind blade facility at Halol (450 blades/year, ~600 MW) commissioned June 8; Chitradurga facility expected by FY27
items.quote: On the wind side, we commissioned our wind blade manufacturing facility at Halol, Gujarat on June 8th — with an annual capacity of 450 blades, sufficient to support approximately 600 MW of wind installations per annum

items.statement: FY28 capacity addition target in same range as FY27 (~3 GW); will announce details soon
items.quote: Yes, it will be in the same range. It will be in this range only.

items.statement: Multiple states interested in Mahanadi Unit 4 PPA; C&I and group captive projects in FY27 pipeline
items.quote: There are more than one state who are interested. Keeping in mind now that with so much of solar and this question was asked in the very beginning that maybe the technical minimum coming down, so some of the buyers are preferring 600 MW and lower capacity tie -up because even if they have to do the back down, it is comfortably at 50%.

items.statement: SECI pump storage tender required Stage 1 forest clearance (not ready); Karnataka Narihalla project PPA expected soon
items.quote: See, in this in this tender, the condition was that there has to be forest clearance, stage 1, in place, those only can apply. That was the case. So we were not having any other site ready with forest clearance stage 1 clearance. So we had decided not to participate.

items.statement: CO₂ emissions avoided: ~16-17 MT in FY26, ~4.5 MT in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Further, I am also pleased to share that, as a reflection of our strong green focus and long -term commitment to carbon neutrality, our expanding renewable portfolio enabled us to avoid approximately 16-17 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions in the fiscal 2026 and about 4.5 million tonnes in Q1FY27

items.statement: Q1 FY27 marks third consecutive profitable quarter with margins improving by 1,000+ basis points despite seasonally soft quarter
items.quote: Q1 of FY27 is our third consecutive profitable quarter. This is a very important milestone for us because it reaffirms our shift to profitability and makes it structural and enduring. Despite Q1 being the industry's softest quarter, our margins improved by 1,000+ basis points.

items.statement: Internal target to make Housing.com profitable within three to four quarters; public guidance of four to six quarters
items.quote: Our internal target is three to four quarters; we are today saying four to six quarters. Housing is larger scale, a lot more synergy opportunities, larger brand, and we and it's the marketplace. So that is why we are factoring in one or two extra quarters.

items.statement: Acquired Housing.com from REA Group; REA becomes 24.9% shareholder; total dilution ~20% including prior 5% from PropTiger deal
items.quote: 20%, right. Because around 5% odd percent was already with REA Group due to the PropTiger acquisition, which we had bought at 1x if you recall. We had issued shares worth 84 crores and the business that we are doing now in PropTiger makes that at almost 0.5x of the dilution.

items.statement: Housing.com commands ~24% of India's online portal market with 58M average monthly visits and 12M monthly active users
items.quote: Housing.com already commands approximately 24% of India's online portal market, supported by one of the country's strongest consumer brands, attracting over 58 million average monthly visits and 12 million monthly active users on its app.

items.statement: India sees ~2.5 crore property transactions annually; 1.2 crore digitally addressable; only 7-10 lakh intermediated online; annual transaction value exceeds INR 15 lakh crores

items.statement: Fuel cost pass-through lag in B2B Express due to hundreds of customers requiring individual negotiation

There, it takes a negotiation with each one of them. So it takes time to pass on the fuel cost increase in B2B.

items.statement: PAT includes INR 4 crores non-recurring interest on income tax refund; operating PAT ~INR 21.4 crores
items.quote: I do want to call out that our PAT in this quarter includes INR 4 crores of interest on income tax refund. You will see that in the other income line, which is not expected to be recurring income in the subsequent quarters. If you remove that number, our operating PAT is approximately INR 21.4 crores.

items.statement: Contract Logistics EBITDA margin expanded from 6.6% to 6.9% YoY despite gross margin dilution
items.quote: These have been offset by our overhead efficiencies and operating leverage, leading to an EBITDA growth of 31% year-on-year and margin expansion from 6.6% to 6.9%.

items.statement: B2B Express EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 1.6 crores from INR 11.8 crores YoY
items.quote: EBITDA performance in this business also continues to improve with an EBITDA loss of INR 1.6 crores in this quarter versus an INR 11.8 crores loss in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: New contract logistics sites take 3-4 months to normalize; small last mile sites normalize in 10 days
items.quote: Generally, we have seen that when you are coming up with a new site, if the site is small, it is a matter of a couple of weeks. But if we are also winning some very large sites where it takes almost 3 to 4 months for a site to come fully normalized in operations. We have recently opened a very large site for a very marquee customer in Luhari near Gurgaon. I mean, just to give you an idea, it's alm

items.statement: Revised ROA guidance for exit Q4 FY27 to 1.2%-1.4% from earlier 1.6%-1.8% due to external factors
items.quote: Based on this visibility available, we believe an ROA in the range of 1.2% to 1.4% of the exit of Q4FY27 would be probable.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 1.6%-1.8% for FY27
items.quote: And therefore, our credit cost guidance of 1.6% to 1.8%, that continues to remain. So we are not changing that.

items.statement: Full year FY27 credit growth guided at 14% with EEB 5-10% and non-EEB 20%+
items.quote: On the credit growth, what we had guided was for the full year FY 27, we were looking at a 14% growth rate, within which EEB, we were looking at between a 5% to 10% growth and non-EEB would be 20% plus.

items.statement: NIM stable at 6.2% in Q1 FY27 despite funding cost headwinds
items.quote: The NII for Q1FY27 stood at INR 2,921 crores, registering a growth of 6% YoY and 5% sequentially. This performance was supported by healthy growth in advances and a stable margin profile at 6.2% despite the funding cost headwinds witnessed during the quarter.

items.statement: NIM may face moderate pressure going forward due to rising cost of funds
items.quote: So this quarter also, despite challenges, we could maintain the NIM at 6.20%. But as I have told you that going forward, there may be some increase in the cost of the funds & cost of the deposits. So that may moderately affect our NIM.

items.statement: Earlier NIM target of 6.5% by Q4 FY27 now challenged; aim to hold current 6.2%
items.quote: We had a line of sight towards -- we wanted to go towards a 6.5% by the end of Q4FY27. But given the fact that the cost of funds in the industry has gone up due to these particular external factors, that's where our revised guidance is to see how exactly we can maintain.

items.statement: Gross advances at INR 1.56 lakh crores, up 16% YoY and 1% QoQ
items.quote: For advances, as of 30th June 2026, the gro ss advances stood at INR 1.56 lakh crores, representing a healthy 16% growth YoY and a 1% sequential increase

items.statement: Non-EEB portfolio grew 27% YoY, now 2/3 of loan book; secured portfolio 57% of advances
items.quote: The non-EEB portfolio grew by 27% YoY and now contributes 2/3 of the overall loan book, underscoring the transformation of our business mix over the last few years. Growth within the secured businesses remained particularly strong.

items.statement: EEB portfolio at INR 52,641 crores with lower seasonal moderation than prior years
items.quote: The EEB portfolio stood at INR 52,641 crores, while the book witnessed the customary seasonal moderation typically seen in the first quarter, the extent of the decline was significantly lower than what we have experienced in the most previous years.

items.statement: Retail assets up 45% YoY; wholesale banking up 38% YoY
items.quote: Retail assets recorded 45% YoY expansion, led by products such as commercial vehicles, construction equipment, auto loans and gold loans. Wholesale Banking also maintained strong momentum, growing 38% YoY.

items.statement: Loan mix: EEB 23%, SBAL 11%, wholesale 33%, housing 22%, retail & other 11%
items.quote: EEB group lending accounts for 23% of advances, SBAL at 11%, wholesale banking at 33%, housing finance at 22% and retail and other loans at 11%.

items.statement: Cost of funds rising despite no repo rate hike; savings bank cost up 20-25 bps QoQ
items.quote: I can also see that the effect of the reduced cost of funds on account of the reduction in repo rate that has happened and the benefit of which we have got till Q1 may not be available Q2 onwards because already the savings bank costs, the cost of funds have increased by around 20 - 25 basis points.

items.statement: Technology costs up 65% YoY due to supply chain constraints from Middle East war
items.quote: We all know that the availability of chips, etc all these are impacting the Indian economy for that matter. And as you have seen that my tech cost has gone, I would say, high by 65% YoY.

items.statement: Gross NPA 3.1%, Net NPA 0.9%, PCR 71.1% (74.3% incl. security receipts)
items.quote: Consequently, our headline asset quality metrics improved further. Gross NPA reduced to 3.1%, while net NPA remained contained at 0.9%. Provisioning coverage also remained robust. The reported stood at 71.1%. And if we include the security receipt related provisions, the PCR stood at 74.3%.

items.statement: Collection efficiency ex-NPA 98.9% overall; EEB 98.5% in June 2026
items.quote: level, the collection efficiency, excluding NPAs, remained healthy at 98.9% in June 2026. Within the EEB portfolio, collection performance was impacted by the usual seasonality associated with the first quarter, including a concentration of holidays during the month of April. Despite these temporary factors, the collection efficiency for E EB for the month of June 2026 stood at 98.5

items.statement: Gross slippages INR 1,079 crores (EEB INR 604 crores, down from INR 690 crores)
items.quote: The gross slippages for the quarter stood at INR 1,079 crores, broadly stable compared to INR 1,028 crores in the previous quarter. This is at the bank level. Encouraging slippages within the EEB portfolio improved sequentially to INR 604 crores, down from INR 690 crores in Q4

items.statement: EEB 0-90 DPD rose to 3.5% from 3.1% due to April holiday disruptions; viewed as seasonal
items.quote: On early delinquency indicators, the 0 to 90 DPD pool in the EEB segment increased to 3.5% from 3.1% in the previous quarter. This was driven primarily by a temporary increase in the SMA 0 bucket following holiday-related disruptions during the month of April.

items.statement: Sold INR 291 crores housing NPAs to ARC; technical write-off INR 597 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we also undertook proactive balance sheet actions to reduce our NPA book, including the sale of INR 291 crores of housing NPA loans to an ARC and a technical write-off of INR 597 crores.

items.statement: Liquidity comfortable: CD ratio 94%, LCR 140%; FCNR mobilization INR 30 crores
items.quote: Liquidity for the bank remains comfortable. I can say even with a CD ratio of 94%, we maintained a LCR of 140%, which is quite comfortable for the bank. As regarding FCNRB, we have mobilized INR 30 crores.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 18.2% (Tier 1 17.5%) including profits
items.quote: Capital adequacy ratio, including profits improved further to 18.2% with Tier 1 capital at 17.5%, providing significant capacity to support future business growth while maintaining a prudent capital buffer.

items.statement: Bulk deposits down 13% YoY to 26% of total deposits; 86% non-callable
items.quote: Bulk deposits declined by 13% YoY, resulting in their share reducing to 26% of total deposits compared to 32% a year ago. This represents a significant shift towards a more granular and sustainable liability profile. It is also worth noting that the quality of our bulk deposit book remains strong with nearly 86% of these bulk deposits being noncallable in nature.

items.statement: External risks: Middle East war driving energy crisis, higher funding costs, tech cost inflation; unpredictable monsoon
items.quote: Ongoing geopolitical developments, particularly in the Middle East, a less predictable monsoon pattern, elevated funding costs and rising technology-related costs are factors that warrant close monitoring. These developments have the potential to influence customer sentiment, operating costs and overall profitability across the sector.

items.statement: FY27 capacity addition target of 5 GW greenfield RE capacity
items.quote: We remain on track to add 5 GW of greenfield capacity this year.

items.statement: FY27 BESS cumulative capacity target of 10+ GW-hour
items.quote: With this momentum, we are well positioned to achieve our 10-plus GW-hour target this year.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR42,000 crore
items.quote: So, see from a Capex perspective, the FY '27 guidance is about INR42,000 crores of Capex to be done for FY '27.

items.statement: FY30 BESS cumulative capacity target of 50 GW-hour
items.quote: the overall target till FY '30, we have come out and said that we would like to do about 50 GW-hour of batteries till FY '30

items.statement: FY27 run-rate EBITDA target of INR21,000 crore
items.quote: For the expected for the FY '27, it is about INR21,000 crore.

items.statement: BESS EBITDA thumb rule of INR25-30 lakh per MW-hour for FY27
items.quote: It's about INR25 lakh to INR30 lakh per MW-hour in that range where the EBITDA would come in based on the capitalization that takes place over the next nine months of the year.

items.statement: Commissioned 1.9 GW BESS at Khavda in Q1 FY27, total installed BESS capacity 3.5 GW-hour
items.quote: We commissioned 1.9 GW of battery energy storage capacity at Khavda during the quarter, taking total installed capacity to 3.5 GW-hour.

items.statement: 500 MW pump storage project at Chitravathi on schedule for commissioning in FY27
items.quote: We are also on schedule to commission our maiden 500 MW pump storage project at Chitravathi, Andhra Pradesh, in this financial year.

items.statement: Merchant/C&I capacity contracted to Adani Energy on 25-year fixed-price PPAs at arm's length
items.quote: In order to de-risk ourself and concentrate more on the project execution and operational excellence, on a long -term basis, we have contracted on an arm's length basis and with new approval of the Board on arm's length transaction, as well as we have ensured that we have a contracted capacity rather than taking the risk with Adani Energy Limited.

items.statement: Battery storage PPAs with AESL for 15 years fixed price; solar/wind PPAs for 25 years fixed price
items.quote: So, in case of batteries, it is for 15 years and fixed for that period. And, in case of solar and wind, it is for 25 years and fixed for the price at a rate. So, there is no change which is expected.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA from power supply surged 33% YoY to INR4,122 crore at 94% margin
items.quote: And EBITDA from power supply surged by impressive 33% to INR4,122 crore, thereby achieving 94% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Current curtailment impact of 5-7% on overall EBITDA, expected to be eliminated by end of calendar year
items.quote: However, in the current scenario, as was the trend in the past, a curtailment has an impact of in the range of 5% to 7% on our overall EBITDA as we speak.

items.statement: Energy sales rose 30% YoY to 13.7 billion units driven by 4.3 GW capacity addition and strong operations
items.quote: Our energy sales rose 30% Y-o-Y to 13.7 billion units. This was driven by 4.3 GWs of energy capacity addition, a 27% increase, and strong operations.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex of INR8,800 crore, up 41% YoY
items.quote: Our CapEx of INR8,800 crores during the quarter increased by 41% Y-o-Y, highlighting the efficient capital deployment with every passing quarter.

items.statement: BESS capex thumb rule of INR1.5 crore per MW-hour installed capacity
items.quote: a reasonable good thumb rule would be INR1.5 crores per MW-hour of installed capacity.

items.quote: the current is in line with what the merchant power is selling through, including the RECs. It varies, but it is in the range of INR2.5 per unit.

items.statement: PPA coverage 31% in Q1, structural in nature, full-year target 100% with historical average 109-110%

items.quote: I think we do expect, by the end of this year, another 7 GW, which is going to come. That is this calendar year. And another quarter or two, the balances should be there online.

items.quote: what got fired was not the batteries, right? What got fired actually were what is called PCS or inverters because there was what is called IGBT failure.
