items.statement: Working capital days at 25 days; net cash position of INR 133 crores; trade inventory normal with primary sales largely equal to consumer offtake.
items.quote: We closed the quarter with working capital days at 25 days and a net cash position of INR133 crores, reflecting continued balance sheet discipline.

items.statement: Invested ahead of curve in human capital for emerging businesses (switchgear, switches, wires), DTM expansion, and automation at plants; new product launches contribute 30% of fan revenue and 15% of lighting revenue.
items.quote: We have done ahead of the curve investment in the last 2 years. And this is while we were setting up our emerging businesses teams. So switchgears switches, wires, put in people there. We were expanding into D TM businesses. We were getting into those markets.

items.statement: Hyderabad plant certification processes for export markets (SAC countries) completed over last 2-3 quarters; automation initiatives underway to mitigate labor cost inflation.
items.quote: And for getting Hyderabad plant and so there are different countries, especially SAC countries who come and certify your plant. So all those processes have happened in the last 2, 3 quarters, and we are seeing traction there.

items.statement: Export business grew double-digits; focus on Africa markets as Middle East impacted; Hyderabad plant certifications done; Europe seen as opportunity for TPW fans but cost structure not yet competitive vs China.
items.quote: We've had double -digit growth in our exports business. And largely, we've looked at Africa markets, while Middle East got impacted, we've looked at countries. So those are the ones where we've been able to do this.

items.statement: Employee cost rose 10.7% YoY due to minimum wage hikes; as % of sales fell to 8.9% from 9.9% YoY; automation and process studies underway to mitigate labor cost long-term.
items.quote: Yes, the 10.7% has a wage impact of the sudden increase in the minimum wages that's happened. We're taking our actions. We're taking our -- so some of the actions that we're putting in terms of automating our plants, automating processes there, looking at more studies and other things.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit EBITDA margins over time; 3-year revenue CAGR target of 14-15% to cross INR 5,000 crores; mark-to-market better performance sustained for 8-10 quarters.
items.quote: We are committed on our path to double digit. We are committed on our path of mark -to-market better performance and which we've been doing for the last 8, 10 quarters. And we are committed to our CAGR being healthy, healthy double-digit.

items.statement: Commodity volatility (copper, aluminum, paints), currency, freight, minimum wage hikes, and geopolitical uncertainty create unpredictable inflationary pressure that can only be reacted to, not proactively managed.
items.quote: But some of the things that we've seen in the last 4 months in terms of inflationary prices, this is something that all of us never saw even during the COVID time. It's been extremely volatile, unpredictable and something that you can only react to and not proactively manage.

items.statement: Orient took price increases ahead of peers in fans (6x Dec-Jun) and other categories; maintained competitiveness and volume-value growth despite higher pricing; BLDC portfolio differentiated by in-house PCB design and sub-50dB noise.
items.quote: If you do a channel check, you will understand that, yes, we've been ahead of others to take price increase. Like most of the leading brands have not taken price increase in June. We were the only ones who've taken some of the start -up brands have taken almost half of what we've taken.

items.statement: Lighting & Switchgear segment grew 25.4% YoY; B2C lighting high double-digit growth; B2B (C-Loom) high single-digit growth; tender business degrew consciously due to risk profiling.
items.quote: Lighting and Switchgear remained a structural growth engine, delivering 25.4% year-on-year revenue growth, driven by distribution expansion, portfolio premiumization and steady market share gains in consumer lighting.

items.statement: Professional Lighting sees healthy project inquiry pipeline; street lighting and facade project execution aiding traction.
items.quote: Professional Lighting continues to gain traction, aided by execution of key street lighting and facade projects, and we continue to see healthy project inquiry pipeline.

items.statement: Gas sales volume reached 303 MMSCM, up 13% YoY, led by 18% YoY CNG growth and 4% YoY PNG growth
items.quote: During the quarter, gas sales volume reached 303 MMSCM, reflecting a robust growth of 13% year-on-year, led by 18% year-on-year growth in CNG segment and 4% year-on-year growth in PNG segment.

items.statement: Steel pipeline network expanded to 15,987 inch-kilometres
items.quote: At the same time, steel pipeline expanded to 15,987-inch kilometres further strengthening our distribution network to support future growth.

items.statement: Added 38,000 new household connections, total domestic customer base at 11.41 lakh
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 38,000 new households' connection, taking our total customer base to 11.41 lakh households in domestic segment.

items.statement: Added 5 new CNG stations, total network at 707 stations
items.quote: On CNG segment front, we added 5 new CNG stations with our total network of 707 CNG stations currently.

items.statement: Added 392 commercial and 56 industrial customers, 3x and 2x increase YoY respectively
items.quote: We added 392 commercial customers and 56 industrial customers, which is almost 3x and 2x increase, respectively, over the same period last year. Our customer base now stands at 10,422 in industrial and commercial segment.

items.statement: EV charging network expanded to 5,306 points with 58 MW capacity, sold 3.3 million electrons, up 100% YoY
items.quote: On E-Mobility business vertical, our EV charging network expanded to 5,306 charging points within installation capacity of 58 megawatts. We sold 3.3 million electrons during the quarter and delivered robust growth of 100% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Target of 10,000 EV charging points with focus on utilization and operational efficiency
items.quote: This strong momentum reinforce our confidence in achieving our targets of 10,000 EV charging points, with continued focus on improving network utilization and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Joint venture IOAGPL operates across 19 GAs, combined 53 GAs covering 14% of India's population, 13.74 lakh CNG households, 12,326 commercial/industrial customers, 1,167 CNG stations, 28,600 inch-km steel pipeline
items.quote: Our joint venture partner, IOAGPL continues to expand in their 19 geographical areas meaningfully. Together, we operate across 53 geographical areas, which represents 14% India's population, spanning across 125 districts, combined customer base stands at 13.74 lakhs CNG households, 12,326 commercial and industrial customers and our CNG network stands at 1,167 stations.

items.statement: Revenue grew 27% YoY to INR 1,908 crores, EBITDA at INR 281 crores
items.quote: Our strong operational execution was reflected in our financial performance with revenue growth at a rate of -- growing at the rate of 27% year-on-year to INR1,908 crores during the quarter and EBITDA stands at INR281 crores.

items.statement: Margin compression primarily due to gas availability at market-driven prices and declining APM allocation
items.quote: Yes, primarily one of the major reasons in terms of these compressed margins is on the gas availability on a market driven prices. And second is APM allocation, yes, it is going slowly down.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve to previous levels or better once Middle East crisis ends and US/Qatar supply increases
items.quote: So that will help us to get better rates in the coming years -- in the coming months. So once this happens and the Middle East crisis is over, we'll see the margins improving to the last level or better than that.

items.statement: Procuring volumes on mid-term basis to reduce spot exposure, also evaluating longer-term contracts as market stabilizes
items.quote: So, we are looking at various options like procuring some volumes on the midterm basis. So not on the short term because the prices are elevated for the shorter term. But if you look at middle term, then probably it will be more competitive, that will help us to cater to the current exposure to the spot market.

items.statement: Spot volumes around 15% of total consumption after curtailment
items.quote: Spot volumes are around 15% of the total consumption after the curtailment.

items.statement: Domestic APM and NWG allocation around 40%, long-term contracts 48%, pooled gas mechanism withdrawn after peace deal
items.quote: If you look at the domestic APM and NWG allocation, that is around 40%. And on the longer-term contracts, we have 48%. And if you look at the current -- during the pooled mechanism, volumes were available from the allocation and which has been withdrawn after the peace deal, which was, I would say the sudden decision by the government.

items.statement: Domestic volumes 62% of portfolio, imported RLNG 38% (Henry Hub and Brent linked), NWG price at 12% of Indian crude basket, significantly above $5/MMBTU
items.quote: So, if you look at the breakup, nearly domestic volumes are around 62% of our portfolio. And the imported RLNG would be around 38%, which consists of both heavier-linked contracts and the Brent-linked contracts.

items.statement: Slightly higher capex budget than last year, monitoring gas scenarios and growth areas, dedicated task force for domestic connections
items.quote: Yes, we have slightly higher budget compared to last year, but we are monitoring the situation in end-to-end basis, in terms of the gas of the scenarios, in terms of the areas where the growth is very evident.

items.statement: CNG demand growing double digits across light commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles, taxi aggregators; OEMs like Maruti, Hyundai, Tata, Eicher, Volvo growing ~30% in CNG volumes
items.quote: If you see entire CNG segment, whether it is light commercial vehicles or passenger vehicles or taxi aggregators, I mean growth is in double digits, entire value chain in terms of the infrastructure, which is being planned all across country in terms of CNG stations added, it is in double digit.

items.statement: CNG-petrol arbitrage exists but varies by state; evaluating pricing daily per GA to balance customer acquisition and competition
items.quote: If you see the arbitrage between petrol and CNG, there is a room, but at the same time, we have to be conscious of fact of bringing more customers on board, so that people, so we will keep on evaluating that from time to time.

items.statement: Industry-wide training initiatives for gas plumbing with government support, ITI and diploma college tie-ups to address technical personnel shortage
items.quote: Yes, this is happening across India. And even there's a support from government as a skill development, and they are introducing a course on the gas plumbing side specifically. Also, there is a tie-up with ITIs, there's a tie-up with diploma engineering colleges, which are helping us to bring more and more manpower in this industry.

items.statement: Deemed approval mechanism helping in 90-99% of states/districts; coordination needed in few states
items.quote: That has helped us a lot in terms of seeking the permissions wherever it was feasible. And in few states, we do have in terms of coordination where we need to coordinate maximum in terms of making them understand what the regulations have been given to us.

items.statement: Industry representation made for restarting pooled gas mechanism; government may bring it back if Middle East tension continues
items.quote: So yes, representation at the industry level has been going on for -- after the withdrawal. Probably there is some development also, probably government is looking at a bringing impact again because it definitely has an impact on the CGD industry as a whole.

items.statement: Volume growth to continue in similar manner; focus on bridging spot volume gap to maintain momentum
items.quote: So, if you see our volume growth, that will continue to grow in a similar manner. And right now, the challenge is only to build the gap above the spot volumes. That is where we are working towards ensuring that we continually -- we maintain the momentum.

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow at healthy 7% in FY27
items.quote: I believe the cement demand will also grow at a healthy rate of 7% in this financial year.

items.statement: Industry cement demand grew 7-8% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: As per analyst estimates, cement demand for the industry grew by about 7% to 8% Y-o-Y in quarter 1.

items.statement: Dalmia delivered 9% volume growth YoY in Q1 despite state elections
items.quote: Despite these market-specific challenges, we have delivered a robust volume growth of 9% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Premium products share reached 25% in Q1
items.quote: More importantly, this growth was accompanied by a marked improvement in the quality of our sales, and the share of premium products in our portfolio has moved to a healthy number of 25%.

items.statement: Price increases of INR10-15 in South and INR15-20 in East markets
items.value: INR10 to INR15 in South and INR15 to INR20 in East
items.quote: At the same time, healthy price increases of about INR10 to INR15 in South and INR15 to INR20 in East markets enabled us to pass on a significant portion of the input cost inflation.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton improved sequentially to INR1,055 in Q1
items.quote: As a result, EBITDA per ton improved sequentially to INR1,055.

items.statement: Pet coke prices surged to nearly $160/ton before moderating to $130-135/ton
items.quote: Pet coke prices surged to nearly $160 per ton before moderating to between $130 and $135 per ton, well above the pre-war levels of $110 to $115 per ton.

items.statement: Procurement and operational initiatives generated savings of more than INR150 per ton
items.quote: Collectively, these initiatives generated savings of more than INR150 per ton during the quarter.

items.statement: Capex commitment for FY27 expected at INR3,200-3,400 crores
items.quote: Our capex commitment for FY27 is expected to remain at around INR3,200 crores to INR3,400 crores, in line with our earlier guidance.

items.statement: Spent INR510 crores on capex in Q1 excluding acquisition cost
items.quote: Excluding the cost of ac quisition, we have spent about INR510 crores on capex during the quarter

items.statement: Cement capacity to reach about 67 million tons by Q3 FY28
items.quote: With this acquisition, along with our ongoing expansion projects at Belgaum, Kadapa and Pune, our cement capacity will reach about 67 million tons by quarter 3 of financial year '28.

items.statement: Jaypee acquisition adds 5.2 mt cement and 3.3 mt clinker capacity in Central India
items.value: 5.2 million tons of cement capacity, supported by 3.3 million tons of clinker capacity
items.quote: This acquisition brings 5.2 million tons of cement capacity, supported by 3.3 million tons of clinker capacity in the strategically important Central India region.

items.statement: Belgaum expansion expected to commence commercial production in next 6 months
items.quote: Our Belgaum expansion project is also progressing ahead of schedule and is expected to commission -- commence commercial production in the next 6 months

items.statement: Completed Jaypee Cement assets acquisition at enterprise value of INR2,850 crores on 29th May 2026
items.quote: We successfully completed the acquisition of the Jaypee Cement assets on 29th May 2026 at an enterprise value of INR2,850 crores.

items.statement: Gross debt increased to INR9,108 crores, net debt to INR4,431 crores, leverage at 1.47x
items.quote: Our gross debt at the end of the quarter increased to INR9,108 crores, primarily due to the acquisition, while net debt increased to INR4,431 crores. Importa ntly, even after funding this acquisition, our leverage stood at 1.47x, comfortably below 2x net debt to EBITDA

items.statement: Accrued INR45 crores incentives, collected INR60 crores, outstanding INR822 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, we accrued INR45 crores in incentives and collected INR60 crores. The incentive outstanding at the end of the quarter was INR822 crores.

items.statement: Incentive accrual expected to remain INR45-50 crores per quarter for next couple of years
items.value: INR45 crores to INR50 crores per quarter
items.quote: Incentive accrual should remain in a similar range of INR45 crores to INR50 crores per quarter in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Blended fuel cost increased QoQ from INR1.36 to INR1.47 per Kcal
items.quote: The blended fuel cost during the quarter increased Q-o-Q from INR1.36 per Kcal to INR1.47 per Kcal.

items.statement: 48% of power consumption sourced through renewable energy, share to rise
items.quote: Further, 48% of our power consumption has been sourced through renewable energy. This share will continue to rise as we add more renewable energy capacities during the year.

items.statement: Raw material cost per ton increased 12% QoQ to INR823
items.quote: During the quarter, our raw material cost per ton of production increased 12% Q-o-Q to INR823, primarily due to increase in the limestone raising cost and other cost headwinds.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost per ton increased 10% YoY to INR1,045
items.quote: Power and fuel cost per ton of production increased by 10% Y-o-Y to INR1,045, reflecting a sharp escalation in fuel prices.

items.statement: Packing bag prices increased from INR9.5 to almost INR14 per bag in Q1
items.quote: Other expenses rose 3% Q-o-Q to INR632 crores, mainly on account of sharp increase in packing bag prices from about INR9.5 per bag pre-war to almost INR14 per bag in Q1.

items.statement: Expect cost environment to stay elevated in Q2, input cost increase of roughly INR70-80 per ton
items.quote: As the input costs remain above pre-war levels, we expect the cost environment to stay elevated in Q2. The blended fuel cost during the quarter increased Q-o-Q from INR1.36 per Kcal to INR1.47 per Kcal. Further, 48% of our power consumption has been sourced through renewable energy. This share will continue to rise as we add more renewable energy capacities during the year.

items.statement: Depreciation to increase by INR100 crores in FY27 and INR100-150 crores in FY28
items.quote: For full year FY27, we expect depreciation to increase by INR100 crores, as we commission the acquired Jaypee plants and commercialize Belgaum capacity. It would further increase by INR100 crores to INR150 crores in FY28 with the commissioning of Kadapa and Pune projects.

items.statement: Dharmender Tuteja transitioning out as CFO, Yatin Malhotra taking over
items.quote: Before I hand over to Dharmender, I would like to take a moment to congratulate him on a highly successful tenure as CFO of Dalmia Bharat. Under his leadership, the company has delivered robust growth and strengthened its financial strategy. I wish him the very best. Thank you, Dharmender, and over to you.

items.statement: Monsoon progress and El Nino effect warrant close monitoring for short-term fluctuations
items.quote: Inflation has largely stayed wi thin the RBI's comfort range, but uncertainties surrounding the progress of monsoon due to potential effect of El Nino continues to warrant close monitoring

items.statement: Industry capacity addition of 10-11 million tons expected in East in each of FY27 and FY28
items.quote: I think if we just put the numbers that we have in front of us, we are looking at 10 million to 11 million tons getting added in both the years industry-wide, but I think you can be a better judge of that than us. So we have a number of 10 to 11 in each year, '27 and '28.

items.statement: Jaypee assets expected to contribute meaningfully to volumes from Q3 onwards
items.quote: We expect these assets to begin contributing meaningfully to volumes from third quarter onwards.

items.statement: FY27 asset growth target of 25%
items.quote: The strong performance across our asset products has more than offset the impact of macroeconomic headwinds and reinforced our confidence in achieving our FY '27 planned asset growth of 25%.

items.statement: FY27 opex to average assets guidance revised to 6.4%
items.quote: This deferred commencement of expenses, coupled with ongoing efficiency gains will result in full year opex to be lower than earlier planned and now would be around 6.4% of average assets.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost guidance revised to 0.9%-1% of average total assets
items.quote: Accordingly, we are revising our FY '27 credit-cost guidance to 0.9% to 1% of average total assets.

items.statement: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8%-2%
items.quote: we are confident in raising our FY '27 ROA guidance to 1.8% to 2%.

items.statement: Planned capacity building spend of INR250 crores for FY27
items.quote: We already had informed you that we are planning to spend around INR250 crores.

items.statement: 38 new branches operationalized in Q1 FY27, total 814 branches
items.quote: As part of plan for FY '27, bank has operationalized 38 new branches, taking total count to 814 as of June '26.

items.statement: Plan to add 144 branches in FY27, 106 more to open
items.quote: So there are two strategies. Number one, we are adding 144 branches this year. Out of that 38 already we have opened, 106 branches will open which will give us a distribution.

items.statement: Gold loan active branches to increase from 455 to 575 by end of FY27
items.quote: we have a plan to take our active branches from about INR430 crores, INR440 to about INR575 crores by the end of this year.

items.statement: Gold loan monthly disbursement exit rate target INR230-250 crores by March FY27
items.quote: The exit number for disbursement should be somewhere in the range of about INR250 odd crores a month.

items.statement: Affordable housing monthly disbursement capacity INR350-375 crores; micro mortgage target INR140-150 crores by March FY27
items.quote: on the affordable housing side, a capacity of about INR350 crores, INR375 crores a month has already been built. And on the micro mortgage side, you will see INR100 crores a month kind of a disbursement number, which exit March will probably reach in the range of INR140 crores, INR150 crores.

items.statement: Deposit book grew 25% YoY to INR48,129 crores; CASA grew 37.8% YoY to INR12,930 crores
items.quote: We delivered highest Y-o-Y growth in deposits at 25% in the last couple of years, taking the deposit book to INR48,129 crores. CASA deposits grew to INR12,930 crores, up 37.8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross loan book grew 28.9% YoY to INR42,903 crores; disbursements up 41.4% YoY to INR9,245 crores
items.quote: The bank level gross loan book reached INR42,903 crores, growing 28.9% year-on-year and 5.5% quarter-on-quarter. Disbursements for the quarter were at INR9,245 crores, up 41.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Secured loan book at 50.4% of total, grew 42.7% YoY to INR21,638 crores
items.quote: We are pleased to note that our progress towards diversification of loan portfolio remains on track with more than half of the loan book being secured at 50.4% as of June '26. Following a strong performance last quarter, growth in our secured book has continued at robust rates and expanded to INR21,638 crores, up 42.7% year-on-year and 7.8% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Micro banking book grew 16.8% YoY to INR21,371 crores; disbursements up 16.4% YoY to INR4,581 crores
items.quote: Driven by the sustained momentum in the micro banking sector, our micro banking book reached INR21,371 crores, up 16.8% year-on-year, while disbursement grew by 16.4% year-on-year to reach INR4,581 crores.

items.statement: Affordable housing and micro mortgages book grew 40.8% YoY to INR11,210 crores
items.quote: Affordable housing and micro mortgages recorded strong growth with gross loan book increasing 40.8% year-on-year to INR11,210 crores, underscoring resilient customer demand and effective execution across key markets.

items.statement: MSME portfolio grew 54% YoY to INR3,470 crores
items.quote: The MSME portfolio continued its strong momentum, registering growth of 54% year-on-year at INR3,470 crores on the back of maintaining prudent underwriting standards.

items.statement: Gold loan book grew 248.6% YoY to INR1,020 crores; disbursements up 183.9% YoY to INR467 crores
items.quote: Gold loans continues to be strong growth driver with sourcing across 455 branches with an increase of 106 branches in the quarter. Gold gross loan book stood at INR1,020 crores, up 248.6% year-on-year. This increased product penetration and tailored offerings resulted in disbursements growth of 183.9% year-on-year at INR467 crores.

items.statement: Vehicle loan book grew 85.1% YoY to INR1,036 crores
items.quote: The vehicle gross loan book stood at INR1,036 crores, up 85.1% year-on-year.

items.statement: NIM stable at 8.5% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Net interest income increased to INR1,186 crores, while net interest margin remained stable at 8.5%.

items.statement: Cost of funds at 6.86% for Q1 FY27, downward trajectory
items.quote: Cost of funds continued the downward trajectory and stood at 6.86% for the quarter.

items.statement: Affordable housing yield maintained around 12.5%; micro mortgage yield ~19.5%
items.quote: No, I was talking about affordable housing being in the range of about 12.5% yield. And this is something you have to see the mix of ticket sizes and the geographies in which you operate. For us, the affordable housing, we've not had to compromise on yields because of the geographies and the ticket sizes that we've been operating in. There is a business line of micro mortgages, which we started ar

items.statement: MSME LAP ticket size increased to INR80-90 lakhs; working capital to INR1.1-1.2 crores; yield ~10.5%
items.quote: LAP, as you know, was about INR58 lakhs to INR60 lakhs. We are currently in the range of INR80 lakhs to INR90 lakhs. Similarly, on the working capital side, while we were in the range of INR70 lakhs, INR80 lakhs, we have now consciously taken it up to INR1.1 crores to INR1.2 crores. The yield, therefore, cannot be maintained at about 11%, 11.5%, which we used to do earlier. It would be somewhere i

items.statement: GNPA reduced 10 bps to 2.17%; PCR strengthened to 85%; collection efficiency 98.4%
items.quote: Bank level asset quality continued to be stable during the quarter with GNPA reducing by 10 bps to 2.17%. Provision coverage ratio strengthened further to 85%, providing adequate coverage across secured and unsecured products. Collection efficiency for current due plus overdue remained healthy at 98.4%, supported by consistent execution across our operating network.

items.statement: Micro mortgage PAR 1.5%, GNPA 0.55%; bucket X collection efficiency 99.7-99.75%
items.quote: Yes, Pritesh, the PAR number, which was about 1.2% is now in the range of about 1.5%. It's not a very significant increase. Similarly, on the NPA side, we were at about 0.47% and now we are at about 0.55%. Largely on the micro mortgage book also, what we do is we keep measuring the bucket X collection efficiency. Currently, we see about 95% on-time repayment and about 99.7% to 99.75% bucket X coll

items.statement: ROA 2.2%, ROE 18.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: The business growth witnessed across both our liability and asset franchise in Q1 translated into a healthy financial performance with profit after tax at INR317 crores, resulting in ROA of 2.2% and ROE of 18.2%.

items.statement: CASA ratio target ~30% by end FY27, on track or slight over-delivery
items.quote: Of cost as CASA ratio also, we are, whatever we had projected, we are very much committed or we may over deliver slightly.

items.statement: Secured loan mix target 56% by March FY27 maintained
items.quote: Ashlesh, we maintain the same guidance of 56%. 56% of secured by exit March '27.

items.statement: New business lines (gold, vehicle, agri) contribute 7% of loan book, 9% of disbursements
items.quote: Together, the new business lines of gold, vehicle and agri have contributed to 7% of the gross loan book, while the disbursement share was at 9% in Q1.

items.statement: Unsecured Fast Track loan pilot completed, ready for scale-up; pre-owned car pilot in Karnataka; mid-corporate lending commenced; purchase invoice discounting added to MSME
items.quote: Highlighting a few new initiatives on assets front. Unsecured Fast Track loan has completed successful pilot and is ready for a scale-up. This is a pure digital product with the utilization of account aggregators and bureau details. Pre-owned cars has been piloted in Karnataka. It will be creating a growth engine within our vehicle loan business. Lending to mid-corporates has commenced with disbur

items.statement: 1.72 lakh new micro banking customers added in Q1; borrower base growing after 7 quarters of degrowth
items.quote: After seven quarters of degrowth, borrower base has started to grow, supported by 1.72 lakh new customer additions in Q1, marginally above the Q4 FY '26 numbers.

items.statement: Gold loan new-to-bank customers increased to 40% in Q1 due to 100+ new branch activations and microfinance demand
items.quote: If you look at this quarter, we have activated more than 100 branches in gold loan, and that leads to new customer acquisition also. At the same time, we have seen that the demand in microfinance customers have also increased in Q1, leading to new customers from this segment also to come in. So these two factors combined has changed the numbers.

items.statement: Liability focus on top 8 and top 30 markets delivering 75% YoY CASA growth and 36% overall growth
items.quote: Number two, from beginning, we have guided that our focus on liability side is in top 8 and top 30 markets, where we are seeing robust growth of roughly 75% Y-o-Y growth on CASA and overall 36% growth.

items.statement: Affordable housing yields maintained despite competition due to semi-urban focus and INR16-20 lakh ticket size
items.quote: Yes, so on the affordable housing side, our markets are semi-urban, largely urban and semi-urban. We are not present in the metros. We would be present in a small way in the metros. We are present in about 580 to 590 branches. So that has given us a very robust distribution network to be able to maintain growth. And a INR16 lakh to INR20 lakh ticket size also is the right mix that we have found to

items.statement: RBI forex hedging cost dispensations welcome; repo rate unchanged at 5.25%
items.quote: RBI in its June MPC review meeting decided to keep the policy repo rate unchanged at 5.25% while maintaining a neutral policy stance. The forex hedging cost dispensations by RBI have been a welcome step and should help in liquidity and hence stabilizing the deposit rates.

items.statement: Liquidity coverage ratio ~132% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We remain in sound liquidity health with liquidity coverage ratio around 132% for the quarter, reflecting a well-balanced approach towards growth and liquidity management.

items.statement: IBPC, refinance, securitization options available to optimize funding and margins
items.quote: We also have some more avenues to support the funding, if at all required and to optimize the margin, we have the IBPC refinance, securitization options are also open for us.

items.statement: Weather-related uncertainties from El Nino pose risk to H2 economic activity if kharif sowing delayed
items.quote: We believe that harvest of rabi crops has led to better outcomes currently, but any delay in sowing of kharif crops might impact H2 economic activity. This remains a key monitorable.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance for FY27: Rs 95 crore per quarter standalone, Rs 130 crore per quarter consolidated
items.quote: So, the guidance on the employee cost that we gave earlier was Rs 95 crores for the standalone entity and close to around Rs 130 crores per quarter for a consolidated entity. That is the run rate that we are looking at.

items.statement: Other expenses guidance for FY27: 8-10% increase over FY26 base
items.quote: Some things may work out on the AI side. That's why the in the April month we gave a target that 8% to 10% increase on the FY25 -26 number will be the target run rate number for this particular financial year.

items.statement: TER changes fully passed to intermediaries, no margin dilution
items.quote: Mohit, as you can see from our yield number, there are no dilution as far as the margins are concerned. So basically, whatever the impact of the TER changes has been there, we have passed on the impact to all our intermediaries, and there's no impact on our margin number as such.

items.statement: Mutual fund quarterly average AUM reached Rs 3,92,691 crore, group AUM slightly over Rs 20,00,000 crore
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, our mutual fund franchise continued to strengthen with quarterly average AUM reaching Rs 3,92,691 crores, contributing to UTI AMC's total group AUM of slightly over Rs 20,00,000 crores.

items.statement: SIP AUM grew 8.05% YoY to Rs 45,595 crore; gross SIP inflows Rs 2,502 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: SIPs remain a key driver of sustainable growth, with our gross SIP inflows of Rs 2,502 crores during the quarter and SIP AUM increasing 8.05% year-on-year to Rs 45,595 crores.

items.statement: UTI Alternatives total commitment Rs 3,843 crore, up from Rs 2,679 crore YoY; SDOF IV at Rs 887 crore, MOF II at Rs 321 crore
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, UTI Alternatives has an AUM with a total commitment of all active funds, including the co -investment portfolio manager, of Rs 3,843 crores, which is an increase from approximately Rs 2,679 crores in June of 2025.

items.statement: PMS AUM at Rs 12,15,000 crore; EPFO AUM at Rs 10,63,000 crore; PMS declined Rs 3,16,000 crore QoQ due to EPFO mandate transfer
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, UTI AMC's PMS AUM stood at Rs 12,15,000 crores, while EPFO AUM was at Rs 10,63,000 crores. The implementation of the revised EPFO mandate and consequent transfer of assets led to a decline of Rs 3,16,000 crores in the PMS AUM on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Industry average AUM grew 12.6% YoY to Rs 84.18 lakh crore; investor folios near 28 crore
items.quote: the mutual fund industry data, which continued to demonstrate strong structural resilience during the quarter with average AUM reaching Rs 84,18,486 crores in June 2026, registering a robust year-on-year growth of approximately 12.6% from the same period in June 2025.

items.statement: Added 3.89 lakh folios (total 1.42 crore) and 2.51 lakh new PAN investors; presence in 699 districts
items.quote: We added approximately 3.89 lakh folios, taking our total live folio base to 1.42 crores. We also added 2.51 lakh new investors as measured by their PAN as of 30th June 2026. This has been supported by one of UTI AMC's enduring competitive advantages, that continues to be the breadth of our distribution franchise with presence in 699 districts across India.

items.statement: Digital purchase transactions up 23.93% YoY to 60.9 lakh in June 2026
items.quote: digital purchase transactions reaching 60.9 lakh in June 2026 from 49.14 lakh in June 2025, a year -on-year increase of 23.93%, underscoring the growing adoption of digital platforms.

items.statement: Equity assets 70% of mutual fund AUM vs industry 62:38 equity-to-non-equity ratio
items.quote: We remain particularly encouraged by the improving quality of our asset mix, with equity assets across both active and passive strategies accounting for 70% of our average mutual fund AUM, compared to the industry's equity-to-non-equity mix of 62:38 ratio, reflecting our continued focus on long-term wealth creation.

items.statement: Launched MOF II; SDOF IV secured ~Rs 900 crore commitments; passive pipeline includes Nifty 500 ETF, BSE Sector Leaders ETF; active pipeline includes balanced hybrid and sectoral debt funds
items.quote: We also launched our second multi -opportunities fund, MOF II, and continue to see strong investor interest in Structured Debt Opportunities Fund 4, which is the fund we launched earlier this year. This has secured commitments of approximately Rs 900 crores as of 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Targeting first-time investors aged 18-25 (SIP registrations up 18.6% QoQ to 98,127) and 26-40 life-stage segment
items.quote: in the first quarter of FY27, we saw about 18.6% increase on a quarter -on-quarter basis on the SIP registrations which happened between the age group of 18 to 25. They have now jumped up to, in this first quarter itself, to 98,127.

items.statement: Digital marketing partnership with Google reached over 10 crore unique individuals in past nine months
items.quote: Additionally, our digital marketing partnership with Google has expanded us to reach over 10 crores unique individuals over the past nine months, significantly expanding our engagement with India's potential investor base.

items.statement: AI voice assistant V AANI handles over 60% of inbound calls; launched customer experience channel in Mumbai
items.quote: Our AI -powered voice assistant V AANI continues to transform customer servicing and now handles over 60% of inbound calls, improving both responsiven ess and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Flow market share in equity significantly lower than stock market share; focus on SIP and performance improvement to close gap
items.quote: We need to ramp up our flow market share in equity, because our flow market share in equity is significantly lower than our stock of AUM market share in equity products. So that remains the focus area in terms of the number that we need to take up.

items.statement: Large & mid-cap fund achieving 3-3.5% share of industry net sales; mid-cap fund positive net sales YTD; aggressive hybrid averaging 2-3% industry net sales
items.quote: if you look at the large & mid-cap fund that is actually the fund in which we are having maximum traction at this point of time, and based on the month, I think we are pushing almost 3% to 3.5% in terms of our share of net sales on that strategy.

items.statement: Yields: equity/hybrid 72-73 bps, ETF/index 8 bps, cash/arbitrage 12 bps, fixed income ~20 bps
items.quote: Yield for the equity and hybrid fund is close to around 72 basis points, 72- 73 basis points. ETF and index fund is around 8 basis points. Cash and arbitrage funds are at around 12, and for the fixed income fund is around close to around 20 basis points.

items.statement: Final dividend of Rs 40 per share approved (95% payout ratio); maintaining >95% payout policy; no buyback under consideration
items.quote: The shareholders of the company have a pproved a final dividend of Rs 40 per equity share at the Annual General Meeting held on 21st July 2026, representing 95% of the pay-out ratio

items.statement: Mission 2031 target: manage 2x current AUM; organisation well-staffed for this scale
items.quote: we think there is scope for us to manage 2x our current AUM because we've already made all the commensurate investments that we would need in terms of people, technology, etc. Of course, you have some sort of upgrade cycles in all of this, but otherwise, we are well -staffed to be able to do that.

items.statement: International flows negative for ~2 years due to negative India sentiment and scheme underperformance; viewed as cyclical
items.quote: What you are seeing in terms of the flows over the last, I would say, actually, almost 2 years, combination of both the lack of appetite for India, I should actually say negative sentiment towards India and the fact that our own scheme has struggled in terms of performance over the last two years.

items.statement: Investment performance not where management wants it; working on process readjustments and talent to improve execution
items.quote: Investment performance is where, we are not where we would like to be, in my opening remarks I made the call investment excellence, and we've not managed to execute well on that. So that is where we are, sort of working with the team to see what we need to do in terms of both process readjustments and talent to make sure that we are able to execute better.

items.statement: CMD guided 25% revenue growth for full year FY27 with stable margins
items.quote: I remain confident of delivering 25% revenue growth for the full year with stable margins.

items.statement: Management expects FY27 EBITDA margin similar to FY26 full year level
items.quote: For current financial year, for the full year, as we guided during the commentary also, we are expecting a similar kind of margin as we had for full year FY '26.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex was INR56 crores; INR15 crores at Indichem, INR41 crores at ACL mainly for battery chemical project, pilot plant and maintenance
items.quote: capex for Q1 FY '27 stood at INR56 crores, out of which INR15 crores were at the Indichem site, remaining INR41 crores in ACL site, which is primarily diverted towards the battery chemical project at the Jhaghadia site. And then pilot plant at our Sachin site and maintenance capex.

items.statement: FY27 planned capex includes ~INR50 crores electrolyte additives spillover, ~INR40-45 crores pilot plant, ~INR40-45 crores maintenance; R&D center and land acquisition capex to be announced later
items.value: INR50 crores + INR40-45 crores + INR40-45 crores
items.quote: For FY '27, capex is largely the spillover capex of electrolyte additives as well as the pilot plant capex, which is around INR50 crores and around INR40 to INR45 crores of maintenance capex, that is what the already planned capex for this year.

items.statement: Indichem plant construction ahead of schedule; capex completion expected by end of Q2 FY27, revenue from next financial year
items.quote: this is getting constructed even before the schedules and expected to get -- capex is expected to get completed by end of this quarter. And maybe from next financial year onwards, we will have the revenue coming up from that plant.

items.statement: Battery chemicals plant trial run completed, commercial supply started; capacity 2,000 MT VC + 2,000 MT FEC; expect full utilization in 3 years
items.quote: we have a capacity of 2,000 metric tons for VC and 2,000 metric tons for FEC. So it's a total 4,000 metric ton capacity and for which we are more than confident that we will be able to hit the full capacity utilization by end of 3 years.

items.statement: Electrolyte additives Phase 2 (third product) capex completion by end of Q2 FY27, trial runs soon
items.quote: Phase 2, which is for the third product of our Electrolyte Additives segment, which is going on schedule. And as we mentioned earlier also by end of Q2 FY '27, we would be completing our capex. So that looks very well on track, and we are expecting the trial runs to commission very soon.

items.statement: Pharma Intermediates capacity utilization: Sachin 83%, Ankleshwar 23%, Jhagadia 55% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: For the capacity utilization for the Sachin unit, the capacity is 83%. For Unit 2 at Ankleshwar, it is 23% and at Unit 3 Jhagadia, 55% for the quarter.

items.statement: CDMO revenue target INR1,000 crores; confident to beat target based on healthy pipeline
items.quote: we have already guided the market that we would be hitting INR1,000 crores revenue from our CDMO business. That is based on our confidence and looking at our upcoming product pipeline for our CDMO business. And we are very much confident to not only achieve this target. And in fact, we are confident to beat this target.

items.statement: Four validated CDMO products expected to generate revenue from H2 FY27; each product peak potential INR50-100 crores per year
items.quote: For these products, we have already mentioned that these are already validated products. And with regulatory approval in place, we are expecting revenue to kick in from H2 FY '27 onwards. And on a revenue potential side, these all products are expected to generate revenue between INR50 crores to INR100 crores for each year at a peak.

items.statement: Segment margins: Specialty Chemicals ~24%, Pharma Intermediates ~36%
items.quote: So with regard to margin, our Spec Chem business is having around 24% margin and Pharma business is having around 36% margin.

items.statement: Phasing out commodity chemicals in Specialty Chemicals; replacing with higher-margin BFC, battery chemicals and new specialty products
items.quote: we are gradually phasing out commodity chemicals from this financial year, replacing them with newer higher-margin products.

items.statement: AI driving structural CPU and memory chip demand growth, supporting semiconductor chemicals outlook
items.quote: AI is starting to push CPU demand higher and that's pulling memory chip demand up right along with it. At a time when supply is already tight. To us, this isn't the passing phase. It is a structural phase.

items.statement: Working capital 99 days in Q1 FY27 vs 91 days in Q4 FY26; driven by higher inventory days offset by debtor/creditor improvement
items.quote: Our working capital for the quarter stands at 99 days versus 91 days in Q4 FY '26. This was driven by improvement in debtors and creditors, which was offset by higher inventory days.

items.statement: Net cash and cash equivalents INR314 crores as of 30 June 2026
items.quote: Net cash and cash equivalents were around INR314 crores as on 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Electrolyte subsidiary diluted 10% stake to ARZ as pre-agreed equity for business partner responsible for business development and sales
items.quote: this is basically we awarding our business partner, their equity share, which was decided earlier only. This is the one -- the partner is one who actually has been there with us since the starting of this business, when we started with the product development and then the marketing of all those.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance ~INR150 crores for FY27 including annual increments and one-time performance bonus
items.quote: We should typically look at around INR150 crores of employee cost for the current year.

items.statement: Other expenses expected to remain at Q1 FY27 run rate for rest of FY27; savings from solar project and operational efficiencies
items.quote: whatever the expense for the quarter, we are looking the similar kind of expense for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Battery chemicals supplied to multiple customers in North America, Korea and other geographies; not single customer dependent
items.quote: it's not driven by single customer. There are multiple customers. We have time to time shared that we have a number of customers already in place for both VC and FEC. And they are geography -- in terms of geography, they are based in North America also, they are based in Korea also and other part of the world.

items.statement: CDMO concentration risk to dilute as 30-40 new molecules developed annually; diversified by nature
items.quote: annually, we are developing around 30, 40 molecules and submitting to the different customer at a different level of investigation or I can say the innovation. So it is continuous. And out of that, some are moved to the second phase, third phase, fourth phase like that way.

items.statement: No plans to forward integrate into APIs or electrolyte salts/LiPF6; will stick to core strengths in intermediates and additives
items.quote: we do not have any plan move to the upward in the value chain. We do not compete our customer. That's our policy, and we would like to stick to it.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Gulf persist but team secured raw material availability and supply continuity
items.quote: We began the financial year on a turbulent note, driven by geopolitical tensions in the Gulf. While these tensions persist, our team has done a commendable work in securing raw material availability and ensuring supply continuity.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to remain at current levels or around this level for the whole year.
items.quote: We are hopeful of the margins remaining at this level or around this level. The current quarter looks good. And we are hopeful of it carrying forward at these levels for the whole year.

items.statement: Volume growth target for the year is historically in the range of 8% to 11%.
items.quote: Historically, we've always been doing volume growth in the range of 8% to 10% to even 11%. So, we see ourselves getting that much of volume growth during this year also.

items.statement: Export revenue and sales expected to remain at same level for coming quarters.
items.quote: We anticipate the export revenue and the export sales will be in the same level for the quarters to come.

items.statement: Margins anticipated to continue at stellar levels for at least next 1 or 2 quarters.
items.quote: But obviously, we anticipate the margins would be continued to be at a stellar levels for at least the next 1 or 2 quarters to come.

items.statement: Healthy demand across key end-user industries drove performance.
items.quote: Our performance during this quarter was driven by a healthy demand environment across our key end-user industries, coupled with disciplined execution across the businesses.

items.statement: PHPO segment grew 18% YoY driven by personal care, healthcare and pharmaceutical demand.
items.quote: The PHPO segment continued to be our primary growth engine, registering an 18% year-on-year growth, driven by sustained demand from the personal care, healthcare and pharmaceutical sector.

items.statement: PIO business grew 28% YoY supported by transformer, power and rubber manufacturers.
items.quote: Our PIO business also delivered a robust performance, growing 28% year-on-year, supported by healthy demand from the transformer, power and the rubber manufacturers.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 16.20% in Q1 FY27 from 5.1% in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded to 16.20% compared with 5.1% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Gross margin spread expanded to INR 28,145 per kilolitre vs INR 8,274 in normal environment.
items.quote: Gross margin spreads expanded to approximately INR 28,145 per kilolitre compared with approximately INR 8,274 per kilolitre under a normal operating environment.

items.statement: Export volumes increased 54% YoY; exports contributed 51% of consolidated revenue vs 37% last year.
items.quote: Exports continued to perform strongly during the quarter with export volumes increasing by approximately 54% year-on-year. Exports contributed approximately 51% of consolidated revenue compared with around 37% in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Capex plans being drawn up and will be announced in next quarter or so.
items.quote: But yes, our capex plans will be shortly announced. We are drawing up the same, and we'll get back to you on that in the next quarter or so.

items.statement: Total capacity is fungible across PHPO, PIO and lubricant segments; PHPO exceeds 50% of total sales.
items.quote: Please note that the capacity is totally fungible among all the products. So, you will never get segment-wise. PHPO will continue to be in the excess of around 50% of our total sales.

items.statement: Price increases taken across all segments except automotive lubricants where it was delayed.
items.quote: So, the price increase has been across the segment, except a bit for the lubric -- automotive lubricant category, where it is more of a dealer distributor network. The price increase has been taken even in that category but obviously got with a little delayed manner.

items.statement: Agile sourcing strategy shifted buying from Middle East to domestic and South Korean base oil producers due to Hormuz disruptions.
items.quote: But apart from that, we have started -- we've changed our sourcing strategy, buying more from domestic base oil producers as well. So that helped us in navigating the situation. And we could get our key raw material, which is base oil from our suppliers.

items.statement: Focus remains on PHPO and PIO segments; transformer oil expected to have robust growth due to rising electricity demand.
items.quote: See, the company continues focusing on the PHPO category. But having said that, the process and insulating oil category also has done a fantastic growth in the previous quarter. items.statement: Export realization differential vs domestic is about 5-6%.
items.quote: there is about 5%, 6% differential between exports and domestic.

items.statement: Standalone company is debt-free; consolidated borrowings relate to trade finance and Texol subsidiary term loan which is reducing.
items.quote: On the borrowing front, the stand-alone company that is Gandhar Oil, is absolutely debt-free. The borrowing, whatever you see is in Texol, that is our overseas subsidiary. Most of the borrowing is in the form of working capital funding. There is also a bit of term loan funding over there, which was given for setting up of the plant initially. So obviously, over the period, the term loan funding is

items.statement: Trade payables days not increased; 90% within 90 days; INR 600 crores of INR 900 crores not yet due.
items.quote: So, the trade payables in number of days has not gone up. Out of that INR900-odd the trade payables, there is INR600 crores, which is not yet due. On a basic -- historical basis, even currently, 90% of it is within 90 days.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East, Hormuz Strait disruptions, crude/base oil price volatility and supply chain disruptions remain key risks.
items.quote: The operating environment remained challenging, shaped by heightened geopolitical tension in the Middle East, concerns surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, volatility in the crude oil and the base oil pricing and intermittent disruptions across the global supply chains.

items.statement: South Africa entry strategy being worked out; more clarity expected in next 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: The strategy for the South African arm is being worked out. There will be much more clarity being emerging in the next 1 or 2-odd quarters.

items.statement: Targets ~10% volume growth for FY27 and FY28; value growth depends on gold prices
items.quote: Broadly, we are targeting around 10% volume growth going forward. Internally, our primary focus remains on volume growth, and we believe that achieving around 10% growth in volumes is a reasonable target.

items.statement: Two new showrooms finalized (Jabalpur ~3,750 sq ft FOCO, Dahod ~3,200 sq ft COCO); fit-out underway
items.quote: We have successfully finalized the locations for new showrooms in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, and Dahod, Gujarat. All key agreements, approvals, and necessary formalities have been completed. Fit-out and showroom development activities are underway at both locations, and the stores will be operational soon.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume growth ~1-2% YoY; revenue growth 58% driven by gold prices; demand recovering after price stabilization
items.quote: When we compare Q1 FY27 with Q1 FY26, we have delivered volume growth of approximately 1% to 2%. The balance growth has largely been driven by higher gold prices.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps YoY to 11.01%; PAT margin expanded 82 bps to 7.55%
items.quote: At operating level, EBITDA increased by 70% year-on-year to INR93.99 crores in Q1 '27 as compared to INR55 crores in Q1 '26. EBITDA margin expanded by 80 basis points year-on-year to 11.01% as compared to 10.21% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Studded (diamond) mix 6-7% currently; target 12-15% by March 2028 (2-3x increase)
items.quote: As of now our business is doing like between 6% to 7% of the studded mix. And we have targeted by March '28, we would like to increase up to 12% to 15% on an overall basis.

items.statement: Gold inventory mix: 22-kt ~80%, 18-kt ~15%, balance 14-kt and lower
items.quote: As of today, if we look at our overall gold jewellery inventory mix, 22-karat jewellery accounts for nearly 80% of the total gold jewellery inventory, while 18-karat jewellery contributes around 15%. The balance comes from lower-karatage products, including 14-karat and other categories.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth 52% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Operationally, the company continued to maintain healthy customer engagement across all the stores. Our same -store sales growth stood at 52% on an overa ll basis

items.statement: Hedging via real-time replenishment (3-4x daily), old gold exchange, Gold Metal Loans (100% backed), MCX positions; inventory at weighted avg cost ~Rs 1.2L vs market ~Rs 1.5L
items.quote: The company continues to leverage exchange led procurement of gold, gold metal loan, and hedging mechanisms on the commodity exchange platform to mitigate gold price volatility, support margin stability, and improve working capital efficiency.

items.statement: Uses Gold Metal Loans for inventory funding; no explicit debt quantum or repayment discussed
items.quote: This add itional inventory will be 100 % be backed by a GML which is one of the products provided by the banks and nominated agencies

items.statement: Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15% in May 2026; near-term cost and demand sensitivity noted
items.quote: While the recent government announcement and increase in gold import duty from 6% to 15% in May 2026 has introduced near-term cost and demand sensitivity, the long-term fundamentals of the sector remain intact.

items.statement: In Indore, single D.P. store revenue exceeds combined revenue of 14-15 stores of leading national brand
items.quote: In Indore, if we consider all formats of a leading national jewellery brand, there are approximately 14-15 stores in the city. However, the combined revenue of those stores is still lower than the revenue generated by a single D.P. store.

items.statement: Launched e-commerce website and mobile app (Play Store, App Store); expanding on online marketplaces; digital discovery to complement store-driven model
items.quote: This quarter, we launched our e -commerce website and mobile application, which are now available on both the Play Store and App Store. We ar e also actively expanding on leading online

items.statement: Targets 20% volume growth for rest of FY27 and 20% EBITDA growth
items.quote: So, looking ahead, we are still working towards achieving a growth of 20% for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Targets INR 200-250 crore annual capex to support 20-25% volume growth
items.quote: As a company now from the last one year, we have been working a little diﬀerently from what we have been doing in the past. Now, our thought process is to put in about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to keep growing at 20% -25% kind of volume

items.statement: Targets INR 800 crore cumulative operating cash flow for FY27 and FY28 combined
items.quote: The INR 600 odd crore was our guidance for last year and this year combined. Last year , our target was INR 250 crore against which we did almost INR 330 crore. items.quote: We took a hit from INR 7 a kg blended and we came down to INR 2 a kg, wherein we absorbed all that cost. Now once we had that cost increase, the new orders that we booked were again with the right prices. There we were getting even in fact INR 8 a kg blended margin. items.statement: EBITDA margin recovered to INR 7-8/kg from mid-May as new orders reflect higher costs
items.quote: From almost May 15th, we are already back to INR 7-INR 8 per kg margin.

items.statement: IHT and OHT specialty wires target INR 10-20/kg EBITDA at optimal utilization
items.quote: In IHT, I would say about INR 10-20 INR a kg, in that range.

items.statement: B2C segment delivers 20-30% higher EBITDA per tonne vs B2B in low carbon wire
items.quote: And o n the margin front also, this is better than our B2B side margin. I would say about 20% -30% extra EBITDA per tonne is what we are able to get from the B2C segment as compared to B2B in the low carbon front

items.statement: IHT wire approvals at 80% of customers; targeting 50% capacity utilization next month and 60-80% by year-end
items.quote: In IHT, just to give you an example, next month we are targeting 50% capacity utilization. Within this year, we see that we will reach to an optimum utilization level already in IHT, because our approvals are on a very advanced stages. 80% of the customers have already given us approvals.

items.statement: Maintains advance payment to suppliers for procurement leverage; uses payable financing to fund inventory days
items.quote: As of now , we do not want to negotiate with our suppliers and get payable days because that will also , in some of the other way , bring down our negotiation power . We are the largest purchaser of wire rods in the country

items.statement: Growing at 20% vs industry 7-8%; gaining market share by absorbing cost spikes on committed orders to support customers
items.quote: The industry is growing at 7%, 8%, whereas as a company, we have grown at 20% all these years. The thought process is to grab market share every year. items.statement: Q1 volume 112,000 tonnes (+7.7% YoY); revenue INR 1,168 crore (+25% YoY); EBITDA INR 57 crore; PAT INR 20 crore
items.quote: Our revenue for the quarter is INR 1,168 crore, reﬂecting a growth of around 25% on a year - over-year basis. EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 57 crore, and net proﬁt for the quarter is INR 20 crore. As Pranav Sir already mentioned, our sales volume for the quarter is 112,000 metric tonnes as compared to 104,000 metric tonnes in Quarter 1 FY 2026

items.statement: Geopolitical tension in West Asia caused temporary natural gas disruption and cost spike; gas prices remain elevated
items.quote: This year, we entered the quarter with an added layer of complexity as the ongoing geopolitical tension in West Asia created near -term volatility across global supply chain, leading to a temporary disruption in the availability of natural gas. items.statement: Steel Cord export unviable due to INR 10-15/kg higher domestic raw material cost vs China
items.quote: Export for us is not going to be a good or lucrative business because of the raw material price. items.statement: Sanand facility expansion underway (90,000 tonnes wire capacity); excess land may be partially sold
items.quote: We have already started expanding in the Sanand facility with wire CAPEX, about 90,000 tonnes, but we have excess land, we will take a call on that deﬁnitely. Some part of it we might sell, not completely, because we are expanding already there
