items.quote: So, it's about 4% to 5%, depending on which quarter you're looking. The difference between pre and post will be between 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Organization restructuring completed: moved to business unit structure with centralized consumer intelligence, marketing, digital, data and AI functions; hiring talent for deeper capabilities
items.quote: The organization restructuring is now complete. We have reorganized into a business unit structure for the sharper accountability and speed, while centralizing consumer brand marketing, digital, data and AI initiatives to build leverage capabilities across the portfolio.

items.statement: Like-for-like retail growth of 11.6% in Q1; online B2C share of revenue increased to 18% from 15% YoY
items.value: 11.6% LFL growth; online B2C 18% revenue share
items.quote: We delivered a robust like-for-like of 11.6% in retail with an overall retail growing at 18%. Online B2C grew over 38%, taking its share of revenue to 18% from 15% a year ago.

items.statement: West Asia conflict remains watch item for supply lines, raw material, fuel prices, forex; inflationary pressures from wage hikes across states and adverse forex
items.quote: The continuing West Asia conflict remains a watch item for us. It has a potential to impact supply lines, raw material, fuel prices, and forex rates. We're taking active steps to mitigate and protect our performance, including very tight control on costs and a possible revision of product prices, if necessary.

items.statement: Other income expected to stabilize around INR 7-8 crores per quarter; last year Q1 had one-time gain from COCO store closures and Ind AS 116 unwinding
items.quote: Going ahead, we believe that whatever closure will be a balanced mix of stores, and we don't seem to be seeing any adverse spikes in other income. So, it is largely going to be stable around INR7 crores, INR8 crores, what we reported this time.

items.statement: Internal ROA target of 1.5% for FY2027 but will not go below 1.3%
items.quote: Our internal target for ROA of 1.5%; but I am saying that we will not go below 1.3% for this year.

items.statement: ROE trajectory to end FY2027 slightly better than 14.14% achieved in FY2026, aiming for 15% Lakshman Rekha
items.quote: This year, we will try to touch the Lakshman Rekha, if we can execute it right.

items.statement: Fee income guidance of 16-17% of overall income for full year FY2027
items.quote: We will try to come back to our guidance of around 16-17%.

items.statement: Wholesale loan growth 35-40% and gold loan growth 30-35% in FY2027
items.quote: wholesale will continue to grow the way it is growing at this point of time, which is somewhere between 35% to 40%. Gold, I thin k we should be growing around 30% to 35%, somewhere in that range

items.statement: Gold loan mix to reduce from ~54% to ~50% in FY2027 and ~30% by FY2030
items.quote: Directionally, we will continue to have gold loans somewhere around 50% this year and then gradually reduce over the next three to four years, closer towards 30%.

items.statement: Wholesale book target ~32% of portfolio by FY2030, similar to gold loan mix
items.quote: We want to take it to around 32% by FY2030, and gold lo an, which is somewhere around 54%, will also reach the similar level by FY2030

items.statement: CASA to grow at same pace as deposits from FY2028; CASA to grow faster than term deposits from FY2029
items.quote: The plan is that CASA will grow as much as the deposits only from FY2028 onwards. FY2029 onwards, CASA will grow higher than term deposits.

items.statement: Unsecured retail lending focus only from FY2028 onwards, not in FY2027
items.quote: we have said that unsecured business is som ething we will start focusing on only from FY2028 onwards, not in FY2027

items.statement: Deposits grew 26% YoY to significantly outpace industry 13.4%; CASA ratio 19.41%
items.quote: recorded a strong Y- o-Y growth of 26%, significantly outpacing the industry growth rate of 13 .4%. CASA ratio stands at 19.41

items.statement: Advances grew 24% YoY vs industry 18.6%; yield on advances 10.65%
items.quote: On the asset side, the advances grew by 24% Y-o-Y as against industry growth of 18.6%. Yield on advances for Q1 FY2027 stood at 10.65%.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio ~54% of book; repledging (LAS) portfolio down from Rs2,100 Cr to Rs60 Cr, will run off next quarter
items.quote: on the repledger business, though we could have done it til l first April this year- we had taken a call, around two to three quarters back that we will not renew these loans. That i s why the portfolio came down from R s.2100 Crores to around R s.60 Crores now . It has gone down considerably and will run off by next quarter

items.statement: GNPA 1.75%, NNPA 0.39%, PCR 77.96% without PWO; provisioning buffer Rs198 Cr including Rs105 Cr contingency
items.quote: quality metrics, the GNPA and NNPA ratios for the quarter stood at 1.75% and 0.39% respec tively. PCR stands at 77.96% without PWO, almost 78%, which is high compared to what we used to have before. Bank is holding a provisioning buffer of around R s.198 Crores, over and above regulatory requirements, including a contingency provision of around R s.105 Crores

items.statement: Accelerated loan provisioning policy continued to aid transition to ECL framework
items.quote: Contingency provisions are held intact, and bank is c ontinuing with the accelerated loan provisioning policy, which will aid the bank in tra nsitioning towards the ECL framework

items.statement: Technology transformation completed; rolling out retail liability acquisition channel; transaction banking systems in place or coming in 3-4 months
items.quote: went extremely well and now we are going to leverage that. W e are rolling out our retail liability acquisition channel, because now we can launch the products we want to. Even on the transaction banking side, say trade, supply chain or CMS – some systems are already in place and some will be in place in the next three to four months

items.statement: Network of 868 branches and 835 ATMs as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: On the distribution side, we have a network of 868 branches and 835 ATMs as on June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Implemented RBI gold loan regulations; stopped repledging (LAS) business; end-use monitoring controls in place
items.quote: most of the regulations, we have implemented and there are both p ositives and challenges. Positives are on the renewal side and operationally th is becomes a little easier. There are challenges in terms of end use monitoring where we have a lready put in many controls and are working on continuous

items.statement: Insurance business slowed due to stricter compliance measures after RBI scrutiny on mis-selling
items.quote: of various noise in the system, etc with RBI itself looking into customer complain ts more objectively, we took a step back on our insurance and put a lot of things in place

items.statement: CRAR 19.96%, Tier-1 18.96%; risk weights ~42% of exposure; well capitalized
items.quote: On the capital side, CRAR continues to be well above the regulatory requ irement and stood at 19.96%. Tier-1 ratio stood at 18.96%. Our risk weights are at aro und 42% of the total exposure and we are very well capitalized given this low

items.statement: Building retail liability franchise: sales team in place, products launched, targeting granular deposit growth
items.quote: have launched our systems last year- Products are being built- Sales team is being put in place. It is kind of a high road , which we have to take towards building that franchise

items.statement: Management declined to update FY27 guidance, stating it is early in the fiscal year and they will reassess in future quarters.
items.quote: I guess we're 1 quarter into our fiscal year. So, we will hold that for now, and we will look at how we progress through the quarter.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.5% in Q1 FY27, below guided trajectory, driven by transient items.
items.quote: The gross margin performance translated into an EBITDA into an adjusted EBITDA margin of 9.5% for the quarter. We recognize this is below the trajectory we have guided to.

items.statement: Gross profit margin declined to 20.9% in Q1 FY27 from 23.3% in Q4 FY26 due to customer-specific disruptions and a security incident.
items.quote: Gross profit margin for the quarter was 20.9%, which is lower than the levels we exited FY26 at.

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 9.6% year-on-year and 1.8% sequentially to INR 11,515 million in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Our Q1 revenue from operations was INR.11,515 million, representing an increase of 9.6% year-on-year and 1.8% sequentially.

items.statement: New product portfolio (RCS, WhatsApp, IP messaging) revenue grew 14% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter, outpacing overall company growth.
items.quote: New product revenue grew 14% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter, growing meaningfully faster than the company as a whole.

items.statement: Management expects gross margins to recover to the 21.5%-23% range seen over the last 5-6 quarters as transient items reverse.
items.quote: depending upon how much of this correction we are able to do, we can land up in that range of 21.5% to 23%, which we've been operating over the last 5 or 6 quarters.

items.statement: Volume growth expected to increase 10%-15% in the next couple of quarters as seasonality sets in.
items.quote: as we see the season setting in, we were expecting the volumes to grow by 10% to 15% in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Acquired Heltar Technologies via slump sale for brand, IP, platform, and team; fully funded from internal accruals; expected to close in coming weeks.
items.quote: On July 13, we signed a business transfer agreement to acquire the identified business undertaking of Heltar Technologies Private Limited on a slump sale basis.

items.statement: Heltar acquisition adds AI-native omnichannel engagement platform with chatbot, automation, and analytics across WhatsApp, RCS, and voice.
items.quote: Heltar is an AI-driven omnichannel customer engagement platform. At its core, it turns communication workflows into fully automated, self-running programs from a single prompt to a live customer journey.

items.statement: Net revenue retention stands at 98%; one key high-margin customer impacted by product upgrade, expected to recover.
items.quote: the net revenue retention stands at 98% for the year. We had slight impact in just one of the key customers, which we are also working on recovering over the future period.

items.statement: Cash conversion was weak in Q1 due to delayed collections from large clients in India and UAE; full-year conversion expected to revert to 75%-100% EBITDA-to-cash flow.
items.quote: the cash position for the rest of the year should go back to the typical 75% to 100% conversion from EBITDA, which we have, the EBITDA to cash flow from operations conversion.

items.statement: Company has a dividend program returning a portion of cash to shareholders; Heltar acquisition funded from internal accruals.
items.quote: we have a dividend program in place where a certain portion of the cash is returned to the shareholders as well. So that is the way we are looking at the cash utilization.

items.statement: No material increase in headcount expected; employee count to hover around 800 with backfilling and selective hiring for product and sales growth.
items.quote: we would typically hover around the kind of the 800 count mark. It's not going to materially change, but we are backfilling where we need to and then recruiting to support our product and sales growth.

items.statement: Security incident at Colombian subsidiary Masivian under investigation; platform operating under enhanced controls; minor additional costs possible beyond current provisions.
items.quote: The investigation remains ongoing with the support of our cybersecurity specialist. And the platform continues to operate under enhanced controls and monitoring.

items.statement: Wage hikes completed; salary costs expected to remain flat at current run rate in coming quarters.
items.quote: The wage hikes are behind us. So now we're at a run rate. And we don't materially expect the salary cost to go up. It's pretty flat in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Management avoids aggressive pricing in WhatsApp/RCS to protect margins, accepting potentially slower growth vs competitors.
items.quote: There has been some aggression in the marketplace on the pricing of WhatsApp and RCS, and we don't really want to participate around that. We would intend to keep our margins intact and healthy.

items.statement: RCS offers better margins than WhatsApp/SMS; focus on promoting RCS in geographies with exclusive arrangements to improve blended margins.
items.quote: RCS definitely, Bharat, provides a better margin option for aggregators. So our focus and our efforts will be more to take and promote that as a channel.

items.statement: Non-SMS revenue compounded at over 40% annually over past 4 years; central to medium-term revenue mix ambitions.
items.quote: it directly accelerates our non-SMS revenue, which has compounded at over 40% annually over the past 4 years, and is central to our medium-term revenue mix ambitions.

items.statement: No future impairment or bad debt issues expected; past issues are resolved.
items.quote: Yes, that's a fair reflection of the position. So, we're not expecting any future issues like that. They're all in the past.

items.statement: ILD business remains a growth challenge near-term but sustains at current levels; large opportunities being pursued with long conversion timelines.
items.quote: ILD business, which was the principal source of revenue decline through FY26, continues to be a challenge in terms of growth for the near term.

items.statement: Heltar platform enables integration with multiple LLMs (Anthropic, Meta, voice AI) and Meta's new conversational AI framework; flexible for enterprise choice.
items.quote: They offer different LLMs to the enterprise. They have if it is Anthropic or Meta or whichever AI the enterprise wants to use, including voice AI. So it's fairly flexible.

items.statement: Masivian keeping affected customers and regulators informed during security incident investigation.
items.quote: Masiv is keeping the affected customers informed and the regulators informed, as the investig ation is progressing

items.statement: Truecaller partnership in testing phase with enterprise customers across multiple geographies; too early to quantify revenue or margin impact.
items.quote: We are testing the Truecaller as a platform with certain customers. I mean too early for us to identify exactly what kind of margins we can bring in.

items.statement: Claro multi-country firewall deployment delayed but expected to go live this quarter; select networks only, not all Claro operations; fixed plus variable revenue model.
items.quote: we're fairly hopeful that this quarter, we should be up and running with them. And we will have some tangible revenues coming the way very soon.

items.statement: Non-SMS margin profile varies by region; no commitment on margin expansion or dilution from Heltar deployment this year; will take time to assess.
items.quote: for this year, we would not want to commit to any margin expansion or dilution because of these product solutions or the non-SMS product solutions. We'll have to play it out.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY27 maintained at 0.8-1.0%
items.quote: So for this quarter, the credit cost is at 0.8%. And like we had indicated at the start of the year, our guidance is that we will be somewhere between to 0.8 to 1.00%, and we stay by that guidance.

items.statement: ROA guidance for FY27 maintained at 1.6% by Q4
items.quote: Yes. There is no change in the guidance from what we had indicated at the start of the year.

items.statement: ROE guidance for FY27 maintained at 13-14%
items.quote: So as we had indicated in our guidance at the start of the year, Shailesh, we will be in the range of 1.3% to 1.4% and we continue with that guidance at the end of the first quarter.

items.statement: Cost of funds expected around 7.5% for rest of FY27
items.quote: Yes. You can expect the cost of fund to be at around 7.5% for the rest of the year.

items.statement: NIM expected to remain stable at Q1 levels for FY27
items.quote: Yes, yes, very similar to what we are having at the end of Q1.

items.statement: Opex ratio target for FY27 at 67-70%
items.quote: Yes. So I think if you look at our opex, the kind of target that we have assumed for ourselves to be in the range of around 67% to 70%.

items.statement: CGFMU claims for FY27 expected at INR 13-15 crores remaining
items.quote: No. So we have a very small cohort left to be claimed in the current financial year. It will be somewhere around INR13 crores to INR15 crores.

items.statement: PSL income guidance: INR 10-15 crores for Q2-Q3, INR 15-20 crores for Q4 FY27
items.quote: I think for the next 2 quarters, you can expect that our PSL income will be around INR15-odd crores -- INR10 crores to INR15-odd crores And Q4 may be somewhere around INR20-odd crores.

items.statement: Microfinance industry regaining momentum with improving borrower behavior
items.quote: The broader microfinance industry has started regaining momentum with improving borrower behavior and gradual recovery in business activity.

items.statement: Assets growing faster than deposits indicating loan demand
items.quote: The other will be that if you may have looked that assets have started growing at a faster pace as compared to the deposits, which is a good sign. So there's a demand in the market for loans.

items.statement: Yield on advances expected to stabilize at 17.2-17.5%
items.quote: So, on yield, I think our stabilized yield would be in the range of like KC was mentioning will be in the range of 17.2% to 17.5% kind of a thing.

items.statement: No immediate pricing changes planned despite cost of funds pressure
items.quote: Yes. At this particular point in time, we don't foresee an immediate change in pricing across products.

items.statement: Gross advances grew 32.5% YoY to INR 14,376 crores
items.quote: Our gross advances stood at INR14,376 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 32.5%.

items.statement: Deposit base grew 29.4% YoY to INR 14,634 crores, retail deposits at 87.3%
items.quote: Our deposit base stood at INR14,634 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 29.4%. The share of retail deposits stood at 87.3% as of June 2026.

items.statement: Digital deposits at INR 2,222 crores with INR 6 crores daily accretion
items.quote: Deposits sourced to our digital channel stands at INR 2,222 crores with an average daily accretion of INR 6 crores.

items.statement: CLOU business scaling: 6 lakh active users, adding 1.5-2 lakh monthly
items.quote: Currently, we have around closer to 6 lakh customers who are utilising it and around 9 lakh to 10 lakh customers who have been approved. Every month, probably we are onboard around closer to 1.5 lakh to 2 lakh customers.

items.statement: CLOU convenience fee income INR 18 crores with INR 13 crores expense in Q1
items.quote: In this particular quarter, our convenience fee income from the CLOU business has moved to INR18 crores for the quarter. And there is a corresponding increase in the CLOU-related expenses by around INR13-odd crores.

items.statement: Plan to add ~50 branches in Q2-Q3 FY27 focused on inclusive finance and CV
items.quote: We will be adding around closer to 50 branches in this quarter and next quarter. But more importantly, not all our products are available in all our present locations.

items.statement: Mortgage business to expand from 25% to 40-45% of branches by year-end
items.quote: Probably we are present in no more than 25% of our current branches in terms of mortgage business. Intent would be to take it to at least 40% to 45% towards the end of the year.

items.statement: GNPA 6.5%, NNPA 1.2% (adjusted 2.9% and 0.3% with CGFMU receivable)
items.quote: On asset quality, our GNPA stood at 6.5% and NNPA at 1.2% as of June 2026. In absolute terms, GNPA stood at INR 931 crores and NNPA at INR170 crores against which INR134 crores is receivable under the CGFMU scheme. Adjusted for this receivable, the GNPA and NNPA stands at 2.9% and 0.3%.

items.statement: MFI slippages moderated to <INR 20 crores/month, INR 53 crores in Q1
items.quote: I think the good part to note is that if you look at our MFI businesses, our slippages have moderated significantly. Our slippages on a monthly basis are less than INR20 crores a month.

items.statement: Collection efficiency stable at 99.2-99.5%, not expecting 99.9%
items.quote: We are not certainly seeing 99.9%, it's a real portfolio. So to that extent, it will not -- in a period like this. We may not see anywhere closer to 99.9%. We are comfortable in terms of clocking around 99.5%, 99.6%.

items.statement: CV PAR 11.5% elevated due to fuel prices, expected to normalize by Q3
items.quote: Yes. See, we have around 75% -80% of book is in used CV. So as such, the PAR has been slightly elevated in the last quarter more because of the fuel prices increase and also in terms of load availability due to the crisis in Middle East.

items.statement: Individual loans (Vikas Loan) now 80% of monthly onboarding, reducing JLG exposure
items.quote: I think over a period of last 2-3 years, we have been slowly and consciously moving out of this JLG model and moving into individual loans. To that extent that individual loans contribute around 80% of our monthly onboarding.

items.statement: Secured retail assets (CV, mortgages) growing faster than inclusive finance
items.quote: The secured assets are focused on commercial vehicle and mortgages, which are having good traction, and we continue to focus in terms of having a growth rate probably which will be higher than the inclusive finance growth in this portfolio.

items.statement: IBPC funding accessed at <5% as MFI book quality improved
items.quote: A couple of things, which have improved in this quarter, for example, is that with the improvement in the MFI book, the IBPC market has opened up for us again. We took an IBPC funding at around 5%, a little less than 5%.

items.statement: Tier 2 capital raise planned this quarter as existing Tier 2 expires next year
items.quote: We have a Tier 2, which will be expiring next year. So we are out in the market, evaluating our proposals for raising fresh Tier 2. We hope all things going well. We hope to close something this quarter.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 20%, targeting 20-22% range
items.quote: Yes. So at this particular point in time, our capital adequacy fee is 20%. We have a Tier 2, which will be expiring next year. So we are out in the market, evaluating our proposals for raising fresh Tier 2.

items.statement: CASA ratio at 21%, focusing on granular CASA growth
items.quote: Our CASA ratio stood at 21%, and we continue to focus on granular CASA over the coming quarters.

items.statement: SA cost reduced from 5.7% to 5.5%, FD cost at 8.1%
items.quote: If you look at SA, last quarter, our SA had a cost of fund of about 5.7%, which we have been able to bring it down to 5.5%. And insofar our fixed deposit costs are concerned, it is about 8.1%.

items.statement: Raised long-term Blinkit EBIT margin guidance to 4% and Adjusted EBITDA margin to close to 6% from previous 5-6% range
items.quote: We think at this point we're likely to end at the higher end of the range that we had guided earlier and hence, the communication.

items.statement: Confirmed long-term GAAP EBIT margin target of 4% including ESOP and depreciation
items.quote: Yes, there are ESOP expenses and there is depreciation. We are accounting for both of them

items.statement: Blinkit growth primarily from existing cities, not geographical expansion
items.quote: Most of it is from existing cities.

items.statement: Older customer cohorts spending 3x vs three years ago, driven mainly by frequency growth not AOV
items.quote: Directionally, most of it is frequency growth. With passage of time for a customer cohort, we see that NAOV stabilizes. It grows but only slightly, and most of the growth comes from frequency growth.

items.statement: Food delivery MTU growth driven by both new user acceleration and higher frequency
items.quote: We've seen acceleration in new users that we've added to our platform in the last three or four quarters. This is a function of the category growing as well as more customers transacting more frequently.

items.statement: Blinkit NAOV expected to remain flat year-on-year, not grow meaningfully
items.quote: Generally, Aditya, we're not expecting the NAOV to grow from here. If you look at year-on-year, it's flat. That accounts for seasonality for Q1, and we broadly expect NAOVs to remain in the same range.

items.statement: Contribution margin impacted by minimum wage hikes in multiple states and larger store ramp-up
items.quote: There was some increase in the cost of doing business in the quarter because there were a lot of states which implemented increase in minimum wage. That was one factor. Also, we are opening larger stores. So, some of the contribution is also impacted by the earlier stages of these stores, as the contribution is lower than when we open smaller stores.

items.statement: Inventory losses at 1.8% of NOV, asymptotic and not expected to improve materially
items.quote: It has been fairly asymptotic so far. We don't expect it to be materially much better.

items.statement: Blinkit capex per store guided at INR 2.5 crore including warehousing; lumpiness makes shorter periods appear higher
items.quote: We should look at this number more longer-term because there is a lumpiness in investment here because while we are presenting the information as capex per store, a large part of the capex is in warehousing and that investment is lumpy.

items.statement: Blinkit store throughput target 2,100-2,200 orders per day per store for new larger format
items.quote: Based on the new economics for the stores, since they are bigger stores, you're looking at 2,100-2,200 OPD per store, per day.

items.statement: Existing Blinkit stores being upgraded to larger properties, not regularly modified in place
items.quote: We've been upgrading a lot of the existing stores to find more optimal properties which are larger and move to larger store sizes.

items.statement: Competitive intensity peaked in Q1 FY27, now more predictable as rivals focus on grocery subsidies with limited room to deepen
items.quote: First quarter, so far, was the peak of competitive intensity that we have seen till date because the number of players is higher and everybody was more aggressive. But when we look at competitive intensity and the way that it has evolved over the last few quarters, what we are seeing is that most of the competition is coming in the form of subsidies to customers on products and on delivery fees an

items.statement: Discount-led growth unsustainable in quick commerce due to limited shelf space; Blinkit passes scale benefits as sustainable value not temporary discounts
items.quote: We usually don't look at what discounting is happening from peers beyond a certain point. Our baseline is usually what we think product prices can sustainably be in the long run, and that is what we index towards.

items.statement: Net working capital improved to 14 days from 18, targeting 12 days steady-state via lower inventory days
items.quote: What has helped us reduce it from 18 to 14, and what we think will reduce it further to 12, is largely lower inventory days than we initially thought we would need to carry.

items.statement: Tax refund of higher advance tax deposited due to ambiguous expense allowability; non-structural, may recur occasionally
items.quote: The tax refund was on account of a refund because there were certain expenses which were ambiguous on whether they'll be allowable. We had deposited higher advance tax and there's a refund towards that. That's normal course of business and such things may come up once in a while going forward as well, but nothing structural.

items.statement: Blinkit cohort retention data includes all acquired customers (including those who churned); full cohort shows 3x spend over 3 years
items.quote: Yes, it's for the overall cohort. If you acquire 100 customers in the quarter, the percentages are for the entire 100. If 40 of them never show up again, then the retention is only 60%.

items.statement: Food delivery defending share against Toing/Ownly via price competitiveness in aggressive markets; Gold free-delivery threshold cut to INR 99 from INR 199
items.quote: One of the bits that we did was last year when we dropped the eligibility for free delivery for a gold member to INR 99 instead of INR 199. That's one example of how that reduces the cost for a customer who is seeking a low-value order.

items.statement: District (going-out) operates in 5 categories; dining-out and movies largest, retail stores and events showing promise but early
items.quote: Today, dining-out and movies are the bigger categories. Amongst the newer ones, retail stores and events could be the more promising ones, but we are still early on that journey.

items.statement: District customer base smaller than food delivery/quick commerce; will operate in fewer cities
items.quote: It's definitely a smaller customer base, Garima, for going-out compared to food delivery or quick commerce. The number of cities that we will do in this business will also be much smaller than the other two businesses.

items.statement: No ROCE currently as Blinkit EBIT margin negative; ROCE framework for future investment decisions only
items.quote: Right now, of course, the EBIT margin is negative. There is no ROCE. We are all talking about future here. It's a business and industry which is in the making right now.

items.statement: Nugget enterprise AI product in stealth mode; traction good but will share more in coming quarters; costs largely manpower
items.quote: We are still, in some ways, in a little bit of stealth mode here. It's an enterprise AI product business and we are seeing good traction in that but it's an evolving market, as you know, the entire AI space

items.statement: Payables increase driven by business scale (trade payables) and expense payables fluctuation; not over-optimizing brand terms
items.quote: Trade payables have increased because of the increase in the scale of the business. At this point, we are not necessarily trying to overoptimize on terms with brands. It's really more driven by scale, and the expense payables keeps fluctuating.

items.statement: Food delivery restaurant count dip due to LPG supply issues causing some restaurants to go offline temporarily
items.quote: It's a little bit of an impact from the LPG situation in the country last quarter because of which some restaurants went offline. That's why you probably see a slight dip in the monthly active restaurant count.

items.statement: Export revenue target of at least 8% of total revenue in next two years
items.quote: We've mentioned this before is that the plan is to have at least 8% of exports coming in in the next two years' time.

items.statement: Export growth target of 40-45% for FY27
items.quote: We are looking into havi ng a growth of 40%, 45% in our exports for this financial year

items.statement: OEMs indicating strong volume projections from September through March across CV segments
items.quote: We have been indicated very good projections from September onwards right up to March. And it's just that these kind of schedule lines or projections usually don't come into manufacturers as early as June and July.

items.statement: Tractor segment demand consistent and on track to increase contribution meaningfully
items.quote: Demand has been consistent, on track to increase contribution meaningfully over the coming years.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 63 bps YoY to 12.23% due to operational efficiency, better product mix, and backward integration benefits
items.quote: The margins right now are at -- for quarter one are at 12.23%, up 63 bps Y-o-Y, reflecting operational efficiency, a better product mix, and benefits from our backward integration.

items.statement: Steel price pass-through of INR 4,700 per tonne settled retrospectively from mid-July; conversion cost increase settlement expected soon for CV industry
items.quote: So steel, there has been a very recent settlement which has been given retrosp ective to all the suppliers. This has just happened around the 15th of July where INR4,700 per kilo has been given

items.statement: Trailer axle prices increased 3-5% from April 1; further 1-2% hike planned for conversion cost increases
items.quote: It is approximately between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Trailer axle and suspension volumes grew 30% YoY in Q1; Q1 axle volume ~9,500 units, suspension volume ~3,200-3,300 units
items.quote: The extruded axle beam has started production and volumes on axles and suspensions have increased 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: European Tier 1 supplier orders expected from H2 FY27; four to five product segments with one in mass production, three scheduled from H2

So, we expect the revenue of this to start being shown in the balance sheet in, I think, Q3 next year onwards.

items.quote: In our plastic recycling business, our nylon and polyolefin recycling verticals, we expect over a 20% growth this fiscal, followed by a mid -teen growth through FY 2030, while maintaining a stable EBITDA margin of between 10% to 15%, supported by tightening EPR regulation and our continued focus on value-added products.

And bulk of this will be going in, what you call it, expansion of the pyrolysis lines, adding 2 more pyrolysis lines to take us to the 45 KTA that I alluded to in the opening comments as well as the rCB plant, which will be commissioned by October of 2026.

items.statement: Committed to overall INR250 crores investment plan with ~INR100 crores remaining for FY28-29 including 30,000 tons pyrolysis and 12,000 tons rCB in Gujarat

items.statement: Pyrova achieved longest continuous reactor run; pyrolysis and crumb rubber facilities largely stabilized; rCB plant commissioning starting next month, targeting October 2026
items.quote: During the quarter, the plant achieved its longest continuous reactor run since commissioning, an important milestone because stable, continuous operation is the precursor to throughput, reliability, and commercial performance in a continuous pyrolysis process. items.statement: Pyrova achieved 25-day continuous run in July meeting industry threshold; rCB commissioning by October 2026; tire industry approval expected several quarters later
items.quote: The threshold in the industry from a performance perspective is for a run of minimum of 25 days in a month and a 4 -day shutdown on the pyrolysis. I'm pleased to share that in the month of July, we've been able to achieve that level of performance, which gives us the confidence that the technology that we have chosen and the throughput that we are now generating is here to stay.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 233 bps to 11% despite raw material cost inflation; operating leverage, product mix and cost discipline drove improvement
items.quote: Importantly, that growth led to an EBITDA rise of 60% to INR174 million and EBITDA margin expansion by 233 basis points to 11%, even as raw material costs rose sharply during the quarter.

items.statement: Reclaim Rubber EBITDA margin target 10-14% post Pyrova synergies; Pyrova standalone target 15-20% post rCB; Plastics target 12-15%
items.quote: I do believe Reclaim Rubber business, post synergy with Pyrova will get to an EBITDA margin of between 10% to 14%. The Pyrova business post the commissioning of and stabilization of rCB would get to between 15% to 20% EBITDA margin. And the plastic business, which is now kind of stable, but we need to start -- continue to build scale, should generate an EBITDA margin of between 12% to 15% as well.

items.statement: Reclaim rubber volumes grew 12% YoY; export volumes rebounded 20% as U.S. tariff easing normalized customer order patterns; domestic demand healthy with market share intact
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, the segment revenue grew 34%, of which Reclaim volumes grew 12% and reclaim export volumes rebounded 20%, as customer order patterns normalized following the easing of U.S. tariffs. Domestic demand stayed healthy with our market share staying intact.

items.statement: Engineering Plastics volumes grew 27% driven by domestic automotive OE demand and appliance sector approvals; polyolefin volumes flat due to selective customer and product focus
items.quote: Engineering Plastics grew volumes 27%, helped by domestic automotive demand and a more favourable virgin nylon pricing environment. And our Repurposed Polyolefin business, run mostly through our subsidiary, delivered a clear turnaround in profitability.

items.statement: Raw material costs rose sharply; pricing contracts on quarterly/half-yearly/annual basis with lag; achieved large part of cost pass-through to customers
items.quote: But against this backdrop, I mean, our raw material prices have also moved up as is evidenced in the gross margins. And as you know, that most of our pricing contracts run on either quarterly, 6 monthly or annual basis. So, there's generally some amount of lag before the pass -through entirely happens. But we would say we've been able to achieve a large part of the pass-through on raw material cos

items.statement: Natural rubber inflation expected to persist due to El Niño year; synthetic rubber linked to oil prices; no visibility on price reversal timing
items.quote: I think at least the projections, the way things stand, it will take some time before prices will reverse, especially on account of this being an El Niño year, there are expectations of natural rubber to behave in a certain way. Synthetic rubber prices, as you are aware, is very, very closely linked to the oil prices.

items.statement: Export volumes restored to pre-tariff levels with healthier margins; indirect export volumes to non-U.S. markets not fully recovered; new product categories driving adoption in North America, Europe, Latin America
items.quote: Return in the business of direct exports to U.S. is back and at a healthier margin than before. Indirect business impact on account of the tariff to non -U.S. countries is not fully recovered and hopefully will be recovered through the rest of the year.

items.statement: Serve 8 of top 10 global tire manufacturers; over half revenue from exports; first reclaim rubber manufacturer with ISCC Plus certification
items.quote: What distinguishes GRP is not a single product or a single plant. It is a 5 -decade integrated platform spanning reclaim rubber, crumb rubber, and now tire pyrolysis oil and rCB along with engineering plastics, serving 8 of the top 10 global tire manufacturers and with more than half of our revenues coming from exports.

items.statement: Customer conversations combine sustainability, mechanical/chemical properties, and commercial value vs virgin materials; reclaim rubber seen as strong alternative amid virgin rubber volatility
items.quote: I think it's a combination. I wouldn't say it's either or. I mean the circular materials that we offer our positioning is always on the basis of value, not just price. We do offer or our products do offer a certain set of advantages when it comes to mechanical and chemical properties in addition to being sustainable and helping them fulfil their end-of-life obligation.

items.statement: Plastic EPR norms tightening; brand owners more serious about implementation; regulatory tailwind strengthening for recycled content supply chain
items.quote: Behind this sits a regulatory tailwind that is clearly strengthening. Plastic EPR norms are getting tighter, and brand owners are becoming markedly more serious about implementation.

items.statement: Regulatory developments mandate use of circular plastic materials in automotive; expected to create demand maturity for nylon business
items.quote: But we remain fairly bullish because there are regulat ory developments (factually corrected) that govern use or that mandate the use of circular plastic materials in automotive. And we continue to hope that, that will create demand maturity for our nylon business.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved by 8 days to 86 days in Q1 FY27 reflecting operational discipline
items.quote: Beyond the operating performance, we improved our working capital cycle by 8 days to 86 days, reflecting continued operational discipline.

items.quote: I think the deleveraging is -- I mean, timing of that is not entirely in our hands. So, we will take appropriate calls on deleveraging as the opportunity again presents itself. At least as things stand now, we do expect these businesses to start generating cash flow.

items.statement: Renewable energy at 48% of standalone power consumption in FY26, up from 37%; ahead of 50% by FY28 target, expected to reach in current fiscal
items.quote: Renewable energy accounted for approximately 48% of GRP's stand -alone power consumption in FY 2026, up from 37% a year ago. This is well ahead of our stated target of 50% by FY 2028, which we should reach in the current fiscal.

items.quote: As the integration across our end -of-life tire value chain has deepened, we have regrouped our operations into 2 segments: Rubber Recycling, comprising Reclaim rubber, Custom Die Forms, and the newly instituted Pyrova Energy; and Others, comprising Engineering plastics, our Windmill operations, and the residual Polymer composite business.

items.statement: Polymer Composite business permanently shut down due to tariffs; indirect export volumes to non-U.S. markets not yet recovered; rCB commercialization dependent on customer approvals and technology stabilization
items.quote: Loss of volume on account of polymer composite is permanent. Return in the business of direct exports to U.S. is back and at a healthier margin than before. Indirect business impact on account of the tariff to non -U.S. countries is not fully recovered and hopefully will be recovered through the rest of the year.

items.statement: rCB plant commissioning by October 2026; several quarters needed for tire industry approval; carbon black manufacturer market as interim opportunity

So, while we will commission the plant in October of 2026, I do believe it will take us several quarters before we can get a product which can be approved and used by the tire industry.

items.quote: It will be a minimum of 10%, but we are targeting more towards 15%, so we are looking at somewhere between 12% and 15% this year.

items.statement: Value-added product mix target for FY27 at 63-64%
items.quote: In terms of our value-added percentage, we are looking at between 63% and 64% for this year.

items.quote: think compared to last year, we should get about 30% higher. The average value will be 30% higher this year

items.statement: Long-term volume growth target of 15% from FY28 onwards
items.quote: Next year, we might look at a better situation, depending on how the worldwide sourcing will be.

items.statement: FY30 revenue target of 5,000 crores reaffirmed as conservative estimate

items.quote: In terms of our guidance for fiscal '27, that is 20% growth on last year's PAT of INR 34.3 billion and hence, approximately INR 41 billion of PAT. Q1 has delivered 33% of that.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 240 billion; H1 expected at 40-42% of full year
items.quote: In terms of the rest of the year, we reaffirm our INR 240 billion pre-sales guidance for fiscal '27, and we expect H1 to be 40% to 42% of the full year, as we had mentioned in the start of the year itself.

items.statement: Medium-term target of ~20% PAT CAGR to exceed INR 85 billion by FY31; ROE moving from ~16% toward 20%
items.quote: Our guidance of about 20% PAT growth over the medium term, taking us beyond INR 85 billion over the next 5 years, i.e., by fiscal '31. Our return on equity, which is currently about 16% in fiscal '26, moving upwards and inching closer towards 20%.

items.statement: Q1 pre-sales INR 46.3 billion (+4% YoY); deliberately low due to no residential launches (normally ~1/3 of pre-sales)
items.quote: Pre-sales for the quarter were INR 46.3 billion, up 4% year-on-year. That is below our trend line, and I want to explain it properly rather than quickly. This was a decision, not an outcome.

items.statement: Q2 pre-sales expected at INR 50 billion or more on back of planned launch calendar
items.quote: In terms of the immediate outlook for Q2, we are off to a good start in July, and we expect pre-sales to be INR 50 billion or more on the back of the planned calendar for this quarter.

items.statement: Full-year launch calendar: 20+ projects/phases totalling ~INR 250 billion GDV, including first NCR launch and continued growth in Bangalore and Pune
items.quote: For the full y ear, the launch calendar carries about 20 -plus projects and phases totalling approximately INR 250 billion of GDV, including our first launch in NCR as well as continued growth in Bangalore and Pune

items.statement: Q1 adjusted EBITDA INR 21.5 billion (+79% YoY) at 43% margin vs 34.4% YoY; PAT INR 13.7 billion (+101% YoY) at 26.9% margin vs 18.6%
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA was INR 21.5 billion, up 79% at a margin of 43% against 34.4% a year ago. PAT was at INR 13.7 billion, more than double the INR 6.8 billion of Q1 FY26 at a PAT margin of 26.9% against 18.6% in the equivalent quarter a year ago.

items.statement: Prolonged Middle East conflict could raise construction costs 1-1.5% over full year, spread over 3-4 year build; project EBITDA impact 35-75 bps assuming no price response
items.quote: If this situation persists for a full year, we would expect project construction cost to rise by between 1% to 1.5%, with spread across a 3 to 4 year build period and assuming no price response; project level EBITDA impact of between 35 to 75 basis points.

items.statement: Data center build largely self-funded from land sales within same park; does not add to group leverage or compete with DevCo for capital
items.quote: The data center build is largely self-funded from land sales inside the same park. It does not add to group leverage, and it does not compete with our DevCo for capital in any significant manner.

items.statement: Data center park infra capex ~INR 500-700 crores over a period for 3 GW development
items.quote: let's say, a number of more like INR 500 crores to INR 700-odd crores that we will incur over a period.

items.statement: Green Data Center Park: 660 acres with ~3 GW power availability; 130 acres sold, further 150 acres to be monetized over 3-4 years at ~INR 600M/acre (~INR 90B sales) funding ~1 GW powered shell on 90 acres
items.quote: Of this, about 130 acres has now been sold, and we expect to monetize a further 150 acres over the next 3 to 4 years at an average of about INR 600 million per a cre, generating approximately INR 90 billion of further sales just from Phase 1 of our land. This will fund the build-out of about 1 gigawatt of powered shell on approximately 90 acres

items.statement: RentCo exit run-rate June ~INR 3B (ex-data centers); target >INR 30B by FY32 (10x), of which ~INR 20B+ from data centers, INR 6B retail/office, INR 4B warehousing/industrial
items.quote: On the broader annuity business, o ur exit run rate for June was approximately INR3 billion without any contribution from data centers. The target is over INR30 billion, i.e., 10x by fiscal '32, of which about INR20 billion plus will come from data centers, INR6 billion from retail and offices and about INR4 billion from warehousing and industrial

items.statement: Data center powered shell rental ~INR 20M+ per MW per annum
items.quote: Yes, a little over INR 20 million, yes.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 4.5B to under INR 50B; net debt/equity ~0.2x vs 0.5x ceiling; avg cost of debt 7.8% (AA rated); DevCo target net debt free in 2-3 years
items.quote: After investments, we still reduced net debt by INR 4.5 billion to now under INR 50 billion. Net debt to equity now stands at approximately 0.2x against our self-imposed ceiling of 0.5x. Net worth is just under INR 250 billion. Average cost of debt is stable at 7.8%, amongst the lowest in the industry, supported by our AA

items.statement: Q1 collections INR 42.1B (+46% YoY); operating cash flow INR 18.9B
items.quote: Collections for the quarter were INR 42.1 billion, up 46% Y -o-Y. That converted to INR 18.9 billion of operating cash flow.

items.statement: Competition rational, led by consumer affinity to trusted brands; Lodha gaining market share across geographies; industry consolidation favoring branded developers
items.quote: The competition in our market remains rational as it is largely led by consumer affinity towards the stronger and the trusted brands. There is a great desire of the consumers to buy a Lodha property, and we have seen that across the new geographies that we have come in.

items.statement: Capital allocation: fund opportunities with brand fit/execution capacity (20% ROCE DevCo, 15% RentCo), regular dividend 15-20% of PAT, then debt reduction, then buyback/special dividends
items.quote: Our capital allocation hierarchy is clear and publicly stated, fund opportunities where there is brand fit and execution capacity, about 20% ROCE in DevCo and about 15% in RentCo, a regular dividend at 15% to 20% of PAT, thereafter debt reduction and thereafter, any surplus towards buyback or special dividends.

items.statement: Prolonged Middle East conflict increases uncertainty; impact not materially negative to FY27 delivery based on current evidence; will update if assessment changes
items.quote: Where this leaves us is that a prolonged conflict increases uncertainty, and I will not pretend otherwise. But on the evidence in front of us today, the impact does not look materially negative to our fiscal '27 delivery. If Russia-Ukraine is any guide, this kind of volatility works itself out over the medium term, and we will, of course, keep you updated if that assessment changes.

items.statement: Net order book stands at ₹240 billion with EVs accounting for 64% and Robotics and Physical AI at 3%
items.quote: And at the end of Q1 FY27, our net order book stands at 240 billion, with EVs accounting for 64%.

items.statement: EV order book increased to 69 programs across 36 customers with 2 new EV programs and 1 hybrid program added this quarter
items.quote: We have also added 2 new EV programs and 1 hybrid program, which takes our EV order book to 69 programs across 36 customers.

items.statement: Robotics and Physical AI order book totals ₹8 billion with three secured orders adding ₹6 billion
items.quote: Together, these three orders, they add ₹6 billion to our Robotics and Physical AI orderbook, which takes the total order book for Sona Comstar – Q1 FY27 Earnings Call this new vertical to ₹ 8 billion

items.statement: Won ICE differential gear program from traditional North American OEM with order value of ₹2.1 billion
items.quote: We received an ICE differential gear program from a traditional North American OEM with an order value of ₹2.1 billion.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 23.1%, lower by 0.7% YoY due to product mix and higher input prices despite operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 23.1%, which is lower by about 0.7% compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Margins heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases and timing gap in customer recoveries; June showed significant improvement over April and May
items.quote: Margins were heavily impacted by input cost inflation, labor cost increases as well as the timing gap in t he customer recoveries or the pass - throughs

items.statement: Expect recovery measures to become progressively more visible from Q2 onwards
items.quote: We expect that these recovery measures will become progressively more visible from quarter 2 onwards.

items.statement: Demand remained healthy across all markets; India strong in passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers, Europe growing, US improved, China mixed but fastest growing geography due to suspension motor ramp-up
items.quote: Demand has remained healthy across all the markets we serve. India delivered another strong quarter, particularly in passenger vehicles and electric two-wheelers, which was phenomenal.

items.statement: BEV revenue grew 107% YoY to ₹436 crore, constituting 44% of automotive product sales; BEV revenue and mix at all-time high
items.quote: BEV revenue grew by 107% to 436 crores over the same quarter last year. BEV revenue constituted 44% of our automotive product sales.

items.statement: Invested in technology, equipment and product development for Robotics and Physical AI over the past year; already developed products and working closely with customers
items.quote: Over the past year, we've invested in technology, invested in equipment, and we have developed products.

items.statement: Product mix impact from rapid traction motor sales growth dragged margins down as traction motors have lowest margins relative to company average
items.quote: There was also a product mix impact as traction motor sales grew quite rapidly, and as is well known to you, that product category has the lowest margins relative to our average company margin.

items.statement: Fastest growing businesses: EV suspension motors, EV traction motors, and emerging product portfolios including steering bevel boxes, intermediate gears, epicyclic gear trains, input rotor shafts, and railway products
items.quote: Our fastest growing business this quarter was EV suspension motors, followed by EV traction motors, and something that gets l ost in the others category, are emerging product portfolios

items.statement: Secured new business across EVs, hybrids, and ICE across India, Europe, and North America across virtually every product category
items.quote: This quarter we secured new business across EVs, hybrids, and ICE across India, Europe, and North America, and across virtually every product category we operate in.

items.statement: Won hybrid differential assembly order from existing North American customer; won 2 traction motor programs from new age Indian electric two-wheeler OEM
items.quote: This quarter we received a new order from an existing North American customer for hybrid differential assembly, again, surprising but very gratifying.

items.statement: Announced strategic partnership with DENSO comprising two joint ventures: JV1 for high voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems (DENSO majority), JV2 for 2/3 wheelers (Sona majority)
items.quote: The partnership consists of two joint ventures. The first will focus on high voltage electric and hybrid powertrain systems for 4 and 4+ wheel vehicles, so all passenger and commercial vehicle applications, in short.

items.statement: Royalty arrangements are equal and reciprocal: JV2 pays royalties to DENSO for high voltage technologies, JV1 pays royalties to Sona for 2/3 wheeler technologies
items.quote: The royalty arrangements are equal and reciprocal in both. JV2 will pay royalties to Denso for its high voltage technologies, while JV1 will pay royalties to Sona Comstar for our 2 and 3 wheeler technologies.

items.statement: Suspension motor business and all non-traction motor businesses remain completely outside the scope of the DENSO transaction
items.quote: Let me also clarify because we got some calls that our suspension motor business, together with all our other non -traction m otor businesses remain completely outside the scope of this transaction

items.statement: Revenue grew 54% YoY to ₹12,310 crore; EBITDA grew 49% to ₹303 crore; PAT grew 45% to ₹181 crore
items.quote: Our revenue for the quarter grew to 12,310 crores, a growth of 54% over the first quarter of last year.

items.statement: Eastern markets contributed 59% of revenue this quarter, up from 56% last year, showing continued geographic diversification
items.quote: For example, eastern markets contributed 59% of our revenue this quarter. This was 56% last year.

items.statement: Working capital turnover ratio improved due to significant reduction in debtor days; best quarter from operational cash flow perspective
items.quote: Besides this, the working capit al turnover ratio also improved due to a significant reduction in debtor days, which also made this as our best quarter from an operational cash flow perspective

items.statement: Net debt continues to be negative; net debt to EBITDA ratio remains in negative territory
items.quote: Our net debt continues to be negative. Therefore, net debt to EBITDA ratio also continues in a negative territory.

items.statement: Invested around ₹2,750 crore across acquisitions of Comstar, Noveliс, and Railway Business over last 7 years; these 3 businesses contribute ~40% of revenue and ~₹270 crore net annual profit
items.quote: Over the last 7 years, we've invested around 2 ,750 crores across the acquisitions of Comstar, Noveli c, and the Railway Business.

items.statement: Inflation remains biggest near-term challenge; commodities and input costs elevated; trade and geopolitical developments continue to be choppy
items.quote: Inflation continues to be the biggest near -term challenge. Commodities and other input costs remain elevated.

items.statement: More than 35% of revenue comes from products that did not exist in portfolio seven years ago; 19 products conceived, designed, industrialized and scaled entirely through own R&D
items.quote: Today, more than 35% of our revenue comes from products that simply did not exist in our portfolio seven years ago.

items.statement: New products (19) represent ₹1,800 crore annualized revenue business generating over ₹230 crore annual profit based on Q1 annualization
items.quote: If I annualize our quarter 1, together these new products represented 1,800 crore revenue business generating over 230 crore of annual profit.

items.statement: Morgan Stanley estimates global market for radars, reducers, and electric motors could grow 260x, 590x, and 260x respectively over next 25 years, reaching $60B, $1.4T, and $2.5T
items.quote: According to that, the global market for radars, reducers, and electric motors over the next 25 years could grow approximately 260 times, 590 times, and 260 times respectively, like absurdly large numbers.

items.statement: Robotics order book of Rs 800 crore with SOPs starting as early as this quarter and most within 12-15 months
items.quote: They range, some of them are as early as next quarter, some of them next year, but they are not very far in the future. Let's put it that way.

items.statement: JV2 high voltage motor market size estimated at Rs 24,000 crore by 2030 and potentially 3x by 2035
items.quote: Market size, I did say 2030, 24,000 crores, but if you were to look at 2035, this number will be many times that. It will be maybe 3 times that, and that is what we are looking at.

items.statement: JV2 capex intensity low with Rs 1 capex generating Rs 11-12 revenue for high voltage systems
items.quote: It will be at least 11-12

items.statement: No capacity constraints currently; capacity built ahead of market demand
items.quote: Not right now. Vivek Vikram Singh: I can assure you, neither does Vikram. We have always built capacity ahead of markets and that is definitely not our problem

items.statement: EV demand strong in India and Europe; US shifting to hybrids but EV growth still positive
items.quote: India is actually the fastest growing EV market in the world, I think, right now. So India is doing phenomenally well. USA, we are seeing a shift to hybrids as you saw even in one of our events, but the EV market is not doing so well in the US right now.

items.statement: VA per employee declined due to faster growth in motor and railway assembly businesses vs higher value-add driveline
items.quote: So, depending upon which business is growing faster, this ratio tends to change. So while the higher the better is, is obviously the rule, but the thing is that 4.5 times, itself is also very strong.

items.statement: High voltage motor space less competitive due to technology barriers; two-wheeler three-wheeler more competitive but Sona holds leadership
items.quote: High voltage technology is not easy to crack, and hence there will be lesser competitive intensity. I think we'll make a fairly big dent in the market.

items.statement: New product ramp timeline: Year 1-3 no revenue, Year 4 first $1 revenue, Year 5 first $10M, Year 7-8 $100M business; robotics expected faster
items.quote: First 3 years when you make a new product or get into a new technology, you make no money. Year 4, you see your 1st $1 of revenue. Year 5, you start making the 1st $10 million odd dollar number, and year 7 or year 8 is when it becomes a $100 million business.

items.statement: Rare earth magnet restrictions continue; shifted to light rare earth alternatives working fine with no shortage impact on EV traction motor growth
items.quote: Yeah, so then I've answered it, that we shifted to light rare earth alternatives and there is no real magnet shortage as shown by our EV traction motor business growth.

items.statement: JV1 with Denso for two-wheeler three-wheeler traction motors leading; JV2 for high voltage motors following; both structured as one partnership
items.quote: The first, JV will be leading it and the 2nd JV will be following it, so I can't share you the timing exactly. But, the first JV is the one which will kickstart, faster.

items.statement: Robotics product lifecycle unknown as industry still in early generations; generation changes more frequent than automotive
items.quote: I don't think the guys making the robotics right now know also, because even the first generation has not ended its lifespan.

items.statement: Ethical AI guardrails designed before data mapping; radar-based perception provides inherent privacy layer; GDPR compliance for European customers
items.quote: Literally, even before the data structure mapping, you actually designed the guardrails. That what are the guardrails for the data? Also, you must know that because we supply to European customers, GDPR rules are so severe that it has to pass through a v ery high bar for data to be taken

items.statement: Targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over next 5 years for both top line and bottom line
items.quote: we can grow in the range of 15% to 20% CAGR. So 1 year can be here and there because of XYZ reasons. But the way India demand is growing and the plant that the capacities that we have, eventually plant will ramp up and we can have a CAGR growth of 15% to 20% for the next 5 years.

items.statement: Targets ROCE around 20% for new projects including epoxy resin and MPP
items.quote: we would always target to have an ROCE around 2 0%. So we are targeting for that. Rather than giving guidance on margin, I can tell you that ROCE, we are targeting in the range of 20

items.statement: Board approved INR600 crores capex for epoxy resin & formulations (125,000 TPA) and multipurpose plant
items.quote: I'm also pleased to announce that our Board has approved a strategic capex plan for 2 new projects. We are entering into the Epoxy Resin & Formulations with a capacity of 125,000 tons per annum and setting up a multipurpose plant.

items.statement: Capex of INR400 crores each for FY27 and FY28
items.quote: FY28, again, the capex would be in the range of INR400 crores.

items.statement: Epoxy and MPP projects funded 40% internal accruals, 60% debt
items.quote: So around 60% -- 40% will be from the internal around 60% would be from the debt.

items.statement: Epoxy resin capacity 125,000 TPA; pilot plant operational by Q2 FY27
items.quote: In line with our phased development approach, we are also establishing a pilot facility for both epoxy resin and formulations and MPP, multipurpose facility, which is expected to be operational by quarter 2 FY27.

items.statement: ECH capacity expanding from 50,000 to 100,000 TPA; 50% for captive consumption in epoxy
items.quote: After our expansion of new capex of epichlorohydrin. The total capacity of the company will be -- eventually it's around net KTA 1 lakh tons. So out of 50% we would like to consume in-house in the epoxy resin and its derivative and remaining 50% we will sell in the market.

items.statement: CPVC capacity utilization at 50-55% in Q1 FY27; expects ramp-up in H2 FY27
items.quote: CPVC was around 50%, 55%.

items.statement: Targets INR500 crores revenue from multipurpose plant (chlorotoluenes & ECH derivatives) by FY29-FY30
items.quote: our target is to reach all the derivatives, specialty product portfolio, which we are producing in multipurpose plant, along with the chlorotoluene derivatives, we wanted to close to around INR500 crores revenue we would like to target.

items.statement: Epoxy and MPP projects combined peak revenue potential INR1,300-1,500 crores
items.quote: Combining both the projects, the peak can be in the range of INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores -- INR1,300 crores to INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: Chlorotoluenes + MPP combined peak revenue INR700-800 crores
items.quote: once the multipurpose plant commissioned and that starts ramping up, that all put together, we should land end up in the range of INR700 crores to INR800 crores kind of top line.

items.statement: MPP project estimated EBITDA margin 22-23% at optimum utilization
items.quote: So the estimated margin would be in the range of 22%, 23% kind of thing. And again, once we commission the plant, it will take time to ramp up, maybe 1.5 or 2 years' time to reach the optimum level utilization levels.

items.statement: Current ECH realization INR180-185/kg, down from peak INR200-210, now trending up to INR185-190
items.quote: ECH realization is almost close to around INR180 to INR185. Questioner: So the prices have reduced. It was around INR200 to 210, right, earlier? Maulik Patel: Yes. It is compared to all the products which was there during the war time, which has gone to peak, that has reduced. And again, now it has gone down to INR175 level, and I think it is now going up again to

items.statement: CPVC current realization INR110-115/kg; ethylene-based PVC not significantly impacted by MIP on carbide-based PVC
items.quote: currently, the CPVC prices would be in the range of INR115, INR110. So again, now the -- again, how much the price will go up because the impact might come because of the issue in the West Asia where its crude is impacting.

items.statement: Chlorine realization negative INR4,000 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Chlorine realizations have been in the range of around INR4,000 -- negative INR4,000.

items.statement: Energy needs to be met via solar-wind hybrid agreements (40 MW contracted); no further captive power investment
items.quote: We are not going to invest further in the captive power plant. Whatever we are going further, the energy requirement is going to be catered from solar and wind hybrid agreement, which we are doing with the different suppliers on a long-term basis. So we already have a 20 -megawatt hybrid arrangement with one particular agency. Now we are doing -- already we did another contract of 20 megawatts.

items.statement: Glycerin prices driven by palm oil and biodiesel policies, not directly linked to crude oil; logistic costs rising globally
items.quote: The biodiesel policy and based on the glycerin decides which way it is moving and palm oil, the plantation of the palm oil and how the production is coming out in every year based on that glycerin is moving rather than moving in -- moving along with the propylene or the crude oil base, yes. So this is completely different. There is no relation with the crude oil and the current situation.

items.statement: Epoxy resin demand in India estimated 2.5-3 lakh TPA growing double-digit; driven by windmill blades, automotive, construction, renewables
items.quote: the demand for epoxy to our estimate is around somewhere around 2.5 lakh to 3 lakh tons and which we expect to grow in a double -digit percentage from here on.

items.statement: CPVC demand weak in Q1 due to PVC price volatility and monsoon; expects recovery from Q3 FY27
items.quote: If you see the sales will start from quarter 3 and quarter 4 is the major 2 quarters considered as a CPVC for the major growth in the country.

items.statement: Caustic soda demand supported by alumina expansion; India to remain net importer long-term despite capacity additions
items.quote: So, caustic, I believe because of the way the alumina expansion is happening in the country. So, we believe we are going to be net import of caustic continuously in India, irrespective of the capacity addition will happen gradually, which people has announced in the past.

items.statement: Net debt INR474 crores (Jun 2025) vs INR439 crores (Jun 2024); net debt/EBITDA 0.8x vs 0.6x
items.quote: Net debt-to-EBITDA stood at 0.8x as on 30 June versus 0.6x as on 30 June '25 on account of lower earnings for trailing 12 months and also debt increase. We have spent INR62 crores on capex in Q1 '27. Our net debt stood at INR474 crores versus INR439 crores as on 30 June '25.

items.statement: ROCE 16% (Jun 2025) vs 24% (Jun 2024); excluding CWIP, ROCE 18%
items.quote: ROCE stood at 16% as on 30 June versus 24% as on 30 June '25 due to drop in earnings for trailing 12 months and also because of sizable capital work in progress. If you remove capital work in progress then ROCE stand at 18% for Q1 '27.

items.statement: Diversified product portfolio provided resilience; epoxy resin & formulations and MPP to add specialty chemicals and advanced materials
items.quote: Our diversified product portfolio provided a critical resilience in this challenging quarter. While certain segment face tailwinds, our alternative product line stepped into the offset this impact and sustain our overall growth momentum.

items.statement: MIP on PVC mainly impacts carbide-based PVC; ethylene-based PVC (used by Epigral) less affected; helps convince CPVC customers
items.quote: So PVC is a raw material for the CPVC application. And normally, if you see the major difference was coming from -- globally, it is coming from a carbide -based PVC. A carbide -based PVC, which is made out of coal that is having a lower price than the ethylene-based PVC. So I think because of the MIP major effect was on the carbide-based PVC, not on the ethylene-based PVC.

items.statement: West Asia conflict impacting raw material costs, shipping disruptions, logistical constraints; methanol price volatility affecting hydrogen peroxide competitiveness
items.quote: The ongoing West Asia conflict directly impacted the cost structure for both raw materials and finished goods. Furthermore, severe disruption to shipping lines led to the transit delays and the logistical constraints. The market volatility made business execution difficult.

items.statement: KFC store expansion guidance maintained at 60-80 stores for the year
items.quote: The earlier guidance for KFC in terms of 60 to 80 stores in a year remains the same. That continues. No change in that particular guidance.

items.statement: Pizza Hut store expansion to remain cautious for calendar year 2026
items.quote: On Pizza Hut, we have called out that we will be quite cautious in terms of store expansion. That w as the case for calendar year '25. That will remain the case for even calendar year '26

items.statement: Sri Lanka store opening guidance unchanged despite profitability challenges
items.quote: So we won't react. We have said this previously also, our quarter's performance, whether good performance or bad performance, is not good enough for us to react in terms of the store opening plan for the immediate future.

items.statement: Sri Lanka SSSG guidance maintained at high single digit
items.quote: On Sri Lanka, the guidance, we should be in that same region. Sanjay Purohit: High single digit

items.statement: Demand environment remained similar with no material improvement
items.quote: I don't think there's been any material improvement in the demand environment. I would say it has remained similar.

items.statement: KFC SSSG of 5% driven by company-specific value strategy not macro demand
items.quote: Some of the upside at KFC, that we are seeing is as a direct outcome of the work that we have done to improve sales.

items.statement: Pizza Hut achieved 1% SSSG after five quarters with positive dine-in and takeaway
items.quote: Pizza Hut had SSSG of 1%, as mentioned by Sanjay, after five quarters of positive SSSG.

items.statement: Sri Lanka delivered 9% SSSG in LKR terms
items.quote: SSSG was very healthy at 9% and overall revenue grew by 14% in LKR terms.

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA margin 13%, up 80 bps YoY
items.quote: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA was up 23% year-on-year. Margin was 13%, up 80 basis points.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 8.4%, up 37% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA came in at INR75 crores, up 37% year-on-year and margin was 8.4%.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin 16.9%, up 120 bps YoY
items.quote: The overall restaurant EBITDA came at very healthy 16.9%.

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA loss 3.6%, down 110 bps YoY due to higher energy cost
items.quote: However, higher energy cost impacted the restaurant EBITDA, which came at loss of 3.6%, down by 110 basis points.

items.statement: KFC took 2% price increase during quarter, Pizza Hut took 2% towards end of quarter
items.quote: This was a combination of lower discounts compared to last year as well as price increase of 2% during the quarter.

items.statement: Price hikes taken in two instalments: KFC 1% in April and 0.5-1% in June; Pizza Hut 1% each in two instalments
items.quote: We have taken it in two instalments. One percent was taken in April, 0.5% to 1% was taken in June. The s ame thing for Pizza Hut, it was taken across two instalments of 1% each

items.statement: Price hikes restricted to 50-60% of inflation, rest managed through supply chain efficiencies
items.quote: We have always called out that we never take price hikes exactly same as inflation. So we would typically restrict our price hikes to 50% to 60% of the inflation, and the rest of the impact we would try and manage through efficiencies on our supply chain.

items.statement: Discount reduction of 50 bps to 1% combined with 2-3% price hike, but APC remains flat as customers rebalance basket
items.quote: So between the price hike, where we said 2% to 3%, and the discount reduction, and it could be anywhere between 50 bps to 1%. So that's the total impact you can see that would have on the consumer.

items.statement: Added 16 KFC, 5 Pizza Hut India, 1 Pizza Hut Sri Lanka stores in Q1; total count 1,074
items.quote: We added sixteen KFC restaurants, five Pizza Hut in India, one Pizza Hut in Sri Lanka. Our total restaurant count was 1,074 as of 30th June 2026.

items.statement: KFC digital kiosks implemented in ~75% of stores
items.quote: Our digital kiosks are implemented on about 75% of stores.

items.statement: KFC dine-in and takeaway mix improved from 57% to 59% driven by value campaigns
items.quote: Dine-in and takeaway sales for KFC improved from 57% to 59%. This is on basis of the strong dine-in takeaway value campaigns.

items.statement: Pizza Hut dine-in and takeaway mix stable at 50%
items.quote: Dine-in and takeaway mix remained same as the previous year at 50%.

items.statement: Sri Lanka dine-in and takeaway mix at 60%, similar to last year
