items.statement: Expects full-year PAT to be 4.5x-5x Q1 PAT of INR 1,401 crore
items.quote: So typically, we see that the first quarter by the end of the year, it is not just multiplied by 4, but sometimes it is more like 4.5x to 5x that you will see at the end of the year.

items.statement: Capex guidance INR 25,000 crore for FY27; Q1 spend INR 5,300 crore; Q2 expected INR 6,000-6,500 crore
items.quote: On the capital expenditure, for the first time, we spent INR 5,300 crores in the first quarter. And we expect that the INR 25,000 crores that we have lined up for this year, we'll be able to implement.

items.statement: Renewable capacity 6.7 GW currently; adding 2.5-2.7 GW in FY27 to cross 9 GW by year-end; 200 MW commissioned, 500 MW in next few weeks
items.quote: Now this year, we will set up 2,500 megawatt to 2,700 megawatt. Already 200 was commissioned and another 500 will get commissioned in the next few weeks.

items.statement: TBCB projects: Jalpura-Khurja line completing in days, Bikaner-Neemrana by October; pumped hydro 1,000 MW (3x334 MW) with first unit annuity bid, two units in talks with Tata Steel and others; Shirwata PSP 1,800 MW to start later this year;
items.quote: One will get completed, the Jalpura -Khurja line in the next few days. The other one, the Bikaner -Neemrana line will also get commissioned by October.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT up 11% to INR 1,401 crore, EBITDA up 8% to INR 4,249 crore in Q1 FY27; 27th consecutive quarter of PAT and EBITDA growth
items.quote: Tata Power has done exceedingly well, INR 1,401 crores of PAT in the quarter, which is an 11% increase. And so also the EBITDA increase has been 8% to INR 4,249 crores.

items.statement: Rooftop revenue grew ~100% YoY in Q1; 4-year CAGR: revenue 58%, EBITDA 68%, PAT 84%; FY27 target 60-70% growth; added battery storage for residential/industrial
items.quote: In fact, last year, we grew by 100%, and this year also, we have plans to grow by about 60% to 70%.

items.statement: Module plant operating at full capacity, crossed 1,000 MW in Q1; cell production catching up after line change; record PAT in manufacturing
items.quote: For the first time, our module plant we crossed 1,000 megawatt in the first quarter, and we expect that we have virtually peaked over there or peaking over there in terms of our module production.

items.statement: Net debt to underlying EBITDA 3.41x, net debt to equity 1.25x; within self-set guardrails for INR 25,000 crore capex
items.quote: Our net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.41 and our net debt to equity is 1.25. This is within the guardrails that we have set for ourselves for the investment.

items.statement: Mundra SPPA with Gujarat concluded; plant operating under Section 11; tariff per SPPA; advanced stage for 3 state approvals by August, fourth by September; procurers taking 100% capacity
items.quote: Mundra, we have concluded SPPA with Gujarat. The plant is operating, though it is operating under Section 11 for the purpose of scheduling. The tariff we are charging the procurers as per the SPPA.

items.statement: Pumped hydro 1,000 MW (3x334 MW) commissioning from early CY2029 with 2-month gaps; Shirwata PSP 1,800 MW construction to start later this year after approvals
items.quote: We are doing very good construction work over there. And we expect that beginning of calendar year 2029, we will be in a position to commission the plant.

items.statement: Renewable curtailment ~5% industry-wide in Q1; expected to settle in next few quarters as transmission lines progress
items.quote: I think when we generally look around, including our project, there's been a general curtailment of roughly about 5%. And that we think is also the industry trend.

items.statement: RE commissioning: 226 MW in Q1; line of sight for 500 MW in final phase for Q2; targeting 800-900 MW commissioning in Q2
items.quote: As we speak, while in the first quarter, we have commissioned 226 megawatts, but we already have a line of sight for 500 megawatts where the project is almost ready.

items.statement: Odisha DISCOM collection deferred due to govt payment delays and heat-wave no-disconnect order; expect recovery in Q2; 12-month view shows 10.4% unit sales growth and ~6% PAT growth
items.quote: We expect to collect all of them in this quarter. The second is because of acute heat wave, the government asked that don't disconnect supply up to 15th of June and these payments are not made.

items.statement: Tata Projects legacy loss-making projects ~90% closed; final 10% winding down; one more quarter of impact expected then turnaround; strong order pipeline from marquee global clients
items.quote: We are at something like just 10% of the legacy projects in last stage there and cost to correction takes place because of that reason. And you will find that possibly maybe one more quarter will have an impact.

items.statement: Indonesian coal prices up 5-7%; expect up to 5% increase over next 9 months; no major impact from Indonesia's new export regime as KPC already compliant with domestic obligation
items.quote: So one is that coal prices have gone up, but not very much. I would say about 5% to 7%. So in that range, the coal price increase.

items.statement: ALMM-II continues for rooftop/utility; recent proviso only for limited open-access/behind-meter projects (~10% of DCR requirement); no impact on ingot/wafer investment commitment
items.quote: The ALMM-II continues to be there for rooftop and utility scale projects. This is only a special proviso which has been made for projects which have very limited open access arrangements or are behind the meter.

items.statement: Rooftop: 40 lakh consumers served vs 25 crore total addressable; market share 12-13% targeting 25%; monthly installs up from 1,000 to 30,000 units; cumulative revenue target INR 30,000 crore by 2029 (earlier 2030)
items.quote: We have been growing at a very, very high pace. Last to last year, we were INR 2,300 crores. Last year, we did INR 4,800 crores. This year, you can imagine what sort of -- so I think we will cross cumulative INR 30,000 crores maybe in 2029 itself.

items.statement: Solar EPC third-party discontinued; repurposing workforce to in-house 5.5 GW pipeline + PSP solutioning; Q1 EBITDA loss on EPC wrap-up; prior year contributed ~INR 100 crore PAT
items.quote: We have decided to repurpose our EPC workforce and EPC resources to in-house development. So we have discontinued doing the EPC third party.

items.statement: TP Solar manufacturing margin ~25-26%; driven by higher cell efficiency premium and yield improvement; module output at peak 1,000 MW/qtr; cell recovering after line change
items.quote: You will see that we are one of the highest in terms of margin, and you will see consistency in this quarter. Now that the plant has stabilized, you will see that.

items.statement: Renewable auction shift: states moving from central agency (SECI/NTPC/NHPC) bids to customized FDRE/RTC tenders; Tata Power bidding directly to states, avoiding central agencies except for pumped hydro
items.quote: Right now, what we are seeing is solar and wind or even for that matter, hybrid projects, the demand through the central agencies is much less. So we are also avoiding that sort of arrangement, and we are directly bidding to the states.

items.statement: Rooftop growth may cannibalize distribution/IPP long-term; nature of business will change but distribution network, devices, and management tech still needed
items.quote: So those are -- in 10 years, those are certain changes which will happen in the market. So one has to be ready for those. But you will still require the distribution network, you will still require devices.

items.statement: Mumbai transmission: INR 10,000 crore investment pipeline over next 5 years on regulated basis with efficiency/availability upsides
items.quote: And this will continue because we have a huge pipeline of investment, which is there in Mumbai transmission, nearly INR 10,000 crores of investment will happen in the next 5 years.

items.statement: Bhutan hydro: Khorlochhu 600 MW PPA signed with UPPCL, regulatory approval received, returns met, operational by CY2030; Dorjilung 1,125 MW World Bank financed, financial closure in 2 months with PFC/IFC/others
items.quote: We have also tied up the PPA for 600 megawatt of Bhutan project, the Khorlochhu project with UPPCL. And the PPA has been signed with them, and it has got the regulatory approval.

items.statement: TBCB projects under construction: revenue from lease accounting, not operational EBITDA; 2 projects commissioning in H2 FY27 (Q2, Q3, Q4); pure-play EBITDA/PAT to flow from commissioning
items.quote: Yes. So you will start seeing that commissioning happening from quarter 2 onwards. So the revenues -- 2 projects will get commissioned in H2 -- in quarter 2 and then next is quarter 3, quarter 4.

items.statement: Mundra SPPA: tariff on actual coal cost and heat rate, cost-reimbursement without margin; fixed cost covered on normative basis but no return on equity
items.quote: So presently, the supplementary PPA is on actual cost of coal, and all parameters, including heat rate, also will be on actual. So it's more towards cost reimbursement and cost reflective without any margin to be made from the plant.

items.statement: Nuclear: preliminary work on land, geotechnical, water; firm plan after government rules notified
items.quote: Great opportunity for us for doing many more projects -- but as informed to you, we do it on a calibrated basis. We are looking at new opportunities, including nuclear where a lot of preliminary work has happened.

items.statement: Management expects normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores per year, but may invest more if good opportunities arise.
items.quote: So I would put a normal sustainable capex of INR300 crores would be the number we'll look at. But having said that, if there are good opportunities and there are any reasonable return projects coming, we'll not be opposed to look at that.

items.statement: Invested close to INR7,000 crores over last 3-4 years for organic and inorganic opportunities.
items.quote: In fact, last 3 - 4 years, we have invested close to INR7,000 crores, both for organic and inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: Commissioned sulphuric acid and phosphoric acid plants; granulation project on track for Q4 commissioning.
items.quote: Commissioning of these plants has happened at a very opportune time, and this has ensured that we continue to produce and make phosphate fertilisers available to farmers when industry is facing shortage of key raw materials. Happy to note that granulation project is progressing well - as planned, we are on track for commissioning this in Q4 of this year.

items.statement: Fertilizer production moderated to 6.9 lakh tons (72% utilization) vs 8.4 lakh tons last year for inventory optimization.
items.quote: We have taken a conscious call to moderate production to 6.9 lakh tons compared to 8.4 lakh tons, roughly representing 72% of capacity utilization as the business prioritized inventory optimization amid volatile raw material markets.

items.statement: Crop protection capacity expansion of key molecules on track for September commissioning.
items.quote: Capacity expansion of key molecules is on track and is expected to be commissioned by September, strengthening our ability to support future growth.

items.statement: Fertilizer sales volumes moderated 9% to 10 lakh tons; primary market share increased to 22% from 18%.
items.quote: In terms of sales, these are all early part of the season. Volumes have been moderated by 9% to 10 lakh tons as compared to corresponding period last year. Despite this, the company has strengthened its market position, increasing the primary market share to 22% compared to 18% in the last year.

items.statement: Point of sales increased 13% to 7.9 lakh tons, market share improved to 16%.
items.quote: Consumption has been encouraging due to lower MRP stocks in the channel. The point of sales increased by 13% to 7.9 lakh tons, resulting in market share improving to 16%.

items.statement: SSP volumes grew 19%; differentiated products (GroPlus, Urea-SSP) constitute over 50% of SSP sales.
items.quote: SSP business continued its strong growth trajectory with volumes increasing by 19% - we have been focusing on differentiated products like GroPlus and Urea-SSP, which constituted more than 50% of the total SSP sales, highlighting the success of company's strategy to drive premiumization and improve product mix.

items.statement: Senegal rock phosphate mining produced over 1.1 lakh tons, broadly in line with plan.
items.quote: At our Senegal operations, the rock phosphate mining project produced over 1.1 lakh tons for this quarter, broadly in line with our plan.

items.statement: Fertilizer margins under pressure due to elevated ammonia and sulphur costs not factored in NBS subsidy rates.
items.quote: Fertilizer business margins were under pressure due to sudden spurt in key input raw materials like ammonia and sulphur. These prices were not factored in the subsidy rates announced by the government.

items.statement: Crop Protection revenue grew 20% YoY to INR870 crores, EBIT increased 44% to INR159 crores on improved mix and cost pass-through.
items.quote: The Crop Protection business delivered a record performance in Q1, driven by strong growth in exports and B2B sales despite softer demand environment in the domestic formulation segment. Revenue grew by 20% year -on-year to INR870 crores, while EBIT increased 44% to INR159 crores, reflecting improved product mix, traction for its key molecules and the ability to pass on higher raw material costs i

items.statement: NACL EBITDA improved 9% to INR41 crores, margin improved to 11% from 8%.
items.quote: Our subsidiary, NACL Industries improved its performance and EBITDA has moved up by 9% to INR41 crores with margin improving to 11% from 8%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA declined 3% to INR761 crores due to higher input costs from West Asia crisis not fully offset by NBS revision.
items.quote: As far as profitability is concerned, consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was INR761 crores against INR782 crores last year, registering a degrowth of 3%. The decrease in EBITDA is mainly due to higher input cost on account of the ongoing West Asia crisis, and the input cost inflation has not been fully commensurate with the revision in the NBS rates.

items.statement: Phosphoric acid price for Q2 settled at $1,700 vs $1,360 in Q1, reflecting sharp increase.
items.quote: As you are aware, phosphoric acid prices for Q 2 has been settled at $1,700 as compared to $1,360 prevailed in Q1, reflecting a sharp increase in line with the increase in international price of DAP and other raw material inputs.

items.statement: Sulphur prices holding high due to structural demand from EV battery nickel leaching; expected to soften but may take time.
items.quote: Sulphur is actually against our initial expectation - sulphur is holding high. I think sulphur is likely to remain high for some time, but it's not sustainable. If you recollect sulphur used to be a disposal issue for most of the oil companies but suddenly the price has gone up . There are structural shifts happening in terms of demand from EV batteries for nickel leaching leading to higher offtak

items.statement: Optimal sulphur price for backward integration viability is $800 given phosphoric acid at $1,700.
items.quote: Given the Phosphoric Acid price of $1,700, at least we want $800 of sulphur.

items.statement: Specialty Nutrients growing 25-30% top line with 20% EBITDA margin; launched 3 new products in water-soluble and sulphur nutrition.
items.quote: We have been continuously growing the top line of Specialty Nutrient business by 25%-30% with EBITDA margin of 20% .

items.statement: Crop Protection new products share in domestic B2C at 32% vs 23% last year; introduced 3 new products in quarter.
items.quote: Share of sales in the new products in the domestic B2C stands at 32% as compared to 23% last year. We have also introduced 3 new products during the current quarter.

items.statement: Planning to sell 50% of new granulation capacity (750k tons) through own retail outlets; expanding in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Telangana and seeding UP, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh.
items.quote: Capacity is 750,000 tonnes. We want to sell 50% of the volume through our own retail outlets. We are increasing our footprint in Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and also increasing number of retail outlets in Andhra & Telangana. So in the current markets where we have significant presence, we will be maximizing our sales through our own retail outlet. For the balance 50% of around 3,50,000 – 4,00,000 tonn

items.statement: Nano DAP holds nearly 60% market share; exports initiated but banned in UP and Maharashtra moderating growth.
items.quote: The Nano business delivered stable performance with sales volume growing 2% year -on-year, supported by sustained demand for Nano DAP and a market leadership position with nearly 60% of market share. The business also initiated exports during the quarter an d sees encouraging opportunities to expand its presence in international markets, supported by registrations secured in few markets. There has

items.statement: Government approved national urea investment policy for 9-10 million tons additional capacity over 8 years; launched INR37,500 crore coal/lignite gasification scheme.
items.quote: The government has approved national investment policy for urea, which could potentially facilitate 9 million to 10 million tons of additional domestic urea capacity over the next 8 years across 7 proposed projects. In parallel, the announcement of INR37,500 crores coal and lignite gasification scheme is expected to support the development of domestic syngas -based feedstocks and progressively red

items.statement: Government increased NBS subsidy rates ~10% but without factoring Middle East crisis; industry engaging for review.
items.quote: On the subsidy front, the government announced increase of about 10% in subsidy rates across Nitrogen, Phosphatic and Sulphur nutrients under the NBS regime. This rate has been announced without factoring the Middle East crisis situation . These rates do not fully compensate for the increase in global raw material costs, which happened subsequent to Middle East crisis.

items.statement: Pilot National Fertilizer Sales Framework with QR code traceability launched in 10-12 states, 2-3 districts each; seen in Telangana and Karnataka.
items.quote: They are trying to do it in 10 to 12 states, 2, 3 districts in each state. I will get back to you in specifics, that is what my understanding. Of course, it has been picked up major district in Telangana and one more district in Karnataka. That is where we have witnessed the process.

items.statement: Subsidy outstanding INR3,254 crores as of June 30; received INR568 crores additional in July; claims cleared till third week of June.
items.quote: As of today, we have received our subsidy claims till the third week of June. Subsidy outstanding as on 30th June was about INR3,254 crores. We have received additional subsidy of INR568 crores in the month of July.

items.statement: Rupee traded 92.59-96.83 in Q1; company hedges exposures on conservative basis.
items.quote: As far as forex is concerned, during Q1, the rupee traded in a wide range of 92. 59 to 96.83. Coromandel continues to hedge its exposures on a conservative basis.

items.statement: Target nutrient business EBITDA of INR6,500 per metric ton at steady state post backward integration.
items.quote: Our average EBITDA, which used to be INR5,000 need to go up to INR6,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: NPK production and imports down 21% and 38% due to unviable subsidy rates; risk of demand destruction if subsidy not corrected.
items.quote: This sort of subdued subsidy rates, especially for NP /NPK fertilizers have impacted production and imports during the quarter, which were down by 21% and 38%, respectively.

items.statement: Markets grew 4-5% in H1; management expects near-term growth with festival season
items.quote: we believe that the markets we operated in, in the first half or second quarter for that matter, remain robust and very competitive and grew at 4% to 5% range.

items.statement: No specific revenue guidance; aims to grow in line with market (4-5%)
items.quote: I would be very happy if that the market grows by, let's say, 5% or 4% or 3%, whatever it is, if we are kind of growing with the market, that would be a good kind of target for us.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 10.5%, up from 8.3% YoY; H1 EBITDA margin 10.5%, up 2.2 pp YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improvement by about 55% from 8.3 to 10.5 percentage points is primarily driven by the higher margins that we could actually reflect in the current year -- in the current quarter's financials

items.statement: 23% net sales growth driven ~1/3 each by price, volume, product mix; RM cost pass-through varies by contract
items.quote: The growth was driven by price, volume and product mix, almost 1/3 each of that. And roughly, when you're talking about 23% growth overall in net sales, it's pretty robust.

items.statement: Mix shifting toward home care, liquid categories and sustainable/lightweight packaging; blueloop adoption below 30%
items.quote: We are also seeing some volume increase in liquid and home care categories, which are quite aligned with our strategy of differentiation compared to our competitors.

items.statement: Growth broad-based across domestic and exports; same customer base; customers value contingency and scale
items.quote: Our exports and domestic business almost grew at the same growth rate. So it was quite a broad-based growth.

items.statement: Inventory consciously elevated to avoid stock-outs; absolute receivables up due to price/volume but DSO/DOI stable
items.quote: Our operating working capital marginally increased during the period, and that's primarily because of the higher inventory, which is a conscious call that we took to manage any out-of-stock situation

items.statement: Net debt nil; bank balances INR270 cr, liquid MFs INR125 cr, unutilised limits INR427 cr; intercompany borrowing to be repaid early
items.quote: our net debt is nil. Bank balances remain at INR270 crores and investment in liquid mutual funds is about INR125 crores. We have an unutilized fund-based limits during the period, which is about INR427 crores

items.statement: Investing in modernization and productivity; solar captive plant at Khopoli (50% power) commissioned in Q3
items.quote: we have a solar captive generation power plant getting online in this quarter, in Q3, which will actually supply almost 50% of power for our Khopoli plant.

items.statement: Productivity gains absorbing volume growth; comfortable for next couple of years; no utilisation number disclosed
items.quote: we are also doing a lot of work on productivity improvement. So because of that productivity improvement, whatever growth we have is actually taken care of that by that productivity improvement

items.statement: Exports ~30% of volume; growing at same rate as domestic; serve SE Asia, Africa, Europe, Americas
items.quote: Actually, 30% of our sales volume comes from exports. So we are already supplying to Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe as well as Americas.

items.statement: Export duty stability improving after initial challenges
items.quote: Although, as you know, exports, we had a lot of challenges with the duty stability, which was a bit of challenge for us initially, but we see that stabilizing a bit now.

items.statement: Middle East crisis caused RM cost volatility; transparent inventory sharing with customers; pass-through via index or ad-hoc
items.quote: there was a significant disruption to supply chain, and there was a raw material cost variation. Despite this, what you would have observed is that our net sales growth was healthy and solid.

items.statement: EPS grew 77.3% YoY in Q2 to highest in many years; H1 EPS INR9.18 up 36%
items.quote: Earnings per share for this quarter reflect a growth in line with our profitability. The growth we are seeing here is 77.3 percentage points.

items.statement: Total incident rate down 40% YTD; Family Safety Day held; focus on behavioural safety
items.quote: I'm very pleased to inform that we actually had the total incident rate reduction by 40% year-to-date, which is actually a very significant number.

items.statement: Geopolitical tension makes RM procurement hard but manageable; inventory buildup at customers may normalize; blueloop adoption uncertain
items.quote: I think problem, no. Hard, yes. It's not easy, as you know. But like I said, with our reach, with our economy of scale, with our global footprint, I guess we are in a pretty good spot at the moment.

items.statement: Consolidated revenues grew 29.1% YoY to INR6,591 crores in Q1 FY27, driven by 36.8% domestic growth and 12.4% export growth.
items.quote: Our consolidated revenues grew by over 29%. So we had 29.1% versus last year. The revenue has reached INR6,591 crores. The domestic revenue grew by 36.8%. Export revenue grew by 12.4% and the export mix is at 27.5% compared to 31.6% in the previous year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA post forex grew 62.7% YoY to INR814 crores with margin at 12.4% vs 9.8% a year ago.
items.quote: If we come to EBITDA, EBITDA post open period forex has grown to INR814 crores, representing a growth of 62.7% year-on-year. The margin came in at 12.4% compared to 9.8% a year ago.

items.statement: PAT grew 77.7% YoY to INR467 crores with margin at 7.1%, up ~200 bps, marking highest quarterly sales and profit in company history.
items.quote: So if you look at profit after tax, profit after tax has increased by 77.7% to reach INR467 crores from a year ago. The PAT margin came in at 7.1%, so it's up about 200 basis points. This incidentally is the highest quarterly sales as well as profit number that we have achieved in the history of the company.

items.statement: Conductor division pending order book stands at INR10,190 crores with 56.8% export proportion; new orders received in Q1 were INR5,245 crores (65.8% exports), including two large overseas utility orders exceeding INR2,800 crores.
items.quote: The pending order book stands at around INR10,190 crores with an export proportion of 56.8%. New orders received by the conductor division were INR5,245 crores in the quarter, of which exports contributed to 65.8%. This includes large orders exceeding INR2,800 crores from two major overseas electric utility companies, one in the U.S. and the other one in Europe, with a delivery schedule that is sp

items.statement: Conductor revenues grew 19.9% to INR3,338 crores; volumes down 6.7% due to customers withholding manufacturing clearance amid aluminum price surge, but premium segment share rose to 50.3% from 43.7%.
items.quote: Coming to the conductor division. Our revenues grew by 19.9% to reach INR3,338 crores. Volume for the quarter was down 6.7% compared to a year ago. This can be attributed fundamentally to a surge in the metal prices that have impacted delivery schedules of orders which are in hand, where customers have withheld manufacturing cl earance, especially due to the sudden increase in the price of aluminu

items.statement: Conductor EBITDA post forex grew 14% YoY to INR285 crores; EBITDA per ton rose to INR53,418 from INR43,688 due to higher premium mix.
items.quote: EBITDA post foreign exchange grew 14% year-on-year to INR285 crores. EBITDA growth is attributable to a higher share of the premium mix due to which despite a slightly lower volume of conventional conductors, the absolute EBITDA has grown, which came in at INR53,418 per ton compared to INR43,688 per ton a year earlier.

items.statement: Premium conductor products (HTLS, copper transposed conductors, railway busbars) drove margin expansion; conventional conductor volumes delayed domestically.
items.quote: So first, when we're talking about the premium product, the entire category has grown in the quarter. So whether it's the HTLS, as we mentioned, that it's been the highest quarter in which we've done the physical installation that has happened. There's also been growth across the copper range of products, which is your copper tran sposed conductors. There's been supply that's gone to the railways,

items.statement: Received approval from a major U.S. utility for OPGW with 144 fiber counts, critical for U.S. market entry.
items.quote: APAR also has got an approval from one of the largest U.S. utilities for OPGW with 144 counts, which is a very critical approval for the U.S. market.

items.statement: Oil division revenue grew 34.7% to INR1,701 crores; volumes down 13.7% (UAE facility restricted by Hamriyah port closure), India volumes down only 4.4%; auto oil +6.6%, industrial lubricants +12.1%.
items.quote: Coming to the oil division. Revenue here grew by 34.7% year-on-year to reach INR1,701 crores. Volume for the quarter stands at 129,085 kL, down 13.7% compared to a year ago and down -- yes, the volumes were affected really because of our facility in the UAE, which because of this crisis and the resulting closure of the Hamriyah port was restricted to only making local deliveries of the product tha

items.statement: Oil EBITDA grew 214% YoY to INR329 crores; EBITDA per kL at INR25,482 vs INR7,004 a year ago, aided by inventory gains and INR94 crore provision for accounting standards.
items.quote: However, post taking this provision into account, the EBITDA margins came in at a substantially higher level of INR25,482 per kL compared to INR7,004 per kL a year ago. The overall EBITDA has grown by 214% to reach INR329 crores. And this is about 290% more than what it was in the sequential quarter.

items.statement: Oil division made ~INR94 crore provision due to sharp crude/gas oil price rise then fall, following accounting standards.
items.quote: So, with the price of crude oil and gas oil having risen very sharply at the beginning of the quarter and then falling quite sharply at the end of the period, the company has followed the requirements of accounting standards and has provided for approximately INR94 crores for the oil division in the quarter.

items.statement: Cable revenues grew 29.5% to INR1,838 crores; domestic +59.9%, exports -13.7%, export mix 27.6%; U.S. revenue grew 2.5% YoY.
items.quote: Coming to the cable division. Cable revenues grew 29.5% to reach INR1,838 crores. Domestic revenue grew 59.9%. Export revenue is down by 13.7%. Export mix stands at 27.6%, with the U.S. revenue actually growing 2.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Cable division approved for data center supplies to Meta, Microsoft, Google via major electrical contractors; now participating in copper cable RFQs (LV, MV, PVC, XLPE, rubber).
items.quote: Today, APAR is approved in the U.S. for cables being supplied to data centers of Meta, Microsoft and Google by various major electrical contractors. The U.S. market is actually 66% copper and 33% aluminum. With these approvals, APAR has started receiving orders and participating in RFQs, which are for copper cables that cover both low voltage as well as medium voltage segments and are of the PVC v

items.statement: Cable EBITDA post forex grew 36.7% to INR194 crores; margin at 10.6%, up 60 bps YoY, driven by domestic product mix (defence, railways).
items.quote: EBITDA post open ForEx came in at INR194 crores, which is up 36.7%. The EBITDA margin has come in at 10.6% in Q1, which is up by 60 basis points over a year ago.

items.statement: Capacity utilization across divisions at 80-90%; ongoing capex to debottleneck and build capacity for growth.
items.quote: It ranges for different products, and it ranges anywhere between 80% to 90% for different product categories across the division. Chaitanya Desai: And as you know, we are doing a fair amount of capex. So we are building our capacity for the growth

items.statement: Working capital at 45-50 days, fairly constant; conductor division improved debtor and inventory days despite commodity volatility.
items.quote: Working capital is in the range of 45 to 50 days. That has been fairly constant over the period. Kushal Desai: In fact, in this quarter, we have actually improved our working capital number of days, debtors and inventory in the conductor division compared to what it was previously

items.statement: Conductor export order book 56.8% (North America, Latin America, Europe); cable U.S. approvals enable copper cable entry; conductor U.S. market limited to 30% import quota under Section 232 (50% duty).
items.quote: The bulk of the product is coming from the America, North America, Latin America and Europe. And it's the backlog. So out of that INR10,190 crores, export is about -- as I mentioned in the earlier statement, it's about 56.8%. That's coming from the America and Europe -- I mean, North and South America and Europe. The rest of it is all domestic.

items.statement: Wires (B2C) sales grew 46% YoY; active towns +17%, distributors +25%, retail accounts +51%; B2B channel grew 92% with distributors +60%, active towns +73%.
items.quote: Specifically, if you take, in this quarter, sales for wires grew 46%, and our focus has been on increasing distributor and retailer presence. So we've -- the number of active towns that our presence is in has increased 17%. Our distributor addition has been 25% in the quarter compared to a year ago. And the retail account presence has increased by 51%, which has resulted in an overall increase in

items.statement: Metal price volatility caused customer destocking and delayed primary orders; secondary sales stable; oil inventory reduced to limit reversal risk.
items.quote: So volatility is something that it has affected everybody. As Chaitanya had mentioned that in the quarter, you had copper price go up, you had aluminum price go up. Even in the case of oil, some of the lower volumes, part of the lower volumes are attributed that in the first month, there was a huge disruption in the supply chain itself. But subsequently, as the product started coming in with the s

items.statement: Conductor premium mix 50.3% vs 43.7% YoY; domestic premium focus, export conventional focus; export conventional margins higher than domestic conventional due to quality standards.
items.quote: What is heartening to know is that the premium segment of the Conductors division contributed well to ov erall revenues of 50.3% compared to 43.7% a year ago. So most of these delays, which I spoke about, of manufacturing clearance has been largely for conventional conductors going into the domestic market against TBCB projects and other projects of that type, whereas the premium products continue

items.statement: Cable division supplying defence and Indian Railways; domestic channel expansion driving growth.
items.quote: It is the domestic market, which is there. We've been continuing to supply to defense, railways, Indian Railways bought quite a lot of product in the last quarter. Defense bought some products in the last quarter. So it's just a good product mix that has been sold in the domestic market.

items.statement: Conductor EBITDA per ton INR53,418 (blended) vs INR43,688 YoY; oil EBITDA per kL INR25,482 vs INR7,004 YoY.
items.quote: So this year's number is INR53,148 per ton and last year was, at the same time, was INR43,688. So almost INR10,000 higher than last year.

items.statement: Cable division manufacturing capability approved by U.S. data center contractors; no U.S. investment needed.
items.quote: We have the manufacturing capability in place. That's how all the assessments and everything have been done. So it entails some of these big contractors, they do not only product assessment, they also do manufacturing infrastructure, quality systems, all that. So all that assessment has been done after that, only these approvals are in place.

items.statement: Company issued notice for shareholder approval for securities issuance; restricted from discussing funding requirements or guidance.
items.quote: Before we start, I did want to mention that the company has issued a notice to its shareholders seeking the approval under applicable law for the issuance of securities. So under these guidelines, to comply with them, we have specifically restrictions around publicity. The company will not be in a position to actually take any questions on guidance, projections, forecasts pertaining to its busines

items.statement: New leadership team appointed including MD V.R. Sharma, COO Rajiv Kumar, CFO Sandeep Modi, and CHRO Sukhjit S Pasricha
items.quote: I am delighted to introduce our Managing Director, Mr. V.R. Sharma. Though he needs no introduction, let me begin by saying Mr. V.R. Sharma is a distinguished industry leader with over four decades of international leadership experience across the steel, power, metals, and cement sectors.

items.statement: Senior plant heads Debojyoti Roy (Raigarh) and Biju Nair (Angul) have 30+ years experience from Tata Steel and ArcelorMittal respectively
items.quote: One is Mr. Debojyoti, he is heading the Raigarh plant, who hails again about 30 years of experience, and he also come from Tata Steel. The other gentleman is Mr. Biju Nair, who was with ArcelorMittal and he also has more than 30 years of experience, so he is heading the Angul plant.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan ~INR 8,500 cr; INR 2,000 cr spent in Q1; cumulative expansion spend INR 37,457 cr of INR 47,043 cr announced
items.quote: Against our FY27 capex plan of approximately INR 8,500 crores. We invested roughly INR 2,000 crores during Q1. Cumulative spending under our expansion program now stands at INR 37,457 crores out of the announced capex of INR 47,043 crores.

items.statement: Angul BF2 ramp-up: 11,000 tpd currently, target 12,000 tpd by September, 13,000 tpd (100%) by December; BF1 at 11,000 tpd vs 10,000 tpd rated
items.quote: Our plan is that after this monsoon season, we'll be in a position to ramp it up to 12,000 tons per day and by end of December, we'll make it 13,000 tons per day, which will be 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 cr; EBITDA/t INR 11,937 (+INR 1,843/t QoQ); value-added share rose 61% to 66%
items.quote: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 2,667 crores. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA per ton increased by INR 1,843 per ton, taking it to INR 11,937 per ton.

items.statement: Target INR 1,000/t cost reduction via operational improvements (yield, energy, consumables) led by COO and plant heads
items.quote: I think there is a chance of, roughly figures, I am not committing something, but roughly because I have to talk to my colleagues also, at least INR 1,000 per ton reduction is possible in terms of cost.

items.statement: Q1FY27 ASP improved ~INR 7,500/t QoQ; flat NSR up INR 7,000/t, long NSR up INR 4,500/t QoQ per CFO
items.quote: was partly offset by around INR 7,500 per ton improvement in our average ASP, that's the average realization, supported by stronger steel prices and a richer product mix

items.statement: Coking coal cost up $23/t in Q1 (in line with $20-25/t guidance); expect $12-15/t increase in Q2; blending to mitigate
items.quote: This improvement was driven by increase in ASP, partly offset by a $23 per ton increase in coking coal consumption cost, which is in line with our guidance of $20 to $25 per ton of coal.

items.statement: Captive coal mix ~50% currently; Utkal B1 ramping, B2 coming; iron ore backward integration 16% to 28% in Q1, targeting 40% exit FY27
items.quote: We already have this time a coal mix of our own captive mines of around 50% and that will also go up with the Utkal B1 getting ramped up and Utkal B2 coming in, that will also help us to reduce the cost.

items.statement: Inventory at <10-11 days of total production; described as very lean and best in industry
items.quote: Then as far as the inventory is concerned, we are well within the limit. We have less than 10 or 11 days of total production as an inventory, so which is I would say very lean and best in the industry available today.

items.statement: Net debt INR 15,927 cr; net debt/EBITDA 1.71x; target <1.5x by Q2FY27 and maintain through cycle
items.quote: Net debt stood at INR 15,927 crores, translating into a net debt to EBITDA ratio of 1.71x. With the ongoing ramp-up of new facilities and continued focus on the cash generation, we remain confident of achieving the ratio below our stated threshold of 1.5x during Q2FY27.

items.statement: Value-added share 66% in Q1FY27 (up from 61%); only private producer of head-hardened rails (18-19 of 22 metros); specialty plates, round billets, sheet piles, defence grades
items.quote: The share of value-added product has increased from 61% in Q4FY26 to 66% in Q1FY27. As our newly commissioned downstream facilities continue to ramp up, we expect the share of value-added products to increase further.

items.statement: Government banned imports of quenched & tempered plates; JSPL produces these domestically for defence (submarines, warships, gas storage)
items.quote: Now Government of India has given an instruction, and I would say it has banned th ese kind of products coming into the country. So, we are thankful to the Government of India

items.statement: Domestic steel consumption -7% QoQ to 41.5 Mt in Q1 due to monsoon; construction recovery expected post-August; RBI projects FY27 GDP 6.6%
items.quote: Domestically, the steel industry witnessed seasonal softness. This always happens especially in the monsoon season during this quarter. India's crude steel production declined by 6% on quarter-on-quarter basis to 42 million tons, while finished steel consumption declined by 7% to about 41.5 million tons.

items.statement: HRC prices firm sequentially; TMT opened strong but weakened during monsoon; recovery expected from end-August as construction resumes
items.quote: In the domestic market today, we are seeing that HRC prices are increased sequentially and remained firm throughout the quarter, while TMT, that is the rebar prices for the construction steel, they opened on a strong note, but after that the demand came down and during this particular monsoon season, yes, it always happens that the construction activities, they are slowed down.

items.statement: ROCE target 18-20% per capital allocation framework; implies EBITDA run-rate from projects
items.quote: If you look at our capital allocation framework where we have clearly mentioned that we would deliver about 18% to 20% ROCE and you add the nominal depreciation back, you get the guided or our desired EBITDA from these projects.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Ukraine-Russia, Middle East wars) creating economic uncertainty; China surplus exports; monsoon disruptions to operations
items.quote: For the last four years, we are seeing that Ukraine and Russia war is going on, which has shattered the economy, which has shattered not only the economy in Europe but everywhere in the world. Now for the last one year, the ripples and then a big fight in between America, Israel together with Israel and Iran.

items.statement: Jindal port first loading started; two vessels unloaded, one loading; will give logistics savings
items.quote: We also have good news to share about the startup of the first loading at the Jindal port, which also has started and that will also give us savings. I will not be able to quantify at this point of time, but already two vessels have been unloaded, and one vessel has already going loading as we speak currently.

items.statement: Asset and Private Wealth share of operating PAT expected to continue rising due to growing annuity share and low market share headroom
items.quote: We have guided that the share of Asset and Private Wealth businesses will continue to rise because of growing share of annuity businesses and the low market share that we have in these businesses allowing a lot of headroom for us to grow.

items.statement: AMC AUM growth supported by six factors including SIP run rate, NFO collections, vintage funds, mark-to-market gains, and GIFT City entry
items.quote: We believe our AUM growth will be supported by the following factors: o Annualized SIP run rate of around ₹16,000 crores o Collections from proposed NFOs besides discretionary flows o More products crossing the 3-year vintage o Current AUM of nearly ₹1.9 lakh crores is over 15% higher than the FY26 average AUM of ₹1.57 lakh crores o Potential mark-to-market gains after 2 muted years o Entry into m

items.statement: Alternate Asset Management to be key growth and ARR driver on larger fund sizes, new categories, and carry income recognition
items.quote: Alternate Asset Management business will be a nother key growth driver and also an ARR driver of the Motilal Oswal Group on the back of o Larger fund size that we have raised in every subsequent series o Entry into newer categories o More funds entering the carry income recognition threshold, which will boost our carry income run rate.

items.statement: Private Wealth ARR revenue to rise steadily while TBR remains volatile QoQ, improving earnings quality structurally
items.quote: As we scale our ARR -led revenue mix in private wealth, the relative TBR revenue contribution will be volatile QoQ, while our overall earnings quality and predictability will continue to improve structurally due to rising ARR-led revenue in the mix.

items.statement: Wealth Management distribution and lending book to continue driving growth and increasing share of group ARR revenue
items.quote: The distribution lending book will continue to drive growth and increase its share in the overall group's ARR revenue pie.

items.statement: Capital Markets FY27 YoY growth expected but QoQ volatile depending on market windows for deal execution
items.quote: Hence, FY27 as a whole, we'll witness growth. However, on a QoQ basis, it really depends on market.

items.statement: Housing Finance expected to witness strong growth for next 2-3 years with strong capital adequacy and low leverage
items.quote: We expect housing finance business to continue to witness strong growth in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Unlisted alternates fee income and accrued carry income to rise steadily YoY due to new product launches and larger subsequent fund series
items.quote: So, we would like to guide that there should be a steady rise in both the fee income as well as the accrued carry income for this business.

items.statement: Group PBT margins expected to sustain in 50-52% range for current financial year
items.quote: If we look at historically and our last few years , our margins have been around the range of 50% to 52%. Q1 of this year is also around 52%. We expect, historically the margins that we had to sustain over the course of current financial year.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM hiring in FY27 to be fewer in number but higher cost targeting family offices
items.quote: This year, the composition of RM additions will be fewer in numbers, but much higher in cost, targeted at the family offices. Thus, the cost increase will continue to be there, but headcount increase will be lesser in FY27 compared to FY26.

items.statement: AMC net mutual fund flows market share improved to 4.2% from 3.7% previous quarter, SIP flows strong at ₹4,064 crores up 16% YoY
items.quote: Our flow market share continues to be well above our AUM market share, which is 2.9%. In Q1FY27, our SIP flows were strong at ₹4,064 crores, up by 16% YoY with a market share of 4.3%, resulting in an SIP AUM of ₹38,643 crores.

items.statement: Private Wealth net flows grew 37% YoY to nearly ₹4,000 crores, AUM up 37% YoY to ₹2.4 lakh crores
items.quote: Net flows grew by a strong 37% to nearly ₹4,000 crores, leading to AUM growth of 37% on a Y oY basis to ₹2.4 lakh crores.

items.statement: Wealth Management distribution book grew nearly 30% to over ₹45,000 crores, loan book rose 33% YoY to over ₹7,000 crores
items.quote: Distribution book grew by nearly 30% to over ₹45,000 crores. We are confident that our distribution book will grow meaningfully as we continue to harness the cros s-sell potential of our client base of our franchise, which stands at only 18% versus multiple times for our global peers. Our loan book in this segment rose 33% YoY to over ₹7,000 crores.

items.statement: Housing Finance disbursements grew 64% YoY to ₹646 crores, AUM up 23% YoY to ₹6,164 crores
items.quote: In Housing Finance business, our disbursements grew by 64% YoY to ₹646 crores. AUM grew by 23% YOY to ₹6,164 crores in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Asset and Private Wealth net flows robust at ₹10,325 crores, AUM at ₹4.5 lakh crores up 34% YoY
items.quote: Asset Management and Private Wealth businesses continued its momentum during the quarter with robust net flows of ₹10,32 5 crores. AUM at ₹4.5 lakh crores as on June '26 is up by 34% YoY.

items.statement: AMC average AUM grew from ₹1.67 lakh crores in Q4FY26 to ₹1.81 lakh crores in Q1FY27, close to ₹2 lakh crores milestone
items.quote: Our average AUM gr ew from ₹1.67 lakh crores in Q 4FY26 to ₹1.81 lakh crores in Q 1FY27, reflecting the continued momentum in the business and today, we are closer to another milestone of ₹2 lakh crores in this business.

items.statement: Private credit fund second close raised nearly ₹2,500 crores of ₹3,000 crores target, final close in Q2, commercial real estate fund launch in H2
items.quote: We are in the process of executing our final close of our maiden private credit fund of ₹3,000 crores, where we have raised nearly ₹2,500 crores in the second close. We will launch commercial real estate in second half of this financial year and continue to offer a comprehensive suite of product offerings in alternates.

items.statement: Investment Banking completed 11 deals raising over ₹10,000 crores, fee income up 48% QoQ to ₹68 crores, ranked #2 in IPO/QIP league table
items.quote: Despite challenging market conditions, our investment banking business has successfully completed 11 deals during the quarter, raising over ₹10,000 crores, and our fee income delivered a strong 48% revenue growth QoQ to ₹68 crores. We are now ranked #2 in the capital markets league table for IPO and QIPs.

items.statement: Group operating PAT up 14% YoY to ₹609 crores in Q1FY27, Asset and Private Wealth contribute 55% of operating PAT vs 50% in FY26
items.quote: On that base, our operating profit after tax grew by 14% on a YoY basis in this quarter to ₹609 crores, led by Asse t and Private Wealth business, which grew by 44% YoY. The Asset and Private Wealth businesses, now contribute 55% of the total operating profit of the group versus 50% in FY26 and 42% in FY25.

items.statement: AMC contributes 40% of group operating PAT in Q1FY27 vs 26% in Q1FY26, expected to increase further
items.quote: The Asset Management business contributes to 40% of the group's operating PAT in Q1FY27 versus 26% in Q1FY26 and is expected to increase based on all the pointers highlighted above.

items.statement: Private Wealth ARR revenue grew 42% YoY to ₹157 crores, overall revenues flattish on lower TBR
items.quote: The Q1FY27 ARR revenue for the private wealth business grew by 42% YoY to ₹157 crores. However, overall revenues were flattish on lower TBR revenues.

items.statement: Wealth Management ARR revenues grew 26% YoY to ₹304 crores, share of ARR in segment revenue increased from 33% in FY21 to 57% in Q1FY27
items.quote: We continue to have a sharp focus on growing our ARR revenues, which includes distribution income and Net Interest Income (NII). This has led to the share of these incomes in Wealth Management segment revenue increasing from 33% in the year ending March '21 t o 57% in the Q1FY27. The ARR revenues grew by 26% on a YoY basis this quarter to ₹304 crores.

items.statement: Unlisted alternates accrued carry income ₹66 crores this quarter, expected similar for next 3 quarters and higher next year
items.quote: On unlisted equities - the number is ₹66 crores accrued as variable additional return for this quarter and will continue to recur around a similar level for the next 3 quarters as well as for the next year because there's a whole pipeline of products which will keep advancing and coming closer to maturity.

items.statement: Distribution yields stable at around 70 basis points
items.quote: As far as the yields are concerned, it is stable at around 70 basis points.

items.statement: MTF book yields and spreads healthy due to low cost of funds and leverage, book grew 54% YoY
items.quote: Also, on the MTF side, we have very healthy yields and spreads because our cost of fund trajectory and our overall low leverage, gives us more delta in the P&L. While book has grown 54% YoY and the average book has also started catching up, which would result in a delta on the absolute NII growth.

items.statement: AMC launched 1 new active mutual fund in Q1FY27, now represents 87% of industry AUM, 6 funds over 3-year vintage contribute 44% of industry AUM
items.quote: We launched 1 new active mutual fund in Q1FY27, increasing our presence now to represent 87% of the industry AUM. Importantly, only 6 of our funds have a vintage of over 3 years, and these categories contribute a mere 44% of the industry AUM.

items.statement: AMC expects 2 more funds to cross 3-year vintage by March '27 and 8 more by March '28, improving 3+ year vintage participation to 75% of industry AUM
items.quote: We expect an additional 2 funds to cross 3-year vintage by March '27 and a further 8 funds to cross the 3-year vintage by March '28. This will improve our 3 + years vintage fund participation to 75% of the industry AUM from 44% now.

items.statement: AMC to launch 4-5 new passive offers over next 12 months, fewer active funds, small/large cap funds completing 3 years by Dec'26-Jan'27
items.quote: In terms of mutual fund side, you should expect to see more offering on the passive side. On the active side, there would be fewer, but still over the next 12 months, there can be 4 to 5 new offers from our side. The big thing to focus on the AMC is that over the December'26 - Jan'27, we have 2 large funds, the small and the large cap funds, which will complete 3 years.

items.statement: Private Wealth wallet size per customer now closer to ₹25 crores, AUM per banker closer to ₹550 crores, 80% flows from existing clients
items.quote: If you see even the wallet size per customer has steadily moved up, we are now closer to ₹25 crores. And even the AUM per banker is now closer to ₹550 crores. Thus, that number has steadily moved up. Also, the flows from newer customers in any year would be around 20% and 80% is basically deepening from existing customers.

items.statement: MTF adoption rate around 15% of cash customer base, significant headroom for growth
items.quote: I don't have this number immediately, but we can share it. I think it will be around in the range of 15%.

items.statement: Broking retains leadership as largest non-bank full-service broker, overall retail broking market share 7.6% in Q1FY27, F&O premium share up from 7% to 7.6% YoY
items.quote: Our broking business continues to retain its leadership position as a full -service broker amongst non-bank players. We are the largest broker in the cash segment on revenue market share in non-bank segment. Our overall retail broking market share, including commodities, stood at 7.6% in Q1FY27, led by market share gains in F&O premium segment from 7% in Q1FY26 to 7.6% in the Q1FY27.

items.statement: Prop trading regulatory change from July 1 minimal impact on business model, only minor impact on intraday funding from banks
items.quote: There is no much impact because that is mainly impacting the brokers who are heavy on prop trading. From a liquidity perspective, it's very early to assess the impact because of the volatility in the markets. There is no impact for us on the overall business model, except some change on the intraday funding from the banks, which will have minor impact.

items.statement: Housing Finance has strong capital adequacy, very low leverage, no need for further capital infusion for growth
items.quote: Business has a strong capital adequacy ratio, very low leverage, giving us enough growth levers without any need for further capital infusion.

items.statement: AMC unique PAN catered over ₹1 crore as of June '26 vs ₹85 lakhs in June '25, representing ~16% share of all clients in Indian mutual fund industry
items.quote: Our unique PAN catered by our AMC is more than ₹1 crore as on June '26 versus ₹85 lakhs in June '25, which shows strong confidence by retail investors in our franchise. This is around 16% share of all clients in the Indian mutual fund industry.

items.statement: Treasury book grew 22% YoY to ₹10,482 crores, long-term compounded growth 41% since March 2014 led by IRR and reinvestment of operating PAT
items.quote: Our treasury book grew by 22% YoY to ₹10,482 crores in Q1FY27. The long term compounded growth of this book has been 41%, led by strong IRRs and reinvestment of operating profits after paying dividends.

items.statement: Capital Markets revenue volatile QoQ due to West Asia geopolitical scenario, execution dependent on market windows of 2-3 months multiple times a year
items.quote: This whole West Asia scenario keeps changing and is quite volatile. Signed mandates very substantial to show a strong growth in revenue on YoY basis. Also, the business is now reconciled to not having a one clean runway of the whole year, but having pockets of 2 months or 3 months, multiple times in a year, maybe 2 or 3 times in a year to be able to execute this signed mandate pipeline.

items.statement: AMC team additions opportunistic for fund manager and research base on active and passive side, no vacancy to fill
items.quote: In terms of team addit ion, we keep adding as we are launching more funds as we will need more hands. There is no vacancy to fill. But opportunistically as well as from a longer-term perspective, we are looking to strengthen both the fund manager base as well as the research team on the active side as well as the passive side.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM breakeven typically 2-3 years, senior hires breaking even faster due to platform enablement
items.quote: Typically, bankers at an aggregate level, breakeven around 2 to 3 years. However, what we are seeing, which is quite encouraging, is some of the senior bankers that we are hiring are breaking even much faster. I guess that's also the function of the kind of platform that we have because the platform enables the bankers to breakeven much faster than what normally happens.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 NIM guided around 5.8% (adjusted), up from prior 5.75% guidance
items.quote: we feel that margins could broadly stay around the 5.8% handle now for the full year

items.statement: Full-year FY27 credit cost guidance lowered to 150-160 bps from prior 170-180 bps
items.quote: we feel now we could land up more with 150 to 160 basis points on credit cost

items.statement: Targeting full-year FY27 ROA of about 1%
items.quote: we are gunning for reaching an ROA of about 1% for the year

items.statement: Aim to bring cost-to-income ratio below 70% during FY27 from 70.7% in Q1
items.quote: our endeavour would be to take into below 70 during the course of the year

items.statement: Q1 FY27 reported NIM 5.96%; adjusted NIM 5.90% (up 5 bps QoQ) after removing one-offs
items.quote: the NIM has shown an improvement of 5 basis points and the adjusted numbers would look like 5.85% going up to 5.90%

items.statement: Cost of funds fell to 5.96% from 6% QoQ, supporting NIM
items.quote: reduction in cost of fund, which further came down from 6% to 5.96%

items.statement: GNPA improved 10 bps QoQ to 1.51%; NNPA improved 4 bps to 0.44%
items.quote: the gross NPA ratio of the bank, further improved by 10 basis points from 1.61% reported in Q4 to 1.51%. Similarly, on net NPA, we saw an improvement of 4 basis points to 0.44%

items.statement: Retail, rural, MSME GNPA 1.40% (down 7 bps QoQ); NNPA 0.52% (down 4 bps)
items.quote: the gross NPA improved by 7 basis points to 1.40% and similarly net NPA improved by 4 basis points to 0.52%

items.statement: Gross slippages down 2% QoQ and 30% YoY; net slippages down 4% QoQ and 44% YoY
items.quote: gross slippages, happy to report that here we saw a 2% reduction on a Q-o-Q basis and on net slippages, we saw an improvement of about 4%

items.statement: Slippage ratio improved to 2.49% from 2.68% QoQ; collection efficiency stable at 99.5%
items.quote: the overall slippage ratio, that further improved to 2.49% in the current quarter as compared to 2.68% which we saw in the previous quarter. The collection efficiency of the bank continues to be quite stable now for many quarters ; it was at 99.5%

items.statement: MFI SMA 1&2 normalized to 0.71%; 93% of MFI book covered under CGFMU
items.quote: in microfinance, I would say things have largely got restored on the asset quality front; here the SMA 1 and 2 normalized to now only 0.71%

items.statement: Created voluntary contingency provision of INR 515 crore for macro/geopolitical/monsoon risks
items.quote: we have created a contingency provision of INR515 crores. This is purely I would say voluntary and on a prudent basis considering the evolving macroeconomic and the geopolitical uncertainties and the monsoon related factor

items.statement: Loan book crossed INR 3.05 lakh crore, up 20.6% YoY; retail/agri/MSME INR 2.4 lakh crore (+18% YoY), wholesale INR 64,000 crore (+30% YoY)
items.quote: loan book, there also we registered a strong growth of 20.6% on a Y-o-Y basis and that book has now crossed INR3 lakh crores to reach about INR3.05 lakh crores

items.statement: Credit cards in force 4.8 million; card book INR 9,600 crore (+19% YoY); spends +22% YoY
items.quote: the cards in force have now reached 4.8 million during the quarter. The book grew by about 19% on a Y-o-Y basis and was about INR9,600 crores. The spends on the credit card grew at a healthy pace of 22% on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Wealth management AUM reached INR 64,000 crore, up 24% YoY
items.quote: the AUM has now reached almost about INR64,000 crores and it grew at 24% on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: MFI book INR 6,700 crore, marginal increase QoQ; targeting 15% YoY book growth for FY27
items.quote: we feel that we could end up or target a book increase of 15% on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Customer business (deposits + funded assets) crossed INR 6 lakh crore, up ~20% YoY
items.quote: our customer business, which is your deposits plus your funded assets, that has crossed INR6 lakh crores during the quarter and we saw a Y-o-Y increase of almost about 20% both put together

items.statement: Disbursements grew 25%+ YoY in Q1, driving fee income growth of 22.9% YoY
items.quote: backed by disbursements, which almost increased by 25% plus on a Y-o-Y basis in Q1

items.statement: Customer deposits near INR 3 lakh crore (+16.6% YoY, +5.3% QoQ); total deposits +17.7% YoY, +5.9% QoQ
