items.statement: GNPA improved 12 bps Y-o-Y to 2.66%, up 5 bps Q-o-Q; PCR at 42%
items.quote: NPAs improved 12 bps Y-o-Y to 2.66%, though up 5 bps sequentially.

items.statement: Stage 2 ECL increased to 16% from 6%, total provisioning at 1.91% of assets (2x regulatory minimum)
items.quote: As flagged in our last call, we took Stage 2 ECL up to 16% from 6%, bringing total provisioning to assets at 1.91% - The highest we've taken to date and roughly twice the regulatory requirement.

items.statement: Credit cost at 1.45%, expected to remain range-bound at 1.4-1.5% for next two quarters
items.quote: Our credit cost for the quarter is at 1.45%, we expect it to remain in this range in the short term.

items.statement: Cost of funds down 90 bps Y-o-Y to 8.42%; expect to stabilize at current levels
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing for the quarter is at 8.42% which has reduced 90 bps Y-o-Y and 10 bps Q-o-Q.

items.statement: Upfronted borrowing, closing liquidity INR 1,864 crores; intend to keep higher liquidity as AUM grows to INR 15,000 crores
items.quote: we have upfronted borrowing seeing the macro environment and thus have a closing liquidity of INR 1,864 crores. As we grow towards INR 15,000 crores, we intend to keep higher liquidity on the balance sheet.

items.statement: ROE at 14.7%, ROA at 4.53%; PAT INR 130 crores, up 6% Q-o-Q and 29% Y-o-Y
items.quote: PAT stood at INR 130 crores, up 6% Q-o-Q and 29% Y-o-Y, marginally outpacing book growth. That gap reflects the combined efficiency of risk-adjusted pricing, disciplined borrowing costs, and distribution, each working together. We close the quarter at 14.7% ROE

items.statement: New gold loan regulations effective April 1, 2026 reset eligibility norms, reducing loan amounts
items.quote: Second, gold prices were on a declining trend and with new regulations effective April 1st, 2026, resetting eligibility norms, the loan amount landing in customers' hands came down accordingly.

items.statement: RBI circular mandating banks not to accept collateral security for MSME customers within 20 lakh ticket size impacted co-origination (20% of disbursals/book)
items.quote: Third, the regulator's circular mandating banks not to accept collateral security for MSME customers within the 20 lakh ticket size had a direct bearing on our co-origination which accounts for roughly 20% of our disbursals and book.

items.statement: Competitors showing up with competitive pricing or generous loan amounts, adjusted footwork
items.quote: Lastly, a few birds strayed on the badminton court, by which I mean competitors showing up with competitive pricing or generous loan amounts which simply made us adjust our footwork.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM grew 11% Q-o-Q to INR 2,631 crores; gold yields contributed to yield improvement
items.quote: The loan against gold AUM is at INR 2,631 crores with a growth of 11% on Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Company yield range 17.50%-17.75%; Q1 yield 17.9% (up 29 bps Q-o-Q) due to gold portfolio performance
items.quote: That's our range where the yields generally stabilize. One good quarter of either product gives a 10-15 bps up and down. So, that's the range we will be at and which ensures that at say current cost of fund 10 bps up and down will give you a spread of more than 9

items.statement: Household DSR touching 14% (among highest globally); retail credit to GDP at 45%+; sub-10 lakh segment leveraged stress
items.quote: If you had seen the latest CLSA report, on the household DSR in India now almost touching 14%, and which is one of the highest in the world. So, while, people look at retail to GDP which also is now pushing 45% plus and is really high, but what is concerning is the DSR.

items.statement: Guidance unchanged on all fronts for coming quarter; preparing for unanticipated scenarios with anti-fragile approach
items.quote: Our guidance for the coming quarter remains unchanged on all fronts. No surprises there, birds on the badminton court notwithstanding.

items.statement: Employee cost increase due to increments and full-year impact of 20-25 branches opened in H2 FY26 plus 5 in Q1
items.quote: One obviously is the rollout of increment that has happened, that has one impact. The second is that the last quarter we opened close to 20-25 branches, again this quarter we've added five, so, all those employees that we've hired, full-blown cost has come in this quarter.

items.statement: Branches opened in last year need to become productive before further expansion; 60% of distribution from branches >67 crores AUM
items.quote: Now, these addition of branches have to actually start delivering the required returns before we add in any more branches.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of mid-teens for FY27; EBITDA margin to be maintained at FY26 level
items.quote: Overall, we expect the top line to grow in line with the stated guidance of mid -teens. We will continue to invest behind our core brands, super-premium to luxury portfolio and organizational capabilities while maintaining FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY 26.

items.statement: Backward integration expected to deliver ~300 bps EBITDA margin benefit by FY28 and further 100 bps by FY29
items.quote: These initiatives are expected to improve supply security, drive structural cost efficiencies, and support EBITDA Allied Blenders & margin expansion over the medium term, including an expected margin benefit of approximately 300 basis points by FY28 and a further 100 basis points by FY29

items.statement: India-UK FTA expected to improve margins by 70-80 bps in FY27 and 130-140 bps in FY28
items.quote: We expect the benefit to flow in second half of the year and would lead to about 70 to 80 basis points improvement in current financial year. For FY28 on a full year basis, it would help us in improving margins by 130 to 140 basis points.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%; like-to-like gross margin 48.4% (up 522 bps) excluding supply chain impact
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 277 basis points to 46%, supported by a favorable input cost environment and early benefits from backward integration despite the temporary impact of global supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 reported EBITDA margin 12.2%; like-to-like EBITDA margin 14.7% (up 189 bps) excluding supply chain impact
items.quote: Reported EBITDA stood at ₹120 crores compared to ₹119 crores in Q1 FY 26 with EBITDA margin at 12.2%.

items.statement: Total volume grew 6.2% YoY to 9 million cases; Prestige & Above grew 10.7%, Mass Premium & Others grew 2.3%; outperformed industry
items.quote: Total volume stood at 9 million cases, growing 6.2% year-on-year. The growth was supported by continued momentum in the Prestige and Above portfolio, which grew 10.7%, while Mass Premium and others grew 2.3% during the

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value in Q1 FY27 vs 46.2% and 55.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, the Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value compared to 46.2% and 55.8% respectively in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: ICONiQ White volume grew 33.8% YoY to 3.1 million cases in Q1 FY27; monthly average 1 million+ cases
items.quote: ICONiQ White continues to lead this momentum. The brand delivered 3.1 million cases in Q1 FY27 compared to 2.3 million cases in Q1 FY26 with a monthly average of 1 million plus cases resulting in a growth of 33.8% in the quarter on year -on-year basis.

items.statement: ICONiQ White targeting close to 15 million cases in FY27 from 10.7 million in FY26
items.quote: After having done 10 million plus case volume in FY26 I am hoping to make it close to 15 million cases this year, 10% here or there.

items.statement: Malt distillery at Rangapur expected operational in H1 FY27; PET bottle facility commissioned in FY26 and EBITDA accretive
items.quote: The PET bottles manufacturing facility at Rangapur, Telangana was commissioned in FY26 and continues to be EBITDA accretive. The malt distillery at Rangapur is expected to become operational in H1 FY27, strengthening our in-house malt capacity.

items.statement: Capex program funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within defined framework
items.quote: Our capex program is planned to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within our defined framework through the investment cycle.

items.statement: Operating cash flow ₹174 crores in Q1 FY27; net debt reduced ₹33 crores to ₹947 crores; Net Debt/EBITDA 1.7x, Net Debt/Equity 0.6x
items.quote: Operating cash flow generation stood at ₹174 crores in Q1 FY 27, supported by profitability and sustained working capital discipline. Net debt reduced by ₹33 crores during the quarter from ₹981 crores as of March 26 to ₹947 crores as of June 26.

items.statement: International footprint expanded to 39 countries in Q1 FY27 from 36 in Q4 FY26; exports asset-light with superior working capital efficiency
items.quote: ABD has expanded its footprint to 39 countries in Q1 FY 27 compared to 36 countries in Q4 FY 26, reinforcing our position as one of India's leading spirits exporters by volume.

items.statement: Telangana overdues ~₹400 crores; recent supplies paid on time; dialogue ongoing for price increase
items.quote: Overdue from Telangana government is approximate ₹400 crores. So right now, what's happening is Telangana is paying us well within agreed timeline for all recent supplies.

items.statement: Price increase dialogue ongoing with Telangana and 1-2 other states; management optimistic based on historical state responsiveness
items.quote: I can see Telangana which is in sight and there are 1 or 2 other states. I would not like to talk about it right now. But yes, there are 1 or 2 states on the cards.

items.statement: Deluxe vodka and premium whisky launches planned for H2 FY27 to fill white spaces
items.quote: There is a vodka market of 15 million to 18 million case s, where there is a brand leader which is unchallenged. It is a high contribution segment and now ABD can make foray into this space, this in H2 FY27. We will also come up with a premium Whisky in H2 FY 27 which will again be a uniquely packaged product with a new concept altogether.

items.statement: ABD Maestro FY26 revenue ~₹40 crores; targeting double in FY27; 10 brands launched across whisky, gin, vodka, rum
items.quote: We feel that the turnover that we clocked in FY 26 was top line of ~₹40 crores, which we expect to double in FY27. So that is an indication of how the business is moving forward.

items.statement: ABD Maestro premium touch points expanded to over 5,500; portfolio available in 6 international markets and 4 travel retail locations
items.quote: We have now expanded our presence in Odisha and Telangana as well, increased our premium touch points to over 5,500. The portfolio is now available in 6 international markets and 4 travel retail locations.

items.statement: Evaluating new vendor evaluation in buyers' market for packaging materials and value engineering measures to absorb supply chain impact
items.quote: In the current dynamic environment, we are also evaluating and undertaking multiple initiatives, including such as new vendor evaluation in the current buyers' market for packaging materials and value engineering measures.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by ₹33 crores to ₹947 crores; Net Debt/EBITDA 1.7x and Net Debt/Equity 0.6x within guidance
items.quote: Net debt reduced by ₹33 crores during the quarter from ₹981 crores as of March 26 to ₹947 crores as of June 26. Net Debt to EBITDA stood at 1.7x and Net Debt to Equity stood at 0.6x, both comfortably within our stated guidance.

items.statement: Officer's Choice retains leadership in India's Mass Premium Whisky category and position as India's number 1 exported Whisky brand
items.quote: Officer's Choice remains a strong cash flow generator and continues to hold leadership in India's Mass Premium Whisky category while also ret aining its position as India's number 1 exported Whisky brand

items.statement: ICONiQ White recognized as world's fastest-growing millionaire whisky brand for 3 consecutive calendar years 2023, 2024, 2025
items.quote: It also continues to be recognized as the world's fastest -growing millionaire whisky brand for 3 consecutive calendar years 2023, 2024 and 2025.

items.statement: Reiterated FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margins
items.quote: we really remain confident and are happy to reiterate our FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue as well as, EBITDA margins of 40%.

items.statement: Semaglutide demand significantly outpaces supply in Canada and India; generic pens provide access to latent demand
items.quote: The constraint in this market has been supply, not demand. In fact, the demand has been significantly outpacing supply both in the markets where the brand was present or was launching.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin improved significantly due to higher contribution from drug device combination business and H2-heavy base business
items.quote: it's basically the mix which is driving this. You know, the as you see there's a significant improvement in margins which primarily coming from higher contribution from the drug device combination business

items.statement: Order book visibility supports FY28 guidance across DDC, biologics, soft gel, and injectables with multiple pillars of growth
items.quote: each of our business offerings is goin g to be contributing to our FY28 guidance what we have given

items.statement: ~80% of $100 million capex committed, mostly for DDC; biologics expansion capex will be significantly lower
items.quote: last year we mentioned we had taken about US$100 million capex to be invested across sites, most of it coming to drug device combination. As we sit today, almost 80% of that capex has been committed

items.statement: Second DDC cartridge line commercializing in Q2 FY27, doubling sterile days; third line within FY27, fourth line later in FY28
items.quote: second cartridge line being set for commercialization in this quarter. This line will double our number of sterile days available for production

items.statement: Shift toward more commercial sales agreements (CSAs) vs MSAs as new DDC capacity comes online
items.quote: the mix of the company is going to be driven by significantly more CSA. The whole idea is that the capacity has been constrained till now

items.statement: Added six new logos and nine new launches in Q1; first new GLP customer onboarded last quarter; Formycon partnership for biologics
items.quote: We have had nine new launches during the quarter. We added six new logos, which is really expanding our already wide customer base.

items.statement: 12 successful inspections in Q1 including two surprise FDA audits; compliance track record remains exemplary
items.quote: We had 12 successful inspections this quarter across regulatory inspections and customer audits, including two surprise FDA audits across two of our sites.

items.statement: RFP funnel for biologics is nearly 4x vs year ago across innovators, biosimilars, and animal health
items.quote: our RFP funnel today is almost 4x of what it was just over a year ago. And this spans across innovators, biosimilars, as well as animal health companies.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues increase freight time and cost but impact muted due to ex-works contracts; US tariff announcement seen as temporary
items.quote: the geopolitics is in a flux, no doubt about that. Especially what is happening in the Middle East is in nobody's interest. So, for us also, typically it has impacted in terms of the freight challenges

items.statement: Opex for new DDC lines upfronted; optimal EBITDA contribution will come when all lines are in place due to operating leverage
items.quote: while the new line revenue will be coming in as the lines get installed, but the opex is there today already. So, as new lines will come in, the opex leverage will play in more.

items.statement: Injectable site shutdown in Q2 FY27 to add pre-filled syringe and lyophilization capacity; new capacity available for full FY28
items.quote: this first half itself, we will be taking a shutdown on our one of our sterile injectable sites basically to add this capacity.

items.statement: Soft gel capacity (2.4B) being filled via tech transfers over next 12-15 months; greenfield site process initiated for further expansion
items.quote: we see our capacity which was added to be, completely taken over the next 12 to 15 odd months. And I also want to share with you that because, we are completely, we have no possibility to increase capacity further in the current site, we have already initiated a process of starting a greenfield.

items.statement: India's biologics CDMO share still small vs South Korea; integrated drug substance/drug product offering is key differentiator
items.quote: Remember, the capacity which is available in India is still a very small fraction of what is available in countries like South Korea, for example. So, I see this as an opportunity for companies, coming to India and especially to OneSource because we are am ong a very, very small group of CDMOs offering integrated drug substance and drug product in the same site

items.statement: Two customers achieved first-to-file status in US for tirzepatide demonstrating complex peptide and drug device capability
items.quote: the strength of our complex peptide development and drug device capability was also demonstrated once again when with two of our customers successfully getting the first-to-file status in US with tirzepatide

items.statement: EBITDA trajectory to continue upward beyond FY28 driven by biologics commercialization from FY29, Europe/US market openings, and all modalities
items.quote: One clear answer for you is that yes, our EBITDA trajectory will continue to go upward beyond FY28. And this is going to be dependent on all our modalities, which all our service offerings.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 8% to 12% YoY for FY27
items.quote: These strengths support our medium -term target of delivering revenue growth of 8% to 12%.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 140-160 crores for FY27
items.quote: we will probably maintain the range we have said earlier, about INR 140 crores to INR 160 crores per year of capital expenditure, even in this financial year.

items.statement: IoT business expected to grow ~45% YoY in FY27 and 35-40% in FY28
items.quote: Last year, we grew close to 45%, we expect a similar percentage growth on IoT business.

items.statement: Payment solutions expected to grow 10-12% CAGR
items.quote: Payment solutions we expect a decent growth over this year and next year. Maybe , as we go along, we need to see how the product mix evolves and other opportunities evolve. Overall, internally, we have a plan of close to 12% CAGR

items.statement: Communication and fulfillment expected to remain flat
items.quote: Communication and fulfilment, we expect that to be more or less flat.

items.statement: Healthy demand across key verticals driven by deeper customer engagement and technology adoption
items.quote: During the quarter, we witnessed healthy demand across our key business verticals, supported by deeper customer engagement, increasing adoption of our technology-led solutions, and strong momentum in our non -payment businesses.

items.statement: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 due to higher material costs
items.quote: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 as cost of materials consumed increased faster than revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 135 bps YoY to 25.1% despite gross margin pressure
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 94 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.1%, an increase of 135 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: 40-45% of gross margin impact from currency, rest from war-driven commodity and logistics costs
items.quote: maybe 40% to 45% of impact is directly attributable to currency , and the remaining probably is due to the direct impact of the war on the input costs.

items.statement: Expect margin improvement in H2 FY27 from operating leverage and better product mix, assuming stable macro
items.quote: we feel that the margin should definitely have a positive bias as we go on.

items.statement: Won two multi-year PSU bank tenders worth ~INR 73 crores over tender period
items.quote: In this quarter, we won two multi -year tenders from leading PSU banks, which represent approximately INR 73 crores in revenue over the tender period.

items.statement: Steady order pipeline supports FY27 guidance; business is back-to-back with customer demand
items.quote: So, right now we have a steady order pipelin e basis which we have given our guidance for the year. And, as you know our business is essentially back -to-back, with the demand being put to us by the customers.

items.statement: Bengaluru greenfield metal card facility near ready; certification underway; operational by end of calendar year
items.quote: we are setting up a completely new greenfield facility for metal cards in Bengaluru, which we see is almost in the ready state. Now we will be getting into the certification and the compliance processing , and we feel by Q4 ,we should be into that process . Before the end of this calendar year, that facility should be operational

items.statement: IPO proceeds utilization on track; INR 24.4 crores deployed in Q1 FY27 (capex INR 6.7 cr, GCP INR 13.7 cr, issue expenses INR 3.9 cr)
items.quote: During Q1, a total of INR 24.4 crores were deployed, primarily towards capex of INR 6.7 crores, GCP of INR 13.7 crores, and issue expenses of INR 3.9 crores.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization 65-70% on average, peaks at 85-90% during high demand periods
items.quote: capacity utilization, typically for us, in our business currently is around 65% to 70%. Having said that, this also has a cyclical nature to it. So , typically, when customers have higher renewal cycle demands or there are month-end loads of customers, we also reach about 85% to 90% of our capacity utilization

items.statement: SIM card business capacity utilization ~40% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: For the SIM card business, Pratik, we were close to around 40% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Actively working with customers on price revisions to protect margins amid geopolitical and cost pressures
items.quote: we are actively working with customers on price revisions and taking steps to protect margins and maintain healthy profitability.

items.statement: Chip prices flattish in USD terms; marginal improvement offset by dollar impact; inventory holding increased for better pricing
items.quote: We've had some marginal improvement in the chip pricing, but it's got more than offset by the dollar impact.

items.statement: Lead times from chip suppliers have increased; no clear price increase indications yet; monitoring closely
items.quote: as of now, we don't have any . We have a forward bias that probably sometime next year things, you know, could be different. We don't have very clear indications, but right now , for us, the lead times have gone up from the suppliers.

items.statement: Payment solutions 42%, Communication & fulfillment 40%, IoT 18% of Q1 FY27 revenue
items.quote: In terms of revenue mix across our core verticals, payment solutions continue to be the largest vertical, which contributed 42 % of the revenue, followed by communication and fulfilment at 40% and IoT solutions at 18% in Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Premium metal cards gaining strong traction with superior margins; expanding manufacturing at Bengaluru facility
items.quote: Our premium metal card business continues to gain strong traction and remains an important growth driver withi n the payment solution s segment. We are witnessing increasing adoption from banks and Fintech partners as institutions seek to enhance customer engagement and differentiate their premium offerings.

items.statement: IoT growth driven by RFID traceability in retail, logistics, pharma, food supply chains, manufacturing; moving to integrated end-to-end solutions
items.quote: Enterprises across retail, logistics, pharmaceuticals, food supply chains , and manufacturing are increasingly adopting RFID -led traceability and automation solutions to improve visibility, compliance, and operational efficiency.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contributed 56% of revenue; >95% revenue from existing clients showing stickiness
items.quote: The top 10 customers contributed almost 56 % of our revenues , and more than 95 % of our revenues came from existing clients, showcasing the stickiness of client relationships and strong renewal and repeat business characteristics of our business model.

items.statement: SIM business catering to 20-25% of third-largest telecom operator's pre/post-paid SIM requirement
items.quote: We are currently catering to 20% to 25% of their requirement of the SIMs.

items.statement: Insurance client reduction (life 13 to 10, general 9 to 7) due to nominal-business clients going fully digital; no re-tenders or lost business
items.quote: the customers that typically have churned out in insurance are customers who were doing very nominal business with us, you know, almost zero. They've gone completely digital, and there's probably very less business that we were doing with them over these years.

items.statement: Encouraging traction from global markets, particularly Europe and Africa, for metal cards; exploring export channel for growth
items.quote: We are also seeing encouraging traction from global markets, particularly in Europe and Africa, which provides an a dditional a venue for growth going forward.

items.statement: Increased inventory holding of chips for IoT and payment solutions to secure better pricing and manage lead times
items.quote: the strategy that we've adopted over the last couple of quarters is to increase our inventory holding of chips for both for IoT business and the payment solutions business. So , that allows us to basically get better pricing because of the inventory holding at the pricing.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents of INR 369 crores as of June 30, 2026; well-capitalized balance sheet
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, we had cash and cash equivalents of INR 369 crores.

items.statement: Revenue from operations INR 377 crores, up 21.1% YoY, down 6.9% QoQ
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, our revenue from operations stood at INR 377 crores, up 21.1% Y-o-Y and down 6.9% Q-o-Q.

items.statement: PAT INR 60 crores, up 63.8% YoY with 16% margin (+418 bps YoY)
items.quote: Our PAT for the quarter stood at INR 60 crores, registering a growth of 63.8 % Y-o-Y with margin at 16%, up 418 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs. 357.63 crores as of March 31, 2026, with 3-5 year contract life cycles providing visibility beyond 24 months
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our order books stood at Rs. 357.63 crores. Since our contracts are 3-5 years in life cycle, these order books provide visibility beyond 24 months.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 21% from 15% in FY25 driven by operating leverage and cost management
items.quote: EBITDA grew 57% year-on-year to Rs. 48 crore s, while EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 21% compared with 15% in Financial Year ‘25, driven by improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 26.6% from 17.5% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA increased 3% to Rs. 16 crores, with EBITDA margin expanded to 26.6% compared with 17.5% in corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Expect order bookings in FY27 to be better than FY26 due to government digital infrastructure spend in India and Africa
items.quote: With the buoyancy, as I said in my opening speech, with the spend, with the governments in Africa and in India, with the buoyancy, our order bookings are going to be better than last year.

items.statement: See massive opportunities from mining modernization across Indian states and African countries, plus private sector players like JSW and Adani
items.quote: We see massive opportunities coming from the state governments and the ministries across the few countries and we also see tremendous amount of spend being done by the private companies or the public sectors like Steel Authority of India or the Gujarat Mining Development Corporation or Odisha Mining Corporation to that of JSW's and Adani's.

items.statement: Over 90-95% of revenue historically comes from repeat customers with relationships spanning 15-20 years
items.quote: Over 90% to 95% of our revenue are historically come from repeat customer which is a testimony of our work delivery standards.

items.statement: International revenue was 5% and export revenue 9% in FY26, with expectation of growth from new deal bookings
items.quote: Our international revenue I last year was 5% while the other businesses 9% was in export revenue in year Financial Year 25-26 and I am sure that this percentage is now growing at a larger pace because of more deal bookings that have been done last year.

items.statement: DSO increased from 58 to 129 days due to government approval delays, but liquidity and WIP are aligned to manage this
items.quote: So, typically the governments we all know are a little bit slow in approval processes. So, over the past years we have mastered that art that our liquidity and our work in progress are all aligned considering this delay that happens.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs. 0.5 per equity share for FY26 subject to AGM approval
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.5 per equity share for Financial Year 26, subject to shareholders' approval at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Mining remains largest revenue vertical with implementations across Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Kenya and bids in Africa
items.quote: Mining remains as one of the largest contributors to us. We develop software for mining for the governments we call it systems like i3MS in Jharkhand, Odisha we have i3MS, we have the similar system implemented in Jharkhand, state of Chhattisgarh, we have done it in state of Bihar in the past, we are doing it right now in the state of Rajasthan, we have implemented at Kenya.

items.statement: Added two new geographies Malawi and Cabo Verde in FY26, with consolidated Africa delivery center in Nairobi covering Kenya, Uganda, Ethiopia, Malawi
items.quote: You will be happy to know that last year we added two new geographies that is Malawi and Cabo Verde is a country which is west of Senegal to our business portfolio.

items.statement: Recognized one-time exceptional charge of Rs. 2.7 crores for statutory impact of new Labor Codes in FY26
items.quote: During the year, the company recognized a one-time exceptional charge of Rs. 2.7 crores towards the statutory impact of new Labor Codes.
